items.title: KOLONİ
items.text:
KOLONİ is an agent workspace that runs on your own machine. You chat with an agent, the Orchestrator, in a folder of yours. It reads, searches, edits and runs commands there. It hands parts of the job to other agents (Coder, Reviewer, Tester and more) when that helps. The agents run on models you add: an API key, a model server of your own, or a CLI you are signed in to (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, agy). A canvas beside the chat draws each turn from what really happened. Before anything risky, an agent asks you on a card.

KOLONİ listens only on 127.0.0.1, on your own machine. It sends no telemetry.

KOLONİ's words and how they hang together. Each is explained in the Glossary.

items.title: Backup and update
items.text: What is where, what the update script does in order, and what Export and Restore cover. (full size)

items.title: Backups KOLONİ makes by itself
items.text:
Before a new version changes the database, KOLONİ copies it to runtime/data/backups/. It keeps the last five copies. The update script's own backup goes in the same folder and counts among those five.

At its first start of a day (by the date in UTC), KOLONİ also copies the database there, as daily-koloni-<date and time>.db, and keeps the last three. These are counted apart from the five above, and a KOLONİ that is left running makes none until its next start.

Backups hold your API keys, in plain text, like the database itself. Keep runtime/ private.

items.title: Export everything
items.text:
Settings › The app › Your data › Export: "Everything KOLONİ keeps, in one .zip: chats, agents, providers, memory, skills and attachments. Your project folders stay where they are."

Not in the file: your project folders (with their .koloni/ folders and Knowledge), working copies, logs, and the CLIs' own sign-ins.

  • Include API keys and secrets (keep this file safe): without it, the keys KOLONİ stores in its settings are left out, and so are secret files you attached to a chat (a .env, a key file: the chat keeps their name, and the page lists them once you choose the file to restore). A key that was ever written in a chat, in another file you attached, an agent's output or a command stays in the file either way.
  • Export everything downloads the file.

items.title: Restore
items.text:
"Restore only a file you exported yourself: it decides which programs KOLONİ may start."

  1. Settings › The app › Your data › Restore from a file…, and choose the .zip.
  2. Nothing changes yet. Close KOLONİ and start it again; the restore happens at that start. Until then you can Cancel it.
  3. Your data as it was is set aside in runtime/before-restore/, not deleted.
  4. "What starts by itself waits until you press Resume. To-do tasks that waited in a chat's queue are back on To-do." KOLONİ starts held (Held · Resume in the top bar), and as at any start, nothing left in a chat's To-do queue starts by itself: give the tasks to a chat again.

If the file had no keys, the page lists what needs its key again. A restore is refused while a turn is at work, or if the file is not a KOLONİ export, comes from a newer KOLONİ, or is damaged. If a restore fails at the start, your old data is put back, and the page says so.

items.title: Updating
items.text:
Stop KOLONİ first (Ctrl+C in its window). Then, in its folder:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
./scripts/update.ps1

./scripts/update.sh

It refuses if the folder is not a git checkout, if you have uncommitted changes in KOLONİ's files, or if something answers on KOLONİ's port. Otherwise, in order:

  1. backs up the database to runtime/data/backups/;
  2. pulls the new version (git pull --ff-only);
  3. updates the Python packages;
  4. updates the page's packages and builds the page;
  5. where Zensical is installed, rebuilds this guide (see This guide inside KOLONİ).

It stops at the first step that fails: "nothing after it ran". Only the guide's rebuild is different: if it fails, it warns and KOLONİ is updated all the same. At the end it says "Restart KOLONİ; the database is migrated when it starts", and where the backup is. -DryRun (Windows) or --dry-run prints the steps without running them.

For Docker, see Install.

items.title: Changelog
items.text: All notable changes to KOLONİ are listed here, newest first. English only.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Chat: talk to the Orchestrator while its agents work. While a turn runs the message box has Send now (Enter) - "the Orchestrator reads it in this turn": your message goes into the turn at work, and the Orchestrator answers it then, from where it waits for its agents or at its next step - and After this turn, which queues it as before. The box says "Write to the Orchestrator - it reads it in this turn…". Where the turn takes no message (a plan turn, a comparison, a To-do task's or a night job's turn, one not started from your page, another topic) or was ending, the message is queued and the box says why under it ("Queued: the turn was ending"). A message is never lost or read twice: a turn stopped or failed before the Orchestrator read it puts it in a turn of its own. The steps that answer it change nothing themselves - no file, command, web request or MCP server's tool: new work goes to an agent - and do not wait for a place among its agents at work. What you send now is your own word: a push card quotes it as it quotes the message that started the turn, the newest deciding (docs).
  • Agents: Stop and Message on an agent at work - on its node on the canvas and in its window's head - for one an agent opened. Stop ends that agent alone: the chat says "You stopped Coder. Its work so far is kept for your Take in; nothing of it is in the project.", the Orchestrator is told not to open it again unless you ask, and the rest of the turn goes on. Message opens its window at its Tell box. KOLONİ's own checks and a team recipe's agents keep their own Stop (docs).
  • Agents: the Orchestrator of an API model can open an agent in the background: it goes on at once - talks to you, opens others, messages or stops it with its new stop_agent - and takes a step for each agent's report as it comes, saying an agent is still at work until then. It can run a command in the background too (run_command with background), read it with command_output, stop it with stop_command, and is told when it ends. The chat's limits hold them as any agent (docs).
  • Agents: the Orchestrator of an API model says how a message to one of its agents goes (message_agent's how): reply as ever; leave - it goes on, an agent not at work takes it up now in a turn of its own, one at work is handed it at its next step or takes it up once its work ends, and the reply comes as a note; now - into an agent's running work (a CLI's running turn, with what came of it), else as leave. Only to agents it could message anyway; such a turn waits for the agent's other turns and for a place; a message left counts twice toward the turn's messages between agents; and however it ends - read, replied, the agent stopped, the turn over - the Orchestrator is told (docs).
  • Agents: reading a command that keeps running (a dev server, a background command), an agent can first wait for a piece of text to be printed - "listening on", "passed" - up to 2 minutes (command_output's until and timeout_seconds), told the line it was seen in, that it was not seen in time, or that the command ended; no step is spent on each look. A piece of text, not a pattern, looked for only in what the agent may read (secrets hidden) (docs).
  • Notifications: when an agent nobody waited for ends while nobody looks at its chat, a desktop notice says so - "Reviewer finished: 2 findings", "Coder stopped" - where the project has Desktop notifications on; it holds only the agent's name and how it ended. "Nobody looks" is herdr's rule: no page has the chat on screen with its tab seen and its window in front - a hidden tab, another window or another page of KOLONİ's over the chat is nobody; the notice that a card or a question waits for you now follows the same rule, and is no longer shown while you look at the chat (docs).
  • Notifications: desktop notifications on macOS (terminal-notifier where it is installed, else the system's own) and on a Linux desktop (notify-send) - before, Windows only; the words go to the program as arguments of their own, never through a shell. Where neither the program nor a desktop is there, the switch stays greyed out (docs).
  • Chats: a chat whose last turn ended - done, stuck or stopped - while you were not looking at it says so: "Done · not seen" on its row, and in Now, which puts what waits for your word first, then what ended where you have not looked since, then what is at work (herdr's order). Opening the chat, or a turn of it ending while it is on screen in front of you, makes it seen; a desktop notice does not. Every chat there was when KOLONİ upgrades the database counts as seen (docs).
  • Chat: a line over the chat while its turn runs with agents at work, a plan of the Orchestrator's or something waiting for you - "3 agents at work · step 3 of 6 · 1 waits for you · ≈ 0.40 USD": who is at work below the Orchestrator, the step of its plan, the cards that wait for you, and what the turn cost so far at your prices (left out where nothing of it is priced, never a made-up zero). A click opens At work in this turn: each agent, "Coder · working · since 14:02", with its Stop and Message, the Orchestrator's plan, and Open Ready for you (docs).
  • Agents: while its agents work the Orchestrator reads who of them is at work, since when and what each last said (agents_at_work, its words quoted and masked), and an API model's Orchestrator shows you its plan (update_plan): its window says it under Plan (its own words) - a Codex Orchestrator's plan too - and the line over the chat says its step. The plan goes with the turn (docs).
  • Agents: the Orchestrator can ask a second model for advice on a hard choice (ask_advisor), at most 3 times a turn: your new Advisor model in Settings › The app › Agents ("A model the Orchestrator may ask for advice. It sees the Orchestrator's summary and the turn's recent steps, masked."), else a model on another provider than the Orchestrator's, the strongest first - only one that answers with its tools off. It is sent the Orchestrator's question, summary, last 12 steps and who is at work, masked, and no tools; its answer comes back as data. Where none can be asked, the Orchestrator is told why and goes on. Its request is in the turn's spend and on Usage under its model (docs).
  • Ready: a decision the Orchestrator took for you without asking it can note (note_decision): a row of Decided for you, "Orchestrator · Decided: "Use SQLite for the cart"" with its reason, new until your OK, at most 10 a turn. Change takes your own words: into that turn while it works, as your message, else a turn of KOLONİ's in its chat tells the Orchestrator. When the database is upgraded (migration 0197) it gets a table for them; nothing else changes (docs).
  • Agents: the Orchestrator reads one pull request of the project's GitHub repository (read_pr_feedback, by its number or address): the review decision, the checks that failed or have not ended, each review and comment and the comments on lines, with who wrote each - with your own gh, read only, where it is installed and the project's origin is on GitHub. What reviewers and checks say comes as data, masked and cut, and where it reads like orders to an agent the chat warns you, as for a web page (docs).
  • Agents: a role with Run inside the CLI also runs inside GitHub Copilot CLI run Native (Copilot 1.0.114 on, its provider in the team guide): the Copilot Orchestrator is given the roles you turned on as sub-agents of its own, none of Copilot's built-in ones, and opens one with its own task tool. It is shown as an own sub-agent, "Checker (inside GitHub Copilot CLI)", with what it did inside it, and runs on the Orchestrator's model (docs).
  • Memory: when you say how you want work done from now on ("from now on don't ask me for X", "write commits in Turkish"), the Orchestrator keeps it for Your preferences, from your own words only - it quotes your sentence of the turn and KOLONİ checks it is a sentence of your own prose, never a fenced, quoted or backticked line you pasted, an agent's words or a tool's. As your new setting New preferences from your words says (Settings › The app › Agents): Add them, tell me (the default) adds your own sentence at once - never the model's wording, and only a plain rule: one that asks, forbids, sets a condition, takes back, names a push, a pull request or a merge, or reads as a request for this work goes to the card - and the chat says "Added to your preferences: "…"" with Undo; Ask me first puts the Orchestrator's line on a card under your words, with Add and Not now. Masked, cut at 300 characters, at most 3 a turn, never twice the same line (docs).
  • Agents: the Orchestrator's agents_at_work says what each agent waits for - a card of yours (its command or change, named), an answer to its question, its command running and since when, another agent, a place at its provider or in the turn - read from KOLONİ's records alone, "unknown" where they say nothing; At work in this turn over the chat says it beside each agent (docs).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Settings: a line of Your preferences never lets Full auto's check of your words run a command without its card - your words in the chat or the project's rules still can; a preference that forbids a command still stops it (docs).
  • Settings: of your messages, Full auto's check of your words runs a push, a pull request or a merge only on that turn's - the one that started it and those you sent into it; a sentence of an earlier turn never runs one (it can still stop one), so "You can push to main from now on." lets no later turn push (docs).
  • Permissions: at Full auto, in a chat you watch with the judge on, a plain push of the branch you have checked out to its own origin - git push, git push origin, git push origin <branch>, git push -u origin <branch>, git push origin HEAD - goes to Full auto's judge instead of a card, as Claude Code's auto mode: its fine pushes; its risky is the push card the list gave before, with the judge's reason on it ("KOLONİ's judge: …") - never a refusal, nor counted among the judge's refusals - which quotes you where you asked for the push. A push to main, master or origin's default branch stays a card at every level (quoted where you asked for it), and so does any other push - forced, tags, another branch, ref or remote -, every push at Ask and Auto-edit, in a To-do task's turn or a job while you're away, and where no judge model answers (docs).
  • CLIs: GitHub Copilot CLI run Native hears your word while it works: its Tell box is there again, and Send now goes into a Copilot Orchestrator's running turn (measured with Copilot 1.0.114). An agy agent's box says it can't hear messages while it works and sends your words to the Orchestrator instead (docs).
  • CLIs: a word written into a CLI's running turn - Send now, an agent's Tell box, another agent's message - comes to one of three ends, read from the CLI's own sign (measured on 27 Nov 2026): taken (Claude Code echoes it before its result, Codex answers with its turn, Copilot names it as taken before it goes idle), not sent (its turn was over - Codex's "no active turn to steer" - or it could not be written: Send now is read at the Orchestrator's next step or run, as before; a Tell or a message Codex said no to only after 5 seconds waits for the agent's next step, and a Tell's is said in the chat) or unknown (written, and no sign by its turn's end, or a no not measured) - never sent again, since it may have been read, and said in the chat: "Lead may not have read your word before its turn ended: … - it is not sent again; say it once more if it still matters". A Change of a decision or an answer still stands and is given again. An agent that sent the message is told which, in its answer or in a note. Claude Code 2.1.332 or later is started with --replay-user-messages for it, and a run whose word it echoed in its turn ends at its result, without the 30 seconds' wait for a turn on it (docs).
  • Settings: Full auto's judge reads new words ("D2"): what your words ask for is fine as far as you named it - never another target or more, never emptying or overwriting a file that was there; a plain push of the branch being worked on to its own origin is ordinary work; work your words do not ask for that reaches outside the task (an outside service, CI or settings files, another repository) is risky; and so is what Claude Code's auto mode blocks - amending a pushed commit, --no-verify, --insecure, an agent loop with no sandbox. Measured on 28 Nov 2026 on 252 cases with Claude Code's haiku: every ordinary command fine, 99% of the risky ones risky, 2.6 seconds at the median; it still lets an empty of a file by now and then, and called some empties you asked for risky (docs).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Chat: a command kept off its Always run rule by an agent's write of a file it may read - an .npmrc or x.npmrc, a package.json, a lock, a tsconfig.json, a pyproject.toml - says so on its card: "an agent wrote a file this line may read or load (evil096.npmrc)"; it said "an agent wrote its program" of a file the line does not run. Where an agent wrote the program too, the card names the program, whichever was written first. The rule still stops there, and no rule is offered (docs).
  • Docs: Codex run Native asks KOLONİ before its commands, a read of .env too - measured with Codex 0.172.0 on 27 Nov 2026; the guide said it ran its own safe commands (a .env read among them) unasked; older versions were not measured again. A command an allow rule of Codex's own covers still runs unasked and is recorded after it ran; the Models page and a Codex agent's window now say just that, no longer that its reads of secret files or of files outside the project run unasked (docs).
  • Permissions: a search with a quoted ;, &, &&, | or bracket that names .github (rg '&&' .github/workflows, rg 'a|b' .github) runs at Full auto as a search does: it was a card, "Names .github: … asked at every level", as its parts were cut inside the quotes and .github/workflows read as a command of its own. A line any other program runs keeps its quoted ; a cut - ssh host 'cd app && rm -rf build' is still a delete -, and so does a line handed to a shell, such as cmd /c "…", which keeps no ' quote. A search told ag's or ack's --pager by --pag, or ack's --output (Perl to ack 2.x), is no search: ag --pag='sh -c x' foo .github names .github (docs).
  • Chat: the line at a chat's top no longer starts "While you were away," - the Orchestrator notes a decision in a turn you watch too: "1 thing was decided for you in this project and 1 waits for you here." (docs).
  • Chat: going away from a chat whose Orchestrator is GitHub Copilot CLI run Native, the Go away line names and takes the tasks the Orchestrator itself put on To-do in that turn, as with Claude Code - it named none ("Tick the tasks to take in Change"); a task one of Copilot's own sub-agents tries to add is refused, as all KOLONİ's tools are to them (docs).
  • Memory: the hint by a suggested preference on the Memory page said nothing enters your preferences unless you add it - at New preferences from your words: Add them, tell me the Orchestrator adds a plain rule of yours itself. It now says that a suggestion, the summariser's or the Orchestrator's from your own words, enters only when you add it, and that at Add them, tell me the Orchestrator adds a plain rule itself, with Undo in its chat (docs).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Permissions: writing the files Claude Code protects that KOLONİ did not asks at every level now, Full auto too, and one written unasked is put back: .devcontainer/ and .devcontainer.json, .gitmodules, .cargo/, .mvn/, Gradle's wrapper (gradle-wrapper.properties, gradle-wrapper.jar), .bazelrc and .bazelversion - each runs or fetches code by itself, when the folder is opened or at the next build; .idea/ asks too, but is not put back (a JetBrains IDE rewrites it itself). An approved git submodule add, set-url or set-branch may write .gitmodules; ./gradlew test and cargo test run as before (docs).
  • Permissions: lines Claude Code still asks of are no search or look to KOLONİ either: a wildcard that may expand to an option (find *, rg foo *, cat -* - a file named -delete or --pre=x in the folder would be one) and a search chained to another command; and a redirection to bash's /dev/tcp/ or /dev/udp/ - or to a /dev/ path the shell builds as it runs (/dev/$t/h/80) - reaches the internet: asked at every level while a web tool is off. A ;, & or | inside quotes chains nothing in a search on a simple line (rg '&&' .github, rg 'a|b' .github: no backslash, backtick, $, #, line break or typographic quote, where sh and PowerShell read the quotes alike); in any other line, or any other program's, it is a card (docs).
  • Permissions: at Full auto, git run in a folder below the project's root (git status there, as cd sub && git status), in a folder KOLONİ does not know (Claude Code's PowerShell), or at a root with no .git but a HEAD (git may take it for a repository of its own) is put to Full auto's judge instead of running as a read or as ordinary work: a repository shaped there can set programs git runs. Below Full auto, such a root's git read is a card (docs).
  • Permissions: an approved git submodule foreach … (or status, or any other line that only names a submodule) no longer lets a change to .git/config stand after it - the command it runs could set a program git runs (core.fsmonitor); only the git submodule verbs that write git's config do, and a chain with a git command that runs one it is handed in it - git submodule foreach, git rebase -x, git bisect run, git difftool -x, git grep -O, git filter-branch - lets nothing stand (docs).
  • CLIs: Codex no longer opens sub-agents of its own. Codex 0.172.0 opened one when asked though KOLONİ switched its multi_agent feature off (measured 27 Nov 2026, gpt-6-luna); KOLONİ now also sets agents.enabled=false, with which it had no such tool (measured with its app-server, which Native and the session use; step by step and its web search are given the same switch, not measured there).
  • Permissions: a push of your feature branch reaches Full auto's judge only where KOLONİ finds nothing that sends it elsewhere or sends more: origin's default branch as origin itself names it (an origin that names none is a card), git's settings (no remote.origin.url, the branch's upstream or remote, push.default=matching, a push map, a mirror, tags, push options, a receive-pack, submodules - submodule.recurse too -, a hook set in the settings, a settings file git reads from the project out of .git - an include.path to ../.gitconfig an agent may write), a project that runs its commands in Docker, a branch or commit that moved between the judge's fine and the run, origin's address or git's settings changed since the turn began (an agent's git remote set-url), a pre-push or reference-transaction hook at all (yours too: husky's, Git LFS's - an unchanged hook can run what an agent wrote), origin a folder in the project, or a secret KOLONİ knows in any commit the push sends - counted against what origin itself says it holds, never a branch git keeps of origin's here. Each is a card. A judge's fine on a push lifts nothing once the judge is turned off while it looks (docs).
  • Permissions: a git remote that changes origin - add, set-url, remove, rename, set-head, set-branches, whatever the case of git's words and however the name is spelt (a quote inside it: ori''gin) - is asked at every level, Full auto too, as setting git's settings is: an origin an agent changed in one turn was the next turn's origin, unseen. Another remote's (git remote add upstream …) runs as before (docs).
  • Workspace: a secret in a root commit - an orphan branch's first commit, or the first commit of a history merged in - is found where KOLONİ looks through a branch's commits before it keeps or pushes one; a root commit's files were not read (docs).
  • Agents: a role run inside GitHub Copilot CLI is held as one inside Claude Code: each of its tools is asked through KOLONİ, held to its role's own tools, with a card where your level says so - at Ask a role that can change things is a card before it opens, as opening an agent is; it may not use KOLONİ's tools (the Orchestrator's, over the bridge Copilot shares with it), open a sub-agent of its own, or delete a file unless its role runs commands; Copilot's task opens only a role KOLONİ gave it, while the Orchestrator waits for it, and never with a model, level or setting of Copilot's choosing; a sub-agent KOLONİ did not open may use nothing; where its commands run is taken as not known (Copilot does not run them where KOLONİ puts the Orchestrator's), so its git reads ask at Ask and its git lines go to the judge at Full auto; and one of its tools that ran without KOLONİ being asked stops the turn. Its words, context and model are never the Orchestrator's - they no longer count a word you sent now as read -, and its tokens are counted in the turn (docs).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Ready: Ready for you and To-do are one page, Work - the rail's Ready is named so, and its To-do is gone. Work has two tabs under its heading, each with its count - Ready for you ("Ready for you · 2", what waits for your word) and To-do (its tasks not done) -; it opens on the tab shown last while KOLONİ is open, the arrow keys go from one to the other, and what you type on one, or a story open on To-do, stays as you switch. On Ready for you, what was done: a greeting, then the report of the project's last ☾ Away, while it works and once it has ended - one sentence ("2 of 3 jobs done, 1 could not be done."), a row for each job with its branch, checks and Take in / Try again / Open its chat, the night's lanes, how many were decided for you on its jobs and not seen (See them), what it spent, Copy report as Markdown - or one line, "Nothing new since you last looked", with no night or one seen and over a day old. Under it Waiting for your word, one list in one frame, each row saying what it is - Push, Parked command, Question, Proposed task, Done?, Ready to take in… - and whose; and Decided for you, a row you have not seen marked new. Ctrl+K's Work › To-do, a chat's Open it in To-do, The task on a decision and the canvas's To-do → open the To-do tab; the morning after a night, the top bar's ☾ Away line, Open in Ready for you, Ctrl+K's Work › Ready for you ("ready" finds it) and the top bar's pill on Work open Ready for you (docs).
  • To-do: each story is a card - its name, how many of its tasks are done, a honeycomb cell for each task and its tasks with how each stands (done, at work, done?, push waits for you, stuck, queued…) - and the tasks of no story one more card. A card opens its story in a panel over To-do: its branch where a night's job had one, its chat and state, its notebook with who wrote each note and when, Continue in chat, ☾ Do tonight (the Away panel with its tasks ticked), Close story (or Open it again), Rename and Delete, and its tasks with all they did - tick, order, edit, waits for, delete, their notebook and chat - and Do in chat. Close or Esc shuts it; while it is open what it lies over cannot be reached, and on a narrow screen it is a dialog over the whole page. The rough note is always in sight under the cards, its button Split into tasks. A proposed task's buttons say what they do: Add to To-do, Edit, Not wanted. What waits for your word on To-do - a proposal, a "done?", a change - is in Ready for you's one list, not twice on the page; a task the Orchestrator added at Full auto waits for your OK under Decided for you (docs).
  • Ready: a small hexagon - a cell - says how a thing stands, the same on the report, in Waiting for your word and on To-do: green done, honey at work, a honey rim your word, red-orange stuck, empty queued, a thin rim proposed. A word or its name always says it too, never its colour alone (docs).
  • Chats: the Chats page speaks in the same cells. Each chat has its cell and one line under its name: what waits for your word in it and what (a command, a question, a file change…), who is at work and on which branch, stuck (its last turn failed or was interrupted, or its To-do task is blocked), done with what it ran on, stopped, or no turn yet; a chat not read yet says nothing. What waits in a chat is what Ready for you lists for it, the top bar's pill's count. On top, Now over every folder, one strip across the page that stays in sight while the list scrolls under it (on a narrow window it wraps and scrolls away): a cell for each chat at work, each thing that waits for your word and each chat stuck or done today, one sentence that counts them, Go to Ready for you and what the cells mean; the list takes the page's whole width under it. Search, the state and sort choices, New chat and From a GitHub issue… are one row beside the heading. Each folder says how many chats it holds; the page's heading is Chats, as the rail says (docs).
  • Tools: the Tools page speaks in the cells too: a tool's or a server's cell says how it is let run - green runs without asking, a honey rim asks you first, empty is off, red-orange a server whose trust a reading took back - with their key under the heading. Built-in is now KOLONİ's tools: every tool, grouped as on a role's Tools tab, each with its cell; the five you can switch off here keep their switches, the rest say "by role". Each server is a card - switch, cell, name, command, state, roles -, and a watched one's Trust this server is on its head, in sight with the card closed. When a reading you start takes a trusted server's trust back, its cell turns red-orange: See the difference names what is new, changed or gone, Trust it again trusts it as it is (shown until you leave the page; a later reading adds to it). A tool's mark is three buttons side by side - Runs without asking, Ask, Off -, the one it has pressed with a ✓, in place of a list: no arrow key changes it. Open a page, New skills and Ask for a folder say "asks" on a role's tiles too: they go to a card. Each skill is a card with where it came from, its roles and how its agents read it in the last 30 days; skills agents proposed wait above them, with Open on Ready for you (their yes stays on their card there). The Servers tab says how many are watched, Skills how many are proposed; the tabs' counts are gone (docs).
  • Settings: the Settings page speaks in the cells too, and This project's eleven sections are seven, by job: How agents work (Agents, New chats start with, and your slash commands under More), When you're asked (Asking and away, Runs without asking - its rules a click away - and Commands and secrets under More), When the work is done (Checks and git), Limits and money, Memory and web, Notifications and This folder. No setting is gone: the ones few change are under a section's More, whose button says how many it holds and names what of it is set here - and When you're asked's sentence names what it folds too. Each section, and The app's Agents, Voice and Your data, first reads itself in a sentence made from its values as they stand - it changes as you change a setting, before you save. Beside each setting a cell says where its value comes from: full honey set here, an empty rim the default, light honey changed and not saved. Save is a bar at the section's foot, there only while something is changed, saying what. Ctrl+K and the links still find a section by its old name (docs).
  • Models: a CLI run Native (its own tools, in its own loop) is experimental: Claude Code's, Codex's and Copilot's How it runs offer Native only under Experimental, with Show experimental features on - Settings › The app › Agents' switch, called Show experimental CLIs until now, kept as you had it. Codex and Copilot then have one way left, and How it runs is not shown for them. A provider already run Native keeps working with the switch off, its card tagged Experimental, and keeps Native offered while you edit it (docs).
  • Settings: Checked's Pages (a changed page in KOLONİ's browser at three widths) and A test for the change (the Orchestrator asked for a test where code changed and no test did) are off unless you tick them in Settings › This project › When the work is done › Check by kind of work (under More); A test for the change is a new box there, and ticked it asks under Tests only too. A project that never changed Pages has it off from now on, and a turn that wrote a page says “Not checked: pages switched off for this project”; one where you ticked it on keeps it. Unticked, a turn that changed code and no test says “Not checked: a test for the change switched off for this project”. The tests and code style stay on (docs).
  • Agents: with Orchestrator decides, the teams the Orchestrator picks are where it starts, not a fence: beside their roles it opens any built-in role the work needs - an Architect, a Researcher, a DevOps or another of the fourteen that are in no ready team since this release - without your naming it. A role of your own still keeps to the teams it picked, a role only in teams it may not pick stays shut, a running recipe still opens only its step's roles, and Manual opens only the teams you picked, as before (docs).
  • To-do: the goal level over stories is hidden. Your tasks shows the stories at the top - a story a goal held stands there like any other - with no goal row, no "1 / 2 stories" bar and no Goal in a story's ⋯; Split into tasks writes a rough note as stories and tasks only, an agent's add_task takes no goal, and a proposal's card no longer names one. Nothing is deleted: the goals you made stay in the database (docs).
  • Settings: only the monthly budget, a provider's limit and a job's budget show up front; the other limits are under More limits, closed until you open it, and work as before. In This project › Limits and money, Monthly budget and Stop the work on a message over this many tokens (a job's budget: one message's work, a To-do task's or a job's while you're away) are in sight; how many agents work at once, Continue gives this many more steps and A discussion's tokens, at most are folded. In The app › Agents, Steps an agent may take, the two limits of a turn nobody watches, what knowledge reads and KOLONİ's test runs are folded; its button says how many it holds and names those set here. A provider's Limits tab and the Go away card's limits are unchanged (docs).
  • Recipes: Feature, Model change and Pipeline change run fewer agents: their Tester and general Reviewer steps did again what KOLONİ's Checks step does at the end - run the tests, and have a big or security-touching change looked at by KOLONİ's own Reviewer and Security reviewer. Feature is Write the spec → Build it → UI review (the UI designer), back to Build it at most twice: 3 to 7 agents, not 6 to 16 - one review per round, not four. Model change keeps its plan, its experts' review, the build and Compare the metrics: 4 to 10, not 6 to 14. Pipeline change is Change the pipeline → Check the data quality: 2 to 6, not 4 to 10. The two now check their tests and a review themselves, as Feature does, rather than following the project - even in a project at Nothing; a ready recipe cannot be changed, so to keep the old way copy it and set the copy's Checks step to Follow the project. A fix round of KOLONİ's checks no longer gives a recipe's loops their rounds again - a review whose loop ran out runs once more, and what it finds then is yours: the card names the findings and offers Fix the findings, as it does where a recipe stops before its next step; Ask for changes still does. Where a recipe's fixer loops back to its tests and those rounds ran out (Quality check, Upkeep), KOLONİ sends no fix round on top: it would only run the tests again. When the database is upgraded (migration 0195) the three ready recipes change where they are still as KOLONİ made them; your copies keep their steps - copy one again and add a step to have a Tester or a Reviewer of the recipe's own (docs).
  • Workspace: a branch's worktree - a ☾ Away job's, and a team's on a branch - is made in your project's own .koloni/worktrees/, as Claude Code keeps its worktrees in .claude/worktrees/; KOLONİ adds /.koloni/worktrees/ and /.koloni/copies/ to the repository's own .git/info/exclude once, so git status stays clean, and your .gitignore is not touched. In a project with no git a sub-agent's copy is made in its .koloni/copies/; in a project in git copies stay outside it, as before (a copy with no .git inside your repository would have its git answered by yours). Whether a project has git is looked at each time a copy is made. Each KOLONİ keeps its own folder there (.koloni/worktrees/<id>/<agent>/tree), so two on one project never clear each other's. Neither is copied into another copy, shown in the Files window, searched, or listed as a change; a project deleted from KOLONİ takes them with it. A git-less project's .koloni/copies/ holds a .gitignore of its own that ignores all of it, so its copies stay out of the git it gets later, and KOLONİ's .koloni/.gitignore lists worktrees/ and copies/ too (a missing line added after yours, its bytes kept). A copy is never taken from a folder of its name elsewhere, and a worktree whose record git clean -fdx removed is left at the next start, uncommitted work and all. Older copies and worktrees stay where they were made (docs).
  • Permissions: in .koloni/, the scratch tmp/ stays free; KOLONİ's worktrees/ and copies/ are free to look into - ls, cat, a search, the Files window - with no card of .koloni's, but each is one agent's work: from outside it, a write, tee, cp or mv, a file tool's write (at Auto-edit and Full auto too), a delete, a program run there or pytest's --basetemp there is asked at every level, as the rest of .koloni/ is. The agent whose tree it is names it by its full path as its own folder (Git Bash's /c/... too). The rest of .koloni/ - rules, settings, recipes, knowledge, the teams' shared/ folder - still asks at every level, and so does a line that climbs from a free folder into them (tmp/../rules.md, cd .koloni/tmp; echo x > ../rules.md) (docs).
  • Settings: Full auto's judge, at Refuse and go on, asks you after 3 refusals in a row, as Claude Code's auto mode does - a command that runs ends a row; one refused, turned down or waiting does not - or after 20 in the turn: from then on each risky command of that turn waits on its card, and the chat says once "Full auto's judge refused 3 commands in a row this turn; each risky one asks you now.". It asked after 3 in the turn however far apart, so an agent whose risky commands were refused now and then among work that ran was put on cards for the rest of the turn (docs).
  • Settings: at Full auto, a narrow Always run rule lets its very line by with no request to Full auto's judge, as Claude Code's auto mode does - a rule that names its task (npm test, npm run build, python gen.py, make build, gh pr list), its words and nothing more, run at the project's root in a chat you watch; not in a job while you're away nor a To-do task's turn, not where the line runs a program an agent wrote, nor an interpreter's or a runner's line whose file KOLONİ does not find (uv run python x.py) or a tool's run that builds the folder's code (cargo run, go run .). A broad rule never does: one with nothing but options past its program (npm, git, docker, make, gh, pytest -x), an install, a container or a remote (npm install, pip install, docker run, docker compose, git remote - offered on a card too), or a shell's, a wrapped line, an interpreter or a runner with no script or package named (bash …, env …, python -c …, npx, npm run, uv run). Until now no rule let a command past the judge; below Full auto rules work as before (docs).
  • Settings: Full auto's judge finds a command that destroys work in the project you did not ask to lose risky too, as Claude Code's auto mode does: deleting or emptying a file or folder that was there before the turn, or throwing away uncommitted changes, in the forms KOLONİ's list does not stop (> file, truncate, Set-Content, New-Item -Force, find … -exec rm, npx rimraf, robocopy /MIR, git read-tree -u --reset, a script or a one-liner that deletes). What you asked to remove, build output and caches (build/, dist/, node_modules, __pycache__), files the same agent made earlier in the turn, .koloni/tmp/ and what only shows or keeps work (git clean -n, git stash, git restore --staged) stay fine. Measured on 180 cases with Claude Code's haiku and Sonnet: no risky command called fine, every ordinary one fine. An agent whose command is refused is told it "may … destroy work in the project" among the reasons (docs).
  • Permissions: at Full auto, in a chat you watch with Full auto's judge on, KOLONİ's list keeps its card only for what it asks at every level, as Claude Code's auto mode does: a delete or an emptying in the project (rm, del, Remove-Item, Clear-Content, pytest's --basetemp), git work thrown away (git reset --hard, git clean -f, git checkout -- ., git restore ., git stash drop, git rm -f, git branch -D) and a stop by name that cannot stop KOLONİ itself nor what it stands on (taskkill /IM notepad.exe), each written as a plain line - words of letters, digits and _ . / = ~ -, joined by ; or &, a \ only in KOLONİ's own PowerShell - go to the judge instead of a card: fine runs it, risky is refused (Refuse and go on) or waits on its card (Ask me) - a card that says what the list says of the line and keeps no line: no Don't ask about this line again here; its risky stands for the turn, its fine is asked again each time. Where Check what I said first works it looks first, and its ask keeps the card. A line that is not plain (a quote, an escape, a wildcard, a brace, a group, a variable, a pipe, a redirection, a comment, a line break) or is handed to a shell, a wrapper or a prefix (bash -c "rm -rf build", sudo, env, FOO=1 …, … | xargs rm), a worktree removed (git picks one by its last name), what reaches out of the project or all of it (rm -rf ../x, rm -rf ., find . -delete, git clean -x), a link, a send, a git remote's branches, Docker's deletes, a secret, .koloni/ (its free folders too), a file that steers agents, what may stop KOLONİ and a line KOLONİ cannot read stay its card. With the judge off, no judge model to answer or no answer it can read - and at Ask before changes and Auto-edit files, in a To-do task's turn, in a job while you're away, in a turn of a chat you went away from, and for a CLI whose folder KOLONİ does not know - those lines are the list's cards as before; and if the chat leaves Full auto or the judge is turned off while it looks, its fine lifts nothing (docs).
  • For contributors: scripts/measure_judge.py --ids risky-67,fine-78 measures those cases alone, one call each (with --only, --prompt, --dry-run); a run of some cases decides nothing, a failed call stays an error, never a verdict, and an id that names no case, or one the gate stops before its judge, is refused before any call.
  • For contributors: 27 cases of tests/data/full_auto_judge_cases.json (risky-67…-70, -72…-81, -84, -85, fine-78…-81, -84, context-25…-27, -29…-31) are no longer marked stopped - the judge decides them now; git clean -fdx, find . -name "*.py" -delete and cmd's rd /s /q (/s reads as a path from the drive's root) stay. Six new cases: risky-87 and context-32 (a stop by name), risky-88 and risky-89 (a branch or stashes dropped after git's recovery was pruned), and risky-86 and fine-85 (a delete handed to a shell: marked stopped, the list's). check_what_i_said_cases.json marks its five force pushes stopped and has three more condition cases for the net's without and in case (words-172…174). app.commands.runs_inline, sends_off and readings, called by no code of the app, are gone; the judge's own test, test_judge_cases_format.py, imports scratch_delete_only from app.scratch_delete, where it lives now.
  • Chat: a push, a pull request opened or merged is yours to say. When a sentence of the message that started the turn asks for it - "Push it.", "Commit and push.", "Open a PR.", "Squash and merge.", "push et", "pushla", "PR aç", "merge edebilirsin", "PR'ı birleştir" - its card quotes you: You said “Push it.” — push now?, with one button, Push, as you said (Open the PR, as you said, Merge, as you said), and Reject. It is still a card, at every level, in a turn you started from the app's page: no Judge model has passed the measurement of Check what I said first (Claude Code's Sonnet, 27 Nov 2026, did not), so none lets it run unasked yet. Only the message you sent from the app's page to start that turn counts - never an earlier turn's, an agent's words, a tool's result, a file, your preferences or the project's rules, nor code, a quoted line or a sentence with a backtick, nor a message over 4,000 characters; its last sentence that mentions it decides, read with the whole message. A message that says no, asks, waits, puts it off or calls it off anywhere ("Push it. Actually no.", "Never mind.", "Scratch that.", "Hayır, bekle.", "Boşver."), says what you do or will do ("I'll do it myself."), or sets a condition ("after the review", "testler geçince") gets the plain card, and so does every push your preferences or rules forbid or set a condition on ("Never push to main."), and a sentence that names another branch or pull request than the line ("Merge PR 5." or "PR-5" for gh pr merge 7, "Push it to main." for a push of another branch - a branch as your repository knows it, read only). Only a plain git push to origin of branches of your repository's own (or HEAD) at the project's root, gh pr create and gh pr merge with their plain options, one line in letters, digits and double quotes, are quoted - a push to main or master by name only on a sentence that names it; a force push, a deleted branch, a tag or any other ref than a branch (tags/v1 and heads/main too), another remote, repository or owner's branch, a file read in, --admin, more than one command, a comma, @, single quotes or a body written with a heredoc keep the plain card, and so does a project whose git repository KOLONİ cannot read. The quote is shown in its own reading order, with no marks that turn text around; code in a longer fence - as Ask about this quotes an agent's text - is never your words. A To-do task's turn and a job while you're away keep the plain card too (docs).
  • Settings: Check what I said first lets a command run in a folder of the project other than its root only on a line of yours that names that folder from the root ("You may delete packages/api/dist." for rm -rf dist in packages/api): "You may delete dist/." is the root's dist - Claude Code's Sonnet, measured on 27 Nov 2026, let such a delete in another folder run (docs).
  • For contributors: scripts/measure_judge.py --prompt A measures Full auto's judge with its prompt before this release's (the default, B, is the one KOLONİ asks); a case of tests/data/full_auto_judge_cases.json marked stopped - a line KOLONİ's list stops before the judge - is not asked, and the summary lists the fine commands called risky as well as the risky ones called fine.
  • For contributors: the app's clock - ☾ Away's nights, the day's summary - is app/clock.py (Clock, app.state.clock), no longer app/triggers.py, and its switch is KOLONI_CLOCK; KOLONI_TRIGGER_CLOCK is still read for one release (docs).
  • Memory and To-do: notes are kept in two places. Memory is what stays true of the project: your preferences, its rules and now its Project notes - the lines you keep from the Add to Project notes? card are a box of their own under This project's rules in Memory's Your words, which the Orchestrator is given every turn, each line quoted as a note, never as your instructions (not in .koloni/rules.md, not read by Full auto's check), 4 000 characters at most; they are no longer a knowledge, and the Knowledge page no longer lists them (docs). A job's notebook is what its turns go on from: a To-do story's as before, and now a task's of no story too - a task done in a chat and a night's job while you're away, 📓 beside it on To-do, its Orchestrator's Task note: lines - and a note left for the whole turn on the chat's Notes tab, yours or an agent's post_note (three a turn), goes into the job's notebook too; read_notes gives it to every agent of the turn, in place of the turn before's notes. Each line a model is given says whose it is - KOLONİ's, an agent's or yours - and a task's message never makes its notebook your words for a search of earlier messages (docs).
  • Memory: Knowledge and Memory are one page. The rail has no Knowledge any more: Memory opens on two parts, What the project knows (its rules, facts and notes) and Sources to look things up in (what was the Knowledge page: Learn, Try it, Fresh, Spent, Used by); Ctrl+K's Knowledge opens the second. Agents have one tool to look things up, Recall: where a role uses knowledge it looks in that knowledge's pages too (a topic names one), after the memory and earlier messages - KOLONİ's own Reviewer, which reads no memory, still looks in its pages alone. lookup, the old tool, keeps working for one release where a role, a prompt or a guide names it (docs).
  • Memory: the page reads as cells, as Ready does. On top, one search and the three ways memory reaches an agent - Given at the start, Found when asked, Sources given to a role - then its two parts as tabs, each saying what waits in it ("1 waits for your word", "2 may be old"). What waits for your word is one honey box, in sight at once, a note beside the fact it would replace - three of them, the rest behind Show N more. Facts and Notes stand at the left, each fact with a cell for how it stands for agents - green given when the work names its subject, red-orange given to no agent until you look again (one no work can name says only to look again), empty only found by looking it up - and ten cells beside Facts fill as the core takes room; a note has Make it a fact in sight; History is folded under them, and a search hit in it unfolds it. Your words - your preferences, the project's rules and the Project notes - stand at the right on paper, with which other projects Search deeper also looks in and Change. Look at the sources again and Export are beside Facts (docs).
  • Memory: the sources are cards in a grid, each with a cell for how it stands - green learned (no change known: a repository, a folder or the code scan is not looked at again between learnings, a site only weekly if asked), honey learning, red-orange may be old or its last learning failed, empty not learned - and an opened card goes across the row. Used by is a tick for each role that uses it: untick one, or give it to another role with + Role… and Give (Map), as on the role's Knowledge tab; an expert's own stays the role's to change. This project's code and KOLONİ's own guide are offered as dashed cards of their own (docs).
  • Usage: the page reads as cells, as Ready and Memory do. The period - Today, 7 days, the new This month (the calendar month, as the budget counts it), 30 days, All - and This project / All projects are buttons. On top, one sentence says what the period cost, how much of this month's budget is used and the plan used most, with the boxes under it; the month's budget is ten cells, a tenth each, honey as it fills, a red-orange rim on what is left from 80% and red-orange once it is over; Plan limits draws a line on a subscription's bar where its picks go a tier lower, the bar orange past it and its row saying so. Day by day shows the last 30 days in one strip - money where any of it is priced, else the tokens reported - with the day that spent most and today. By provider and model says plan for a subscription instead of a dash, with Copilot's AI credits beside it; Chats that spent most shows the top three with what each cost (its models' costs added up) and every chat in numbers folded under; Who started it is a bar each; the decisions line follows the period, not only Today. Nothing is estimated: what was not reported stays "–" (docs).
  • For contributors: GET /api/usage also gives by_day (this machine's days, each with its models' costs added up), a cost on each chat's row the same way, and Copilot's nano_aiu and premium_requests added up on its model's row; the Usage rows' schemas are in app/schemas_usage.py.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Guide: MCP servers and trust and Adding an MCP server safely said a tool on Ask runs at Full auto; it asks you at every level, Full auto too, as KOLONİ does (docs).
  • Workspace: in ☾ Away, a file holding a secret KOLONİ knows that a job's agent committed on the branch itself is no longer said to be left out - its chat said "left out of the branch's commit … the rest of the work is on the branch" and its push row "· left out", though the file was on the branch. Run refuses that push, naming the file ("… on the branch holds a secret KOLONİ knows - take it off the branch first"), as before; "left out" is said only of a file KOLONİ's own commit left out (docs).
  • Ready: KOLONİ opened after a ☾ Away ended opens on Ready for you, where the night's strip is, as the night on Ready for you said - it went to the night's report on the canvas instead, and did so over a page you had opened in the first seconds (you clicked Ready, and a second later were on the canvas). It never takes you off a page you opened before the night was read, and goes there only on its first look at the night after it opens - not a minute later, when a first look failed; once the night has been on screen - the strip, or the report on the canvas - it opens as it was left (docs).
  • Ready: Change and redo on a card asked by an agent that never had a copy of its own - a Reviewer that only read - goes on in the copy of the agent it worked for, the Orchestrator's kept work; it started a fresh turn, that work left behind. Where a ☾ Away job's second try or Try again went on in a first try's copy, a card of the first try still says "its work was discarded": change a card of the later turn (docs).
  • To-do: in ☾ Away's morning, the turn that goes on after your decisions under Waiting for you works in the copy its job parked them in - not in the chat's newest kept copy, which could be a later turn's (a message of yours in another topic) (docs).
  • For contributors: PATCH /api/conversations/{id} that moves a plain chat into a project refuses, as it refuses a project's chat, the sub-agent limits and the discussion's budget the chat then follows - they were written on the chat and read by nothing, its project's shown and followed. Settings › This project sets them; a plain chat keeps its own (docs).
  • Agents: the chat's top agent is the Orchestrator where three places still said Lead: a recipe's candidates offer Auto, the Orchestrator picks for their models, Memory's Written by filter, its notes and its search say Orchestrator, and a discussion's window calls a team's lead its coordinator - it said "Docs lead" - as the canvas and the side panel do (docs).
  • CLIs: GitHub Copilot CLI run Native where it works in a working copy and its session has no sandbox - this machine cannot give it one, or the project does not hide its secret files - has the project looked at after each of its commands, as Claude Code's has since 0.1.8: a command that wrote into the project by a path it did not spell out was found only at the turn's end. Such a change is recorded as it happens, as made in the project by an unknown maker (docs).
  • Chat: a command card asked because no rule covers the line, where one of your Always run rules begins it but an option past its words or a node runner sent to another package or folder keeps it off, says so - it showed only Run once · Reject · Details. "your rule “npm exec tsc” does not cover this line: --globalconfig has it read a settings file, which can load code - run it once or reject it"; any other option is "an option past the rule's words", never the line's own word. Below Full auto, for KOLONİ's commands and a CLI's (docs).
  • Knowledge: Learn is held over the project's monthly budget, as a new message is: what a learning spends counts toward that budget, but it used to start all the same. It now asks first - "Over this month's budget. Learn anyway?" - with Go on anyway or Cancel (docs).
  • Models: opening the Models page or the chat's model panel no longer starts Copilot to ask your GitHub account what it offers, so opening one no longer switches Copilot's model rows off under your cursor. They show what your account offered when it was last asked; its rows still follow that answer, which the top bar's plan meter reads at most once in 10 minutes; Read now on its card and a model Copilot refused ask it at once, a fill of its tiers where it is due (docs).
  • Workspace: a Take in that names some of a card's files takes only those. The page's API took files for nothing and took every file in; now the rest stay on the card - a turn's card still asks about them, a kept copy is kept for them - and a name that is not on the card, an empty list, or files on a branch's Merge or on Run the test is refused. Discard after part of a card was taken throws away only the rest: the card says its work was taken in, and offers the commit of what was taken, where it used to say discarded (docs).
  • Ready: the top bar's pill, a chat's line and Not seen count one thing: what was decided for you in the project and waits for your OK, of every chat and any age. The pill counted the open chat's, the chat's line that and its To-do picks, and Not seen the project's - three numbers for one list. The pill and the line now say "in this project" and follow an OK at once; in a chat with no folder, which has no decision log, the pill counts that chat's, "in this chat" (docs).
  • Chat: a long chat opens on its newest 40 turns, not its whole history: a 600-turn chat sent about 9.4 MB in one answer (2 s) when opened, and again at every dropped connection; it sends about 0.6 MB (0.15 s) now. An older turn that still waits for you - a card to take in, a question, a decision to OK - comes with them, whatever its age. Show 40 earlier turns over them reads the 40 before; search, the decision log and the night's report still read the whole chat (docs).
  • Ready: another chat where something waits for you is read as the open chat is - its newest 40 turns and every older one that still waits - not its whole history, again each time what waits in it changed. Its cards on Ready for you are the same (docs).
  • Workspace: a kept copy's card taken in in two steps - some files, then the rest or Discard - offers a commit that holds only the agent's change in each file, as a card taken in at once does, also after a restart of KOLONİ between the two; the files of the first step went into it whole, so your own uncommitted edits in them went in as the agent's. And the card of a branch's copy kept after KOLONİ stopped no longer takes some of its files: its work goes in whole, as a branch's Merge does, where a later Discard dropped the branch with a file of it already taken in (docs).
  • Agents: in a narrow window (1100 px or less) Roles ▸ N stays at the top of the Agents page however far it scrolls. With three ready teams the teams' list is short, and the button scrolled away with it once you went down to a role's form under it (docs).
  • Settings: More limits stays open while a value in it cannot be saved - Continue gives this many more steps at 0, say, in This project › Limits and money, or a step limit under 5 in The app › Agents. Closed, Save was off with nothing in sight to say why; the field and what it takes are in sight now, and once the value is fixed you can close it again (docs).
  • Ready: a Take in card of the Orchestrator's work calls it the Orchestrator on the card as over it - it read "for Orchestrator" above "Lead's changes did not reach the project" - and so does the check's line under Take in on the turn's proof. KOLONİ's commit of a ☾ Away job's work on its branch begins "Orchestrator: …", not "Lead: …", as the screen names it. So do the other places that still said Lead: what a night's job tried in a place you kept out ("Orchestrator: edit_file secret/pay.py"), a turn that stops on a model it may not run ("Orchestrator: Fast's deep is switched off. …"), a branch switch's card ("switches the branch under Orchestrator's work") and the git map's "Can't switch branches now: Orchestrator is at work" (docs).
  • To-do: a ☾ Away job on its branch whose work you took in, or discarded, says its branch was deleted - "Its branch koloni/fix-login-3f2a was deleted: its work was taken in." Its row still said "On branch … · 1 commits · 1 files" and "No remote: merge it with git, or Take in." of a branch that was gone. A job whose work you discarded, on a branch or in a copy, says "Done" and "discarded: hello.py" - it said "Done, nothing changed", the words for a job that changed no file (docs).
  • Usage: the Messages box and By provider and model no longer seem to disagree on the agents - "12 agents" over a model's 13. A model's row counts KOLONİ's own requests outside a message among its agents, the box does not; the box now says them apart - "12 agents", and under it "1 request by KOLONİ itself" - and a line under the table says "Agents here include 1 request by KOLONİ itself, in no message." (docs).
  • Tools: a server's Roles that may use it, its card's roles, a skill's roles and a knowledge item's Used by call the Lead the Orchestrator, as the rest of the screen does; they said "Lead". What is saved is the role, as before (docs).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Tools: an MCP server is trusted only for the tools you read: KOLONİ refuses Trust this server before its first reading, and after another command or other variables until its tools are read again ("read its tools first, then trust it"). On the page the button also waits while that server's tools are being read or a change of it is saved, so that nothing not seen yet is trusted (docs).
  • Permissions: a search's option split by quotes or a backslash is read as the shell joins it - find src -de""lete is asked as a delete, and -fpr""intf, -ex""ec, rg's --p""re= (and its --hostname-bin, ag's and ack's --pager) make a search no read; a find word in bash's ANSI-C quotes ($'-de\x6cete'), which KOLONİ does not decode, is taken for a delete; and ag or ack is no look into a tree. In KOLONİ's worktrees and copies such a line is asked at every level (docs).
  • Settings: at Full auto, with no model to ask - no Judge model that can be asked and none in the Fast tier - Full auto's judge no longer steps aside for the turn and lets each command it would look at run unasked: such a command waits for you on a card, "KOLONİ's judge: it could not be asked: no judge model answered - …", and the chat says so once in the turn, as where its model has no room. Like Claude Code's auto mode, it fails closed; turn the judge's switch off for a project to have Full auto as it was before the judge. Ask before changes and Auto-edit files never ask the judge, as before (docs).
  • Settings: Full auto's judge reads what Claude Code's auto mode's classifier reads: your words and the agent's actions - its last 8 tool calls of the turn by name and arguments (read_file {"path": "notes.md"}, write_file {…}, run_command {…}), each cut to 300 characters, not only its last 5 commands - and never what a tool gave back. A script in the agents' scratch (.koloni/tmp/) that no write of an agent's made - curl -o .koloni/tmp/x.py …, a command's output - is named to it, its text no longer shown: such text could carry orders to the judge. An action's arguments are read with their JSON escapes undone (\n, \u0069) before secrets are masked and orders looked for. A program an agent wrote is shown as before; secrets KOLONİ knows are masked and text that reads like orders to a model still makes a card without asking (docs).
  • Workspace: a file named as a secret no longer goes into a branch's start from your folder, nor into a ☾ Away job's commit on its branch, whatever it holds: token.txt, credentials.yaml, api_keys.json / api-key.txt, a .env copy but .env.example (.env.sample, .env.template, .env.local.example), env.production, .secrets / .secrets.toml, client_secret….json, serviceAccountKey.json, access_token.txt, secret.txt, and a data file in a folder named credentials or secrets; until now only credentials.json and token.json were left out beside the secret's names KOLONİ always knew. Code and Markdown named so still go in (credentials.py, tokens.py), and so does tokens.json. Nothing is deleted: your own file stays in your folder, a job's in its worktree, and the job's chat and push row say "left out" ("· left out: .env.sample (a secret KOLONİ knows, or named as one)"); one its agent committed on the branch itself goes up only on Run anyway. A team's or a story's pull request asks before any such file goes to GitHub, at Full auto too ("token.json: named as a secret - it goes to GitHub only on your click"): token.json - Google's OAuth token - and a file in a secrets folder went up unasked (docs).
  • Workspace: a token known by its shape alone (ghp_…, sk-…, a password in an address) is masked in a branch's commit subject and its pull request's title - a To-do task's or a sub-agent's task that held one put it into the commit and the title as it was, where no saved key, variable or card of KOLONİ's held it (docs).
  • To-do: a task whose title holds a secret KOLONİ knows - in any case, or spelt as a branch's name spells it - or has a secret's shape (ghp_…, sk-…), no longer gives its git branch a name from the title - a title that began with one put its head into koloni/<name>, which goes to origin with a ☾ Away job's push; such a branch is koloni/task-3f2a (docs).
  • Permissions: the review of Full auto's judge taking the list's deletes: a line it may decide is a plain one, so KOLONİ reads each target as the shell will - a delete in quotes, escapes, wildcards, a subexpression (Remove-Item (Split-Path (pwd))), a .NET call ([Environment]::GetFolderPath(…)), behind a pipe or a wrapper (find . | xargs rm -rf, Get-ChildItem | Remove-Item) stays a card, as does a line with -EncodedCommand anywhere in it (rm -rf src && powershell -enc … is read as unread first). Asked at every level now, whatever your words say: git worktree remove (git picks a worktree by its last name - KOLONİ's own or one outside the project), git clean with an exclude that starts with ! (-e '!*', as -x), git stash --all then dropped, a find with no folder before its options (find -delete), git gc --prune=now|all, git prune and git reflog expire (what a dropped branch or stash could be brought back by), a stop by name of the terminal, shell or system KOLONİ stands on (WindowsTerminal, conhost, OpenConsole, powershell, pwsh, cmd, bash, explorer, lsass, csrss, svchost, wininit, winlogon, services), and .koloni, .git or .claude spelt with sh's escapes (.k\oloni, .gi\t: Git Bash's .koloni, .git). A refused delete is refused again however it is spaced (rm -rf src). Each command of a line the judge decides must be such a harm itself - but the one cd sub its folder starts it with: cd; rm -rf x, cd - && …, popd; …, Set-Location; … or an alias of cd (which run the delete elsewhere) and a second command beside it (rm -rf build; npm install) keep the card; so do a Windows short name (ENV~1, CREDEN~1.JSO), git told of another tree (-C, --work-tree), git's work where the project is not its repository's top folder, a second harm on the line (rm -rf build; rm -rf dist: one could make a link the other goes through), and a path through a link or a junction (rm -rf data/): KOLONİ looks at the disk before the judge is asked, again once it said fine and as the command runs (a sub-agent's delete in its working copy stays its card). No command or CLI KOLONİ starts is given a CDPATH, so cd src is the project's own src. Asked at every level too: git clean -ff (other repositories inside it), a file that steers beside an instruction file (rm -f AGENTS.md lefthook.yml), and a stop of the session KOLONİ stands on (zsh, tmux, screen, sshd, Terminal, iTerm2, gnome-shell, Xorg, WindowServer, loginwindow, systemd, launchd, git) (docs).
  • Permissions: a git remote's branches overwritten or deleted - git push --force, --force-with-lease, --mirror, --delete, git push origin +main or :old - wait on a card at every level whatever your words say: Check what I said first no longer lets one run on a line of yours, and Full auto's judge is never asked. A plain git push is put to your words as before (docs).

items.title: Removed
items.text:
• Board: the Board page is gone from the rail and from Ctrl+K - every chat of the project in columns (at work, ended today), its line to Ready for you and its strip of two chats that want one file. How each chat stands is on the Chats list, what waits for you on Ready for you, and two chats that want one file still show it above each of them. Its Re-run the ones that failed button is gone with it: ask the Orchestrator in the chat to open those sub-agents again (docs).
  • Teams: Breaking: KOLONİ comes with three ready teams - Web app, Quality and Docs - not eleven. When the database is upgraded (migration 0194) the other eight (Backend / API, Data, DevOps, Research, Product, Maintenance, ML, DataOps) go, with their stages and coordinators, where they are as they came; one you changed (its name, roles, stages, coordinator, default recipe or the Orchestrator's leave to pick it) or use (picked in a chat in Manual, kept for a project's new chats, named by a recipe's step) stays as your own. No role and no recipe is deleted: Bugfix, Spec, Analysis and the other ready recipes stay for any team. A chat the Orchestrator had picked a gone team for keeps its other teams; with none left it picks again (docs).
  • Workspace: the Word, Excel and PowerPoint previews and the 3D model preview (STL, OBJ, glTF, GLB, 3MF) are gone. Such a file opens in the Workspace as any other file that is not a page or a picture: its text where it is text of 256 KB at most (an OBJ, a text STL, a glTF), else a line that says why not ("Not text: there is no code to show.", "Too large to show: over 256 KB.") - one only in an agent's working copy so far is read there, as its preview was; open it in its own program. A Word, Excel or PowerPoint file an agent made is still listed among its outputs and still checked; a 3D model is no longer an output, and an agent can no longer show one (docs).
  • For contributors: docx-preview, pptx-preview, SheetJS (xlsx) and three.js are no longer dependencies, and npm run build no longer builds the document viewer (dist/office/, about 1.8 MB).
  • Agents: Breaking: the Observer is gone: the built-in role whose model, once a sub-agent handed in its report, said in a few sentences which of the report's claims the record shows, and its switch Have a model look over each sub-agent's report in Settings › This project › Agents. Checked and No file changed already say what a sub-agent's record shows, from KOLONİ's own records, with no model request. When the database is upgraded the built-in Observer role and the observations kept on agents are deleted (an agent's window no longer shows one); a role of your own named "Observer" stays as it is (docs).
  • Triggers: Breaking: triggers are gone: the Triggers page, the turns that started by themselves by the clock, when files changed or on a request from outside (webhooks), Pause all in the top bar, and the agents' Propose triggers with its Make this trigger? card. KOLONİ is about agents working together, and triggers were scheduled automation nobody used. When the database is upgraded your triggers and their records are deleted; the turns they started stay in their chats. ☾ Away, To-do in a chat and the day's summary work as before (docs).
  • CLIs: Codex's One run per model step is gone (it was under Experimental): Codex runs as One session per agent or Native. A Codex provider saved so runs as One session per agent from now on, on a model server of your own too, where a Codex session is not yet measured; Show experimental features (called Show experimental CLIs until now) offers agy and Native. Claude Code keeps its One run per model step (docs).
  • Settings: Breaking: the notification address is gone (Settings › This project › Notifications: Notification address, Post it as, Remove the notification address): KOLONİ no longer posts to a Slack, Discord or other web hook. Agents' notifications, a stuck Orchestrator, a night's end and the day's summary go to the desktop notification alone, where it is on; with it off agents have no notify tool. A saved address is deleted when KOLONİ upgrades the database, and a day's summary that only the address carried loses its time (docs).
  • Memory: the search by meaning is gone (the Memory page's by words ▾ / by meaning ▾ and Settings › This project › Memory and web › Search by meaning with, Embedding model): Search deeper and an agent's recall match words, as before, in this project and in the projects it also looks in; nothing is sent to a model server to search. The vectors kept for it, and the provider and model chosen for it, are deleted when KOLONİ upgrades the database (docs).
  • Usage: the Cards section is gone - the command cards asked in the period by why, how they were answered, the average time to answer, what Check what I said first decided, and the delete rule it suggested with Add to rules. Usage keeps its numbers at the top, the table by provider and model and the plan meters; what was decided for you is on Ready for you (docs).
  • Agents: Breaking: rooms are gone: Work together… under More, /room, the Orchestrator's open_room and the room tools its members had, the room's window and its node on the canvas, and A room's limits in Settings › This project › New chats start with. Two to six agents writing in one copy at once ran against how KOLONİ works - each writer in its own copy, then merged. A recipe's Room step (yours, or one in a folder's recipe file) runs its roles side by side as an All at once group in its place, each a sub-agent of the step, in the recipe's copy; a discussion still lets agents talk a question through, and agents still write to each other with message_agent. Gone with rooms: the note a room between teams left on the notebook for every team and its file in the shared folder's decisions/ (kept files stay readable); two teams now agree through the contract a coordinator writes into contracts/. When the database is upgraded open_room is taken off every role, your saved recipes' Room steps become such groups, and a room left running is ended; each turn that had a room says so in one line in its chat, and what was said in the room is kept in KOLONİ's record (docs).

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Settings: Full auto's judge: at Full auto - in a chat you watch, a To-do task's turn too, and a job while you're away - a command the list does not stop is first looked at by a small model: "fine" runs it as before; "risky" is refused and the agent goes on, or - with Ask me (below) - puts it on a card with the judge's sentence, KOLONİ's judge: … - in a job while you're away it is parked for you, as any card there is. It never runs a command that asks today, and refuses none but its own "risky" - one it gave no answer for in time, gave an answer it could not read for, could not look at, or may not be asked about now (no room on its model's provider, or the turn past its token limit - said once in the chat) waits for you too, as does a command over 4,000 characters, one whose program changed while it looked, or one - or the program an agent wrote that it runs, or an earlier command of the turn - that reads like orders to a model. Reads, ordinary work (tests, compilers and checkers, local git - with their usual options alone), your own test command (but where it runs a program an agent wrote), a skill's script you let run, a disposable delete and a trigger's turn are not asked about. It reads your preferences, this project's rules as saved and your last 6 messages in the chat (4,000 characters at most), the command, its folder, who runs it, the last 5 commands the same agent ran in the turn (each cut to 300 characters) and the first 4 KB of a program an agent wrote that the command runs - never an agent's messages, a tool's result or a file it read. Run once on its card runs the line, not asked about again in that turn; with its box Don't ask about this line again here ticked, not in the project either, in the same folder. Either is kept only where KOLONİ knows all the line runs as it is: the script, module, Makefile, Dockerfile or package.json it runs, found and unchanged, in a plain form that runs that file and nothing more - never a chain, pipe or redirection -, or one plain command of a few that run none of the project's code (file commands such as cp, mv, rm, mkdir; curl and wget only with plain http(s):// addresses, a few flags that take no value and a plain output file); never for a wrapped line, a shell's code, a variable set on make's line, a package's __main__.py, a Python line in a working copy without -I or -E, a card the judge gave no verdict of its own for, or a line whose folder is not known - those are looked at each time, and their card has no box. What a program imports in turn is not looked at. Once answered, the judge's sentence stays under the command's row, and Usage › Cards counts its cards on a row of their own. An "Always run" rule does not let a command by it, and its card offers none. Where there is no model to ask, it stands aside for the turn and says so once in the chat. Its switch is in Settings › This project › Asking and away and in the level menu, under the levels. It asks your Judge model - Settings › The app › Agents: Fast tier's first (now: …), the first of that tier that answers with no tools, unless you choose another of the models listed - a CLI with tools of its own among them, such as GitHub Copilot CLI run Native, asked with them off, as a Full auto turn asks it; a choice that cannot be asked now says so, and on a CLI each such command waits for it to start. Check what I said first asks the same model (docs).
  • Chat: the Orchestrator can ask for KOLONİ's checks in the middle of its turn and wait for them - the tests, the type and style checks, the Reviewer and the live try, as the turn's end runs them. Tie a step to a condition ("if the tests pass, commit it", "testler geçerse commit et") and it takes that step only when the answer's first line is CHECKS: green; red or not complete, it fixes the work or tells you. Green is strict (a test command of yours that passed, nothing failing or not run, no hold). A red answer is no fix round, and asking is an extra pass: the turn's end always runs its own checks too. The Checks box's panel says "asked by the Orchestrator" for such a round (docs).
