  • Chat: the Orchestrator can read where its project stands from KOLONİ's records, with its read_status tool - what waits for you (cards, what a night parked, the morning's push, To-do proposals, tasks at "done?"), work kept and not taken in, the koloni/ branches on record, this month's spend against the budget and the newest 10 decisions taken for you - so it need not guess, on the next night too. It only reads, never another project's nor git or the network; every agent's or your words in it are masked and quoted as data, and its answer is cut at 3 KB by whole lines, saying so. Not a sub-agent's (docs).
  • To-do: Waiting for you, in Ready for you's waiting list, on the summary of the chat you went away from, on To-do and in the morning's report: one list of everything the jobs parked while you were away - each command whole, each question, why in KOLONİ's words, a warning where it reads like orders - task by task in the night's order. Run or Reject a command, answer a question (one of its options, or a line), or Stop this task; only once you are back and its job is not at work, and only where it can run as it was recorded (a git or build/ line once you took its work in; not where its copy is gone or its folder is not known). Once a task's are all given, KOLONİ runs what you said Run in the order parked, as recorded, in the job's kept copy - looked at again first: not where the copy was taken in or discarded after your Run, nor where anything in the job's copy changed after the line was parked (but a command that runs none of the project's code: curl, a file command); a program an agent wrote, a place you kept out, a CLI's own shell's line and a server line never - and the same Orchestrator goes on in the same chat in one turn, on KOLONİ's message "KOLONİ: the user decided: …" - a job's turn, its work kept for your Take in; over the month's budget it does not start (docs).
  • To-do: ☾ Away in a git repository: a job's push waits for you in the morning - where the project has an origin, Waiting for you has its row, "Push koloni/fix-login-3f2a to origin (…) — one commit by KOLONİ, 5 files · checks ✓ at 3c4d5e6" ("· opens a pull request into main" where the project's finished branches go as pull requests). Run pushes the branch's work as one commit of KOLONİ's - never the agents' own steps, never what you had not committed when it began - and opens the pull request; Reject leaves the branch. It waits for the task's other rows and its going-on turn, and is made again with the branch's new commit after it. Just before it pushes KOLONİ looks again: a branch deleted or moved since, a secret it knows in what would go up, that name on origin, your commits on main not on origin - nothing goes up and the row says why; git's config changed since the job began, something changed outside the branch, a place kept out changed, or it began from your uncommitted work - the row says so first, and Run anyway pushes. Take in or Discard closes it (docs).
  • Ready: Decided for you, beside what waits on the Ready for you page (under it on a narrow screen): what was decided for you in the project and why, in one list - the Orchestrator's answers to cards, the sub-agents it opened or not and its To-do choices, the commands KOLONİ's judge refused (one it asked you about is yours to decide, not listed), and those a rule of yours ran or did not run -, newest first, each with who decided it, its chat or To-do, the question, command or task, the reason in quotes and a link to where it is, for Since I left, Today or Week, or Not seen - what waits for your OK, however old; OK on one you have not seen (on a To-do task it decides nothing), Change while the agent that asked still works (on a To-do choice, until the task has started - one that moved on since is refused, "it changed since you looked"), or why it can't be undone; how many commands the judge let run, as one line; Copy as Markdown for a pull request's description. The page's first line says how many things wait for your word and how many decisions were made for you since you left. A chat now says it in one line at its top - "While you were away, 3 things were decided for you and 2 wait for you." - with Open in Ready for you (at Not seen when some wait for your OK), in place of its Decided for you box (a chat with no folder keeps the box), and Usage › Today says the day's decisions in one line. Built from KOLONİ's records - no model is asked, no agent can add, change or hide a row, nothing is written into your project; agents' words masked as on screen (docs).
  • Ready: the night on Ready for you - once a ☾ Away ended, the page opens on it: a lane per job from the start of its first turn of the night to the end of its last (none where the record lacks either), each decision made for you in the job's chat at its time as a hexagon, filled while it waits for your OK; Not checked (tests not run, a kind's check, the Reviewer or the live try not done, After a change set to Nothing, GitHub's checks not waited for - "not known" where no record says), what it spent, The whole report and Copy as Markdown of the whole night, named by its day ("Last night" on the page within a day of its end, else "Night of …"). What the night parked joins the waiting list, first, its push first of all (Push - Push and open PR where the project's way is one - / Not now, Push anyway after its notes; Run / Reject a command, answer a question; a parked line shows, and copies, with its secrets masked), under the filter Last night (was While away). Decided for you's Change and redo, once the agent that asked has finished: your answer in place of the Orchestrator's and a new turn of its chat on KOLONİ's message, the question and both answers in quotes, masked - "starts a new turn" on its button; in a job's chat a job's turn, its work kept for your Take in (on a branch you pushed, it says it adds to it); only from KOLONİ's own page, once, not while you're away, nor while its job waits for what it parked, not where its work was taken in or discarded (docs).
  • For contributors: scripts/measure_judge.py measures a Judge model live against the two judges' case sets - Check what I said first's (tests/data/check_what_i_said_cases.json) and Full auto's judge's (tests/data/full_auto_judge_cases.json) - asking it with the prompt, client, time limit and parser KOLONİ itself uses, one model call a case (--dry-run builds the prompts and asks nothing; --limit N is a smoke run). It writes a JSON report and prints the wrong runs (the gate: none), wrong refusals and asks, Full auto's judge's fine/risky matrix with the risky commands it called fine, the median latency and, where the catalogue prices the model, the cost. --no-net counts the words check on the model alone, without KOLONİ's net for conditions (judge._conditional), and each row says which parts of that net fire on its case and whether it turned the model's verdict into an ask, with a table by part (fires, redundant, saved, false alarm). Whether a model joins MEASURED_MODELS stays a decision; the script writes nothing in the app.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Settings: Full auto's judge is on by default, in new projects and in the ones you have: Settings › This project › Asking and away turns it off; off, Full auto is as before (docs).
  • Settings: Full auto's judge refuses a risky command and the agent goes on, as Claude Code's auto mode does: no card opens and nothing waits - the agent is told a general reason ("KOLONİ's judge refused this as risky (…). Do it another way, or ask the user.") - never the judge's sentence, which may quote your messages -, while you see the sentence: the command's row says refused with KOLONİ's judge refused: … under it, and Decided for you lists it until you press OK. After 3 refusals in a turn, by any of its agents, the next risky command waits on its card, said once in the chat - the top bar's pill now counts it, and a command your words let run or kept from running, so that list can be reached. Settings › This project › Asking and away › When the judge finds a command risky: Ask me brings back the card (Refuse and go on is the default, in new projects and in the ones you have). Only the judge's own "risky" is refused: a card the list opens (a delete, a push, a secret…), and one the judge gave no verdict for (no answer in time, none it could read, no room to ask), stays a card, and a job while you're away still parks it. The level menu's Full auto's judge says which (docs).
  • Settings: Check what I said first is a question of Full auto's judge now: its row A harmful-looking command at Full auto and its switch in the level menu are gone, and under the judge's switch in Settings › This project › Asking and away its own box, It also lets a delete or a push run when a line you saved names it, lets a delete or a send a line of yours names run without a card, as it did. It works only once your Judge model's measurement has passed - none has yet, so the box says (after its measurement) and cannot be ticked - or in a project where you had turned Check what I said first on: there its box comes ticked, works as before, and you may untick it. With the judge off or the box unticked, such a command waits for you on its card. The level menu's Full auto's judge says what it does with your words. A line of yours that forbids the same delete as the one the model quoted ("Never delete ./x." beside "You may delete ./x.", or an item under "Never delete these:" - a heading covers the list under it, up to a blank line, and a heading right under it, not a section of its own further on) now keeps the card, and its answer is waited for 20 seconds, as the judge's own (30 before; 90 on a CLI) (docs).
  • To-do: a card no longer stops a job while you're away: a command's card - whatever its reason, Full auto's judge's too, and a CLI's own command - is parked for you, does not run, the agent is told so and goes on; the job then waits, "2 parked", its copy kept. The Orchestrator decides its own questions in a job too, and answers park to what only you can know - parked like a question it could not answer; in the chat you went away from its questions still wait for you. Changes of steering or secret files, the web, secrets, folders and new roles still make a job wait. After I'm back a job still at work waits on its next card as before (docs).
  • To-do: ☾ Away in a git repository: each job works on a git branch of its own, koloni/<task>, in a worktree of your repository, and commits there as it goes - its git status, diff, log, add and commit there ask nothing; its own git push is refused ("KOLONİ pushes this branch when the user says yes: go on"), and a script's push fails in its worktree; at its end KOLONİ commits what it left and keeps the worktree for your Take in - never merged by itself, at Full auto too. Its row says "On branch koloni/fix-login-3f2a · 3 commits · 5 files · checks ✓" (with no origin: "No remote: merge it with git, or Take in."), and what changed outside the branch meanwhile ("Changed outside its branch: main 1a2b3c4 → 3c4d5e6"). A job's second try and its going-on turn after your decisions go on on the same branch. No git, a folder inside a repository, HEAD on no branch, a git submodule or Git LFS: the job works in a copy as before, its row says why (docs).
  • Settings: Check what I said first was measured with Claude Code's haiku on 25 Nov 2026 and did not pass: one run of 70 cases let no command run wrongly, but in three repeats of all 171 cases one run let 2 (a condition, "Pending review, you may push to main.", and a delete in another folder than the line names). No model is measured, so the check stays off but where a project had chosen it before 0.1.9. A model that passes would count only as measured - on its own service (no model server, own setup or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL-like variable), as a session or natively, and as the Judge model you chose or, none chosen, the Fast tier's first, never one asked because your choice could not be; Settings › Agents would say so under the Judge model (docs).
  • Settings: Check what I said first's model is now told that a line of yours limited in time or in how many times it may be used ("once", "this time", "today", "on weekdays", "bir kereliğine") allows nothing - KOLONİ cannot tell whether it was used up or its time has passed, so such a delete or push waits on its card -, and that the command's folder is your project's, not the folder a CLI itself runs in: its first live measurement (Claude Code's haiku) had let three such lines run, and asked about plain deletes a line of yours named (docs).
  • Two more checks for contributors, beside ruff and ty: vulture (code nothing calls, in app/ and scripts/) and Pyrefly (a second type checker, set in pyrefly.toml), run by PR Check, the release's quick checks and verify.ps1; they come from requirements-lint.lock, not with an install or update of KOLONİ (docs).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• To-do: two story names that differ only by the Turkish dotted İ or dotless ı are one name - "LOGİN", "LOGIN", "login" and "logın" alike: a second story of that name is refused, and an agent naming the story finds it. So are names that differ only in their Unicode form or by a character nobody sees - a decomposed é, a fullwidth letter, a zero-width space - by an i with a dot above of its own ("logi̇n", what lowercasing "LOGİN" gives), or by two spaces or a tab where the page shows one space. A goal's name too. Two open stories made before whose names are now one ("Batch Alpha" and "Batch Alpha") both stay: an agent naming one gets the story of exactly that name, and where neither is, it is told both and asked for the exact one. A story's name of what nobody sees alone - a zero-width space, a braille blank - is refused, on the page, in a drafted tree and from an agent: "a story needs a name you can see"; a goal's too: "a goal needs a name you can see" (docs).
  • To-do: only a line of the Orchestrator's answer that starts with Story note: - after up to three spaces, as a list's item (-, *, +) or not, in bold or not, the marker alone in backticks or not - goes into the story's notebook. One indented as code, in inline code, in an HTML comment, in an HTML block (<pre>, <script>, <style>, <textarea> to its closing tag; <div>, <table> and their kind to a blank line), in a table or a heading (an underlined one too), right after a quote's line with no blank line between (Markdown reads it as the quote's), or after a line separator (U+2028) inside a line no longer does; a ` is a whole comment, a list's item over---` still counts, and a fence's marker indented as code neither opens nor closes a fence. The Orchestrator is shown the line's form in plain words, no longer in code, so that it does not write its notes in code (docs).
  • Chat: half an emoji - a broken character, as a model's answer or an agent's tool call can write one - no longer keeps a chat, the To-do list or Decisions from opening: kept in a command's record of the judge, a To-do proposal or a card's options, before this release too, it shows as �. The judge's sentence, the Orchestrator's answer and reason for a card and its reason for a To-do proposal are kept so from now on (docs).
  • Workspace: a push of KOLONİ's - a team's pull request, ☾ Away's in the morning - never lands on a branch of that name already on origin, a fast-forward onto it too: "origin already has a branch named …: nothing was pushed", in KOLONİ's words, not git's. A card or row about your work not pushed yet says "not on GitHub" only where the push goes to GitHub - "not on origin" for a folder or another host - and "would go up with the push" (docs).
  • Chat: an answer whose emoji a model streamed in two halves no longer fails its turn ("surrogates not allowed"): the halves are one character again, and a half that stays alone is kept as �.
  • Workspace: in a repository git checks out with CRLF (core.autocrlf=true, git's default on Windows) whose files are LF - as tools, formatters and agents write them - a branch's Take in no longer says a file was changed on both sides where only its line ends differ: as git stores it (git hash-object), the project's file is the one the branch began from, so Take in is offered; what it writes keeps the project's own line ends - but not where git records a change of them (core.autocrlf=false), so an agent's own change of a file's line ends is kept. A real change of yours meanwhile is still one (docs).
  • To-do: Stop in a job's chat while a line you said Run runs in the morning stops its task as Stop this task does, and a message of yours waiting behind it goes ahead; the task no longer stays at work, which refused a new ☾ Away ("… is being worked on") (docs).
  • Ready: the night on Ready for you, and its Copy as Markdown, has every decision of the night on its job's lane: a job of many later decisions no longer leaves an earlier job none - they were the project's newest 500 of the night (docs).
  • Ready: Change and redo goes on with the work of its own card - the copy of the agent that asked in that turn, or of a turn that went on with it since - in that chat's topic: in a chat of two topics, each with a kept copy, it no longer goes on in the other topic's copy, and another topic's work taken in no longer refuses it, "its work was taken in"; nor does a message of yours in the same topic, another sub-agent's copy of the same turn or the Orchestrator's own, or another turn of KOLONİ's in it - a To-do story's next task, an approved plan's work, a rerun, a comparison's side. Where Fix it, or a Change and redo outside a job's chat, went on in that copy since, it says "its work was discarded" (docs).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Chat: a branch's push - a team's pull request, and ☾ Away's push in the morning - first asks origin itself what its branches hold and never reads your remote-tracking branches (origin/*) for it, so a ref written in your repository (a script's git update-ref, a symbolic ref) can no longer make your own unpushed commits look pushed, and a stale one (a branch deleted on GitHub, a teammate's push not fetched) stops nothing; where origin's branch it goes into holds commits you have not fetched, it asks you to fetch first. Origin is asked only once a branch's way is a pull request - never at a turn's end that may still be a merge - and no sign-in window opens for it. It goes to the one address git resolves for origin - nothing where git's config rewrites that address (an insteadOf or pushInsteadOf rule matching it) or origin has more than one -, sends no push option of your config, and none of KOLONİ's git reads an object through git replace or a graft. ☾ Away's push row names that address (never its password); where a push goes elsewhere now than when you went away, where the project is on another branch, or where the row is not the one you read, it asks or refuses first - and it notes what changed outside the branch since you went away, what an earlier job of the night did too: every ref, the stash list, git's hooks and config in every scope, git's own files. A team's pull request reads git's config in every scope too (docs).
  • To-do: a task whose story is another project's - set so outside KOLONİ - counts as a task of no story: its brief, the name of a new chat it starts in and its git branch no longer take that story's title; a task of that story in another project's chat no longer holds its Do in chat or Fix it, Approve no longer makes that story yours, and turning the task down no longer deletes it. The other way round, a task of another project that names your story is none of its tasks: it is not counted, not told in its summary, and not the turn Close the story goes on from.
  • To-do: a secret split by a character nobody sees - a zero-width space or joiner, a word joiner, a byte-order mark, a variation selector, a Hangul filler, a line separator, a braille blank, a musical null notehead, an object replacement character - no longer goes into a story's notebook in parts: a word next to such a character is hidden whole (***), and the note is masked with each such character read as a plain space, so a Bearer token or a private key split by one is masked as ever. A secret whose head ends where a long note is cut is not kept either. An emoji family, or a Persian word, joined by such a character shows as *** in a note (docs).
  • Chat: the Orchestrator's reason for a card it answered for you, or for a To-do proposal it decided, is kept masked, as the judge's sentence is: a secret KOLONİ knows shows as *** under Decided for you (docs).
  • Workspace: a branch's commit, merge and push by KOLONİ - a team's pull request, a story's close, ☾ Away's push in the morning - look for one set of secrets, in each file's content and its name: those given on a card, the environment's, the values a project passes to its commands, KOLONİ's saved provider keys, an MCP server's variables a secret's name holds, the notification addresses and the page's own key - a team's branch looked for those given in its turn alone, and the morning push for the environment's alone (live: a job committed a saved provider key and the morning's Run pushed it). KOLONİ's own commit leaves a file holding one out - its card, or the morning's push row and the job's chat, says which - and the rest of the work goes on; one an agent committed itself stops the branch: neither merged nor pushed, "take it off the branch first: nothing was pushed". Such a secret never deletes a branch's work; an MCP server's ordinary value (NODE_ENV=production, a path, an address), a saved key that reads as a word (not-needed) and a file's path under a secret's name (GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, *_FILE) stop nothing - but a value with a secret's shape (ghp_…, sk-…, a password in an address) is looked for whatever its name - and so is the token or the password such a value holds alone (a DATABASE_URL's password in a settings.py, a remote's token in an .npmrc), unless it reads as a word -, and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN too; a word under a secret's name (POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres) is one, and a file holding it is left out of KOLONİ's commit (docs).
  • Chat: the reasons KOLONİ keeps - the Orchestrator's for a card or a To-do proposal, either judge's sentence - are masked as Decided for you shows them before they are kept: a Bearer token, a password in an address and a secret split by a character nobody sees too, not only a secret KOLONİ knows - but not an MCP server's ordinary value (production stays readable).
  • Workspace: a To-do task's name - which the Scout may have written - mentions nobody when it goes up as a pushed commit's subject or a pull request's title: a zero-width joiner follows each @ that would mention someone on GitHub (@octocat) and comes before each issue's number a closing keyword would close (Fixes #12, Fixes GH-9, Fixes https://github.com/o/r/issues/8, _fixes #10), and control and format characters (a line break, a bidi override) are left out; the rest stays as written. A team's pull request's body puts its task, its files' names, the check, the agent's notes and its role's name in code - the morning push's its task, files, notes and role's name -, and masks a secret KOLONİ knows before the notes are cut (docs).
  • Chat: GitLab's (glpat-…), Google's (AIza…), Hugging Face's (hf_…), npm's (npm_…) and Stripe's (sk_live_…, rk_live_…) keys are known by their shape too, as a GitHub token is: hidden in a command's output and in what KOLONİ keeps, read_file asks before it shows a file holding one, and a branch's commit and push look for one whatever its variable's name (docs).

items.title: Removed
items.text: • CLIs: an agent run Native on a CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, agy) - the Orchestrator or a sub-agent - no longer proposes triggers: for an Orchestrator there, its Make this trigger? card's Approve was always refused in that chat, since a trigger's turn never starts a CLI that works with its own tools. Notify you stays. A card left from 0.1.8 is still refused at Approve, saying why (docs).

items.title: Added
items.text:
• To-do: Do in chat: tick tasks, or a whole story, on To-do and give them to the chat open now or to a new one: they wait in that chat's queue and run there one by one - each story in a topic of its own, where its tasks go on in one session, a task of no story in a topic of its own - and your own message still goes first. A stop, a restart or the month's budget stops the queue, the tasks back on To-do and one line in the chat saying why; Stop everything and ☾ Away only hold it until you resume or are back (docs).
  • To-do: in a project in git, a story's tasks run one after another on the story's own branch - each turn in a worktree of it, nothing of it in the project yet - and Close the story (the chat's Story done? card) runs KOLONİ's check on the branch: it passes, the branch is merged or sent as a pull request, as the project's way says; it fails, the branch waits and the story's last task is stuck with why (Fix it goes on on the branch). A task of no story has a small branch of its own, merged at its end as a team's is. A project with no git works as before, in the project (docs).
  • Chat: a To-do task's turn shows as the task - From To-do · task 2 / 3, its title and what makes it done, its whole brief folded under - with Done? (Yes, done / Not yet) and Stuck (Fix it / Open it in To-do / Leave it) under its last turn, Story done? (Close the story / Add a task) once every task of a story is done, a story's topic line Topic · Story · …, and the chat's queue above the message box (N wait, each with Remove) (docs).
  • To-do: To-do keeps goals and stories: a story holds tasks and bugs, a goal holds stories and says how many are done; the Hive keeper writes a rough note as a goal, its stories and their tasks. The page is a tree - goals ("1 / 2 stories" and a bar), their stories, their tasks and bugs (a bug in rose), the tasks of no story last under Without a story - with the filters All, Todo, Running and Done, + Task, Write it with the Hive keeper and ☾ Away on its bar. A story's state comes from its tasks (todo, running and in which chat, stuck, done? - each task done or waiting at "done?" for your word); it is done only when you close it (⋯ → Close the story, once each task is done), and its notes open from 📓 N notes. A task's Story and Type are set as it is added or in Edit (New story… names one there); a story's ⋯ gives it a goal (New goal…), renames or deletes it, and deleting a goal or a story keeps what was under it. Write it with the Hive keeper opens a box for the note: the draft shows the goal, each story with its notes and tasks, and the tasks that stand alone, all to change - a story's Add adds it under the goal, Add all the rest, at most 4 stories and 12 tasks; an answer of tasks alone is still read. An agent's add_task may name the story it goes on with (an open one by its title, or a new one with a goal) and say whether it is a bug; its card says where adding it puts it (In story “Login” (new) · goal “Auth” · bug), an added proposal's story and goal are yours from then on, and a story it opened goes when all its proposals are rejected (docs).
  • CLIs: GitHub Copilot CLI run Native goes on in its own session from the topic's previous turn, as Claude Code on its own sign-in does: it is sent only what is new, with this turn's tools, permissions and KOLONİ's tools given again, and compacts the session itself - its record says when, with the size before and after. A new topic, another model, folder or permission level starts a new session; where Copilot cannot go on in its session it starts a new one sent the whole chat, and its record says so once. Its tokens and AI credits are counted per turn, not as the session's growing total. A session is not gone on in once it holds Summarise a long context at (%) of 100,000 tokens - Copilot's dearer price step begins there; a smaller window on its role lowers that, a larger one does not lift it - or did not say its size: the next turn starts anew from the history KOLONİ keeps and summarises, and the record says so. Its context is measured against the window its session says (272,000 for gpt-6-luna, at most 100,000) instead of the catalogue's, and its details show how full it is while it works. Each session's home is kept under runtime/cli-homes/copilot-sessions/, never your own ~/.copilot, and removed with a new session, when you move to another topic, with its chat or project, and at KOLONİ's start where no agent goes on in it (docs).
  • CLIs: Codex run Native with Sign-in: Its own for KOLONİ goes on in its own thread from the topic's previous turn, as Claude Code does: each turn resumes it with this turn's folder, permission level and sandbox given again and is sent only what is new; its tokens are counted per turn. The thread is kept in the provider's own sign-in folder under KOLONİ's runtime, never your ~/.codex, and removed with a new topic, its chat or project. A thread past Summarise a long context at (%) of 166,000 tokens, or one Codex compacted itself, is not gone on in - KOLONİ's summary comes before Codex's own, which it cannot read - and the agent's record says so. On your own sign-in, still the default, Codex starts each turn anew, as before. Not yet tried with a real Codex: on Codex 0.164 a new KOLONİ sign-in folder answered read-only for a writing sandbox, so roles that write might not run on such a provider until measured (docs).
  • Settings: The app › Your data lists the working copies kept for your word - how many, what they take, and each one's chat, agent and when it was kept, with Discard, which asks first and deletes that copy as its card's Discard does; over 1 GB a line warns. They have no cap and KOLONİ deletes none unasked, so a trigger over its budget, which keeps one each time it fires, piled them up out of sight (docs).
  • To-do: each story keeps a short notebook - what was decided, the files touched, the results, the questions left - given at every turn of the story as data, so that what matters is not lost when a long session summarises itself: KOLONİ writes how each of its tasks' turns ended and the files it changed, the task's Orchestrator may end its answer with up to three Story note: lines, and the Hive keeper adds its notes as it drafts; 📓 notes beside the story shows it (docs).
  • To-do: a story's tasks go on in one topic of a chat - one session of its Orchestrator's CLI - and the next task starts a new topic of the story, told the story so far by KOLONİ's own record (each earlier task and how it stands, the files their turns changed) and its notebook, where a task of it got stuck or went back to To-do, or a day after its last turn - a session's size starts none: Claude Code compacts its own session, and Copilot's and Codex's are bound by KOLONİ already, at 75% (by default) of their window; an Orchestrator is told how each other topic of the chat that is a story's or a task's stands - done, done? or stuck (docs).
  • Chat: while a story of To-do works in a chat, one line over its messages says so - Story · · 1 / 3 · next: · 📓 notes, the next part while its next task waits in the chat's queue - and 📓 opens the story's notebook; in a narrow chat only the story's name and place stay (docs).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• A 1,500-line limit per source file, for contributors: scripts/check_file_size.py, run by PR Check and verify.ps1, fails on a file under app/, frontend/src/, scripts/ or tests/ over it; the files over it today are listed with their size in scripts/file_size_allow.txt, may only shrink, and come off the list once under the limit (--update lowers the list, never raises it); nothing the user sees changes (docs).
  • CLIs: an Orchestrator on Claude Code, Codex or Copilot run Native can now notify you and propose a trigger, as one on an API model can: Notify you only where the project has a notification address or the desktop switch on, at most 6 desktop notifications a minute; Propose triggers always as a card you approve, never in a turn nobody watches (docs).
  • Chat: while a dev server an agent started keeps running, an agent that may run commands can read what it printed since - in a later turn of the topic too, and the last output of one that ended - with secrets hidden and text that tries to give orders flagged, and stop a server it started itself, waiting until it has ended; one another agent or an earlier turn started is still yours to stop under Previews. Not in a turn nobody watches or a job while you're away, nor for a CLI run Native; what a server whose line names a secret file printed is not read again, as with any output read on your word for that once (docs).
  • Settings: Longest command (minutes) in This project › Commands and secrets - 10 by default, up to 60: an agent's command may ask for that long, and KOLONİ's own test runs (the whole suite after a change, a job's tests while you're away) are given it, so a test suite or build over 10 minutes is no longer cut. Existing projects keep 10 minutes (docs).
  • CLIs: agy, and Codex run One run per model step, are experimental: the Models page offers them only with Show experimental CLIs on (Settings › The app › Agents, off by default), under Experimental in Kind and How it runs, and Let agy search too (This project › Memory and web) shows only then. A provider already set up so keeps working, its card tagged Experimental; a Codex provider added with a model server of your own still starts as One run per model step. The first start no longer adds an installed agy (docs).
  • To-do: a night's job while you are ☾ Away runs at the level of the chat you went away from - no longer the lower of it and the To-do page's.
  • To-do: the board is read again when a turn's status moves, not at every update of a turn.
  • To-do: the Scout's follow-up tasks after a turn of a story - one of its tasks' turns, or yours in its topic - go into that story while it is open; after any other turn each stands alone. One that comes from a step that failed is a bug, any other a task, by the words it came from rather than by what the Scout says. The Scout now looks after a To-do task's turn too (docs).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• CLIs: GitHub Copilot CLI on your GitHub account offers only what your Copilot plan does. KOLONİ asks Copilot which models and Auto tiers your account offers beside what is left of your plan (models.list and account.getQuota, one start, no model turn) as the provider is added, as the Models page or the chat's model panel opens - at most once in 10 minutes - and at once after Copilot refuses a model or a routing. A model the account does not list is switched off with why ("not on your Copilot plan now", or "no premium requests" with premium at 0) and on again once the account lists it anew; one you switched off, or one Copilot refused while it was listed, stays off. Fill from the catalogue and Fill tiers proposed every GitHub model, each failing at its first turn and staying off for good: they propose only the account's (a Copilot whose account did not answer is left as it is), and the fill says when it lists none. A routing offers only the account's tiers by its own names (Standard, Fast; Fusion's from its Fusion tiers), a tier it has off dimmed, "not on your plan"; Auto's Fast, on in the account, was dropped and is sent now, and fusion is off where no Fusion tier is on. The plan card read only premium requests - premium of 0 showed "100% used" and no room: chat requests and premium requests are shown apart, premium of 0 is "none on your plan", and auto runs while chat requests are left (a named model is held back when either counter is used up) (docs).
  • CLIs: a Codex turn that ends while one of KOLONİ's tools it called is still running - a long command, say - now waits for that call to end by its own limit, and Codex's answer says so; the command was killed with the turn and its call left "interrupted", the turn Done. Stop still ends it at once. A question to you left open (ask_user) is not waited for: its card closes with the turn, as before (docs).
  • Chat: a sub-agent whose role writes (a Coder, a Debugger) that says it is done having changed no file says No file changed over its report and on its row - it showed only "Done" - and the Orchestrator is told so before the report's own words, "KOLONİ: this agent changed no file", so it no longer passes on a change that was never made. A file it changed by any way on record - a picture diagram_image drew, a file a command made, an MCP tool's call, a write its Take in still holds - keeps it unmarked, and a change turned down on its card is no change. A role that only reads is not marked; existing agents keep their record as it was (docs).
  • Chat: Code style and types reads a tsconfig.json's files through what it extends, up to 8 deep: one that names none - itself or by a base's files: [] - is said "not checked", never passed; one that extends a file outside the project or not there is said too, and a tsconfig with a byte-order mark or a // comment ended by a lone carriage return is read as tsc reads it (docs).
  • Chat: in a .js, .ts or .vue file, a line separator (U+2028, U+2029) ends a line for Code style and types as it does for eslint and tsc - a problem on a line the turn wrote was counted as on a line it did not change, and the other way round.
  • Chat: Code style and types does not offer a card for a program an earlier turn's agent wrote in an install folder while it was in a working copy, or that was merged in - it read only writes already in the project; such a write, while the file still holds it, is said "not run" as one in the project is (docs).
  • Chat: Pages reads a page's accessibility half a second after it loaded and again 0.3 s later (some 0.8 s a width) - a page that put an image's alt or a button's name a moment after it loaded was sent back to fix, one that added an image with no alt then went through; a rule found in both reads fails as many as the fewer, however the rest of the page moves (a count going up, a clock, an image's address that rotates); what one read finds more of, or a rule found in one read only, is "not judged … for what changed after it loaded", by its rule, neither sent back nor passed. A page whose script took its root away says "accessibility not read … the page has no root" (it passed with no word). A button named only by the CSS ::before or ::after words of it or of what is in it has a name (one with display: none, or an icon font's glyph, is none), a label of an image's alt names its field, an empty <a href> - a tab stop whatever its size - with no name is failed, and an image of a data: address is named "an inline image (#hero)", not "gif;base64,R0lG…", in the fix round's words too. A page nested over 1,000 deep is read only in part, and one Chrome's tab crashes on (some 1,600 deep, measured on Windows) is "not checked: the page crashed the browser's tab" at once - every later call waited 30 s, and the turn's later pages went unchecked; the next page is read in a new browser (docs).
  • Chat: a problem KOLONİ's check by kind of work found (a page, a document, a config file, a script) that the Fix rounds left - or that a round answered with no change left - ends the Checked section as failing tests do, "Still failing after 1 fix rounds: you decide (Fix it)", with Fix it: it stopped at "Sent back to fix: 1 of 2 rounds", and nothing to click. Fix it's turn is told the problems as data; work in a copy (a recipe's, an Away job's, a branch turn's) is not taken in by a plain Take in, at any level, as with failing tests - nor let in by a later look's MERGE or a stronger model's pass of its tests while the kind still fails (nor, before, by such a MERGE while fewer tests ran or the tests failed, nor where Until it passes stopped at the token limit or the budget with tests failing); a later pass of the same turn never lets that hold go (Take in anyway or Fix it), and one held for its tests goes to Ready for you only where a later pass runs every test command to a pass - "Not taken in: KOLONİ's checks of what it wrote still fail after its fix rounds", Take in anyway or Fix it (docs).
  • Chat: a role named in the Orchestrator's answer inside a table row, a quote (>) or code - a fenced block, one left open, or inline code - is no claim of its own: "| Review | Reviewer checked the diff |" no longer put "Reviewer was not opened this turn." under the answer. A claim in its own words beside them still does.
  • Agents: each model step loads only the tool calls of the messages it sends, by an index - it loaded every tool call of the chat, its sub-agents' too, so a long-lived chat (a trigger's) got slower at every step. A migration adds the index.
  • Chat: Stop pressed again while the turn's own branch or copy was being saved after a first Stop (its Take in card waiting) no longer lets the turn end under the save: the turn waits for it, so its copy is not deleted while it is kept or looked at for a secret given this turn.
  • Agents: the copies of images an agent looked at, under the project's .koloni/tmp/images/, were never deleted; one over a week old now goes as a new one is made, as the browser's screenshots go as a browser starts - a model is shown one in its own turn only (docs).
  • Chat: a Fix it turn that answered without changing anything left no Checked section, and with it no Fix it under the newest turn, while the tests or the page still failed. A turn that changes nothing right after one whose checks still failed now says "Still failing as last checked - this turn changed nothing", with those failing lines and Fix it under them - not after a turn you undid, nor once the chat's checks are off; the canvas draws no Checks node for it (docs).
  • Chat: Fix it on work not taken in ended its Checked section with "Not checked on the last change: pages" and "Tests not run on the last change: the turn ended before KOLONİ's check" though nothing was written after the check: its Take in at the turn's end put records of its own on the turn, read as a later change. Where Fix it's turn changed nothing - its model breaking after a round too -, "Not checked: documents - the turn ended before KOLONİ's check" stood under the lines of that very check. Something written after the check is still said - now also after a run that saw no change on record (a command's only), where it went unsaid (docs).
  • Chat: after Take in anyway, the Checked section kept Take in anyway and Fix it (after a reload too), and the turn's line still said "Not in the project yet: … wait in Ready for you - Take in to apply them": Take in anyway goes, the section says "Taken in anyway." and Fix it asks for the fix as for work in the project (a turn that changes nothing after it says the work still fails); work discarded, or gone on in a Fix it turn, loses both buttons, and the turn's line of where its work is is written anew when its kept copy is taken in, discarded or goes on in a Fix it turn (docs).
  • Chat: a turn undone after turns that changed nothing still had the next turn say "Still failing as last checked" of work that was gone - only the turn right before was read; it is now followed back to the turn the failure came from. And right after an Undo, the undone turn's section, or the last that said it again, kept Fix it (after a reload too), asking to fix what was gone: it is offered no more (docs).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• To-do: a night's job while you are ☾ Away runs at the level of the chat you went away from: where that chat is at Full auto and the project's Full auto check is Check what I said first, the Orchestrator may run, by your own written words, a command the night's level asked you about before (docs).
  • To-do: Close the story merges or sends a story's branch without a card only at Full auto, or where its check ran and passed; below that a branch nothing tested waits on its Merge card, as a chat's branch does. A branch holding a secret KOLONİ knows is held - its last task stuck with why - never merged nor deleted, and Discard on its card keeps the branch and the story open.
  • To-do: Breaking: a To-do task's turn no longer holds to a night's rules at every level: it runs at its chat's level, on its chat's model - Claude Code and the other CLIs with tools of their own included - and asks on cards there as your own message does: at Full auto a command that runs another program or holds inline code runs as the chat's Full auto lets it, a standing file asks as at that level, the chat's MCP tools are offered, and a sub-agent's question at Full auto is the Orchestrator's as in any chat. ☾ Away's jobs keep the night's rules; a task's turn still ends where nothing moves (docs).
  • Chat: Code style and types tells tsc to write nothing outside the project - --composite false --generateTrace null after its other words, on its own line, which win over the tsconfig and what it extends: a composite project, an incremental one with a tsBuildInfoFile, or a generateTrace made tsc write its build info or a trace where they said, outside the project too. Such a project is now type-checked, not passed over (docs).
  • Chat: an Always run rule no longer covers, past its words, ruff's --fix, --fix-only, --unsafe-fixes or --add-noqa; eslint's --fix, --plugin, --parser, --init, --inspect-config, --suppress-all, --suppress-rule, --prune-suppressions or a --format other than its own (stylish, json, json-with-metadata, html), nor its --cache-file or --suppressions-location outside the folder, in any spelling (--outputFile); mypy's --install-types, nor its reports outside the folder (--html-report, …); tsc's --incremental, --composite, --noEmit false, --generateTrace, -b / --build - but for false and null, which write nothing -, nor its --generateCpuProfile outside the folder: the rule Code style and types offers is a check that writes nothing outside the project. A word past a rule written in pieces a shell joins - fal""se, --incre"mental", ".."/x - is never taken for a harmless value or a path inside the folder (a value after = quoted whole, --select="E,F", is that value), a short option's = is read past as ruff and eslint read it - -o=../x wrote ruff's report outside under Code style's own rule -, and tsc's --p and --b are read as its -p and -b. This reaches agents' own commands too - uv run ruff no longer covers uv run ruff check --fix ., npx eslint no longer npx eslint . --fix -, and tsc's options are read in any case, as tsc reads them (--OUTDIR is --outDir) (docs).
  • Chat: Code style and types does not run eslint or tsc where an agent wrote in a node_modules above the folder they run in - Node loads their packages from the root's too -, and an Always run rule - or a yes given before - for a program in a node_modules asks on its card while such a write stands (docs).
  • Chat: in a working copy, Code style and types runs its tools without the copy's own code first on PYTHONPATH - a mypy/__init__.py an agent wrote there was imported in place of the project's mypy; KOLONİ's test runs and the agents' commands keep the copy's code first (docs).
  • Chat: an Always run rule - or a yes given before, or a trigger's leave - for uv, uvx, poetry, pipenv, pdm, hatch, pip or pip3 - run as a module too (python -m uv, py -m pip), and python -m build - (uv run ruff, poetry run mypy, pip install -e .) asks on its card, and is not run where nobody can be asked, while an agent's write of any pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg anywhere in the project stands - a workspace member or a path dependency is built with the project, running its code -, or of uv.toml, poetry.toml, pdm.toml, hatch.toml, Pipfile, .python-version, .pdm-python, pipenv's .env, a lock (uv.lock, poetry.lock, pdm.lock, Pipfile.lock, pylock.toml) or requirements*.txt; only one in the folder or above it counted. A test run (uv run pytest) is read as before (docs).
  • Chat: a node runner's rule (npm install, npx tsc, …) also stops at an agent's write of a lock (package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, bun.lockb, bun.lock) or a binding.gyp anywhere in the project - an install fetches what a lock's address says and runs node-gyp on a binding.gyp -, and at a package's package.json in a node_modules below the folder; and --ignore-scripts past such a rule is harmless only while it is on: --ignore-scripts=false, or a false after it, is covered by no rule, nor is a runner's option written in pieces a shell joins ('--ignore-scripts=false') (docs).
  • Chat: a rule for tsc (tsc, npx tsc, npm exec tsc, pnpm exec tsc, yarn tsc, or node_modules/.bin/tsc as Code style and types offered it in 0.1.7) asks on its card while an agent's write of a tsconfig*.json or jsconfig*.json anywhere in the project, or of a JSON file a tsconfig the line reads extends, stands: a tsconfig can make tsc write a trace or a composite build's info outside the project. Code style and types' own line, word for word, is covered as before: its --composite false --generateTrace null win over a tsconfig's composite or incremental build info and its trace (measured) (docs).
  • Chat: an Always run rule for make no longer covers a quoted SHELL= past it (make 'SHELL=/x' build, make "SHELL=/x" build), nor one written in pieces a shell joins (docs).
  • Chat: Check what I said first no longer lets a command run on a Turkish sentence that sets a condition with "-se" / "-sa" after any consonant or an apostrophe ("Kontroller yeşilse k-* dallarını push edebilirsin.", "Hata yoksa …", "Testler OK'se …") - only "-rse" / "-yse" were read so -, nor with "-ınca", "-dığında" or "sürece" ("Testler bitince …"); such a sentence now asks on the card, and so does one with "-dığımda" / "-diklerinde", "-ken", "-dikçe", "ise" / "isen", "durumunda", "-dığı zaman", "sonra", "-ene kadar", "dek", "madem", "yeter ki", or "as long as", "so long as", "provided", "providing", "whenever", "while", "in case", "assuming", "else"; an apostrophe written as ´, ʼ or ‘ is read as one (docs).
  • Chat: on Windows, KOLONİ writes no file whose name, or a folder's in its path, ends in a dot or a space - Windows dropped them and wrote pyproject.toml for pyproject.toml., while the record named another file, so no rule's check of what an agent wrote saw it (docs).
  • Chat: a node runner's rule also stops at an agent's yarn .env.yarn or bun .env, .env.local, .env.production or .env.development in the folder or above it, and a tsc rule at node node_modules/typescript/lib/tsc.js; what the rules do not see is listed in the guide's Known limits (docs).
  • CLIs: a sub-agent on Claude Code run Native in a working copy has the project looked at after each of its commands, as native agy's is: no sandbox holds its commands to the copy, and at Full auto one that wrote into the project by a path it did not spell out was found only at the turn's end - a write of KOLONİ's in the project meanwhile took it in unrecorded. Such a change is recorded as it happens, as made in the project by an unknown maker; each look costs one pass over the project's files (some 0.1 s for 3,000) (docs).
  • Workspace: a draw.io diagram's frame is handed a port of its own as it first loads, and the diagram's text and the Save as PNG / SVG asks go by that port alone - they were posted to the frame for any page in it to read ('*': a sandboxed frame has no origin to name), so a frame a link in the diagram took elsewhere without a new load could be sent the next ones. Only what comes back by the port is heard.
  • To-do: what agents write in a story's notebook - an Orchestrator's Story note: lines, the Hive keeper's notes, a task's title and why it is stuck - is masked (the secrets KOLONİ knows and what the project passes its commands), a line that reads like orders is left out, each note is one line of at most 200 characters and at most 20 are kept; models are given it quoted, as data, and what was stored before this is checked again as it is given (docs).

items.title: Removed
items.text:
• CLIs: Qoder. KOLONİ no longer runs it, and Add a provider no longer offers it. A Qoder provider you added before stays on the Models page, switched off with its settings: its card says "no longer supported", its switch cannot turn it on, and its window says why and offers Delete provider. A chat or a role still on it fails with that reason, as on any provider switched off, until you pick another model; once it is deleted they run on your default provider. Nothing of yours is deleted by the upgrade (docs).
  • To-do: Breaking: Run the backlog, Runs by itself and Run settings: tasks run in a chat you give them to (Do in chat), at that chat's level and on its model; a project whose backlog ran by itself stops, and the To-do page's level, model and Who changes the files are not kept (docs).

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Usage: Cards counts the command cards of the period - asked, approved, rejected and not answered, by why KOLONİ asked each one (a delete, a send off this machine, an install, a secret file …), the average time to answer, and what Check what I said first did (ran on a line of yours, not run, still asked); a delete you approved unchanged 5 times is suggested as a line for the project's rules ("You may delete ./build."), added only when you press Add to rules (docs).
  • Chat: Pages also reads each page the turn changed for accessibility, at each width: an image with no alt text, a button, link or field with no name, a page hidden whole from screen readers and a control one tabs to inside aria-hidden - failed, and sent back as a fix round with the page's words as data; text below WCAG 2's contrast (4.5:1, 3:1 for large text) over the backgrounds under it, in the light colour scheme, is a warning with its ratio, never sent back; what it cannot judge is said, never guessed: text with an image, a gradient, gradient text or a positioned layer under it, a page whose colour scheme is dark only, frames and shadow roots, a page with no body. In the page, by KOLONİ's own browser: no model, nothing installed, a page's first 2,000 elements (an inline svg counts as one) for 3 seconds at most, and a page read only in part says which limit it met (docs).
  • Settings: Config joins Settings › This project › Checks and git › Check by kind of work (on in every project, new and existing): under Test and review, a JSON, YAML or TOML file a turn wrote must parse - else its line says the parser's first complaint and line ("package.json:3: does not parse - …") and it goes back as a fix round - and a package.json, pyproject.toml, GitHub workflow or Compose file must have the shape its tool reads; a secret file is never read, nor a file nested too deep or YAML with aliases. A recipe's Checks step offers it too (docs).
  • Agents: each recipe in the Recipes list, and in the chat's recipe picker, says how many agents a run of it opens, counted from its drawing - "Feature · 6–16 agents": the fewest where no review finds a problem, the most where every loop goes back all its rounds (docs).
  • Settings: Scripts joins Check by kind of work (on in every project, and in a recipe's Checks step unless unticked): under Test and review, a .sh, .bash, .ps1 or .psm1 file a turn wrote must parse - read by bash -n (Git's bash on Windows, never WSL's) or PowerShell's own parser, never run, with none of your variables, in an empty folder of its own; a script whose reading would still make PowerShell look a module or an assembly up (an Import-DscResource, a using it cannot take out) is not read; else its line says the shell's first complaint and line ("build.sh:4: does not parse - …") and it goes back as a fix round. The turn's tests and review run on it as before; a secret file, one over 1 MB and more than 20 a turn are not read (docs).
  • Settings: Code style and types joins Check by kind of work (on in every project, and in a recipe's Checks step unless unticked): under Test and review, the project's own ruff, eslint, tsc and mypy - only where the project sets one up and has it installed here, never a download - check the files a turn changed; a problem on a line the turn added or changed goes back as a fix round ("app/x.py:12: ruff F401 - …"), warnings there and the problems on other lines are counted in notes. Running one runs the project's code, so it goes as the test command goes: at Ask and Auto-edit a card, whose yes is that very line in that folder for the turn and whose Always rule is that line (never the bare program: another config, a plugin folder or a report written elsewhere is asked again); not run while you are away, or in a trigger's turn without its leave for the line; never a program the turn wrote itself, in any case of its folder's name or through a link, nor where the turn wrote a node.cmd in its folder; one at a time with KOLONİ's test runs; in a recipe's copy what it writes is put back. A file a tool cannot parse is a problem too ("ruff invalid-syntax - …"); a file too large to compare in time is "not judged", the tool's settings the turn changed are said beside what it found, and a run that checked none of the turn's files (ruff's "No Python files found") is a note - never "no problems"; the project's own check stands for a tool only where it runs the tool as a command's program (docs).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Canvas: KOLONİ's checks of a turn are one box: the agents its checks opened (the Reviewer, the Security reviewer, the Tester, a stronger model's) and those the Orchestrator opened to fix what it sent back are drawn in it, right of the Orchestrator's work with an arrow from it, each role once with how many there were (×3, its earlier rounds as shadows behind it) - a dashed loop, Checks · KOLONİ on its frame's top edge, saying "⟲ 3 looks · 2 fix rounds · on hold" or "● round 2 · looking…", where work went back; the long line down to it and the rounds' lines back to the Orchestrator are gone. In a recipe's turn the box is its frame's last part, right of the recipe's steps: KOLONİ's looks and the Coders of its send-back rounds are in it, the recipe's own loop stays in the frame, its line back grey; sent back for the tests alone, the loop's left end is the tests ("48 → 45 (3 removed)" ⇄ Coder · fix). Who is in the box and each round come from what KOLONİ wrote as it checked - never from the order agents were opened in: a room's or a discussion's members and the agent written for the ask for a test stay the Orchestrator's, a stronger model's diagnosis is its own card; the box's title and cards are buttons (Enter or Space: its panel, an agent's window). Click it for its rounds in the panel on the right: who looked and what each said, the first blocking finding, who fixed it, why the last round stopped, with Fix it and Open the Checked section (docs)
  • Agents: the Product owner is now the Hive keeper, the Assistant product owner the Scout - same jobs, names anyone can read: the Hive keeper keeps the To-do list (Write it with the Hive keeper), the Scout keeps watch on it - it splits vague tasks, flags duplicates, stale and blocked tasks and checks finished tasks against what makes them done, and after each turn KOLONİ suggests follow-up tasks in its name (its box on the canvas, "Proposed by the Scout"); each place they show says what they do. Your recipes and saved slash commands that named the old roles name the new ones; a role of your own already named Hive keeper or Scout keeps its name, and the built-in is then "Hive keeper (built-in)" or "Scout (built-in)"; a slash command of yours named scout is renamed scout-command (the role's chip would hide it); an agent asking for an old name is told the new one. Past conversations keep the names they had; a recipe file in a folder's .koloni/recipes that names an old role is renamed by hand (docs).
  • Agents: the ready Bugfix is Reproduce it → Fix it → Checks: KOLONİ's own checks run the tests and, for a big or security-touching change, have it reviewed - two agents for a small fix instead of four, and no agent review of a small change; a failing test or Ask for changes goes back to Fix it, keeping the failing test Reproduce it showed, and the Debugger is told to reproduce the bug itself. A copy of Bugfix you changed keeps its steps (docs).
  • Chat: under Orchestrator decides, a small change - a few lines in one or two files - gets no team: the Orchestrator makes it with one agent (or itself, where the project lets it write) and says why in one line, and KOLONİ's checks run at the end all the same; picking a team, it sees how many agents each recipe opens (docs).
  • Docs: Memory has a Topics section - what a topic is, what New topic does, what the Orchestrator and its agents are given of the turns before, which models go on in a session of their own, and when to start a new topic - with a diagram of who remembers what; Data and privacy lists the sign-in and session folders KOLONİ keeps for the CLIs and what deleting a chat or a provider does to them; the glossary has Topic (docs).
  • Settings: Test before adding is gone, and the command you had in it is not kept (migration 0175 drops it): KOLONİ's guess takes its place - asked on a card at Ask and Auto-edit until you say Always, not run while you are away. To keep your own, write it on the project map's first row, the whole project (Settings › This project › This folder); it then runs beside the other parts' commands - a project with Python parts of its own runs those tests twice. Before a sub-agent's work is added, only the tests it wrote or changed run (Java's *Test.java, C#'s *Tests.cs, Rust's tests/*.rs and Ruby's *_spec.rb too) - each part's test command narrowed to them, in its working copy. They are its code: they run by themselves at Full auto, or where the part's command is yours (yours on the map, or a saved one an Always rule covers); otherwise the card waits for your Run the test before Take in, and while you are away or in a trigger's turn a guess never runs them. A part whose command cannot run just those files is said on the card and under Checked, with why; tests that ran none (pytest found none) are a note, never a pass; a sub-agent's change to its part's package.json test scripts or .npmrc keeps them from running. One that wrote no test is added with no test before ("No tests of its own to run before it is added"); KOLONİ's check at the turn's end still runs every test. The whole project's "no test" on the map stops the guess (docs).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Chat: Coverage and Code style and types compare a large file's changed lines in bounded time - a 21 000-line file with a change every 40 lines took 127 s; one too large to compare in time is said ("Coverage: not counted - too large to compare: …"), never counted as run or passed (docs).
  • Chat: a review that closes with a line such as "Findings: see above, nothing blocking." after its own Findings section is counted from that section - it said "Review gave no findings section: not counted", its suggestions were lost and a blocking finding under a MERGE went through; several sections are read together, a "Findings: 1 blocking" line above the rows takes none away, and a Findings section quoted from an earlier look (indented, >) is not read (docs).
  • Chat: a review's Findings section goes on past a code block in it (the block's own lines are still not read), a ### Blocking or ### Suggestions subheading under ## Findings, a Checked: line in it, and an earlier look's section quoted inside it (whose rows are then read with the rest) - each ended the section, and the rows after it, a blocking one too, were not counted (docs).
  • Chat: Scripts says a .sh whose first line names zsh, fish, Python or another shell as not checked instead of failed by bash (a Windows path to bash.exe is bash); what bash only warns of (a here-document ended by the file's end) is a note, not a failure - and where bash also fails, its error is said, not the warning; a PowerShell script left unread says why: "not checked: it may load a module or an assembly (it names using or Import-DscResource)"; no empty koloni-script-* folder is left in the temp folder (docs).
  • Usage: a rule the cards suggest ("You may delete ./build.") is no longer offered, nor added, where a line of your own preferences or of the project's rules names that path already - "Never delete ./build.", a list under "Never delete these:", "Keep build/", a folder it is in ("anything under out"), a full path to it or a pattern that takes it in (out/*, *.db) - Add to rules says which line (docs).
  • Chat: KOLONİ's checks run at the end of a turn whose Orchestrator, told "Not the end yet: say in one line why no team", answered without doing more - the answer said "Tests not run: the turn ended before KOLONİ's check" (docs).
  • Chat: Fix it after a stronger model's rounds that were no pass says why in KOLONİ's own words, chosen by KOLONİ - never by text a model wrote in the Checked row
  • CLIs: a file a sub-agent's work brought into the project is no longer, now and then, put down to the Orchestrator working with its own CLI beside it - also at its last look as its turn ends: KOLONİ's looks at the project wait while Take in writes files
  • Agents: a recipe with no Review step of its own, at Test and review, no longer opens KOLONİ's Reviewer again and again on a big or security-touching change; one look, as the rule says.
  • Chat: Config's check reads a tsconfig.json or .vscode/*.json with a comment after a trailing comma ("strict": true, // on) - it said "does not parse" and sent a valid file back to fix; a file broken before the turn is no longer the turn's error when a line added above moves its problem (the same complaint on a line the turn wrote still is); a YAML complaint is one line, a tagged value its tag cannot read is never said back, and NaN or Infinity in a .json does not parse - npm's reader and JSON.parse break on them (docs).
  • Agents: the guide says the agents a recipe's line counts are its own - the Orchestrator, the team leads and what KOLONİ's checks at the end open come on top of them (docs).
  • Agents: KOLONİ's Reviewer, Security reviewer and Tester look at a recipe's work where it is - the recipe's copy, as KOLONİ's own tests there - not in the project, which does not have it yet: no more "the file does not exist" and "the change was never applied" holds, nor a wasted fix round; what their commands write there is put back. Work a look still holds after its fix rounds is no longer taken in by itself at Full auto nor offered on a Ready for you card, at Auto-edit either: Checked says "Not taken in: on hold" with Take in anyway (your word, no look first) and Fix it, whose turn checks and looks at the whole kept work again - the held change with the fix - never the fix alone (docs).
  • Chat: tests that were failing before the turn (said "Were failing before this turn", not sent back) no longer keep KOLONİ's review and live try off: a big or security-touching change is still looked over (docs).
  • Chat: work a stronger model's rounds made pass is looked over by the Reviewer (a big or security-touching change) before it is taken in, instead of keeping the first pass's "No review: the tests still fail" (docs).
  • Chat: a Reviewer's "Verdict: MERGE - blocked" (or "MERGE (blocked)", "MERGE: blocked until the fix") is read as a hold, and a test run that writes a coverage report file (--cov-report=html, xml, json) as one that may change files; a Put back button says it is its own turn's - an older turn's puts back only what is still as its run left it (docs).
  • Chat: tests deleted outside KOLONİ - by hand, a pull, another branch - no longer count against the next turn, where KOLONİ can show it test by test: the last green run and this one list each of their passes by name (pytest -v), every test missing lives in a file the turn did not touch, and the turn touched no test file at all (a test it added to a file makes the drop its own), ran no command that may write files and left what decides which tests run alone - then "Tests went from 48 to 45 - not this turn's change" is said and nothing is sent back; anything less sure is the turn's, as before. A whole suite that finishes after the answer is held to the last green run too, and says a drop on its turn's Checked. Where the rounds end with fewer tests or more skipped and none failing, the last line says so and work in a copy is not taken in, "fewer of its tests run, or more are skipped", not "its tests still fail" (docs).
  • Chat: an Orchestrator that answers a fix round without changing anything ends its turn with the closing line a spent round gives ("Still failing after 1 fix rounds: you decide (Fix it)"); a look whose verdict says MERGE but marks a finding blocking is said as the hold it is; a recipe step's findings for the next step's role or for none - suggestions too - can be handed to that next step with findings_from, never to a step further on (docs).
  • Settings: where no test command was found, Checked said to set one in Settings › This project › Checks and git, which has none since Test before adding went - it now says the project map (Settings › This project › This folder: the whole project's row or a part's); Check by kind of work's note says Pages reads accessibility too, and a recipe's Checks step names Code style and types as Settings does (docs).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Chat: an Always run rule - or a yes given before - no longer covers a command whose program, named by its path in the project, an agent wrote, or that sits in an install folder (node_modules, .venv, site-packages) an agent wrote in, while the file still holds what the agent wrote: below Full auto it asks on a card that says so, and a trigger's turn, with nobody to ask, does not run it whatever its leave. A rule matches by its words in any folder, so the root's node_modules/.bin/tsc rule ran a tsc an agent wrote in a subfolder's node_modules. A package runner's rule (npx tsc, npm exec tsc, yarn tsc, bun x tsc, corepack pnpm exec tsc, uv run ruff, python -m mypy) is read so too: where the runner finds its program - the node_modules of its folder or one above it, and the .npmrc, yarn's settings and loader, bunfig.toml that make it run code of their own; for uv, poetry, pipenv and python -m any .venv or site-packages of the project; and for python -m (without -I or -P) any .py module or package the agent wrote in its folder, which it imports before the standard one (subprocess.py) - in a working copy also at the copy's root and in its src, which every command's Python reads first there, for a uv run rule or a .venv console script too, and a sitecustomize.py there even for python -m pytest; pnpm's .pnpmfile.cjs counts as yarn's settings do; and an agent's package.json in the folder or above stops a runner's rule (npx and npm exec run the package's own bin first, yarn and pnpm its scripts), a pyproject.toml or setup.py stops uv's, poetry's, pipenv's, pdm's and hatch's (a script run by its name - npm run build, npm test, uv run pytest - runs the project's code by design and is covered). Such a card offers no Always run rule, which would not cover it either - Run once or Reject. The rule offered for poetry run ruff (pipenv, pdm, hatch) names the program, never poetry alone, uv run python -m ruff the module, never uv run python, and npx.ps1 tsc is read as npx tsc - a wider rule kept from before covers none of them. A runner's line sent to another package or folder (npm exec tsc -w sub, --workspace=, --ws, --prefix, npx -w, pnpm's --filter / -r / --dir, yarn's workspace x, bun's --filter / --cwd) runs that package's own bin: no rule covers it, none is offered, a trigger's turn does not run it; nor does npm exec tsc cover npm exec tsc -c x (--call). A node runner's rule is now closed: while an agent's write of any package.json, *.npmrc, .yarnrc*, .yarn/, .pnpmfile.cjs, pnpm-workspace.yaml or bunfig.toml anywhere in the project stands, no node runner's rule covers a line (an npm install rule ran a workspace's postinstall an agent wrote; npm's and pnpm's run / test of a script under its own rule are the exception, by design) - so after an agent edits a package.json, those rules ask until the write is replaced; and past the rule's words only options that change output, the fetch source or run less (--silent, --loglevel, --offline, --no-audit, --ignore-scripts, --frozen-lockfile …) are covered - --globalconfig=x (whose node-options loaded an agent's file), --shell= and any other option are not, nor offered. The rule a card offers for bun x tsc is bun x tsc, and for corepack pnpm … the package manager's own past corepack, never corepack alone (docs).
  • Chat: on Windows, commands KOLONİ runs, servers it starts and the agents' CLIs find a program named bare - node, which an npm .cmd shim calls - on PATH only: cmd.exe looked in the folder it ran in first, where an agent could have written a node.cmd. A batch file of yours that calls its neighbour by its bare name (call helper.cmd) now calls it as .\helper.cmd (%~dp0helper.cmd in a batch file) - the command's result says so where cmd.exe did not find one the folder has (docs).

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Chat: under Test and review, KOLONİ tries a turn's change as a user would, once a turn: a changed command-line tool that answers --help by itself (a parser it imports, or its own case for it) is asked for it, never run plainly, and a big change of screens is tried by the Tester in KOLONİ's own browser on the chat's preview - started by KOLONİ (npm run dev, a free port) where none runs, and stopped after; what fails goes back as a fix round (docs).
  • Chat: under Test and review, a turn that wrote more than 80 lines of documents is read once by the Reviewer against what you asked for - what they leave out or contradict goes back as a fix round; where code is reviewed too, the same look takes them in (docs).
  • Chat: a web page a turn changed is opened in KOLONİ's own browser at phone, tablet and desktop widths (375, 768, 1280 px) - console errors and a page wider than the screen go back as a fix round; a changed component or style is looked at on the chat's running preview. Pages joins Settings › This project › Checks and git › Check by kind of work (docs).
  • Agents: every recipe ends in a locked Checks step, between its last step(s) and its end - KOLONİ checks before Ready for you asks (a fix round sends the recipe back to work), and failing work is never offered: it follows the project's After a change, or is set for the recipe - Tests, Review, Docs, Diagrams, Data, Slides and Fix rounds (0 checks only) - so a report recipe checks its documents and runs no tests; the ready Bugfix and Feature check tests and a review, Docs its documents and a review, Evolve its tests (existing ready recipes get it) - a recipe the Orchestrator picks only adds to the project's checks, and on the canvas the Checks node is the recipe's last step inside its frame (docs).
  • Chat: after a turn that wrote documents, diagrams, data or slides, KOLONİ checks them without a model (links, headings, whether a diagram parses and is connected, CSV rows, notebook cells, empty slides) and says what it could not check; a sure problem goes back as a fix round under Test and review, and each kind can be switched off in Settings › This project › Checks and git › Check by kind of work (docs).
  • Chat: where the project has GitHub Actions workflows, KOLONİ offers their lint, typecheck and test lines once, one plain command each (never e2e, a chained or piped line, a step with an expression, a secret or an install; the files are read with limits), and only in a form that checks - a line that changes files (ruff check --fix, ruff format, eslint --fix, tsc --build, a test run's -u), downloads (npx, uv run --with, mypy --install-types), sends (--pastebin), does not end (ruff server, --watch), runs code of its own (--init-hook, pytest -p x, go test -exec) or a file in place of the tool by its name (./pytest, lint.cmd, python -m lint) is not offered and its step says why; a tracked file that changed while one of KOLONİ's own runs went on - the related tests or the whole suite, in the turn or after the answer - is said ("Changed while KOLONİ's run of … went on: calc.py"), with Put back - the user's click, never KOLONİ's by itself, and not while a test run of the turn still goes on; a lint, format or type line that fails only on files the turn did not change, each finding there on the old code too, says "Were failing before this turn: old.py (from CI: ruff format --check .)" and sends nothing back; after Run these - exactly the lines its row showed - they are the test run at a turn's end, one line each "(from CI)" - not before, at Full auto and away too; a change to a workflow asks again, and one changed in the same turn is not used (docs).
  • Chat: a turn that changed code but no test is asked once for a test (for a bug fix, one that fails without the fix first) - or one line of why none fits, quoted under the answer; the new tests show there, and a removed test shows as a failed line the Reviewer judges; agents that write code are told to run only the tests near their change (docs).
  • Chat: under the answer KOLONİ tells failures that were already there before the turn from new ones (and sends only the new back), re-runs a failing test once on its own to tell a flaky test (noted in the project's memory), keeps the project's last green state - fewer tests or more skipped ones go back unless the answer says why in a sentence that names the tests, and even then they are shown as a note - and in a bug fix shows whether the new test fails on the old code (written back byte for byte); a test name the run printed is run again only when it is a plain one; a recipe's Reproduce step must leave a failing test of a file it wrote - one that did not even load shows no bug (docs).
  • Chat: after a turn that changed code, KOLONİ runs the project's tests once and says under the answer what was checked and what was not; failing tests go back to the Orchestrator at most twice; while you're away a guessed test command is not run (docs).
  • Chat: with no test command set, KOLONİ finds one by the project's files in any language (Go, Rust, Java, .NET, Ruby, PHP, Elixir, Swift, C/C++, Make, besides Python and Node), by part; failing that, an agent's run of one, or one look by the Fast tier's model at the code - an agent's or the model's line only if it is a plain test command, nothing beside a Test before adding command of yours; the first that really runs tests is saved as the project's test command, shown in Settings › This project › Checks and git at once; a saved command is no leave of yours: at Ask and Auto-edit it runs on a card until you say Always on it, and while you're away it is not run without that (docs).
  • Canvas: a checked turn has a Checks node under its Orchestrator - the test run at work, then what came of it with its counts, the related tests and a whole suite running after the answer with its clock - and each fix round is a line back to the Orchestrator; its ⋯ menu has Stop this check while a check runs and Open its log (docs).
  • Chat: a long test run no longer holds the answer: KOLONİ first runs the tests related to the changed files (pytest, vitest, jest, go, cargo, dotnet; none where you left tests out of the suite), then the whole suite goes on in the background, shown under the answer and on the line over the message box, and Fix it appears if it fails; Stop this check stops a running check, and a newer turn running the same suite in the same project takes the place of an older run (docs).
