  • Chat: Test and review changes in the permission level's menu turns KOLONİ's checks after a change on or off for one chat, whatever the project's setting; off, the level says "· no checks", the Checked section says "Not checked: off for this chat" and the canvas draws no Checks node - free at every level, said under the switch at Full auto; the Checks node's ⋯ menu has Off for this chat too; a turn running a team's recipe follows the recipe (docs).
  • Chat: under Test and review, a change of more than 80 lines or 3 files, or one that touches security, is looked over at the turn's end by a read-only Reviewer agent KOLONİ opens (and the Security reviewer, told to try to refute it); each ends with MERGE or HOLD, blocking findings go back to the Orchestrator and it looks again until MERGE or the Fix rounds are spent - then Fix it asks for them to be fixed (the Orchestrator is handed the findings as data, not as your words). Each look is an agent's work, shown under the answer, on the canvas and in Usage (docs).
  • Chat: failing work is never taken in: when the Fix rounds are spent and a test still fails, KOLONİ hands the fix to the next stronger tier on the Models page (fast, balanced, strongest) - its model says what is wrong first (fix-incomplete, test-wrong, approach-wrong) - and if nothing passes, a recipe's or an Away job's work stays in its copy: Checked says "Not taken in" with Take in anyway and Fix it (your answer to the stronger model's question); at Full auto a recipe whose tests still fail is no longer taken in (docs).
  • Settings: Settings › This project › Checks and git › Then a stronger model (on unless you switch it off): once the Fix rounds are spent with a test still failing, the next stronger tier on the Models page tries the fix - a Reviewer's hold after the rounds waits for you (Fix it) (docs).
  • Chat: where the project already measures coverage (pytest-cov, Vitest's coverage, c8 in its own node_modules), the whole suite's run says under the answer what share of the turn's changed lines the tests ran, and on the canvas's Checks node; the new lines no test ran go to the Reviewer as data. Nothing is installed, only report flags are added, the report stays in the project's scratch folder, and flags the runner does not know are dropped (docs).
  • Settings: Settings › This project › Checks and git › Fix rounds (Until it passes, the default, or 1 to 10): how often failing tests and the Reviewer's blocking findings go back in a turn (docs).
  • Chat: Until it passes, Fix rounds' new default: failing tests and blocking findings go back while each round makes progress, and stop - said under the answer - where a round changed nothing (the same failing tests, or the same blocking findings two rounds in a row), at the turn's token limit or the project's monthly budget, or after 20 rounds: "Sent back to fix: round 3 (until it passes, 3 failing → 1)", "Stopped after round 4: no progress in two rounds"; then a stronger model, by the same rule. A project still on the old default, 2, moves to it; a number you chose is kept. A recipe's Checks step may choose it too (docs).
  • Away: while the project is not on Test and review, the Away panel suggests it, with Use Test and review (docs).
  • Settings: Settings › The app sets how many of KOLONİ's own test runs go at once (1) and how many test processes each may use (2) (docs).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Settings: Finish only when the tests pass is now After a change (Test and review / Tests only / Nothing) in Settings › This project › Checks and git, for every model, not only Claude Code; a project that had turned it off gets Nothing (and Settings says so), the rest Test and review; the line under it says what it does in this project now - the test command it runs, when the Reviewer reads a change, the Fix rounds (docs).
  • Agents: Coder, Tester, Reviewer, Debugger and Security reviewer are always on and keep the tools their job needs (a Tester keeps run_command); a role that lost one gets it back (docs).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Memory: a project's Memory opens again after KOLONİ noted a flaky test in it - the note names no model, and the list failed to load from then on.
  • Chat: where the project has its own test command and a stronger model's fix fails Take in's check, the turn still says what was checked - the hand-off, "Still failing after rounds by …" and that the fix was not taken in - instead of no Checked section (docs).
  • Agents: Make it a recipe (and the Product owner's draft of tasks) asks the model of the chat you are in, then every tier, then your newest chat's model, when the Fast or Balanced tier's model is not running - it said "No model answered: Local (not running)" though your chats ran on another provider; with none answering it says how to fix it (docs).
  • Settings: the line under After a change names the test command you set for a part on the project map, before what KOLONİ saved for another folder, and changes as you save one there (docs).
  • To-do: Write it with the Product owner asks the next model when one does not answer - your next fast model, then the Orchestrator's - as Or write it does, instead of stopping at the first (docs).
  • Chat: the Reviewer that looks over a big change can now run a command that only reads and the project's approved test command exactly as it is set (your check or part test command, a saved one an Always rule covers, a CI line you approved) - anything else is refused and it is told why, and a Reviewer's command never opens a card (docs).
  • Install: closing KOLONİ with the page open no longer waits five seconds nor prints "Cancel N running task(s)": the page's stream ends on Ctrl+C (docs).
  • Memory: a fast model's notes on a turn that hold a long run of space inside their code fence are read at once - 100 000 spaces took a minute on KOLONİ's own loop.
  • Agents: Or write it on the Recipes tab no longer fails with "Local isn't answering" while your local model server is not running: it passes over a model whose server looked down, asks the next model of the tier and then the Orchestrator's own, names every one it tried when none answers, and the note under it says which model it will ask (docs).
  • Agents: a Candidates step with a loop (the ready Evolve recipe) runs one round only when the project has no measure command - with no score nothing reaches the target, so its other rounds opened up to 9 more Coders for nothing; the candidates' card says why (docs).
  • Chat: a heredoc written to a file or handed to git as a message (cat > notes.md <<'EOF' with 1) first in it), a comment (echo done # 1) first step), sh's case … esac patterns and a group only printed in quotes (echo "(npm ci)", git commit -m "run (npm ci) first") are no longer asked at every level as brackets that do not pair, nor read as an install (docs).
  • Agents: the ready Bugfix recipe sends a failing test back to Fix it and starts with a failing test; a Tester or reviewer that reports nothing wrong while a test run on record failed no longer passes - unless its "Already failing before" lines name every test that failed - nor does a Tester that ran no command but reads; a check whose command you declined stops at Ready for you, not checked (docs).
  • Agents: KOLONİ no longer freezes for seconds when a tool's output holds a long run of digits (a command that prints a big number, a file of numbers read), when the fast model's notes on a turn start with many blank lines, or when a fixer's report holds a long line of spaces.
  • Install: closing KOLONİ with the page open takes one Ctrl+C (up to five seconds), and it now stops its local model server and the agents' browsers on Linux and macOS too (docs).
  • Chat: coming back to a chat whose over-budget question is still open no longer moves the focus to "Go on anyway"; a new question still takes it.
  • Chat: with Auto-read on, an answer that holds a long run of dots no longer slows the page on every word that streams in.
  • Chat: a coloured test run (--color=yes in the project's pytest settings, or FORCE_COLOR where KOLONİ was started) is read as a plain one: its counts show in the Checked section, a run that only skipped tests is no pass, a failure it prints is one even where its exit is hidden, and a guessed command that ran tests is saved instead of asked about again every turn (docs).
  • Chat: a file that steers later work (AGENTS.md, .koloni/rules.md) written by KOLONİ's own test run is said to be KOLONİ's test run's on its card, not the Orchestrator's, and while that card waits after the run, the Checked section says "waiting for your answer on a file the tests wrote" instead of a clock that keeps counting (docs).
  • Agents: in a recipe, a failed test run is no longer cleared by a later run of the same test tool that runs no tests (-h, --version, --collect-only, a list of the tests, none found) or only some of them (-k, a test name, --ignore, its own -c or PYTEST_ADDOPTS) - only by the same command passing again, the whole suite passing in the same folder, or a run of the files that hold every failing test; and a Tester that ran only commands that check nothing (echo, python -c "pass", --version) does not pass, nor - where the project has a test command and the recipe changed code - one that ran no test that really ran tests (docs).
  • Chat: a turn whose only change a command made (python -c "open(…).write(…)", sed -i, a heredoc to a file, a redirection into one - cat a > b, git show HEAD:f > f -, a formatter, black . && pytest -q, a test run that writes - jest -u, --junitxml=a.py, go test ./... -update, pytest --inline-snapshot=fix, INSTA_UPDATE=always cargo test, PYTEST_ADDOPTS=--junitxml=a.py pytest) is checked too, and a test file such a command deleted says "Test removed": KOLONİ runs the tests and says under the answer "A command of this turn may have changed files KOLONİ did not record: …" - in a git project only where git lists a file written since the first such command began, or one committed during the turn, named in that line - and "No review: changes made by a command are not recorded"; a turn that only read or tested - or, in a git project, ran a command that wrote nothing - opens no check (docs).
  • Chat: answering the card of a file KOLONİ's test run wrote (AGENTS.md, .koloni/rules.md) after the turn had ended - Keep, Take back, or Stop this check - no longer puts the turn back to running with nothing at work; its Checked line is updated and the turn stays ended.
  • Chat: a Reviewer's verdict written another way is read: Final verdict: HOLD, My verdict: HOLD, 1. Verdict: HOLD, a ## Verdict heading or Verdict: with the word on the next line, Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES / REJECT / NEEDS CHANGES / FAIL / do NOT MERGE hold, APPROVE and LGTM merge, and Verdict: MERGE is not possible, a MERGE on a condition (MERGE once the SQL injection is fixed), a blocked, wrong or crossed-out one (MERGE blocked by the failing test, MERGE would be wrong, MERGE ✗) or MERGE or HOLD? HOLD. is no MERGE; a ~~~ fence or an indented code line is no verdict (docs).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Commands: a command line built to make KOLONİ's command reader slow (a long run of spaces) is read in time - so are a test run's output and a reviewer's report.
  • Agents: a command that only reads no longer runs unasked when a path it names leads out of the project, or to a secret file, through a link or junction inside it (cat out/secret.txt where out points elsewhere) - it is asked as other commands are, as reading the file already was (docs).
  • Chat: under Test and review, a change that touches sign-in, secrets, permissions, the network or running commands gets a second, adversarial look by a read-only Security reviewer agent, told to try to refute that it is safe; the Reviewers get read tools only and no MCP server, whatever their role is given, and are never opened on a CLI that works with tools of its own; their findings reach the Orchestrator as data, and Fix it sends your words only.
  • Chat: a line a launcher hands to a shell is read as the command it is - Start-Process powershell -ArgumentList '-Command','taskkill …', Start-Process cmd -ArgumentList '/c …', npx -c '…', [scriptblock]::Create('…'), schtasks /tr "…" - and a command PowerShell is handed encoded (-EncodedCommand) is asked at every level (docs).
  • Chat: an install in a $( … ) (out=$(npm ci)), a stop in code an interpreter reads on stdin (echo "…" | python, python - <<'EOF') or is handed by php -r, lua -e, R -e or julia -e is asked; a branch switch and a patch are read behind a wrapper (time git switch main, bash -c '…'), and cmd's ^ at a line's end continues it (docs).
  • Chat: what an agent's command runs inside a group is read as a command of its own - (cd web && npm ci), { npm ci; }, if exist x (npm ci) else (npm i), for %a in (*) do (npm ci) and PowerShell's script blocks (if ($true) { npm ci }, ForEach-Object { … }, & { … }, Invoke-Command -ScriptBlock { … }): an install, a rebuild, a write through a working copy's linked folders, a stop, a delete or a send there is asked as it is on a line of its own, with web off too; a group whose brackets do not pair is always asked (docs).
  • Chat: cmd's if "%a%"=="x" …, trap -- '…' EXIT and npx --call="…" are read to the command they run, and a branch switch, inline code, a patch and a git command that rewrites .git/config are read in a continued line too (git⏎switch main) (docs).
  • Workspace: a pull request of a branch never sends a commit of yours that origin does not have when it came onto the branch without a merge commit of the agent's - a fast-forward to your branch, a rebase onto it or a cherry-pick - also once you amended, rebased or dropped it: only what the branch's own history says was committed on it counts as the agent's (docs).
  • Workspace: a pull request never sends a file that holds exactly what a commit of yours not pushed yet put there (an agent's squash, pick or amend of it), and while your branches hold commits not on GitHub a pull request waits for your click at every level, Full auto too, saying how many (docs).
  • Workspace: what a pull request reads as yours not on GitHub now also takes in your stashes, commits on a detached HEAD and the uncommitted files a branch began from: an exact copy of one is never sent, and a branch that began from your uncommitted work, or while you have a stash or commit not on GitHub, waits for your click before its pull request at every level, the card saying why at Ask and Auto-edit too (docs).
  • Workspace: a commit of yours on a detached HEAD in another worktree of yours counts as your work not on GitHub too - an agent's copy of it is never sent in a pull request, and the pull request waits for your click; the card says "a stash" for a stash instead of counting the commits git keeps it in, and a commit on the branch that neither its history shows as the agent's nor your branches hold (a pick of yours, or the agent's own once that history expired) is held without being called yours (docs).
  • Workspace: in a branch's worktree, an agent's command that finds your repository's own path (git rev-parse --git-dir, --git-common-dir), or writes to a place made when it runs - > "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/…", >|, cp x "$D/…", Set-Content (Join-Path …), [IO.File]::WriteAllText(…), cmd's for /f … %i, a link made there, or any write after a cd to such a place - is asked at every level, Full auto too: it could rewrite your repository's own .git (point another worktree of yours elsewhere, rewrite its HEAD and history, or forge a branch of origin's) and let a commit of yours not on GitHub go out with a pull request. The temp folder by its variable, the folder the command runs in ($PWD/out.txt), a date in a file's name and a for loop over names written out still run - not where the place climbs (..) or the line sets that name (docs).
  • Chat: a runner that downloads a package and runs it - npx -p (before what it runs), npm exec --package, uv run --with, uvx, pipx run, bunx, pnpm dlx, yarn dlx, npm create, npm init <x>, yarn / pnpm / bun create, deno run npm:…, go run <module>@<version>, corepack pnpm dlx - counts as an install: asked with web off, and in a working copy whose dependency folders are linked to yours; a plain npx <tool>, and npx tsc -p tsconfig.json, are read as before (docs).
  • Chat: an Always run rule no longer covers a line that adds an option that runs another program, fetches code or writes outside the folder, alone or in a bundle (pytest -qo …) - pytest's --basetemp, -p, --rootdir, --confcutdir, -o or -c, go's -exec or -C, cargo's --config or --manifest-path, gradle's -I, -p or -b, npm's --script-shell, --prefix, --userconfig or --node-options, make's SHELL= or -f, tox's -c, maven's -Dmaven.ext…, uv's --with, bash -c - while -p no:…, -o log_cli=… and a script's own words after -- stay covered; a pytest --basetemp is a delete wherever it is given (its line, addopts, PYTEST_ADDOPTS) but in the agents' scratch (docs).
  • Workspace: a pull request no longer calls the agent's own commits yours when you look at its branch in a worktree of yours (git worktree add --detach … koloni/…), nor counts another KOLONİ's worktrees as yours - but a commit you made in such a worktree before, or one a branch, tag or other remote of yours holds too, stays yours; a worktree of yours whose branch you deleted still counts, and the card names the worktree that holds your commit not on GitHub - and says git worktree prune lets git drop one whose folder you deleted (docs).
  • Chat: what a runner runs is read as a command of its own - poetry run cmd /c rd /s /q src, uv run rm -rf src, cargo run -- …: a delete there is asked, at Full auto too, and an Always run rule for the runner never covers a shell it is handed, its path spelt out too (C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /c …) (docs).
  • Chat: a model's tool call never passes for one of KOLONİ's own by its id: one named as KOLONİ names its own (koloni_…, cli_…) gets an id of its own when it is recorded.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Settings: Settings › This project › Asking and away has A harmful-looking command at Full auto: Ask me (as before, and the default; existing projects keep it) or Check what I said first - before a command that deletes, overwrites or sends something off this machine waits for you at Full auto, the first model of your Fast tier reads your preferences, this project's rules as saved on the Memory page and your own messages in the chat, and the command runs without a card only when a whole line of yours names it - one that forbids nothing and sets no condition; one a whole sentence of yours forbids ("Never push to main.") is not run and opens no card - its agent is told that sentence (of a message of yours in the chat, only that one forbids it), and not to run it again or anything that does the same - while a sentence that sets a condition or asks to be asked ("unless", "ask me before") keeps the card, and after 3 such refusals in a row or 10 in a turn KOLONİ says so and the rest of the turn asks on a card; secret files, .koloni, files that steer later turns, paths outside the folder, a delete or a send of the whole folder and a CLI's command whose folder is not known are always asked, and anything that goes wrong opens the card as before (docs).
  • Chat: a command that ran without a card that way, or was not run by a sentence of yours, says so under it, with the line of yours it rested on and where that line is (Your preferences, This project's rules or your message), and waits under Decided for you until you press OK; when the check found nothing of yours that covers a command, its card says "Nothing you said covers this."
  • Chat: ☾ Away on a chat's status line opens the Away panel: that chat finishes its turn, then the To-do tasks you tick (the ones proposed in this chat ticked already, at most 10, in an order you set and that To-do keeps) are worked through one at a time, each in its own copy, until you are back - I'm back, or a message of yours. The panel says what the Orchestrator decides for you and what always waits, and takes a stop time, a spend limit and places kept out, none unless you set one. While away the line says "Away · To-do 1 of 2: … · 3 decided for you · 1 waits"; coming back, the chat has one summary, "While you were away (23:10 – 07:42): 2 of 2 To-do done · …", with what was decided, what waits (Allow and go on / Refuse), Review and take in and On the canvas (docs).
  • Chat: told you are going away, the Orchestrator puts the work on To-do and offers one line under its answer, "☾ Go away now? Add a bye line, Say hello twice · Until 08:00 · at most 2.00 USD", with Go away and Change - the line takes only the tasks it put on To-do itself in that turn, never a sub-agent's or an earlier one's; nothing starts before your Go away (docs).
  • Chat: Check what I said first in the permission level's menu - the project's check of your own words before a harmful-looking command waits for you - also holds while you're away, in a To-do task's chat at Full auto, reading the chat you went away from - there, and in that chat, for a one-line delete in the folder only: a command of more than one line or continued, a send, a git remote, Docker's prune or volumes and an instruction file keep their card (docs).
  • Memory: when the folder's .koloni/rules.md differs from the rules saved here, the page says so and shows both: the box keeps the saved rules, which Full auto's check reads, and Use the folder's rules here takes the folder's text into it.
  • Models: a GitHub Copilot CLI provider on your GitHub account has a Routing on its auto and fusion rows, beside Context - Auto: Efficiency, Balance or Intelligence; Fusion: Standard, High or Max (several models try each turn and one is kept; High and Max cost more than auto) - and the chat's model panel shows the same choice under Thinking. It is saved on the model's row, so every chat and agent on that provider and model uses it. The catalogue offers fusion, with no tier. High and Max are only on some Copilot plans: on one without them the turn stops saying so and to pick another routing (docs).
  • Settings: Settings › This project › Asking and away has Agents may delete what is disposable without asking (off; existing projects keep it off): at Auto-edit files and Full auto, in a chat you started, a delete KOLONİ checks is disposable runs without a card - a build or cache folder git ignores (build, dist, __pycache__, .next, target and the like) holding no file git tracks and no link, a clean worktree of yours that is not locked and not KOLONİ's, and a merged local branch that no worktree, the turn or the project stands on (never main, master or the default one). Only such a delete alone on its line, never forced; worktrees and branches only from the project, never a sub-agent's copy. At Ask before changes it still asks (docs).
  • Chat: the card of such a delete offers Allow such deletes in this project, which turns that setting on and runs the command once; a delete that ran without a card that way says "Ran without asking · disposable: …" under it.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Complexity wave F4 (part 1): 7 frontend functions of complexity 51-91 split to 12 or under; nothing the user sees changes.
  • Complexity wave F4 (part 2): App and the Inspector split to complexity 12 or under; nothing the user sees changes.
  • Complexity wave F4 (part 2, the chat): the chat's panel, message box and message list split to 12 or under; no function of the frontend is over 12 now.
  • Chat: when the Orchestrator answers a question for you, it also reads your preferences and this project's rules as saved on the Memory page.
  • Chat: smaller, steadier type, as in VS Code - answers and your messages at 13 px, headings 16/14/13 px, code 11.5 px - and the Orchestrator's turns no longer sit in cards: a small head (who answered, with which model, when), its steps, its answer, and under it Copy and Read aloud (always under the latest answer, on pointing at older ones) with what it did at the right (docs).
  • Chat: steps are rows with an icon for their kind; a group of steps is open while it runs and closes to one line when done, and once the turn is over everything before the answer folds into one line, "Completed 5 steps in 32s", which counts what failed or was rejected (a test run that exited with an error too), with the first failed step's reason in one line under it; sub-agents, rooms, discussions, a server still running and every card that waits for you stay outside it. A command opens by itself while output comes or when it failed, its output 6 lines tall, then scrolling (docs).
  • Chat: the message box is one box. Its top line says "Orchestrator is ready" with the model (choose the model there), while a turn runs what it does now, for how long, the tokens written and the tier, with Stop and how many messages are queued, and "waits for your answer" while it asks; under the message one row: Attach, the permission level as three comb cells and its name (a click lists the levels, each with a line on what it does, and the Plan first switch; while Plan first is on, the level reads, say, "Auto-edit · plan"), Auto-read, Dictate and Send. Under the box: Workspace with its number, New topic, Chat settings, More and "2 more wait elsewhere" (docs).
  • Chat: the Orchestrator's question waits just above the message box - numbered options, your own answer and Submit; keys 1-9 pick, Enter sends; "‹ 1/2 ›" when it asks two. In its turn one line says it asks (a click goes to the card) and, once answered, "Question: … / Answered: …" opens to its options. KOLONİ's own cards and sub-agents' questions stay where they were (docs).
  • Canvas: an agent at work says on its box what it does, how long it has worked, the tokens it wrote (where its CLI tells them) and its tier or model (docs).
  • Chat: an agent's window, a discussion's, Workspace and a room's window no longer open over the open chat on a small window; beside it they may lie over each other, the one opened last in front.
  • Chat: in a 340 px chat the "details" of what a turn did no longer drops to a second line.
  • Agents: an agent on a branch is told that git works in its copy (status, diff, history, commits on its branch) and that the rest of git is asked about (docs).
  • Settings: a new project lets the Orchestrator decide a waiting card after 5 minutes (Settings › This project › Asking and away › When you're away); a project from before keeps what it had - turn it on there - and in a chat with no folder everything still waits. The rule is the same everywhere: at once while you're away, after those minutes otherwise, in To-do task chats too; it also decides going on or stopping at a sub-agent's step limit, and while you type an answer it waits (docs).
  • Chat: the "While you're away" card is gone, with its Start, Change the list, Not now and its row in Ready for you: ☾ Away and the Orchestrator's Go away line take its place; Run the backlog and Try again wait until you are back (docs).
  • Chat: Plan first is set in the permission level's menu only (or with /plan): the button beside the level under the message box is gone, and while Plan first is on the level says so ("Auto-edit · plan").
  • CLIs: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114, which speaks a newer protocol, runs Native again: KOLONİ asks before every tool of Copilot's own through a hook of its own, never letting one through by itself, and each of Copilot's PowerShell commands starts in the project folder. KOLONİ asks Copilot its version and protocol as it starts it - an update Copilot made of itself reaches KOLONİ too; a version of the older protocol not measured with KOLONİ, a Copilot that does not say its version, or a protocol KOLONİ does not know, runs as One session per agent, and the provider's card on the Models page says why in one line (docs).
  • Chat, CLIs: on GitHub Copilot CLI's auto or fusion, the Orchestrator's turn head names the model Copilot picked ("fusion → gpt-6-luna") with Copilot's own reason on a quiet line under it (two lines at most), and the model button over the message box says it too ("fusion → gpt-6-luna · Copilot"; what its last turn ran on, and why, in its tooltip). A reason shows only under the model it was given for (docs).
  • Workspace: KOLONİ's worktrees for agents on a branch are locked while their agents work (git worktree list -v says "KOLONİ: an agent works here; KOLONİ removes it"), so your own git worktree prune, remove or move leaves them alone; KOLONİ unlocks one before it removes it, and at start removes only its own records whose folder is gone - never another worktree, never a branch (docs).
  • Agents: an agent in a copy is told that other agents may work at the same time, each in a copy of its own: to change only the files its task needs, to write, move or delete nothing outside its copy, to stop only processes it started and never programs by name, to start a server or test on a free port, and - where node_modules, .venv and venv are linked in - to install nothing into them and say in its report what to install (docs).
  • Workspace: a team's branch starts from your folder as it is - your edits, staged files and new files git does not ignore are in the agent's worktree - not only from your last commit; KOLONİ makes that one commit ("KOLONİ: your folder as koloni/… began") from an index of its own, leaving your files, index, branch and HEAD as they are; what git ignores, files named as secrets, the dependency folders, KOLONİ's own .koloni folder and every link or junction stay out, staged or not, and the card names in one line which of your files were left out as a secret or a link (docs).
  • Workspace: a branch's card, its merge and its pull request carry the agent's work alone, measured from your folder as the branch began - never your uncommitted files (docs).
  • Workspace: a branch's merge waits for your commit where the agent changed what you had not committed, at Full auto too - no agent puts your lines together - the card names another agent's Take in that is in your folder and not committed yet, and work that changes a file you had not committed when the branch began waits for your Merge (docs).
  • Workspace: where your folder had more new or changed files than a copy takes, your git is older than 2.40, or git could not take your folder as it is (a file another program holds open, a path too long), a branch starts from your last commit and its card says so in one line (docs).
  • Agents: the Orchestrator is told that sub-agents it opens together work at the same time, to give each its own files or folders, and that koloni/… branches and the worktrees in KOLONİ's copies folder are not its to delete, rename or switch to (docs).
  • Docs: the guide says what 0.1.2 to 0.1.5 changed where it was still missing or wrong: Check what I said first at Full auto in full (what it reads, a line that allows or forbids, Decided for you, what it costs, where it ends), ☾ Away on the chat's status line and the job's level, the Orchestrator answering in a To-do task's chat after the project's minutes, the folder's rules that differ on the Memory page, Copilot 1.0.114 and its routing in the CLIs table and Every setting, the slow model's card in Ready, disposable deletes in the form each shell reads, upgrade notes for each version, and the README's box, models and security; the main screen, agent window, Ready, Take in, team and Settings pictures and the four videos are taken anew (no Plan first chip, ☾ Away on the status line, the window icon on each box), Work while you're away has pictures of the Away panel and of the summary when you are back, and the permissions, working copy, CLI, Away and agent runner diagrams are drawn anew (docs).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Agents: in a recipe such as Quality check or Upkeep, a test run that failed now runs the fix step even when the Tester's report says it found nothing; a command that is no test run (a search with no match) still does not (docs).
  • CLIs: with Codex run Native, a command that prints nothing for more than 30 seconds (a quiet test run, a build) no longer ends Codex's turn as one that never started; only a command still at work after 11 minutes ends it (docs).
  • Chat: a message still queued when KOLONİ restarted is no longer marked "Interrupted by a server restart" as if it had run: it says "Not sent: KOLONİ restarted", and its Send sends it as your newest message; nothing sends it by itself (docs).
  • Workspace: a file you pick right after the page loads stays open; it fell back to "Pick a file in the tree." once KOLONİ had read the project's git branch. Only a switch to another branch opens the Workspace anew.
  • Canvas: an agent's line at work keeps what it does in sight: where its box (or the line over the message box) is narrow, its tier goes first, then its tokens, then its time, each whole - then, over the message box, the model's name, down to its icon - and what it does is cut only after them; in the chat, a discussion's row keeps its name and topic and cuts what it says of itself first.
  • Chat: the row under the message box no longer runs past the chat's edge (it did in a 480 px chat while something waited elsewhere): Chat settings reads Settings and "2 more wait elsewhere" reads "2 wait" whenever the row has no room for all its words; in the narrowest chat Settings keeps its word beside the icons of New topic and More.
  • Chat: a kept working copy's long folder path now wraps on its card in a narrow chat; it made the whole chat scroll sideways.
  • CLIs: GitHub Copilot CLI run Native on models other than Claude (such as gpt-6-luna or mai-code-2-flash) can change files again: it is given Copilot's own apply_patch, the only file tool those models have, and each file of a patch is its own card, as a write is; refusing one refuses the whole patch (docs).
  • Models, CLIs: GitHub Copilot CLI's card on the Models page names the version KOLONİ runs, which KOLONİ asks Copilot as it starts it, no longer the number a plain copilot --version says; an error that Copilot could not be asked before it acts names that version too.
  • Chat, Canvas: an agent's window no longer opens by itself when it starts (on any provider, Lead or sub-agent): on a Native provider the Orchestrator's window opened on every message. Open it from its node - the new window icon at the right of its name, or a double click -, from Open window in the Inspector, or from the Orchestrator's name over its turn in the chat (docs).
  • CLIs: a model GitHub Copilot CLI's fusion picked now says fusion and goes on with fusion: before, fusion's picks were recorded as auto, and an agent that went on from one asked for auto (docs).
  • Workspace: a copy made while another agent's work was being taken in now gets all of that work, not part of it; a Take in waits while a branch is merged; and the other agents' copies now get what a branch's merge brought, as they get what a Take in brought (docs).
  • Workspace: a Stop while a branch is being merged by itself at Full auto waits for git to finish: the merge is on its card and the branch's worktree goes, where before the merge landed with nothing on record.
  • Chat: in a window under 1200 px wide, an agent's window opened while the Inspector lies over the canvas no longer reaches 6 px under the Inspector where the open chat leaves too little room beside it: it opens where it would without the chat, over the chat's right edge, in front.
  • Workspace: a branch's working copy kept over a restart merges a file you changed too line by line, from what the branch was made of, where it showed both files whole; and its Discard deletes its branch and git's record of its worktree, which stayed behind (docs).
  • Workspace: on Linux and macOS, a branch whose agent ran git add -A in its worktree no longer brings KOLONİ's own .venv or node_modules link with it: its merge card no longer waits on .venv as in the way, and neither the merge nor a pull request carries it (docs).
  • Chat: on Windows, a disposable delete written the way sh writes it (rm -rf build) no longer goes without a card: KOLONİ's own commands run in PowerShell there, which answers it with an error and deletes nothing, yet the row said it went. Only the shell's own form counts (Remove-Item -Recurse in PowerShell, rm -r in sh and in Claude Code's Bash tool); where the shell is not known (Codex, agy) a folder's delete keeps its card. A disposable delete that then fails says so ("… and failed: exit 1").
  • Chat: at 340 px, a task's name in the ☾ Away panel takes its row's width (it was squeezed to a word a line; its tag and buttons now go under it), and a long path on a branch's merge card - what is in the way, where it started, what it left out - breaks instead of running past the card's edge.

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Workspace: a pull request of a branch that took in commits of yours not on origin - your branch merged into it to resolve a conflict, or by the agent, or another branch of yours - is not pushed until you push them, also once you amended, rebased or dropped them: before, after such a rewrite their earlier content went up with it, at Full auto unasked (docs).
  • Workspace: your repository's git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, also from a core.hooksPath such as husky's) no longer run for an agent's own git commands in its copy, nor for an MCP server's it starts there, and git's fsmonitor and commit signing are off for them (docs).
  • Agents: on a branch, an agent's command that clears or sets git's own environment (unset GIT_…, env -i, $env:GIT_… =, Remove-Item Env:\GIT_…), or runs one of git's own programs by its name (git-push), is asked at every level, Full auto too: it would bring your repository's hooks back (docs).
  • CLIs: with GitHub Copilot CLI on its newer protocol, a tool of Copilot's own that ran without KOLONİ being asked stops the turn, and the run says so (docs).
  • Chat: a command an agent runs in its copy that names another agent's copy, a worktree of the project or a place above its copy (../.., also past a cd KOLONİ cannot follow, in quoted code or in a variable; a full path also with doubled separators or as %LOCALAPPDATA%, $HOME or ~), writes in the linked node_modules, .venv or venv, or installs into them (npm --prefix web install, cmd /c "npm i", python -m pip, updates and rebuilds too; in a turn you watch), is asked at every level, Full auto too (docs).
  • Chat: a command that stops programs by their name (taskkill /IM, pkill, killall, Stop-Process -Name), or looks a process up and stops it (Stop-Process -Id (Get-Process x).Id, lsof -ti:8000 | xargs kill, fuser -k, npx kill-port), is asked: from a copy always; in the project, Full auto's Check what I said first may let it run on a line of yours - but never one that may stop KOLONİ itself or another agent's CLI (python, node, uvicorn, claude, codex, copilot, qodercli, agy, a filter, a wildcard, everyone's or a group's pid such as kill -1, a process looked up). Stopping a program by its id (taskkill /PID, kill 1234, Stop-Process -Id 1234) stays as before (docs).

items.title: Added
items.text: • Chat: when the Orchestrator's model has said nothing for 5 minutes in a turn you started (or Qoder has kept its free model queued for 90 seconds), a card asks whether to keep waiting or stop and pick another model, instead of the turn sitting there until you press Stop; like any card, it waits for you on the Ready page, in the Chats list and in a note in the corner (docs).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Chat: answers are easier to read at length - larger, airier and softer type, bold words and code without loud colour or a box - and each turn of the Orchestrator's is one card: who answered, with which model and when, its steps as quiet pills and its answer, and once the turn is over a quiet foot with what it did, Copy (the answer as written) and Read aloud, shown when you point at or tab into the card (always, under a turn with nothing else at its foot). Read aloud reads the turn's answer only, no longer each line written on the way. A question the Orchestrator was not let ask stands on its own line ("Wanted to ask: … · not asked"), not folded into the step's line.
  • Chat: while the Orchestrator asks you something, its question waits in that turn's card, whose head says waits for you where its time would be; the closed chat's line says what it asks ("Orchestrator asks: …"), its box on the canvas shows the question's first line when you point at it, and the message box says to answer above or queue a message. A message you queue meanwhile is said to wait once a turn, not once a question; who asks is said once, on the question's card; and once the turn is over its line counts the questions it asked you.
  • Chat: the open chat is a column at the left of the canvas, as tall as it, with no gap around it; drag its right edge (or use the arrow keys on it) to make it 340 to 760 px wide, and the width is kept. It no longer moves about the canvas or changes height; closed, it is the one-line box in the corner as before. Workspace, opened beside the open chat on a window at least 1400 px wide, stands as tall as it too, from under the Teams button; on a narrower one it keeps its height at the bottom, so the canvas keeps room. The model's button under the message box is as wide as its name (docs).
  • Models: while KOLONİ's browser tab is in the background, the page no longer asks every 15 seconds whether the model server answers; it asks once as you come back to the tab.
  • CLIs: GitHub Copilot CLI run Native, on a version whose code was read or measured (1.0.67 and 1.0.105 so far, by the version Copilot reports; after an update of Copilot's, not until that version is measured), works in the agents' scratch folder: a command that starts in a new shell of its own (one that names no shell) is judged in the project folder, so cd .koloni/tmp/...; python a.py runs without a card at Full auto; a delete inside .koloni/tmp/ is still asked there, and on any other version, in a shell it named, or after one that did, the cd is still asked too (docs).
  • Chat, Canvas, Models, Agents, To-do, Memory, Triggers, Usage: nothing you see or do changes. More of the page's code - the chat's messages and message box, rooms, the canvas and its lines, the Models and Usage pages, roles and recipes, To-do, Memory, Knowledge, triggers and the approval cards - was split into smaller parts, each checked to behave exactly as before, so later fixes there are safer.
  • Canvas: in a turn with no team, the members of a discussion or room standing under it in one column join it by one line round the right side of the column, into its right side with an arrow, instead of lines that doubled back behind the cards; an agent waiting for a file held by another in its column is joined the same way. Members' lines have a colour of their own, picking a room lights its members as picking a discussion does, and dots no line uses are no longer drawn (docs).
  • Canvas: the Lead is called the Orchestrator everywhere the canvas names it - on a discussion's or room's card, in their windows, in the side panel, the box of what was said, notes, memory rows, what an agent waits for and the timeline - and a team's lead is its coordinator, as its own box says, on discussion and room cards, in the side panel's discussion, room and wait notes, in what an agent waits for and in the timeline. While a discussion runs, its opener says "Waiting for the discussion" and a member opened for it "Waiting for its turn to speak". A room's card shows its goal, no longer who opened it; discussion and room cards stand in the order they began; words a card cuts show in full on hover; the legend has a row for every line drawn, also in a turn with no team; and a sub-agent you declined says "Rejected", no longer "Not started" (docs).
  • Agents: a speaker in a discussion is told that a speech is at most 1500 characters and that a longer one is cut there (docs).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Ready, Chat: a sub-agent's work kept in its working copy for you to take in (it stopped at its step limit, or its turn broke off) now waits for you everywhere, as it did in its own chat: on the Ready page while that chat is not open, as a mark on the chat in the Chats list, and in a note in the corner (docs).
  • Chat, CLIs: the Orchestrator is now told never to ask you a question in its answer and carry on in the same turn as if you had answered, nor to tell another agent you approved or chose what you did not say: it decides and says what it decided, or, where the decision is yours, asks on a card and waits. It is not told to ask more often. When Codex tries its own way to ask you, KOLONİ declines it and tells Codex to ask on KOLONİ's card, or, where that card cannot be put to you, to decide; run as a session, that no longer counts towards the refusals that stop it (asking that way three times in a row, with none of KOLONİ's tools between, still stops it).
  • Chat, Ready: a question now says who asks - "Orchestrator asks", "Coder asks" - on its card, on the Ready page (no longer "Lead asks"; KOLONİ's own card about an agent, such as its step limit or its work waiting for Take in, says "for Coder") and in the note in the corner ("Orchestrator asks you", no longer "waits for you"; KOLONİ's own card about an agent, such as its step limit, still "waits for you"); a question KOLONİ did not put to you reads "Wanted to ask: … · not asked", with why when you open it (docs).
  • Canvas, Chat, CLIs: a KOLONİ tool call that a CLI agent stopped waiting for - a command, a wait for another team, a message to another agent, a web request - no longer shows as running after the turn: it ends as interrupted, as when you press Stop, also when the CLI cancels it in the middle of its turn (the agent then shows as at work again, not waiting). What it started is stopped as by Stop; a server you let keep running keeps running. After a restart, such a call left running by an earlier turn is closed too. A discussion broken by an error now shows Failed, not Stopped.
  • Models: a model server of your own that has stopped now shows as not answering also when you wrote its model name yourself; before, once its model had answered, KOLONİ kept saying it answered. On Windows the check of a stopped server on this machine takes about a second instead of about 2.
  • CLIs: Qoder's Native way of running now says what was measured, on the Models page and in its agent's window: the Qoder versions tried so far do not apply KOLONİ's hook, so a native turn stops before Qoder does anything and says to run it as a session. It used to say that Qoder asks before every tool, not yet measured, and that one tool could run before the run stopped (docs).
  • Chat: on the card that asks which candidate's work goes on, a candidate that stopped before its end is said to have "stopped before its end", no longer that "nobody is watching this turn".
  • Canvas: lines that were missing, crooked or pointing the wrong way are fixed: talk between the Orchestrator and a sub-agent it opened has a 💬 you can click; your message's line down to its Plan is short and straight; a folded box of five or more files keeps its lines; findings handed out of a team's frame get their line; the Orchestrator's lines go straight into the teams' doors; a member's line to a discussion between teams lands on its dot, leaves a folded frame by its side and no longer runs through an approved plan; arrows inside a team's frame point at the right end; and in a compare turn the second Everyone card stands beside its own Orchestrator.
  • Canvas: a paused room no longer looks busy: its card loses its "at work" ring, the lines of the members it holds stop moving (one still finishing its step keeps its moving line), and such a member says "Paused with the room" (docs).
  • Workspace: a 3D model you have not turned yet stays seen whole when its window grows, shrinks or is still taking its size as it opens; before, it kept the view framed for the window's first size.

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Chat: a PDF attached to a chat is read with pypdf 6.21.4, which fixes known flaws in reading crafted PDF files.
  • Canvas: a chart in a PowerPoint file shown in the Office view is drawn with Apache ECharts 6.1, which fixes a cross-site scripting flaw; the page's build and test tools (Vite, and undici under jsdom) are updated past their known flaws too.

items.title: Changed
items.text: • Canvas, Chat, Agents, Models, Settings: nothing you see or do changes. The page's code that draws the canvas, follows the chat's events, summarises tools, rooms, commands and triggers, reads pasted text and attachments, and shows the cards, the Models, Agents, To-do, Board, Triggers and Settings pages was split into smaller parts, each checked to behave exactly as before, so later fixes there are safer.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Canvas, Chat: a discussion whose Orchestrator gave up waiting for it (a CLI that stops a tool call it has waited on too long), or that broke off with an error, no longer shows as running for good: it ends as Stopped (one given up on also has its call shown as interrupted, as when you press Stop).

items.title: Changed
items.text: • Agents, Settings, Models: nothing you see or do changes. The code behind an agent's turn, taking work in, teams' recipes, rooms, discussions, the Orchestrator's answers in your place, and the chat, project and provider settings was split into smaller parts, each checked to behave exactly as before, so later fixes there are safer.

items.title: Added
items.text: • Install: KOLONİ copies its database at its first start of a day to runtime/data/backups/ and keeps the last three, beside the copies it makes before an update changes the database (docs).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Chat: the Orchestrator no longer stops at a fixed count of steps; it stops when its work is done, when it goes round in circles (it is told once to try another way; then a card asks you Go on or Stop here, tells you on the desktop and at the project's notification address, and ends the turn with its work kept if nobody answers in 10 minutes), or at a limit you set on the Lead role or a trigger. Steps an agent may take now holds sub-agents (docs).
  • To-do, Triggers: in a run nobody watches, an Orchestrator going round in circles ends with the reason on record, and a night or the To-do run goes on with the next job or task; such a turn ends once nothing has moved for Stuck after this many minutes with no progress (Settings › The app, 30 unless you change it), and a To-do task's turn or a night's job after An unattended turn runs at most (hours) (8; empty: no limit) - a night's job no longer stops at 60 minutes (docs).
  • Canvas: where the default provider isn't answering and the Models page holds another one that is switched on, First steps offers Use … for new chats, which makes that one the default; the step is done once the default answers (docs).
  • To-do, Tools, Knowledge: an empty list of tasks, skills or knowledge says what one is and where on the page to add the first; a page that needs a folder, in a chat with none, has a Choose a folder button.
  • Knowledge: in a project whose Project notes are first made from this version on, the Orchestrator uses them from the first note you add (it is told where their guide is and can look them up) until you switch them off on the Lead role's Knowledge tab; other roles have them only if you switch them on. A project that already has Project notes is not changed: switch them on once on the Agents page, the Lead role, Knowledge tab. An Orchestrator with any knowledge on Map is now told where its guide is, as a sub-agent is (docs).
  • CLIs: when the context of an Orchestrator on a CLI fills during a turn in a chat you are in and the CLI's own error says so (GitHub Copilot CLI's wordings: one seen in a live refusal, the others taken from its package; Claude Code's and Qoder's are not recognised yet), KOLONİ summarises its earlier work and starts the turn again from the summary by itself, once, with a line in the chat saying so; if it fills again, the turn fails and says what to do. Where nothing of its earlier work is left to summarise (a single message larger than its model takes), nothing is started again and the failure says so. Where it had opened sub-agents, a room or a team's recipe, the turn is not started again: its earlier work is summarised after it, and your next message goes on from the summary. A CLI lead with no context window on its role can also be summarised after a turn against the catalogue's window for its model, which only a very long chat reaches (docs).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Chat: an agent's work inside its scratch folder, .koloni/tmp/, no longer raises a card at every permission level: a command run in a folder there (or one that starts with a plain cd .koloni/tmp/...) is judged as any other, and deleting a folder of the scratch (rm -rf .koloni/tmp/out, Remove-Item -Recurse) runs unasked at Full auto as deleting a file there does. A line that then leaves the scratch, looks up where it is, runs git there or deletes through a link is still asked; so are a cd into the scratch by a CLI that does not say where its commands run and may keep the folder (Qoder run Native, Claude Code's PowerShell and Monitor tools and its own sub-agents, GitHub Copilot CLI, agy; docs), and deleting the browser's own folder there (.koloni/tmp/browser).
  • Ready: a team whose coordinator KOLONİ stopped while one of its agents was still at work keeps running until that agent is back, and its work is offered at Ready for you; Ready for you is also asked before the Orchestrator ends its turn where nobody asked it earlier.
  • Models: with a model server that is not running, KOLONİ's check of it takes about half as long (on Windows about 2 seconds instead of 4): a server that takes no connection is asked once, not twice.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Chat: talk to the Orchestrator in a folder of yours, or in no folder for a plain chat; messages sent while agents work wait their turn (docs).
  • Chat: the Chats list, a Board with every chat in columns, and a chat started From a GitHub issue… with the issue attached, read with your own gh (docs).
  • Chat: other folders can join a chat, each read only or read & write (docs).
  • Chat: three permission levels, Ask before changes, Auto-edit files and Full auto, with "Always run" rules you can see and remove (docs).
  • Chat: Plan first gives each new message a plan to approve before anything changes (docs).
  • Chat: Undo these changes and Restore to before this message, each showing first what goes back.
  • Chat: Stop and Stop everything stop the work and keep what was half done, to take in or discard; Stop everything also holds triggers, To-do and work while you're away until Resume.
  • Chat: under the Orchestrator's last answer of a turn that changed files, KOLONİ says from its own records where the work is: in the project, waiting in Ready for you, or nowhere (docs).
  • Chat: work that was open when KOLONİ stopped is marked interrupted, and nothing is run again by itself (docs).
  • Chat: while you're away, the Orchestrator plans jobs on a card; each runs in its own copy after your Start, and you decide what comes in when you are back (docs).
  • Chat: work while you're away has a stop time and a spend limit only if you set them; the project's monthly budget still holds.
  • Chat: Compare sends one message to two models side by side, and you keep the work of one (docs).
  • Chat: attach files, screenshots and videos (sent as frames), and save attachments into the project (docs).
  • Chat: a long context is summarised past Summarise a long context at (%), for API models and most CLI modes; the context button shows how full it is, with Compact now (docs).
  • Chat: slash commands of your own, a command palette on Ctrl+K, and an agent's dev server shown as a preview, on this machine only (docs).
  • Chat: dictation and answers read aloud (docs).
  • Canvas: each turn is drawn from its record: every agent a box, with lines for work handed on, talk, findings and waiting; a legend explains every line and sign (docs).
  • Canvas: teams in frames, rooms and discussions between teams in a lane of their own, and a step's earlier rounds folded into one line each.
  • Canvas: click an agent for its report, waiting approvals, changes and tokens; Open window shows what it did step by step, with Details below.
  • Agents: ready roles (Orchestrator, Planner, Coder, Reviewer, Tester, Product owner and more) and your own, each with its tools and skills (docs).
  • Agents: three ready roles for a website, in the Web app team: SEO specialist, Copywriter and Accessibility reviewer (docs).
  • Agents: a role's Model cards: which model, how hard it thinks (Auto lets the agent that opens it choose), and how much it reads.
  • Agents: teams with steps, picked per chat; a team can wait for another one (docs).
  • Agents: recipes with steps, loops, branches and conditions, drawn, copied or described in a sentence; the ready ones include Feature, Bugfix, Review only and Evolve (docs).
  • Agents: candidates: one job given to 2 to 5 agents, each scored by your measure command; a card lists the scores and you pick, and at Full auto the best goes on by itself (docs).
  • Agents: rooms: two to six agents on one goal at once, with a budget, Pause, Resume and End (docs).
  • Agents: a room an agent opens gets at least 60,000 tokens, so a small budget no longer ends it before anyone posts. Change the number under Tokens, at least in Settings › This project › New chats start with; the most still wins. Existing projects and chats get 60,000 too (docs).
  • Agents: discussions: agents talk one question through in rounds, and you can join in (docs).
  • Agents: reviewers end with findings that go to the role they name; the Observer, when on, says what each sub-agent's record shows (docs).
  • Agents: tell an agent something while it works; at its step limit a card offers Continue (+25 steps) or Stop here, and Steps an agent may take sets the limit (docs).
  • Agents: when you are away, the Orchestrator answers the safe questions, if you switch it on (Settings › This project › Asking and away), and shows them under Decided for you (docs).
  • Models: an OpenAI-compatible server with tool calls, such as llama.cpp's llama-server or a hosted API, the Anthropic API, and CLIs, side by side; each agent shows the provider and model it really ran on (docs).
  • Models: start, stop and restart your llama.cpp server from KOLONİ, with its output and NVIDIA GPU memory and load (docs).
  • Models: tiers (fast, balanced, strongest) tried in your order, so a role or a job can ask for a tier; Agents may use keeps a model to your own picks (docs).
  • Models: limits per provider, in dollars per day or month or as a plan, and stepping down a tier when a plan runs low (docs).
  • CLIs: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Qoder and agy on your own plans, signed in by you in your own terminal (docs).
  • CLIs: under How it runs, a CLI runs with KOLONİ's tools and cards (One session per agent, now Codex too, or One run per model step), agy Reads with its own tools, or Native with its own tools: Claude Code, Qoder and agy ask KOLONİ before every tool, Codex before commands and patches, Copilot before commands, writes and reads (docs).
  • CLIs: a Codex provider added from now on runs as One session per agent (recommended), but as One run per model step on a model server of your own, where its session is not yet measured; one saved before keeps its way of running (docs).
  • CLIs: several Claude Code or Codex accounts side by side, each with its own sign-in for KOLONİ (docs).
  • CLIs: Copilot's thinking levels Off to Max, its auto model, and its tokens and AI credits in each agent's record (docs).
  • CLIs: agy is added switched off, and its card warns that Google's terms forbid using it through another app (docs).
  • CLIs: while a Qoder free model waits in its queue, the agent says so (docs).
  • Workspace: agents work in their own working copies; Take in brings the work into your folder and Discard drops it; Run the test tries the project's test on the copy first, and at Auto-edit and Full auto work comes in by itself only when that test passed (docs).
  • Workspace: Changes groups every change by what it needs from you, with Approve, Reject and Revert (docs).
  • Workspace: a team's work can get a git branch, merged or sent as a pull request from its card; an agent told to go on goes on in its own branch (docs).
  • Workspace: Where the work is shows your branch, the agents' copies and other branches; KOLONİ commits when you ask (docs).
  • Ready: everything that waits for you in Ready for you: Needs your answer, Ready to take in and Told you (docs).
  • Ready: every card has a title, one sentence, the same verbs (Take in, Reject, Approve, Discard) and folded Details.
  • To-do: a project's tasks in your order, each run in a chat of its own, by hand or one after another with Run the backlog; you decide when a task is done (docs).
  • To-do: Write it with the Product owner turns a rough note into draft tasks, saved only when you add them.
  • To-do: after a turn that did something, the Assistant PO suggests at most three follow-up tasks to Add, Edit or Reject; a task added for you never runs without your OK (docs).
  • Triggers: start work by the clock, when files change, or from a webhook, each with its own permissions and budget (docs).
  • Triggers: a trigger is not saved on a chat whose Orchestrator would run on a CLI working with its own tools, and the form says why (docs).
  • Memory: facts that rest on lines of files and are checked again each time, proposals you approve, your preferences, and search by meaning (docs).
  • Knowledge: experts that learn a source, such as docs or the project's code, and that agents ask; learning again reads only what changed (docs).
  • Knowledge: a role is Full in one knowledge of a project; choosing another turns the first to Map, and an expert asked about a topic it does not use looks in all its knowledge instead (docs).
  • Knowledge: a public GitHub repository: cloned outside the project with nothing of it run, its code mapped for free, and guides written from its docs and from how its code works; Learn more goes on with more code files (docs).
  • Knowledge: a folder on this machine, git or not, learned as a repository is: read in place with nothing written into it or run in it, added only by you; the most files and MB a repository or a folder may hold are yours to set in Settings (docs).
  • Knowledge: Add KOLONİ’s own guide makes this guide a knowledge your roles can be given (docs).
  • Knowledge: after a turn, Add to Project notes? keeps fixed findings and docs changes in a Project notes knowledge (docs).
  • Tools: built-in tools by group (files, commands, web, a browser on the sites you allow, team, To-do, memory), given to each role on its Tools tab; five can be switched off for every agent (docs).
  • Tools: MCP servers; What does it do? looks inside an npx or uvx package before you add it (docs).
  • Tools: skills from a folder or GitHub, given to roles, with a record of how each did (docs).
  • Usage: tokens and known cost by turn, day and month, and a monthly budget per project (docs).
  • Usage: plan meters for Claude Code, Codex, agy and Copilot, from what each CLI last reported (docs).
  • Settings: one place in three levels, This chat, This project and The app, with a short sheet for the chat under the message box (docs).
  • Settings: a folder's rules and run settings live in the folder and go into git; settings from another machine are asked about before they are used (Use them / Not now) (docs).
  • Settings: Export everything and Restore from a file… (docs).
  • Settings: notifications to a webhook (Slack, Discord, ntfy), a desktop notification on Windows only, and a daily summary (docs).
  • Settings: Delete project… removes KOLONİ's record of a project, never its folder (docs).
  • Install: Python 3.12 to 3.14 on Windows (tested daily) and Linux (automatic tests, less daily use); macOS not tested yet; a Docker image, the newest and least tested (docs).
  • Install: the update scripts back up the database, update, and rebuild the guide where Zensical is installed (docs).
  • Install: licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later (docs), with a commercial license for those who cannot meet its terms (docs).
  • Docs: a user guide in English, published on GitHub Pages and, after one build with the optional Zensical package, served by KOLONİ itself at /guide/, offline and matching the version you run; hints link to it with Learn more → (docs).
  • Docs: pictures of the main screens, short videos, diagrams, and pages for KOLONİ in 5 minutes, Which way to work, troubleshooting and known limits (docs).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Install: KOLONİ listens on 127.0.0.1 only and sends no telemetry; every request to its API needs the page key, so a plain or injected command an agent runs cannot approve its own cards (docs).
  • Install: exports and backups are downloaded without the page key in their address, so it stays out of your browser's history.
  • Settings: an export without keys also leaves out secret files you attached to a chat (a .env, a key file); the chat keeps their name (docs).
  • Install: a link with a wrong key, from a web page or an agent's answer, no longer locks the page out: the page keeps its key unless KOLONİ accepts the new one, and links in agents' answers and diagrams open in a new tab.
  • Ready: reading secret files, writing most files that steer agents, and commands that delete or send data off the machine stop at a card at every level, with a few exceptions for CLIs run with their own tools (limits); at Full auto these checks are for honest commands, not a wall (docs).
  • Ready: a command an agent runs is judged together with the folder it runs in, so a relative path inside .claude or another protected folder stops at a card as if it were named; Claude Code and Qoder don't say where their shell stands, so their commands are judged at the project root (a cd into a protected folder is itself a card).
  • Ready: KOLONİ's own cards have fixed titles and say KOLONİ asks; an agent's question says The agent asks, so it cannot pass for one of KOLONİ's.
  • Workspace: sub-agents work in working copies, not in your folder, until you take their work in.
  • Agents: your home folder and a drive's root cannot be a project, and KOLONİ's own folder is never opened, even inside a project; a CLI's own Grep and Glob cannot search it either (docs).
  • Agents: web pages, search results, MCP results, knowledge, a GitHub issue and a learned repository's code reach agents framed as data, not instructions; the frame tells the model, it is not a wall; text that tries to give orders shows a Text tried to give orders card (docs).
  • Settings: secret files open only on your Allow once and searches skip them (at Full auto a command that doesn't name the file can still read it); keys in command output show as ***; variables with secret names are kept from commands and CLIs unless you name them (docs).
  • Settings: a planted test key stops a command, web request, browser or MCP call that would send it out.
  • Chat: an agent asks for a key on a Give a secret to its commands? card; the value never reaches the model or the record, and never leaves on a branch (docs).
  • Triggers: turns nobody watches may do only what the trigger allows, and never start a CLI that works with its own tools (docs).
  • Tools: commands can run in a fresh Docker container, with the network off unless you allow it (docs).
  • Tools: MCP servers get only their own variables and what programs need to run, none of KOLONİ's or a CLI's sign-in; one you have not trusted asks before every call (docs).
  • Tools: web searches and requests reach only public addresses; the agents' browser opens only previews and the sites you allow.
  • CLIs: on Windows, a CLI and everything it starts run in a Windows job that is ended on Stop or when KOLONİ closes.
  • Docs: the guide at /guide/ loads its scripts, styles, fonts and pictures only from KOLONİ itself.
  • Docs: report a security problem privately through GitHub's Security tab (docs).

items.title: Sources to look things up in
items.text: Knowledge is "what agents can look things up in": documentation, files or a topic that KOLONİ reads once and turns into a short guide. A role uses a knowledge only if you give it to the role. Since 0.1.10 it is the second part of the Memory page: open Memory on the left rail and press its second tab, Sources to look things up in (Ctrl+K: Knowledge). The tab says how many sources may be old ("2 may be old"). Its first part, What the project knows, is the project's rules, facts and notes.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: The sources part
items.text:
Each knowledge is a card, the cards side by side in a grid. A card's head has a small hexagon, a cell, for how it stands, its topic and its first source. Under them it says when it was last read (Fresh:), how much it spent (Spent:) and which model it learns with (Learns with:); then Used by:, a tick for each role that uses it; then Try it and Learn (later Learn more or Learn again), with what learning may cost beside it.

Cell What it means Green, filled Learned (for this project's code, scanned), and KOLONİ knows of no change since. That is all it says: KOLONİ looks at a project's files again each time, at a site or a topic only once a week and only with Learn again weekly on, and at a repository, a folder on this machine or this project's code not at all until you learn or scan again. Honey, filled Learning (or, for this project's code, scanning). Red-orange, filled May be old - its sources changed since it learned, a file it read changed or went, or its guide is a week old and Learn again weekly is on (Fresh: old, the reason on hover) - or its last learning failed. Empty Not learned yet.

The cell's word is its name for a screen reader, and Fresh: says it too: never its colour alone.

Memory's sources, with this project's code and KOLONİ's own guide offered as cards of their own.

Click the topic to open the card: it goes across the row. Its tabs are Guide, Pages, Not known yet, Settings and Copy. Try it opens across the row too.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: Adding knowledge
items.text:
Press + Add knowledge. Pick what it is:

Kind What it reads A docs site A web address. Only the pages under the path you give are read. Files here A folder or a file in this project. A repository A public GitHub repository's address: its code and its docs (below). A folder on this machine A folder outside this project, by its full path, read as a repository is (below). Research a topic A topic to research on the web.

Then:

  • Topic: its name, at most 40 characters. "How agents and the canvas name it."
  • The sources, one a line, at most 10.
  • Learn again weekly (web sources only).
  • Agents may search the web when it has no answer.
  • At most this much a learning (USD): 0.5 unless you change it. It holds only where the model's price is known. On a CLI or a plan the price is not known, so the caps below are what bound a learning.
  • Learn with: the model that writes the guide. By default, the model of a role that uses it. If no role uses it and you pick no model, learning stops and says to choose one.
  • Under More: At most this many pages (a safety cap), 500 unless you change it. For a repository or a folder on this machine, also At most this many code files a learning, 100 unless you change it; 0 writes no guide to its code.

Press Add and learn, or Add without learning to learn later.

What a learning spends counts toward the project's monthly budget (Usage shows it as "KOLONİ itself"). Over that budget, Learn asks first, as a new message does: "Over this month's budget. Learn anyway?" Press Go on anyway or Cancel.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: What learning does
items.text:
KOLONİ reads every page under the sources, up to the page cap, and keeps their text in the project's .koloni/knowledge/ folder. A model then writes a guide: what the subject offers, ready functions, short examples and pitfalls, each marked as official, from a single source, or unsure.

The pages read are other people's documents, so KOLONİ keeps them out of the project's git. The guide itself is kept in the folder.

Web pages are read only from public addresses, following the site's robots.txt, and never from another site the page redirects to. Reading stops after 10 minutes.

Learning again reads only what changed. If nothing changed, no model is asked.

This project's code is offered as a dashed card until you add it. "Free: KOLONİ reads the files here, no model." Press Scan the code: it becomes a card like the others.

Try it asks a question as an agent would, and shows the answer.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: A repository
items.text:
A repository is learned from three things:

  • Its docs: its README and its other Markdown files, read for a guide as any source's pages are.
  • How the code works: a second part of the guide, written by the model from its code files, the most central first: where a program starts (main, cli, app, index, __init__…), then the files most imported by others. Tests, vendored code and examples are left out. It says what the project does, its main flow, its modules, its key types and functions, and where to start reading.
  • A code map, free: KOLONİ scans its Python, JavaScript and TypeScript files with no model, so agents can ask where a name is defined and who calls it, as for This project's code. The code guide is written from these files too.

On Learn, KOLONİ clones the repository into a temporary folder outside your project, and deletes that folder once it has read it. Only its last commit on its default branch is fetched, over https only, with no tags, submodules or Git LFS files. Nothing of it is run: no hooks, filters or settings of the repository's, and none of your own git settings or credentials. Its files are counted before they are written out: a repository of more than 50,000 files or 300 MB is refused, and so is a clone where less than 2 GB is free (more, for a higher size limit). Both limits are yours to change for every project, in Settings › The app › Agents (under More limits): Knowledge reads at most (files), from 100 to 1,000,000, and (MB), from 1 to 10,240. A learning keeps the limits it started with. Cloning and reading together stop after 10 minutes.

What stays in your project is text, in the knowledge's folder .koloni/knowledge/<topic>/: its guide, its pages, and its code under code/: the code map, and each code file the map read as code/files/<path>.md, line for line. Test runners and builds look for code files, not .md ones, so they do not pick these up unless set to read Markdown. Files under hidden folders (.github/, .claude/ and the like) are not kept. The code map reads at most 4 MB a file and 64 MB in all. Agents read the code there with read_file, at the file and line Recall names; what they read there is marked as data, not instructions.

What the knowledge keeps is kept out of git, Take in, search and the list of changes. A working copy links to it rather than copying it, so an agent there reads it too.

Each Learn clones the repository again and reads its docs, the code files already in the guide, and then the next ones, up to the code-file cap. Learning stops at that cap, the page cap, the reading time or the money limit, whichever comes first. The card shows N of M code files in the guide, what stopped it, and Learn more while some are left. With nothing new and nothing changed, a Learn asks no model.

Removing a repository's knowledge deletes its code and pages from the folder; its guide stays. So does making it another kind of source. A knowledge cannot be changed while it learns.

Only GitHub repositories, https://github.com/<owner>/<name>, can be added for now.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: A folder on this machine
items.text:
A folder that is not on GitHub, with git or without, is learned as a repository is: its docs, how its code works and a free code map, the same caps and Learn more. Give its full path, as folder: C:\work\mylib. It is its knowledge's only source.

On Learn, KOLONİ first counts the folder where it is, against the same limits as a repository (50,000 files and 300 MB unless you change them in Settings); over one, the learning stops and keeps nothing new. The count goes into no link or junction, no hidden folder (.git, .github, .vscode…) and no dependency, build or cache folder, in any case (node_modules, .venv, venv, __pycache__, build, dist, target, .next, .tox, htmlcov and the test and type-check caches). Files that are in the cloud alone (OneDrive's, not on this disk) are skipped, not downloaded. Then only the files it counted are read: one added after the count waits for the next Learn.

Nothing is copied into your project but the same text a repository leaves, and nothing is ever written into the folder. Nothing in it is run, not even git: its .git folder is not read.

Only you add one, on Memory's sources part: an agent cannot add or change a folder source, and its expert never learns it by itself. A path is refused if it is not a full path, not a folder, a link or a junction, a drive's root, your home folder or a folder holding it, a hidden folder of your home (.ssh, .claude, .config…), its AppData (on a Mac, its Library), a folder named as secrets are (.ssh), this copy of KOLONİ's folder or its runtime/, another KOLONİ's runtime or checkout (one with data/koloni.db), or this project or a folder in it or around it (use This project's code, or Files here, for those). It is checked again at each Learn.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: KOLONİ's own guide
items.text:
Add KOLONİ's own guide, on a dashed card of its own until you press it, adds this guide as a knowledge called KOLONİ guide. Its source is koloni-guide:. KOLONİ reads only the Markdown pages of its own docs/ folder and keeps them in the project, as for any source. Its code, its .env and runtime/ are never read, and agents read only the kept pages, never KOLONİ's folder.

Adding it learns nothing, because learning costs model calls. Press Learn on its card when you want it; the cost stands beside the button, as for any knowledge. An expert in it never learns it by itself. Give it to a role, and a chat can then ask "what does Summarise a long context at do?" and be answered from the guide.

To remove a knowledge, use the link on its Settings tab. "Its guide stays in the folder." A repository's kept code and pages are deleted.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: Giving knowledge to a role
items.text:
On the Agents page, open a role and its Knowledge tab. Switch a knowledge on, then choose:

  • Map: "its guide, read when its work touches it". Any role can use Map.
  • Full: "its whole guide at each step". Only for your own roles that only read. A role is Full in one knowledge of a project: choosing Full for another of the same project turns the first one to Map. A knowledge of another project, or of every project, stays as it is; where a role is Full in both the project's own and one of every project, the project's own is what it is an expert in.
