If the role's description is still the one Create expert wrote, it then names the new topic; its name stays. Copying a knowledge to a project where the role is already Full gives it Map.

A role with knowledge can look things up in it while it works.

The same is on the knowledge's card, under Used by:: untick a role and it no longer uses the knowledge; choose another role in + Role… and press Give to give it the knowledge, as Map. A role that is Full in it (an expert) has its tick marked "full" and greyed: change that on the role's Knowledge tab. A refusal is said on the card.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: How agents look things up
items.text: An agent has one tool to look things up: Recall. It looks in the project's memory and earlier messages, and - for a role that uses knowledge here - in that knowledge's pages too: the parts that hold most of the question's words, each under its topic, page and line, as data. A role whose agent may not read the memory (KOLONİ's own Reviewer) looks in its knowledge's pages alone. Until 0.1.10 the pages had a tool of their own, lookup: a role, a prompt or a guide that still names it keeps working for one release, as it did.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: Experts
items.text:
An expert is a role that knows one topic and only advises. To make one: Agents → New role → An expert. Fill in Knows (the topic) and its sources, and press Create expert. "It reads its sources once, writes a short guide in the project, and answers from it: it advises and reads only."

The role is named "topic expert". An expert changes nothing: it reads, and answers from its guide. The Orchestrator, or a team's lead, opens it when a job needs it.

When its guide has no answer, an expert with Agents may search the web when it has no answer on may search the web. Below Full auto, an expert's search always asks you first. Without that option, it asks you whether to search. After it finds something on the web, a card asks whether to add it to the guide (Add / Not now); it is added the next time the knowledge learns.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: Project notes
items.text:
Since 0.1.10 the Project notes are part of the project's Memory: the lines you keep from the Add to Project notes? card, under the project's rules, given to the Orchestrator every turn. They are no longer a knowledge, and this page no longer lists them; the folder .koloni/knowledge/project-notes/ an earlier version wrote is left as it was.

Knowledge is not the project's Memory.
path: Sources to look things up in

items.title: Memory
items.text:
Memory is what a project remembers between chats: your preferences, the project's rules and its Project notes, facts you approved, and notes agents wrote while they worked. Open it with Memory on the left rail. Each project has its own memory.

The Memory page has two parts, as two tabs near its top: What the project knows - this page - and Sources to look things up in, the documents, files and repositories agents read (Sources to look things up in; until 0.1.10 the Knowledge page). Each tab says what waits in it: "1 waits for your word" (a fact an agent put forward), "2 may be old" (a source whose guide may be out of date).

Memory is one of the two places KOLONİ keeps notes. The other is a job's notebook: what a To-do story's or task's turns, or a night's job, note for the turns after them, for as long as the job runs. Memory is what stays true of the project.

KOLONİ never shows a memory as surer than it is. A fact rests on lines of a file, and KOLONİ checks those lines again each time it reads the fact.

From a note to an approved fact, and how agents get it.

items.title: The page
items.text:
What the project knows: what waits for your word on top, what agents were told at the left, your own words at the right.

From the top:

  • The search: "Search everything this project remembers" (Searching memory).
  • Three ways memory reaches an agent, one line each: Given at the start, Found when asked and Sources given to a role (below).
  • The two parts' tabs, each with what waits in it.
  • What waits for your word: a honey box, only while an agent's proposal waits for you (Who writes what).
  • At the left, Facts (the core) and Notes (the journal), and under them History, folded.
  • At the right, Your words: your preferences, this project's rules and its Project notes, set apart from what agents wrote. Only you write them. Under them, which other projects' memory Search deeper and Recall also look in, with Change (Settings › This project › Memory and web).

items.title: The cells
items.text:
Each fact has a small hexagon, a cell, that says how it stands for agents. A word always says it too: its name for a screen reader, the line above the facts and the words under the fact. A cell never says a fact is right.

Cell What it means Green, filled Given when the work names its subject. Red-orange, filled Given to no agent until you look again: its source changed or moved. One with no subject, or one too general to match, says "its source changed: look again - only found by looking it up": looking again does not make it given. Empty Only found by looking it up: it has no subject, or one too general to match.

Ten smaller cells beside Facts fill in honey as facts take the core's room, with the count beside them ("1 240 / 4 000 characters").

items.title: The kinds of memory
items.text:
Kind Who writes it Where you see it Your preferences You - and the Orchestrator, from your own words (how). One text, used in every project. Your words, at the right This project's rules You. Kept in the folder's .koloni/rules.md, so they go into git with the project. Your words Project notes You, ticking lines on the Add to Project notes? card at the end of a turn. Your words, under the rules Facts (the core) You, or an agent's proposal that you approved. Facts, at the left Notes (the journal) Agents, while they work, and KOLONİ's own note-taker if you switch it on. Notes, under the facts

A fact has a subject (a few words, such as test command) and usually a source: a file and a range of lines. The core holds at most 4 000 characters of facts; Facts shows how much is used.

The rules you save here are also written to the folder's .koloni/rules.md. When that file says something else (a git pull or a script changed it), Your words say so - "The folder's rules.md differs from what you saved here; Full auto's check goes by what you saved." - and shows the folder's text, with Use the folder's rules here to take it into the box. Full auto's Check what I said first reads the rules saved here.

KOLONİ may also suggest a preference: its summariser, from a finished message, and the Orchestrator, from your own words, where it does not add them at once (how). A suggestion shows under Your preferences with a "suggested" tag and the buttons Add and Reject. It is not kept until you press Add.

items.title: Project notes
items.text:
At the end of a turn, KOLONİ may ask Add to Project notes? It lists findings that were fixed and changes to the project's docs/, at most 8, in the words of the agent or the file. Tick the ones to keep and press Add, or Not now. The card never holds the turn: answer it whenever you like.

Each line you add goes into the Project notes box under This project's rules, in Your words, as - <line>. The Orchestrator is given them every turn, each line in quotes, as notes written from the agents' work: they are not your instructions. They are not written to .koloni/rules.md, and Full auto's check of your words does not read them. Correct a line or take it out in the box, then press Save Project notes. They hold at most 4 000 characters; past that, Add asks you to take some lines out first, and the card waits.

Before 0.1.10 the Project notes were a topic of Knowledge. At the upgrade their lines were copied here (Upgrade notes).

items.title: The three ways memory reaches an agent
items.text:
The strip at the top of the page says them, one line each:

  1. Given at the start: your preferences and rules, to every agent; the Project notes, to the Orchestrator; a fact, when the work names its subject.
  2. Your words are "Said to every agent, always": your preferences and the project's rules are put in every agent's briefing. The Orchestrator is also given the Project notes, every turn.
  3. Facts are "Given to an agent when its work names the subject." When every word of a fact's subject appears in the agent's task, the fact is given to it. The agent is also told how many other facts exist, so it can look them up. A fact whose subject is too general to match is only found by looking it up: its cell is empty.
  4. Found when asked: an agent's Recall tool ("look in memory") finds notes and facts, earlier messages and linked projects' memory. Notes are "Found only when an agent looks": they are never given by themselves.
  5. Sources given to a role: only a role you give a source looks in it - docs, repositories, folders (Sources to look things up in).

History, folded under the notes, shows decisions and what was removed.

While an agent works, KOLONİ keeps checking what it was given. If a fact it was given changes or is removed during its work, the agent is told.

In an agent's window, under Details › Every step as recorded, you can see what that agent got: Given from memory and Looked up in memory.

items.title: Sources and evidence
items.text:
Most facts and notes point to a file and its lines. KOLONİ keeps a fingerprint of those lines and compares it each time memory is read. Next to each one you see what it found:

What you see What it means source unchanged since noted The lines read exactly as they did when the record was written. source moved since noted: check again The same lines are now somewhere else in the file. source changed since noted: check again The lines are different now, or gone. no source The record does not point to a file.

"Source unchanged" only means the file lines read as they did. It does not mean the record is right.

A fact whose source changed or moved is given to no agent until you look at it again. Open it with Look again. You see the lines as they read now, and you can choose:

  • These are the same lines (only when they moved): the fact now points to the new place.
  • Correct: rewrite the fact.
  • Remove: take it out of the core.

Look at the sources again, beside Facts, checks every source again.

A record written in a turn nobody watched (a trigger's turn, before 0.1.10) is tagged "written with nobody watching".

items.title: Who writes what
items.text:
Agents write notes. An agent with the Remember tool ("note what it found") adds a note to the journal. A few rules apply:

  • A note about a file must name the lines, and the agent must have read those lines in this turn.
  • Text that reads like an instruction is refused.
  • A newer note on the same subject replaces the older one.

KOLONİ notes a flaky test. A test that failed in a full run and passed alone once is noted in the journal as KOLONİ's, under "flaky test: test", with how many times it was seen so (Not this turn's).

Agents propose facts; you approve them. An agent can put a note forward for the core. Nothing enters the core unless you approve it. Waiting proposals show at once in a honey box at the top of the part, headed such as "1 fact waits for your word"; the part's tab says so too. The box shows three; the rest wait behind Show N more, so that the facts and your words stay near the top. For each one you can choose Approve, Edit and approve (then Approve as edited) or Reject. If it would replace a fact on the same subject, you see both side by side: Would replace and Put forward. Once you decided the last one, the box says "Nothing waits for you." until you leave the page.

A proposal can be approved only while its source is unchanged, and not if the file was changed in the same turn the note was written. A note on a subject the core already has a fact on waits for you too; until you decide, no agent is given it and Recall does not find it.

You write facts yourself. Under the facts, ＋ Add a fact asks for the fact, its subject and, if you like, a file with its first and last line. Add to the core saves it. It replaces any fact on the same subject. A fact's ⋯ menu has Correct and Remove. A note has Make it a fact in sight, which opens Add a fact with its words and subject, and Remove in its ⋯ menu.

Your words on a card become a fact. When you ask for changes on a card and say why, that text is kept as a fact, shown as "said by you at a card, asking for changes".

This project's rules are yours alone. No agent writes them. Into your preferences the Orchestrator adds by itself only your own sentence, as below; a line a model worded enters only on your Add.

The Orchestrator keeps what you say about how you work. When you say how you want work done from now on - a rule, not a request for this one task ("from now on don't ask me for X", "write commits in Turkish", "never push without asking") - the Orchestrator can keep it for Your preferences. It is made only from your own words: the Orchestrator quotes your sentence of that turn, and KOLONİ checks the quote is in a sentence of your own prose - never a fenced, >-quoted, indented or backticked line (what you pasted: an agent's report, a file), an agent's words or a tool's. What then is your setting, New preferences from your words (Settings › The app › Agents):

  • Add them, tell me (the default): your own sentence - never the model's wording, which could turn it around - goes into Your preferences at once, and the chat says so: "Added to your preferences: "…"" with Undo, which takes exactly that line out again (and never an edit of yours made meanwhile). Only a plain rule is added so: a sentence in a message that asks nothing, says no to nothing, sets no condition and takes nothing back, that opens with no quotation mark and is under no heading ("The bot said:"), names no push, pull request or merge (those are your word each time) and reads as no request for this work ("please …", "now", a file's name). Anything else waits on the card below, your own sentence on it.
  • Ask me first: a card in the chat, Suggested by the Orchestrator, shows "The Orchestrator suggests, from your words "…":" and "Add this to your preferences: "…"?" with Add and Not now. Add keeps the line as shown; Not now writes nothing. The Memory page and Ready for you show the same suggestion.

Either way it is masked and cut at 300 characters, one that reads like orders to an agent is refused, a line you have or that waits already is not kept twice, and at most 3 are kept in a turn. A sub-agent cannot do it. Your words it came from are kept with it. A line of Your preferences never lets Full auto run a command without its card - it can only stop one (Check what I said first).

Automatic notes are off by default. Switch them on under Settings › This project › Memory and web › Note what the work found, by itself. After each message's work, a fast model writes at most three notes of what it found. That is one more model request after every message, on your plan or your bill. These notes go into the journal, signed as that model's. They never go into the core by themselves and never replace an agent's note or a fact.

items.title: Searching memory
items.text:
One search box sits at the top of the page: "Search everything this project remembers".

  • Typing filters what is on the page, grouped by where it is: Waiting for your word, In Your words, In Facts, In Notes and In History. Every word must match. A hit goes to its row, whatever the filters say, and unfolds History for one of its rows.
  • Search deeper (or Enter) runs the same search an agent's Recall does in memory (an agent's also looks in its role's sources). It looks in the project's memory, in earlier messages, and in the memory of linked projects. Results are grouped under "In earlier messages" and "In linked projects".

Search deeper finds the word in earlier messages, with who said it and when.

Earlier messages means your messages, the Orchestrator's last answers, sub-agents' reports and closed To-do tasks. Tool output is not searched.

You can also start a deep search from Ctrl+K with Search in messages.

Memory of other projects. Under Settings › This project › Memory and web › Also look in the memory of, tick other projects. Their records are found by Search deeper and Recall, but never given to an agent at its start.

items.title: Topics
items.text:
Memory is what a project keeps from one chat to the next. Inside a chat, what an agent remembers of the turns before is its topic: the turns that go on with one piece of work.

  • A chat's first message starts its first topic, named after the message's first line. Each message after it goes on with the topic you were last in. Rename a topic from Recent (top bar): the list names the topic on screen, with a pencil.
  • New topic, under the message box, makes your next message start a new one; press it again to go on instead. Its tooltip says which topic the next message goes on with. In the chat a line marks where the topic changes: "New topic: …", or "Continuing: …" back in one seen before.
  • A trigger's turns (triggers were removed in 0.1.10) are a topic of their own. A message you send while one of them is on screen still goes on with your own topic; Write into … instead sends it into the trigger's.

What each agent is given:

  • The Orchestrator is sent its own topic's turns - your messages and the Orchestrators' answers - and of the chat's other topics only their names (the last 20), with the words "what was said and done in them is not shown to you".
  • A sub-agent sees only its own work. Within a topic the Orchestrator can go on with an agent of an earlier turn - one it opened that finished by itself, or one stopped with its work kept on a branch of its own: an agent of the same name is opened again, and what the earlier ones did and said is its history. Never one of another topic.
  • Claude Code run Native with Sign-in: Its own for KOLONİ goes on in its own CLI session from the topic's previous turn: it is sent only what is new, and compacts the session itself. A new topic starts a new session, and so does a turn run with another model, folder, permission level or setup.
  • GitHub Copilot CLI run Native does the same: it goes on in its own session from the topic's previous turn, sent only what is new, and compacts the session itself, with a line on the agent's record when it does. Past a size, about 75,000 tokens by default, it is not gone on in, so that it stays below Copilot's dearer price step: the next turn starts anew from the history KOLONİ keeps. Its session is kept in a folder of its own under KOLONİ's runtime, removed when you start a new topic or go back to another one, when a turn starts a new session, and when its chat is deleted (Data and privacy). Where Copilot cannot go on in it, it starts a new session sent the whole topic, and its record says so once.
  • Codex run Native with Sign-in: Its own for KOLONİ does the same with its own thread, kept in its provider's sign-in folder (never your ~/.codex). Past about 124,500 tokens by default (75% of 166,000) it is not gone on in, so that KOLONİ's own summary comes before Codex's, which KOLONİ cannot read; when Codex compacted its thread itself, a line on the agent's record says so and the next turn starts anew too. On your own sign-in, the default, each Codex turn starts anew, as before. Going on in its thread is not yet tried with a real Codex (Codex).
  • On any other model the Orchestrator is sent the topic's history each turn, and KOLONİ summarises its older part past Summarise a long context at (%) of the window (75 by default; see Going on from the last turn).
  • A To-do story goes on in a topic of its own, so in one session; its next task starts a new topic of the story after a task of it ended badly, or a day later - told the story so far - never for a session's size. Every turn of the story is given its notebook, as data (A story's session). The other topics' names come with how a story's or a To-do task's stands: (done), (done?) or (stuck).

Who remembers what, by topic and by kind of model - and a To-do story in its own topic.

When to press New topic: when the next message is about other work. The Orchestrator then starts with a short history - cheaper, and nothing of the other work leads it astray - and Claude Code, Copilot or Codex with a new session. Keep going in the topic when the message builds on what was just done: the Orchestrator sees that work, and can go on with the agents that did it.

items.title: Sources to look things up in
items.text: The page's second part, its second tab, holds the knowledge: expert topics learned from web pages, project files, a repository or a folder. Roles use them while they work, and an agent's Recall looks in a role's own (Sources to look things up in). What the project knows is short facts and notes, each checked against its source; a source is longer material an expert reads.

items.title: History and Export
items.text:
History, folded under the notes with how many it holds beside it, says "Decisions and what was removed. Nothing is deleted."

  • Recent decisions lists the latest decisions, such as "Approved into the core", "Corrected", "Rejected" or "Removed".
  • Removed / replaced lists what was removed or replaced. Any of these can be brought back with Take back.

Correcting a fact keeps the old one as replaced. Removing or rejecting never deletes a record.

Export, beside Facts, downloads the core as MEMORY.md: each fact with its subject, who wrote it and when, and its source with its status now. Only facts are exported, not notes. The file is a copy to read; editing it does not change the memory.

To take everything KOLONİ keeps, memory included, use Export everything under Settings › The app › Your data. See Settings.

items.title: FAQ
items.text:
Why didn't an agent use a fact I approved? A fact is given only when the agent's task names every word of its subject, and only while its source is unchanged. Check the fact's cell and its line under Facts. The agent can still find it with Recall.

A fact says "source changed". Is it wrong now? Not necessarily. Its lines changed, so KOLONİ stopped giving it to agents until you look. Open Look again and correct, confirm or remove it.

Can an agent change the core without me? No. Agents write notes and proposals. Only your approval, or your own words, put a fact in the core.

How do I make agents always follow something? Write it in This project's rules (for this project) or Your preferences (for every project). Both are told to every agent.

Does memory leave my machine? Memory is given to the models your agents run on, as part of their work. Searching it sends nothing: it matches words on this machine.

Can I delete a memory for good? Not from the page. Removing hides it from agents and keeps it in History, where you can take it back.

items.title: Roadmap
items.text: What is planned after 0.1.0. Plans change; nothing here is promised.

items.title: Planned for 0.2.0
items.text:
• Go back to any step of a turn and run it again from there. KOLONİ keeps a hidden snapshot of each step.
  • Watch a pull request: its checks and reviews on the canvas as a Watch node, and an agent that fixes what fails.
  • Add a GitHub issue to the To-do (a chat can already start from one).
  • Pull requests outside GitHub, such as GitLab.
  • Who wrote this line: the agent and the turn behind each change.
  • Voice: your own speech server, hands-free spoken conversation, and a voice for each role.
  • Models that make images, audio and video, on the canvas and for roles.
  • Remote MCP servers (reached over HTTP, with sign-in).
  • Plugins that install a package's parts into KOLONİ.
  • Arranging agents on the canvas: tools to group and place them.
  • Screen control: only apps you pick, each action or session asked, never in a turn nobody watches. This needs a design first.

items.title: May come later
items.text:
• Versioned documentation, and a "What's new" note after an update.
  • New screenshots and videos in this guide.

items.title: Settings
items.text: The Settings page holds everything you set for one chat, for one project and for KOLONİ as a whole.

items.title: Opening Settings
items.text:
• Press Settings (the gear) at the bottom of the left rail. It opens on This project, or on The app for a chat with no folder. Press it again, or the close button, to close the page.
  • Or press Ctrl+K and choose Settings. Ctrl+K also lists each section by name (the app's with "(the app)" after it), and opens Settings right at it. A section's name before 0.1.10 finds it too: "Asking and away" finds When you're asked; one folded into another is listed by its old name after the one it is in now - How agents work › Slash commands - and opens it there, its More or rules shown.
  • Under the message box, Chat settings (Settings in a narrow chat) opens this chat's short sheet; its All settings opens Settings at This chat.

Choosing another page on the rail closes Settings. The chat under it stays as it was, so a message you were typing is kept.

items.title: Three levels
items.text:
The levels are listed on the left, always in this order, each with its sections under it:

Level What it covers This chat The open chat's own settings. Shown while a chat is open. This project The project of the open chat. Shown only when the chat has a folder. Every chat of the project follows it, the ones made before too. The app The whole app, in every project. Always there.

A chat takes what it does not set from its project, and the project from the app. Each setting is set at one level only: This chat shows what it takes from the project, read only, with a link up. What you type at one level is kept while you look at another.

items.title: How a section reads
items.text:
Each section of This project and The app first reads itself in a sentence or two: what happens now, made from its values as they stand - "At Full auto a small model looks at each command the list does not stop; one it finds risky is refused…". Change a setting and the sentence changes with it, before anything is saved.

Beside each setting a honeycomb cell says where its value comes from, and the foot of the section says what the cells mean:

Cell Means Full honey set here: this project (or the app) has its own value. An empty rim the default: as a new project (or a new KOLONİ) has it. Light honey changed, not saved: you changed it here and have not saved it yet.

The settings few change are under a section's More (More limits in Limits and money and in The app › Agents), closed until you open it. Its button says how many settings it holds and names those set here - "· 6 settings, 1 set here: secret files are not hidden from commands" - so a closed one never hides a setting of yours unsaid (When you're asked's sentence says them too, "Under More: …"). It stays open, and says so, while one of them holds a value that cannot be saved.

items.title: Saving
items.text:
A section's Save is in a bar at its foot, there only while something in the section is changed. The bar says what, in a status line a screen reader reads out: "2 changes not saved: When the judge finds a command risky, When you're away" - or that a value cannot be saved yet, with Save off until it is fixed. After saving, the bar goes, "Saved" stays in that line, and the focus goes to it. Enter in a field saves only where something changed.

A section with changes you have not saved shows a not saved tag next to its name in the list. You can move between sections without losing those changes. Some rows save on their own, with no Save: Runs without asking's rules, Slash commands and This folder's map. This chat's settings take effect as you change them.

items.title: This chat
items.text:
The same rows as the sheet Chat settings opens under the message box:

Setting What it does Teams Who picks this chat's teams, and the ones picked. Set with the Teams button over the canvas. Folders Where this chat's agents work, and its other folders. Set with the folder button. Page scripts Ask each time or Always run in this chat, for a page an agent shows in the Workspace. Also offered over the page's preview. Runs without asking A project's chat: how many rules it has, and a link to This project › When you're asked, its rules shown. A chat with no folder keeps its own list here.

Its permission level, Plan first and its model stay under the message box. Under them, From the project lists what the chat takes from its project (who changes the files, opening a sub-agent, when you're away, the agents' limits, money, where commands run) with Change in This project, and Change in The app leads to the app's. A chat with no folder says that its sub-agents use KOLONİ's defaults: ask when it matters, 2 at the same time, 2 levels, 6 per request.

items.title: This project
items.text:
The sections are listed on the left, in this order, each by its job (0.1.10: eleven became seven, and no setting is gone - what few change is under More):

Section Holds (its name before 0.1.10) How agents work Agents · New chats start with · Slash commands, under More When you're asked Asking and away · Runs without asking · Commands and secrets, under More When the work is done Checks and git Limits and money Limits and money Memory and web Memory and web Notifications Notifications This folder This folder

items.title: How agents work
items.text: "Every chat of this project follows these, the ones made before too." Its sentence: who changes the files, the Scout's follow-up tasks, and what a new chat starts with.

items.title: Agents
items.text: Setting What it does Who changes the files Orchestrator delegates the work: it plans, asks and checks; sub-agents change the files. Orchestrator decides: a small change (one or two files, a few lines) it makes itself, bigger work goes to a sub-agent. Orchestrator does it itself: it changes the files itself, and may still hand a part to a sub-agent. Suggest follow-up tasks after each turn On by default. After a turn that did something, the Scout - the role that looks for what is left - proposes at most three follow-up tasks for the To-do list; they wait for your Add to To-do, Edit or Not wanted. One small model request per such turn, made once the turn is over, and at Full auto in a turn you started one more for the Orchestrator's decision. Follow-up tasks from picks the tier: Fast tier (the default), Balanced tier or Strongest tier.

items.title: New chats start with
items.text:
"A new chat of this project starts with these; each chat then sets its own." Its teams are in sight; its other folders are under More.

Setting What it does New chats' teams Orchestrator decides, Manual or No teams. With Manual, the teams a chat kept with Use for new chats in this project. Other folders The folders a new chat starts with, besides the project. Remove one here; add one from a chat's folder button with Keep for this project.

items.title: Slash commands
items.text: Under More: your own commands for the message box. Each has a Name, What it does, the Text it puts in the box, and can Hand it to a role. Tick In every project to use it everywhere. Add command saves a new one; Edit and Delete change the list.

items.title: When you're asked
items.text: Its sentence says what Full auto's judge does now, who answers a card that waits, and when a sub-agent asks - and, "Under More: …", what is set under its More. Its parts are Commands, While you're away and More.

items.title: Commands
items.text:
Settings › This project, at When you're asked.

Setting What it does Full auto's judge On by default, in new projects and in the ones you had. At Full auto - in a chat you watch, a To-do task done in a chat, and a job while you're away - a command the list does not stop is first sent to a small model, your Judge model (The app › Agents) - since 0.1.10, in a chat you watch, a delete in the project, git work thrown away and a stop by name too, written as a plain line, which the list asked of before (which), and since 0.1.11 a plain push of your feature branch to its origin (which; one it finds risky waits on its card, never refused): one it finds risky is refused and the agent goes on, or waits for you on a card - as When the judge finds a command risky below says -, and a job while you're away parks it for you and goes on. Reads, ordinary work (tests, compilers and checkers, local git), and your own test command (unless it runs a program an agent wrote) are not asked about; it never lets a command run that asks - one it gave no answer for, or may not ask about now (no room on its model's provider, the turn past its token limit - said once in the chat), waits for you on a card at either choice, and so does each where there is no model to ask, said once in the chat. Its card's Don't ask about this line again here keeps the line in this project, offered only where the judge itself looked at it and KOLONİ knows all the line runs: a project file it runs in a plain form (python x.py, make, npm run x, docker build .), or one plain curl, wget or file command (cp, mv, rm, mkdir…); any other line - git too - is asked about each time. One request of your Judge model for each such command. The same switch is in the level menu, under the levels. Off: Full auto as before. Since 0.1.11 the judge reads new words, "D2". See Full auto's judge. When the judge finds a command risky Under Full auto's judge, and only while it is on: Refuse and go on (the default, in new projects and in the ones you had) or Ask me. Refuse and go on works as Claude Code's auto mode: the command does not run and no card opens - its agent is told a general reason ("KOLONİ's judge refused this as risky (it may send data off this machine, …). Do it another way, or ask the user.") - never the judge's sentence, which may quote your messages - and goes on; you see the sentence: the command's row says refused with KOLONİ's judge refused: … under it, and Decided for you lists it until you press OK. After 3 refusals in a row (a command that runs ends a row) or 20 in a turn, by any of its agents, each risky one waits on its card for the rest of the turn (said once in the chat). Ask me puts it on a card, "KOLONİ's judge: …", as before 0.1.9's change. Only the judge's own "risky" is refused: a card the list opens (a push, a secret, a delete out of the project…), and one the judge gave no verdict for (no answer in time, none it could read, no room to ask, a command too long or with orders in it), stays a card either way - and a job while you're away always parks it for you. The Don't ask about this line again here box is on Ask me's card only. See Full auto's judge. It also lets a delete or a push run when a line you saved names it Under Full auto's judge: Check what I said first, a question of the judge's since 0.1.9 - it replaces the row A harmful-looking command at Full auto. It works only once your Judge model's measurement has passed - none has yet (Claude Code's haiku, measured on 25 Nov 2026, did not): the box says (after its measurement) and cannot be ticked - or in a project where you had turned Check what I said first on: its box comes ticked there, and you may untick it. With the box unticked, a push or a send waits for you on a card at Full auto - one that quotes you, one click, where this turn's messages (the one that started it, or one you sent into it with Send now) asked for a push, a pull request or a merge (how) -, except a plain push of your feature branch, which goes to Full auto's judge (which); a delete in the project goes to the judge too (with the judge off, its card). A force push or a branch deleted on the remote waits on a card at every level, whatever you said. Where it works, your Judge model (The app › Agents) first reads your preferences, this project's rules as saved on the Memory page and your own messages in this chat (while you're away, in the chat you went away from) - not the folder's .koloni/rules.md, nor anything an agent wrote - and the command runs without a card only when a whole line of yours names it and what it touches ("You may delete build/ and dist/.") - one that forbids nothing and sets no condition. A line of your preferences never runs a command, it can only stop one; and of your messages, only this turn's run a push, a pull request or a merge, never an earlier turn's (this project's rules still can). A command a whole sentence of yours forbids ("Never push to main.") is not run and opens no card: the agent is told your sentence (of a message of yours in the chat, only that one of yours forbids it - the sentence itself stays with you), and not to run it again or anything that does the same, and carries on with the rest of its task. A sentence that sets a condition or asks to be asked ("unless", "ask me before") keeps the card, and so does a line that forbids the same delete beside one that allows it ("Never delete ./x." and "You may delete ./x."). Either way the command says which sentence it rested on, and waits under "Decided for you" until you press OK. After 3 such refusals in a row, or 10 in one turn, KOLONİ says so in the chat, and the rest of that turn asks you on a card. Secret files, .koloni, files that steer later turns, paths outside the folder, a delete or a send of the whole folder, a force push, and a CLI's command whose folder is not known are always asked, and anything that goes wrong - no model to ask, over the budget, a slow or unreadable answer - opens the card as before. Each such command is one request of your Judge model (on a CLI, of your plan).

items.title: Runs without asking
items.text:
The last row under Commands, saying how many rules there are ("2 rules"), with Show the rules: each is removed there at once, not by Save.

  • Sites agents open: the agents' own browsers open these in every chat of this project without asking, unless marked Ask first. Add one with Allow site.
  • Commands and requests, by chat: the rules made with Always run on a card, grouped by chat. Remove one with its ✕. You can also allow plain GET requests to a host for a chat.

See Permission levels for what a rule can and cannot cover.

items.title: While you're away
items.text: Setting What it does When you're away Everything waits for you, or The Orchestrator answers what it safely can, after a number of minutes (0 to 1440; a new project: the second, after 5 minutes). With the second, once you haven't answered for that long - at once while you're away (☾ Away on a chat's line) - the Orchestrator picks, says why, and you see it under "Decided for you". It opens a sub-agent on its role's own model unless that model is at its limit, out of credit, or over this month's budget; a move onto another model that may cost money, commands it may not run, deleting, reaching outside and Take in still wait. An Orchestrator on a CLI uses one request of your plan for each answer. Opening a sub-agent Ask when it matters, Always ask or Never ask. With Never ask, sub-agents open on their own in every chat of this project.

items.title: More
items.text:
Under More, closed until you open it: disposable deletes first, then, under the heading "Run commands on", where commands run and what they may see (until 0.1.10 the section Commands and secrets).

Setting What it does Agents may delete what is disposable without asking Off by default. At Auto-edit files and Full auto, in a chat you started, a delete KOLONİ checks is disposable runs without a card: a build or cache folder (build, dist, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .ruff_cache, .mypy_cache, coverage, .next, .turbo, target) below where the command runs, spelt as it is on disk, that git ignores, holding no file git tracks or does not ignore, no link and no repository of its own; a worktree of yours that git lists, not locked and not one of KOLONİ's, holding nothing its commits do not, no link, no secret file and nothing else git ignores; a local branch that neither the project, the turn nor any worktree stands on (with -D, only one whose commits the default branch has). Only such a delete alone on its line, in its shell's own form (in PowerShell, KOLONİ's own commands on Windows: Remove-Item -Recurse dist or rm -r build, never rm -rf; in sh, on Linux, macOS, Docker and Claude Code's Bash tool: rm -rf build; git's git worktree remove ../wt/x and git branch -d old in any), never a forced worktree remove; a folder's delete by Codex or agy, whose shell is not said, keeps its card; worktrees and branches only by the Orchestrator in the project. Its row says "Ran without asking · disposable: …", or, where it then failed, "… and failed: exit 1". At Ask before changes it still asks. The card of such a delete offers Allow such deletes in this project, which turns this on. See Disposable deletes. This machine Commands use the project's own tools as they are. They are not isolated. The page also says which shell commands run in. Docker container A fresh container for each command, with this folder mounted. Only the folder is kept. Needs Docker running. Then: Image (for example python:3.12, never pulled for you) and Allow network access. On Linux and macOS a command runs as your user, not as root, so the files it makes are yours, except under rootless Docker. Longest command (minutes) 10 by default, at most 60: the most an agent's command may ask for (one still stops after 2 minutes unless it asks for more), and how long KOLONİ's own test runs are given (the whole suite after a change, a job's tests while you're away). Raise it for a test suite or build that takes longer. A command that keeps running (a dev server) has no limit. A CLI working with its own tools (Native) runs its own commands under its own limits, and Codex run Native still ends its turn when one of its own commands runs past 11 minutes. Hide secret files from commands On by default. Covers commands in Docker and in Copilot's sandbox. Secret variables commands may see Environment variables with secret names are held back from commands and CLIs. Name the ones they may see, separated by commas, for example OPENAI_API_KEY, NPM_TOKEN. The page lists what is held back. Copilot's commands never get GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN or COPILOT_*, whatever you name here: it signs in its own way. Planted test key (canary) On by default. Each message's commands get a made-up key that no agent is told of. A command, web request, browser or MCP call that would send it out is refused and the work stops: something the agent read may have told it to.

items.title: When the work is done
items.text: Its sentence says what runs after a change, how far failing work goes back, and how the work reaches git. Check by kind of work, Found by KOLONİ and Measure command are under More; what runs before a sub-agent's work is added is said in sight.

items.title: After a turn that changed code
items.text:
Check by kind of work and Found by KOLONİ are its rows under More.

Setting What it does After a change Test and review (the default) or Tests only: after a turn that changed code, KOLONİ runs this project's tests once on the work as it now stands and says under the answer what was checked and what was not; under Test and review, a big or security-touching change is looked over by a read-only Reviewer too. Failing tests and its blocking findings go back to the Orchestrator until it passes, or as many times as Fix rounds says; then, with Then a stronger model on (the default), the next stronger tier on the Models page tries the fix, and failing work is never taken in (A stronger model). In a turn you watch the answer waits for the tests related to the change (with none, at most 1 minute for the whole suite), and the whole suite goes on after it; where the work is in its own working copy it waits at most 2 minutes for them all (How long it waits). Nothing runs nothing, and the Checked lines still say so. A project that had turned off the old Finish only when the tests pass switch is on Nothing, and says so here. One chat can differ: Test and review changes in its permission level's menu (for one chat). Fix rounds Until it passes (the default), or 1 to 10: how often a turn's failing tests, a sure problem in what it wrote, and the Reviewer's blocking findings go back to the Orchestrator - one count for all of them. Until it passes goes on while each round makes progress, and stops where a round changed nothing, at the turn's token limit or the monthly budget, or after 20 rounds - saying why. Then you decide (Fix it), or a stronger model tries (below). A project still on the old default, 2, moved to Until it passes; a number you chose is kept. A recipe's Checks step may set its own (The Checks step). See When the tests fail. Then a stronger model On unless you turn it off. The rounds spent with a test still failing, the next stronger tier on the Models page tries the fix - it says what is wrong first, and its model's use is said; failing work is never taken in, at any level: you decide (Take in anyway or Fix it). Off, the work waits after the first model's rounds. A Reviewer's hold is not handed on: you decide. See A stronger model. Check by kind of work Documents · Slides · Diagrams · Data · Pages · Config · Scripts · Code style and types · A test for the change; all on but Pages and A test for the change, which are off unless you tick them (since 0.1.10). Under Test and review, after a turn that wrote such files, KOLONİ checks them without a model - links and headings, whether a diagram parses and is connected, CSV rows and notebook cells, empty slides, JSON, YAML and TOML files that parse (a package.json, pyproject.toml, GitHub workflow or Compose file in its expected shape), shell and PowerShell scripts that parse (read by their own shell, never run), the project's own ruff, eslint, tsc and mypy where it has them (each asks before it runs unasked, a yes for that line); with Pages, a changed page (or the running preview, for a component) in its own browser at 375, 768 and 1280 px, for console errors, sideways scrolling and accessibility - and a sure problem goes back as a fix round. A test for the change asks the Orchestrator once for a test where code changed and no test did, under Tests only too. Untick a kind to leave it unchecked; the answer then says "Not checked: slides switched off for this project". See Checked, Pages and A test for the change. Found by KOLONİ Shown only where KOLONİ saved a test command itself: each, by folder, with where it came from (the project's files, an agent's run, or its look at the code) and when. Forget it clears them, found again at the next change. Yours (a part's test command) always wins. See Checked.

items.title: When a sub-agent's work is added
items.text: Before a sub-agent's work is added, the tests it wrote or changed run in its working copy - only those, each part's test command from the project map narrowed to them (python -m pytest -q tests/test_new.py). None written: no test before adding, and its card says so; KOLONİ's check at the turn's end still runs every test. There is no command to fill in for it (0.1.7: Test before adding is gone).

items.title: How the work reaches git
items.text:
Setting What it does Save each sub-agent's work as a git commit One commit per piece of work, offered on the card once the changes are in, and only where this folder is the top of a git repository. It is always your click, never made by itself, and nothing is pushed. How a team's finished branch reaches yours Merge here or Open a pull request. If you have not chosen, the first finished branch on a GitHub project asks.

Under More, with Check by kind of work and Found by KOLONİ:

Setting What it does Measure command A command whose last line of output is a score from 0 to 100, for example python measure.py. Recipes use it to pick the best of several candidates.

items.title: Limits and money
items.text:
Two are in sight: Monthly budget and Stop the work on a message over this many tokens, a job's budget. The rest are under More limits, closed until you open it; it says how many there are and how many are set here (· 6 settings, all at their defaults), and stays open while one holds a value that cannot be saved - Save is off until it is fixed. A provider's own limits are on its Limits tab (Models), and a night's limits on the Go away card.

Setting What it does Monthly budget For this calendar month's messages, in the currency of your prices (else USD). At 80% you are told. At 100% a new message asks before its work starts. Work on a model with no price is not counted. Stop the work on a message over this many tokens A job's budget, in tokens: all the agents working on one message together - yours, a To-do task's, or a job's while you're away. Over it, the work stops as failed and says so: "this turn used N tokens, over the project's limit of M". A job tried again, or a message that goes on with it, starts from zero. Only what a model reports is counted. Empty: no limit. See Usage. At most this many agents at work in this project Counted over all of this project's chats together. A new agent waits for a free place. Empty: no limit. Agents at the same time The most agents at work at once for one message. 1 to 32. Each provider has its own limit too. Above 8 the page warns that this may strain this machine and your subscription. Sub-agent levels How deep sub-agents may open their own, from 1 to 4. Sub-agents per request The most sub-agents opened for one message outside a recipe. 1 to 20. Continue gives this many more steps How many more steps Continue gives an agent that stopped at a step limit, on its card or on its kept work's card. 25 unless you change it, 1 to 200. A go on by message gives a new step limit instead. The step limit itself is the app's: Steps an agent may take, a link away. See Step limits. A discussion's tokens, at most A token budget for each discussion. Empty: no limit. Its speakers count toward the job's budget too: above that, the job stops first. See Discussions.

items.title: Memory and web
items.text:
Its sentence says what is noted by itself and where a web search asks. Also look in the memory of is under More.

Setting What it does Note what the work found, by itself After each message's work, a fast model writes at most three notes of what it found. One more model request after every message. Off by default. See Memory. Also look in the memory of Tick other projects. Agents' look-ups and your deep search find their memory too. Search address (SearXNG) Your own SearXNG server, for example http://localhost:8888. An agent's web search asks it first; turn on its JSON format. When it does not answer, the search goes on as below and says so. Otherwise search with The built-in search first, then a CLI or A CLI first, then the built-in search. Let agy search too Lets agy search the web. While it searches, agy is not held to its search tool: it may read files on this machine or open pages unasked. Shown with Show experimental features on (The app › Agents), or where it is already ticked.

items.title: Notifications
items.text:
Its sentence says whether a desktop notification shows and when the day's summary comes.

Setting What it does Show a desktop notification On Windows; on macOS (terminal-notifier where it is installed, else the system's own); on a Linux desktop with notify-send. Greyed out where none is there. Where an agent's notifications go, and what KOLONİ tells you while you are away; off, agents have no notify tool. At most 6 a minute for one chat. Send the day's summary at A time of day, by this computer's clock, for a daily summary: Usage's Today numbers for the project as text, counted from the record; no model is asked. Needs desktop notifications. If KOLONİ is closed then, it sends the summary late, when it next opens, and only for the last day it missed.

items.title: This folder
items.text:
Its sentence says which of the project's settings and rules the folder's .koloni/ keeps.

Project map is a table of the project's parts: Folder, Language, Files, AGENTS.md and Test command. You can change a part's test command and save that row; Use guess puts back the one KOLONİ found. A command you write there runs in its part's folder without a card, at every level; saved empty, the part has no test. Where no project file makes the root a part, the first row is ./, the whole project: a test command there runs from the project's root, beside the other parts' commands (Which tests) - the place for the command you had in Test before adding (gone in 0.1.7).

This folder's rules are shown when the folder has .koloni/rules.md. Read-only here; you change the rules on the Memory page.

items.title: Delete project
items.text:
Under This folder, Delete project… removes the project from KOLONİ: its chats with their messages, agents' work and usage, its memory, knowledge, To-do tasks and work while you're away. The dialog counts what goes, offers Export first (the same .zip as Export everything, without API keys), and deletes only once you type the project's name. It cannot be undone.

The folder on disk is not touched: its files, its git and its .koloni/ stay. Opening the folder again makes it a new, empty project. What KOLONİ kept of its chats under runtime/ goes, as a chat's delete takes it: their attachments and their CLI sessions.

While anything of the project is at work (a turn, a sub-agent, the To-do's turn, jobs while you're away), while a command it started still runs (such as a dev server), while finished work waits for Take in or Discard, or while its knowledge is learning, the delete is refused and says why.

items.title: Agents, in every project
items.text:
Its sentence says the language agents answer in, when a context is summarised, whom KOLONİ's judges ask and whether experimental features are offered. Answer in and Summarise a long context at (%) are in sight. The step limit, the two limits of a turn nobody watches, what knowledge reads and KOLONİ's test runs are under More limits, closed until you open it (it says how many are set here, and stays open while one holds a value that cannot be saved). The links between Steps an agent may take and Continue gives this many more steps open the other's More limits.

Setting What it does Answer in The language the agents write in, in every project. Auto means the language you write in. Pick one from the list (English, Türkçe, Deutsch, Español, Français, Italiano, Português) or type another. KOLONİ's own screens stay in English. Steps an agent may take The most model steps one sub-agent takes on a job before it stops: 25 unless you change it, a whole number from 5 to 200. Coordinators get more for their recipes. The Orchestrator counts no steps: it stops when it goes round in circles, or at its role's own limit if you set one. What Continue gives on top is each project's: This project › Limits and money, a link away. What happens at the limit, and who may give more: Step limits. Stuck after this many minutes with no progress In a To-do task's turn, and in a job while you're away, the Orchestrator's turn ends once nothing has moved for this long: no file of the turn changed, no agent finished its work, no failing command passed. Each of those starts the minutes again; a card waiting for you, a command or a model step under way, or an agent below the Orchestrator at work keeps them from running out. 30 unless you change it, a whole number from 5 to 1,440. The turn fails with the reason, its work kept; a To-do task gets its fix round, then is stuck, and its chat's queue goes on. See Step limits. An unattended turn runs at most (hours) A last resort: a To-do task's turn or a job while you're away ends after this many hours however it goes, its work kept. 8 unless you change it, a whole number from 1 to 72; empty: no limit, so a turn that keeps working (changes, agents at work, messages between agents) can run without end. Summarise a long context at (%) Once an agent's context passes this much of its model's window, the older part is summarised before its next step. A whole number from 50 to 95. It does not apply to a CLI run step by step. Claude Code run Native on its own sign-in for KOLONİ compacts its own session. GitHub Copilot run Native, and Codex run Native on its own sign-in, go on in their session only until it holds this much of 100,000 tokens (Copilot) or 166,000 (Codex), or of the window set on its role where that is smaller; the next turn then starts anew from KOLONİ's summary. Any other CLI starts each turn anew: KOLONİ compacts it, against its role's window or, with none set, the catalogue's for its model. See Set up a CLI. Knowledge reads at most (files) Knowledge from a repository or a folder on this machine stops before it reads more files than this: 50,000 unless you change it, a whole number from 100 to 1,000,000. A learning keeps what it started with. See Knowledge. Knowledge reads at most (MB) The same, in MB: 300 unless you change it, from 1 to 10,240. KOLONİ's test runs at once How many of the test runs KOLONİ makes at a turn's end go at the same time; the rest wait their turn. 1 unless you change it, a whole number from 1 to 4. More finishes sooner and loads the machine more. The agents' own commands are not counted. See Checked. Test processes per run How many processes one of KOLONİ's test runs may start, where its runner reads it (pytest-xdist's -n auto). 2 unless you change it, a whole number from 1 to 16. The agents' own commands are not limited. Show experimental features Below the rest, saved as you change it: off by default. Offers agy, and Native (a CLI with its own tools), under Experimental on the Models page, and Let agy search too in This project › Memory and web. It is less measured than the rest. A provider already set up so keeps working either way, tagged Experimental. Kept as you change it, without Save. See Experimental CLIs. Judge model Below the rest, saved as you change it: whom KOLONİ's judges ask, in every project - Full auto's judge, and its question of your words (Check what I said first). Fast tier's first (now: …), the first model of your Fast tier that answers with no tools, unless you choose one of the models listed (of every tier, those that answer with no tools - a CLI with tools of its own among them, such as GitHub Copilot CLI run Native, asked with them off). Kept as you change it, without Save. A choice that cannot be asked now (its provider gone, closed to agents or down) stays chosen and says so; the Fast tier's first is asked meanwhile. With none to ask, each command Full auto's judge would look at waits for you on a card, and the chat says why. On a CLI each such command waits for it to start. Advisor model Below the Judge model, saved as you change it: "A model the Orchestrator may ask for advice. It sees the Orchestrator's summary and the turn's recent steps, masked." - for its ask_advisor, at most 3 times a turn, in every project. Another provider's than the Orchestrator's unless you choose one of the models listed (the Judge model's list: those that answer with no tools): then a model on a provider other than the Orchestrator's, the strongest tier first. A choice that cannot be asked now stays chosen and says so. Each ask is one request of that model, in the turn's spend. See Talking while agents work. New preferences from your words Below the Advisor model, saved as you change it: what the Orchestrator does when you say in a chat how you want work done from now on, in every project. Add them, tell me (the default): your own sentence - never the model's wording - goes into Your preferences at once, and the chat says so, with Undo. Ask me first: a card in the chat shows your words and the line, with Add and Not now. Only a sentence of your own prose counts, never what you pasted. See Memory.

items.title: Voice
items.text: Its sentence says whether Auto-read is on, what it reads, and whose voice reads aloud. This browser's, for every chat: Auto-read reads (the whole answer or a short summary), the Dictation language, Read aloud with the browser's own voice (its Rate and Pitch) or Read aloud with Gemini (a Gemini API key, and How Gemini says it), and How the Orchestrator speaks. Dictate and Read aloud stay beside the message box. See Voice.

items.title: Your data
items.text:
Its sentence says what KOLONİ's data takes on this machine and how many places no agent opens.

Export: your KOLONİ data in one .zip: chats, agents, providers, memory, skills and attachments. Not in it: your project folders (their .koloni/ knowledge too), working copies, logs, previews, the CLIs' own folders and the database's own backups (before an upgrade, and daily).

  • Include API keys and secrets (keep this file safe): without this, the keys KOLONİ stores in its settings and secret files you attached to a chat (a .env, a key file) are left out. A key that was ever written in a chat, in another file you attached, an agent's output or a command stays in the file either way, so keep the file private.
  • Export everything starts the download.

Restore: "Restore only a file you exported yourself: it decides which programs KOLONİ may start."

  • Restore from a file… takes a .zip you exported.
  • Nothing changes at once. The restore replaces your data the next time KOLONİ starts: close KOLONİ and start it again. Until then you can Cancel it. Your data as it was is set aside, not deleted.
  • After a restore, what starts by itself waits until you press Resume. To-do tasks that waited in a chat's queue are back on To-do, as at any start of KOLONİ: give them to a chat again.
  • If the file had no keys, the page lists the providers that need theirs again.

Under them: how much space KOLONİ's database, backups, working copies and logs take; the working copies kept for your word - how many, what they take, and each one's chat, agent and when it was kept, with Discard, which asks first and deletes that copy as its card's Discard does (KOLONİ never deletes one unasked, so over 1 GB a line warns you); and Always blocked, the places no agent ever opens, in every project; the list is KOLONİ's own and cannot be changed here.

items.title: Settings kept in the folder
items.text:
A few project settings are also written to the folder's .koloni/settings.json, so they travel with the project in git: where commands run (this machine or Docker), the Docker image, Docker's network access, and the web search order. The first time, the page says "Saved in .koloni/ in this folder (kept in git)". Secrets, your addresses and this machine's folders stay in KOLONİ only. Everything under The app stays in KOLONİ too.

When a folder's settings differ from KOLONİ's (for example, after a git pull from another machine), the top of This project asks whether to use them, with Use them and Not now.

items.title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
items.text: The messages below are the ones KOLONİ shows, word for word. Text in {braces} is filled in by KOLONİ.

items.title: Starting and opening
items.text: "Open KOLONİ from the link in its window" ("Each start of KOLONİ makes a new link.") You opened an old tab or a bookmark after KOLONİ restarted. Each start makes a new page key. Copy the link KOLONİ printed in its window (KOLONİ is open at http://127.0.0.1:8790/#key=…) and paste it there. "KOLONİ cannot reach its server" The page cannot reach KOLONİ. Check that KOLONİ still runs in its window, then press Try again. "This page could not be shown" "Often the page and the server are different versions: restart KOLONİ, then reload. The other pages still work." This often happens right after an update. Restart KOLONİ, then press Reload. "KOLONİ serves your keys and files with no TLS: bind to this machine (KOLONI_HOST=… is not), or run the image." KOLONİ stopped because KOLONI_HOST names an address other than this machine. Use 127.0.0.1 (the default), ::1 or localhost, or run the Docker image. The port is already in use KOLONİ has no message of its own for this; the error comes from the system. Another KOLONİ (or another program) uses port 8790. Start KOLONİ on another port with KOLONI_PORT, and give it its own KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT. See Install.

items.title: Updating
items.text:
The update script stops at the first problem and prints update: {why} - stopped, nothing after it ran. The reasons:

{why} What to do tracked files have uncommitted changes: commit or stash them first Commit or stash your own changes to KOLONİ's files, then run it again. something answers on 127.0.0.1:{port} - stop KOLONİ first (Ctrl+C in its window) Stop KOLONİ, then run it again. this folder is not a git checkout; update it with git first (git clone) KOLONİ's folder must be a git checkout. this is a linked working copy; run the update in the main checkout Run the script in the main KOLONİ folder. {step} failed That step's own output says why.

When it works, it says Updated to {commit}. Restart KOLONİ; the database is migrated when it starts, and where the backup is.

items.title: Models
items.text: "{Provider} isn't answering at {address}." The bar at the top. The model server does not answer. Start it (for a server on this machine, Models → the provider → Server), or press Pick another model. The bar speaks only of the providers the open chat would run on: the one chosen for the chat, and where its Orchestrator and roles would run. With several down it names them all ("2 providers aren't answering: …"); Details lists each. ✕ hides it for this session until something else goes wrong. "{Role} can't run: {why}" The bar at the top. A role this chat would use (the Orchestrator, too) cannot run where it would now: its model is not one its provider may run, or the provider cannot be opened here. Pick another model for the role on the Agents page, or change the provider's list on the Models page. "{Provider} has no model it may run with by default." The provider's default model is not one it may run. Open the provider on the Models page and check its Default model. "{model} does not support tool calls; chat works, file tools are off." This model can talk but cannot use KOLONİ's tools. Pick a model that supports tool calls. For llama.cpp, start llama-server with --jinja. "The {command} command was not found on this machine. Install it in your own terminal (KOLONİ does not), then press Check on the Models tab" The CLI is not installed, or not on your PATH. Install it with the command shown, or set Path to the command on the provider's Connection tab. The card says "not installed". "{command} is not signed in. Sign in in your own terminal (KOLONİ does not), then press Check on the Models tab" Sign in to the CLI in your own terminal with the command shown, then press Check. The card says "not signed in". "The {command} command was found. It was not run, so sign-in is not checked." This is what Test says for a CLI. To check sign-in too, press Try a real run. It counts against your plan. "{name}: Qoder is no longer supported (0.1.8) …" A chat or a role still names a Qoder provider added before 0.1.8, which KOLONİ no longer runs. Pick another model for the chat or the role, then delete the Qoder provider on the Models page. See Qoder is no longer supported. "Copilot can't use {model} on your account: pick another model" Or, when Copilot runs as a session: "GitHub Copilot CLI exited with code 1: Error: Model "{model}" from --model flag is not available." KOLONİ's list offers a model that your Copilot account or CLI does not. KOLONİ switches that model off on the Copilot provider's Models tab and asks your account again; pick another model. See Copilot on your GitHub account. "not on your Copilot plan now: Copilot's own list does not offer it" Beside a model switched off on the Copilot provider's Models tab: your plan no longer lists that model. With your premium requests used up it says "your Copilot plan has no premium requests now: its named models are off until Copilot lists them again". KOLONİ switches it back on once your account lists it again; a model you switched off yourself stays off. See Copilot on your GitHub account. "{CLI} {version} could not be asked before it acts ({why}); run it as a session instead" KOLONİ runs a CLI with its own tools only when the CLI asks KOLONİ before each tool, and this one did not, so nothing ran. Open the provider and set How it runs to One session per agent, with KOLONİ's tools. See Set up a CLI. Tokens show as "–" or "unknown" for a CLI GitHub Copilot CLI run as a session reports no token counts, and KOLONİ estimates none. The Usage page shows "–" and the agent's window "unknown". Run Native, it reports its tokens and AI credits (or premium requests). A CLI on a plan never has a cost either. To see how much of your plan is used, look at the provider's plan meter, which Copilot has on your GitHub account (not on a model server of your own). See Usage and budgets.

items.title: When a turn fails
items.text:
A failed turn shows "Run failed: {Provider}: {reason}." with a next step under it:

Reason Next step shown limit reached, resets "Wait until it resets, or pick another model." out of credits "Add credits to that account, or pick another model." not signed in, or its key was refused "Sign in to it again, or pick another model." the CLI stopped without finishing "Send the message again." it ended without an answer "Send the message again." model server unreachable "Check that the model server is running, or pick another model." no model provider is set up "Add one on the Models page." "the CLI stopped without finishing" The CLI closed in the middle of its turn. The turn ends within a few seconds, even if a command the CLI started was still running. The programs it started end with it, as they do when you press Stop, so none keeps running or spending your plan. "model server did not start answering within {seconds} seconds" The model took too long to start. A large local model can be slow to load. Raise KOLONI_MODEL_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS (default 900) before you start KOLONİ. "model server sent nothing for {seconds} seconds" The model stopped in the middle of an answer. Raise KOLONI_MODEL_STALL_SECONDS (default 120) if your model pauses for long. "Interrupted by a server restart. Send a message to continue." KOLONİ stopped while the turn ran. Nothing is run again by itself. Send a message to go on. "Not sent: KOLONİ restarted" KOLONİ stopped while your message was queued, so it never reached the Orchestrator. Press Send under it to send it now, as your newest message. "Stopped at its step limit." An agent used all its steps for this job. A sub-agent's limit is Settings › The app › Agents › More limits › Steps an agent may take, with more for a coordinator's recipe. The Orchestrator has none unless you set one on the Lead role. Send a message to go on, or split big work into smaller messages. See Step limits. "stopped going round in circles: …" The Orchestrator repeated a call with the same result 10 times in a row, or the same call failed the same way 5 times, with nothing moving in between. In a turn you started a card asked you first: Go on or Stop here. Read its last calls in the chat, then say in a new message what to do differently. See Step limits. "{name} came to its limit of {taken} steps before its work was done." A sub-agent with nothing kept reached the app's step limit, and its card asks: Continue (+{n} steps) or Stop here. At Full auto the Orchestrator answers it once for each agent in a turn. See Step limits. "stopped at its role's limit of {limit} steps" A sub-agent reached the step limit set on its role. While the turn still runs, its kept work's card offers Continue (+{n} steps); {n} is Settings › This project › Limits and money › More limits › Continue gives this many more steps. Without kept work there is no card. Only you give more past a role's limit: the Orchestrator's go on is refused there, at Full auto and while you're away too. The role's limit counts the agent's earlier steps, in later turns too: after the turn, raise At most this many steps under Safety stops for one agent in the role's form (Agents page), then ask the Orchestrator to go on. A CLI working with its own tools takes no steps KOLONİ can count, so this limit does not hold it. "Stopped after the {n} steps it was given" An agent reached the end of the steps it was given by a Continue, or by the Orchestrator's call at Full auto. {n} is the job's whole count, the steps it had taken plus those given: after a Continue of 25 at 25 steps it reads 50. No Continue / Stop here card comes for it again in this turn. If it changed files, its kept work's card has Continue while the turn runs; otherwise ask for more in your next message. See Step limits. "could not work: Codex kept trying its own tools, which are off when it runs one step at a time (in a discussion, or on a Codex version not measured with KOLONİ)." Or "could not review: …" for a reviewer. Codex runs one step at a time when it speaks in a discussion, and on a Codex version KOLONİ has not measured whose session did not answer (its card then says "not measured; running the old way"). There its own tools are off, and Codex sometimes tries them. KOLONİ tells it to use KOLONİ's tools and tries the step again. A step that asks for any of KOLONİ's tools starts the count anew. The third such step in a row (one that tried Codex's own tools and asked for none of KOLONİ's) ends the agent. Each step tried again counts toward its step limit. On a version not measured, update Codex, or set How it runs to Native to let it use its own tools. See Set up a CLI.

items.title: Money
items.text: "Over this month's budget. Send it anyway?" The project's monthly budget is used up. Press Go on anyway to send it, or Cancel. A   provider's own limit shows the same way, starting "Over {provider}'s limit of …". Change the budget   under Settings › This project › Limits and money, and a provider's limits on its Limits tab.

items.title: Commands and Docker
items.text:
"Docker is not running: a container cannot be chosen." Settings › This project › When you're asked. Start Docker, then open the page again. "the image {image} is not on this machine; run: docker pull {image}" KOLONİ never pulls an image for you. Run the command shown in your own terminal. "Permission denied" on files in the project, with commands in Docker on Linux Commands in Docker run as your user now. Files an older version of KOLONİ made in the project, such as dist/, node_modules/ or .coverage, may still belong to root. Give them back to yourself in your own terminal, in the project's folder: sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" . You rejected a command, and the same change comes back as a file change

You rejected a command that writes a file or applies a patch. The agent is told "If the change is still needed, make it with edit_file / write_file", so it makes the same change as a file change:

  • at Ask before changes, it waits on a file-change card with its diff;
  • at Auto-edit files, it is written at once, and Revert takes it back;
  • from a sub-agent, it comes back with its working copy's card (Take in or Discard).

If you do not want the change at all, tell the agent so. See Permission levels.

items.title: Taking work in
items.text: "Changed on both sides, and git does not put them together: {files}" You and an agent changed the same lines. Press Let an agent resolve the conflicts, or resolve   them yourself. "Your uncommitted changes are in the way (commit, stash or unstage them first): {files}" Commit, stash or unstage your own changes to those files, then try again.

items.title: Folders
items.text: "{path} cannot be opened as a folder: {why}" Some places are never opened as a project: a drive's root, a folder that holds your home folder's secrets (such as .ssh or a CLI's settings), KOLONİ's own folder, and network paths. In the folder browser they are tagged "always blocked". Pick a folder inside your projects instead.

items.title: Restore
items.text: "not restored: {why}" The file could not be restored. For example, "it is not a KOLONİ export: it has no manifest.json", or "it was made by a newer KOLONİ (…): update KOLONİ first". Restore only a file you exported yourself. "A restore could not be applied at the last start: it is kept in {path}, and KOLONİ's log says why." Your data was not replaced. KOLONİ's log, in runtime/logs/koloni.log, says why.

items.title: This guide
items.text: "The guide is not built yet" At /guide/, or after a Learn more → link. KOLONİ serves this guide only once it is built. Run the commands that page shows in KOLONİ's folder, then reload. See This guide inside KOLONİ. On GitHub, the guide is not published Only in your own copy of KOLONİ on GitHub. The Guide workflow builds this guide and pushes it to the gh-pages branch; it publishes by itself only once the repository variable PAGES_ENABLED is true (a run by hand always publishes). The site shows only after Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch, gh-pages, / (root). A broken link or anchor fails the build, and nothing is published.

items.title: FAQ
items.text:
Is anything on screen simulated? No. The canvas, the agents and the usage come from what was recorded. A value KOLONİ does not know is shown as unknown.

Does KOLONİ send anything about me? No telemetry. What leaves your machine is the requests to the providers you add, and the web searches, requests and tools you allow. See Data and privacy.

Can I give a running command some input? No. Commands cannot be given input while they run.

Why can an agent still read .env at Full auto? A script that opens .env without naming it (it builds the name, say) is not caught. A command that names it, or searches the whole folder, is asked about at every level, but when it runs Native, Codex runs a read an allow rule of its own covers without asking KOLONİ (0.172.0 asks before a plain read of .env), and agy reading with its own tools reads it without asking at any level. Only Docker and Copilot's sandbox hide secret files from commands. See Known limits and Permission levels.

Are canvas positions saved? No. The canvas is drawn from the record each time.

Which systems are tested? Windows the most. Linux and the Docker image less, macOS not yet. See Install.

items.title: Discussions
items.text: A discussion is several agents talking one question through in rounds, while nobody changes anything.

items.title: Who starts one
items.text:
An agent starts a discussion when it has the discuss tool. You cannot start one yourself, but you can join it.

An agent invites 1 to 5 agents or roles, for 1 to 20 rounds (3 unless it says otherwise). The agent that opened it speaks last in each round.

A speech is at most 1500 characters, and each speaker is told so when its turn comes. A longer one is cut there and ends with "[the rest was cut]"; the rest is not kept.

items.title: When it ends
items.text:
A discussion ends when nobody has anything to add, at its round limit, when it reaches its token budget, or when you end it. It also ends at the message's and the project's own limits. One that broke off with an error shows Failed; one its Orchestrator stopped waiting for shows Stopped.

On the canvas, while it runs, the agent that opened it says "Waiting for the discussion" and a member opened for it "Waiting for its turn to speak".

Each step of a speech sends the speaker's whole work so far again, so the token count grows faster than the talk does. The budget is set under Settings › This project › Limits and money › More limits › A discussion's tokens, at most.
