Its speakers count toward the job's budget (Stop the work on a message over this many tokens) too: above that, the job stops first. Empty means no limit. It applies to discussions opened after you save it. A chat with no folder has no token limit for its discussions.

items.title: The Discussion window
items.text:
The Discussion window shows its state ("Round 2 of 3", or why it ended), and each round with what each agent said, or that it has nothing to add.

  • Say something to everyone, then Say, adds your words.
  • End discussion ends it.

items.title: Recipe cookbook
items.text:
The ready recipes KOLONİ comes with. Ready recipes cannot be changed; press Copy it on the Recipes tab to make your own from one. "Review" means the step is done only when it has no findings. An in end takes the work into the project (on the Teams' work is ready card); a report end tells you what was found. Agents is how many agents a run opens, as the Recipes tab counts them: the fewest where no review finds a problem, the most where every loop goes back all its rounds. The Orchestrator and what KOLONİ's own checks open at the end (a reviewer, the agents of a fix round) come on top (Recipes and candidates).

Recipe Steps Loops back Ends Agents Feature Write the spec (Spec writer, asks you to approve) → Build it (Coder) → UI review (UI designer, review) → Checks (tests and a review) UI review → Build it, 2 rounds in 3–7 Bugfix Reproduce it with a failing test (Debugger) → Fix it (Coder) → Checks (tests and a review) — (KOLONİ's fix rounds go back to Fix it) in 2–2 Review only at once: Reviewer, Security reviewer, UI designer, all reviews — report 3–3 Integration Learn (the team's experts) → Plan (Planner) → Experts check the plan (review) → Build (Coder) → Test (Tester, review) check → Plan, 2 rounds in 5–9 Quality check Run the tests (Tester, review) → Find and fix the cause (Debugger, only if a problem was found) → at once: Code review (Reviewer), Security review (Security reviewer) fix → tests, 2 rounds report 3–8 Model change Plan the experiment (Data scientist) → Experts review the plan (review) → Build it (ML engineer) → Compare the metrics (Model evaluator, review) → Checks (tests and a review) experts → plan, 1 round; metrics → build, 2 rounds in 4–10 Pipeline change Change the pipeline (Data engineer) → Check the data quality (Data analyst, review) → Checks (tests and a review) quality → change, 2 rounds in 2–6 Infra change Change the infrastructure (DevOps) → at once: Security review (Security reviewer), Performance review (Performance engineer) → Review it (Reviewer, review) reviews → change, 2 rounds in 4–10 Docs Write the docs (Docs writer) → Review it (Reviewer, review) review → write, 2 rounds in 2–6 Research Find it out (Researcher) → Sum it up (Summarizer) — report 2–2 Spec Break it into tasks (Hive keeper) → Write the spec (Spec writer) — report 2–2 Analysis Analyse the data (Data analyst) → Review the analysis (Reviewer, review) — report 2–2 Upkeep Update the dependencies (Dependency keeper) → Run the tests (Tester, review) → Find and fix the cause (Debugger, only if a problem was found) fix → tests, 2 rounds in 2–7 Evolve Try it three ways (3 Coders as candidates, target score 80) try again, 3 rounds in 3–12

items.title: Which team runs which
items.text:
Each ready team has a ready recipe as its default: Web app runs Feature, Quality Quality check and Docs Docs. The other ready recipes are no ready team's default since 0.1.10: pick one for a team in Teams for this chat (Manual), or make it a team's Default recipe on the Agents page - Bugfix for a team with a Debugger, a Coder and a Tester, Spec for one with the Hive keeper and a Spec writer, and so on.

In Bugfix the Debugger only shows the bug: it writes a test that fails because of it, runs it and reports the failing output, and fixes nothing; the Coder's fix must make that test pass. Its Checks step then runs the tests, and has a Reviewer look at a big or security-touching change - the rule of every turn (What KOLONİ checked); a small change gets no agent review. A failing test or a blocking finding goes back to Fix it, not to Reproduce it: the failing test it showed stays. Ask for changes goes back to Fix it too. Before 0.1.7 Bugfix had its own Test it and Review it steps; a copy of it you changed keeps its steps - to have every change reviewed, copy Bugfix and add a Review it step.

Feature, Model change and Pipeline change lean on their Checks step the same way (since 0.1.10). Feature's one review is the UI designer's - a judgement of the screens KOLONİ's checks do not make; Model change keeps its experts' review of the plan and the Model evaluator's metrics, Pipeline change the Data analyst's look at the data. Their tests are KOLONİ's to run, and a big or security-touching change gets KOLONİ's Reviewer and Security reviewer; a small one gets no review of KOLONİ's. They check so even in a project at Nothing: to leave it to the project, copy one and set the copy's Checks step to Follow the project (The Checks step). Before 0.1.10 Feature had a Code review, a Security review and a Test it beside its UI review (6 to 16 agents), and Model change and Pipeline change a Tester and a closing Reviewer; a copy you made keeps them.

If you renamed or removed a ready recipe or team, yours may differ.

See Recipes and candidates.

items.title: Recipes and candidates
items.text:
A recipe is the drawn steps of a piece of work: who does each step, what runs at once, where it loops back and how it ends. "A chat's team runs by the recipe picked for it, else by its team's default." Recipes are on the Agents page, tab Recipes.

Teams, recipes and discussions in one picture.

items.title: Making a recipe
items.text:
• + Draw a new recipe starts an empty one.
  • Pick a ready recipe and press Copy it. Ready recipes cannot be changed: "A ready recipe: copy it to change it."
  • Or write it: describe the recipe in a sentence and press Make it a recipe. The note under it says which model it asks first ("Asks Balanced: Local · qwen3"). It asks, each once and in turn: the balanced tier's models, then the fast and the strongest tier's, then the Orchestrator's model in the chat you are in (the one its model picker chose), then the model your newest chat ran on - passing over one whose server is not running, and never a CLI that keeps its tools. If one does not answer, the next is asked. Where none answers, it names every model it tried, each with why, and how to fix it ("No model answered: Local · qwen3 (not running). Start Local on the Models page, give a model a tier there, or pick a model in the chat."). The model draws the recipe in the editor; nothing is saved until you save it.

The ready recipes include Feature, Bugfix, Review only, Integration, Quality check, Model change, Pipeline change, Infra change, Docs, Research, Spec, Analysis, Upkeep and Evolve.

Each recipe in the list, and in the chat's recipe picker, says how many agents a run of it opens, counted from its drawing: "Feature · 3–7 agents" - the fewest where no review finds a problem (a step that runs only on a problem left out), the most where every loop goes back all its rounds. A team's experts or stages count as one agent there, and the helpers a step's agents open are not counted. The number is the recipe's alone: the Orchestrator, each team's lead and what KOLONİ's own checks at the end of the turn open (a reviewer, the agent of a fix round) come on top of it - a one-step recipe says "1 agent", and a turn of it may open several more.

items.title: The parts of a recipe
items.text:
The toolbar adds parts to the drawing: + Step, + All at once, + Loop back and + Ask me. Tidy up lays the drawing out again.

A step says who does it:

  • The Orchestrator picks;
  • The team's experts;
  • A role, with At most 1 to 5 agents;
  • Candidates (the best one goes on) (see below);
  • A team's stages.

A step can also have Done when, Only if the step before found a problem, If it fails (ask me or stop), and Ask me to approve its work before it goes on. That last one gives a card with Go on, Ask for changes and Stop.

Before a step that runs only if a problem was found, a test run that failed is a problem, whatever the agent's report says. At any other review step it is one too where the report says nothing is wrong, unless its Already failing before lines name every test that run says failed - with its file or suite where the run gives them (a bare name only where no other failing test has it), and never one the run's reproduce step showed failing: that is the bug. A later pass clears a failed run only where it is the same command in the same folder, or a run of the same test tool in that folder that picks none of its tests (pytest and python -m pytest are one tool): a narrower pass - a test name, -k, ::, -t, --grep, -run, --filter, tests left out (--ignore, --deselect), options of its own (-c, -o, --rootdir, PYTEST_ADDOPTS) - clears no wider failure. A pass of files or folders clears it only where it counted tests and every test the failed run names as failing is in one of them. A run that never started its tests (the tool not found), one that runs none (-h, --help, --version, --collect-only, a list of the tests, no tests found, or a summary that counts 0 passed and 0 failed) and one whose exit is hidden (; true, || true, a pipe after it) gives no verdict either way. In a step with the id reproduce (Bugfix's first) the failing test is the work: the agent's report says it "fails as it should". It is told to write and run that test itself and to open no other agent. In a recipe with no loop, Ask for changes - and a fix round of KOLONİ's checks - goes back to the step after such a step once it is done: the failing test it showed stays, and the fix goes again. Any other recipe with no loop goes back to its first step.

A Tester at a review step, or any agent of a step with the id test or tests, passes only on a command it ran that checks something. Where the project has a test command (yours, one KOLONİ saved, or one its files name) and the recipe changed code, that is a test run that really ran tests - its runner counted some, or your own test command ran. Elsewhere a mere read (ls, cat, git status) checks nothing, nor does echo, true, cd ., sleep, python -c "pass", a --version or --help, or a test run that ran none. Its task says so, and one that ran none does not pass - "it is a check that ran no test on record". Where you declined its command, the recipe stops at Teams' work is ready, "Not checked: you declined …", rather than sending the work back. A reviewer that only reads (a Data analyst, a Performance engineer) passes on its report. (Where an agent's CLI keeps its own commands off KOLONİ's record, its report is taken as it is.)

All at once runs steps side by side. It waits for all branches or for the first one done.

Loop back goes back to an earlier step, at most 1 to 5 rounds. Ask for changes gives a recipe's loops their rounds again: your word is a new start. A fix round of KOLONİ's checks goes back the same way but does not: a review whose loop ran out runs once more, and what it finds then is yours on the card - it names the findings and offers Fix the findings - not another round of the loop. Where a recipe's fixer loops back to its tests (Quality check, Upkeep) and those rounds ran out, KOLONİ sends no fix round on top: it would only run the tests again. In Integration, whose one loop goes back to Plan, a fix round plans again, has the experts check the plan, and stops before Build if they find something again.

A Room step of a recipe drawn before 0.1.10 (rooms are gone) opens as an All at once group in its place, with a step for each of its roles: they run side by side, as sub-agents, in the recipe's copy. Its arrows and loops are kept. Each of its steps is named "<the step's name> · ". A Room step that reviewed (no finding is left) becomes a review by each of its roles but one that does the recipe's work at a step of its own: that one works in the group (a role does not check its own work); where every role does, all keep reviewing and the recipe says which would check its own work. A Room step that ran only if the step before found a problem now always runs: a group runs on no condition.

Ask me is an end: Ask me, then in, or Tell me what was found. Every recipe needs an end.

items.title: The Checks step
items.text:
Every recipe ends in a Checks step 🔒: what KOLONİ checks before the recipe's work is done (What KOLONİ checked). It stands between the step(s) that lead to the end and the end itself ("Ask me, then in", "Take in", "Tell me"): the arrows go last step → Checks → end, one Checks step before all of the ends, and it moves with them when you add or move a step. It cannot be removed or dragged. KOLONİ runs its checks first, on the work in the recipe's copy, and only then asks Ready for you: a fix round sends the recipe back to work, and work whose tests still fail after the rounds is never offered nor taken in.

Click it to choose:

  • Follow the project (the default): the project's After a change - Test and review, Tests only or Nothing - with its Check by kind of work and Fix rounds.
  • Set for this recipe: Tests, Review, Docs, Diagrams, Data, Slides, Pages (a changed page in KOLONİ's own browser at phone, tablet and desktop widths), Config (JSON, YAML and TOML files parse), Scripts (shell and PowerShell scripts parse - read, never run) and Code style and types (the project's own ruff, eslint, tsc and mypy, asked before one runs unasked, as in Checked), each on or off (Config, Scripts and Code style and types start on), and Fix rounds - the project's, until it passes, 1 to 10, or 0 - check only (a problem is said, nothing goes back to be fixed). With Review on, a big change of screens is also tried by the Tester (the live try).

A recipe that makes no code - a report, the docs - turns Tests off and its kind of work on: its turn runs no tests and checks the documents it wrote; a fixable problem (a broken link) goes back as a fix round, as a failing test does. With every check off, the answer says "Not checked: this recipe's Checks step checks nothing". The choice is kept with the recipe - in a folder's .koloni/recipes/*.json too, as its graph's checks.

The ready recipes come set: Bugfix, Feature, Model change and Pipeline change check their tests and a review, Docs its documents and a review, Evolve its tests; the others follow the project. A recipe set for itself checks so even in a project at Nothing - set its Checks step to Follow the project to leave it to the project (a ready recipe cannot be changed: copy it, and set the copy's Checks step). Only a recipe you picked (Teams for this chat: Manual) can check less than the project does; one the Orchestrator picked (Orchestrator decides) only adds to the project's checks and takes the larger Fix rounds - it never turns them off. A recipe's turn follows its Checks step, never the chat's Test and review changes switch. Rounds never stack: where the recipe's own loop of test and fix ran out, the Checks step sends nothing back on top.

items.title: Where a recipe is kept
items.text: Choose Kept in KOLONİ, for every folder, or Kept in this folder's .koloni/recipes (in git). A recipe kept in the folder travels with the project, but only recipes kept in KOLONİ can be picked under Teams for this chat or as a team's default.

items.title: How a recipe runs and ends
items.text:
The team works in one working copy, step by step, following the drawing. When the work reaches its end, the Teams' work is ready card asks whether to take it into the project: Take in, Fix the findings or Ask for changes. See Ready and approval cards.

At Full auto, the work is taken in without the card, unless a team failed or a check was skipped.

How a recipe runs, loops and ends. (full size)

items.title: Candidates
items.text:
A step whose Who is Candidates (the best one goes on) gives the same job to 2 to 5 agents. Each works in its own working copy. For their models choose Auto, the Orchestrator picks, Same model or I pick each.

Each candidate's work is scored by the project's Measure command (Settings › This project › When the work is done): a command whose last line of output is a number from 0 to 100. A card then lists the scores and asks which candidate's work goes on. At Full auto the best score goes on by itself.

With a Target (0 to 100) and a loop, the step is tried again while the best score is below the target, and a new result replaces the kept one only if it scores higher. The ready recipe Evolve works this way: three Coders try the job, each their own way. With no measure command there is no score to compare, so the step runs one round only, and its card says so.

items.title: Roles
items.text: A role is what an agent is for: a description, instructions, the tools it may use and, if you like, its own model. Open Agents on the left rail ("Who does the work, in which teams, by which recipes"). The page has three tabs: Teams & roles, Recipes and History.

items.title: The roles
items.text:
The Orchestrator is the agent you talk to. It opens other roles as sub-agents when a part of the work needs them. KOLONİ comes with these roles:

Orchestrator, Planner, Coder, Tester, Reviewer, Researcher, Debugger, Architect, Security reviewer, Docs writer, Refactorer, UI designer, Data analyst, DevOps, Spec writer, Performance engineer, Database engineer, Dependency keeper, Translator, Summarizer, Hive keeper, Scout, Data engineer, ML engineer, Data scientist, Model evaluator, MLOps engineer, Designer, SEO specialist, Copywriter, Accessibility reviewer.

Two are named for KOLONİ's hive. The Hive keeper keeps the To-do list: it turns a goal into tasks, each with what makes it done, and puts them in order. The Scout keeps watch on the To-do list: it splits vague tasks, asks what is missing, flags duplicates, stale and blocked tasks, and checks finished tasks against what makes them done. After each turn KOLONİ also asks a model, in the Scout's name, for follow-up tasks (see To-do). A role of your own that already had one of these names keeps it; the built-in one is then "Hive keeper (built-in)" or "Scout (built-in)". A slash command of yours named scout would hide behind the role's chip in the message box: it is renamed scout-command.

Before 0.1.7 they were the Product owner and the Assistant product owner. Your recipes and saved slash commands that named the old roles were changed to name the new ones, and an agent that asks for an old name is told the new one ("Product owner is now the Hive keeper"). Past conversations keep the names they had. A recipe kept in a folder's .koloni/recipes is a file of yours, not changed: one that names an old role is renamed there, by hand.

The Roles list on the Teams & roles tab shows them all. Filter roles… searches it, and the buttons All, In no team and Off narrow it. Each role has an on / off switch. The Orchestrator and the Planner are always on. So are the Coder, Tester, Reviewer, Debugger and Security reviewer: KOLONİ's checks and recipes use them, so they have no switch (a chat's teams still decide whether they are opened there).

In a window narrower than 1280 px the list folds to a Roles ▸ N button over the teams, which opens it as a drawer; it stays at the top of the page however far you scroll.

items.title: A role's panel
items.text:
Click a role to open its panel. It has four tabs:

  • Overview: its category, the teams it is in, what it may do, and its Model as four answers: Which model, How hard it thinks, How much it reads and Who may move it (and Runs as where a role can run inside the CLI). Click an answer, or Edit, to change it.
  • Instructions: what the role is told.
  • Tools: the tools it may use, grouped (Files, Commands, Web, Browser, Team, To-do, Memory). A click switches a tool on or off and saves at once. A role needs at least one tool. The Coder, Tester, Reviewer, Debugger and Security reviewer keep the tools their job needs: reading files for all five, writing files for the Coder and the Debugger, Run commands for the Coder, the Tester and the Debugger. Those tiles stay on, greyed: "Kept: KOLONİ's checks and recipes need it". Their other tools are yours to change, and Reset to default still works. A sub-agent never has a tool its opener may not hand on: an Orchestrator without Run commands gives no Tester one. Tools marked "asks" wait for your yes, as the chat's permission level says. Below, the MCP servers and skills the role has; you change those on the Tools page.
  • Knowledge: a switch for each Knowledge topic. On, choose Full ("its whole guide at each step") or Map ("its guide, read when its work touches it").

items.title: Editing a role
items.text:
Edit opens the role's form:

  • Name, and What it does: "The Orchestrator reads it to pick the role."
  • Category and Instructions.
  • Model: a card for each question. Each says one line; Learn more holds the rest.

Which model asks Who picks it?, then only what that choice needs:

Choice What it needs What it means Orchestrator From and to "It picks a tier for each job, inside this range, and says why." As the chat nothing "Whatever the chat's model picker says." One tier Fast, Balanced or Strongest "Always this tier. The Orchestrator can't change it." One model a Provider and a Model name "Always this model, whatever the job."

The Orchestrator itself has no Orchestrator choice. Try first lists up to 5 models from the team guide, tried in order before the choice above; + Add a model adds one. See Tiers.

How hard it thinks (Thinking) is Auto or One fixed level, and one ladder of the levels Off to Max:

  • Auto: the agent that opens a sub-agent picks a level for each task: Low for reading or summarizing, Medium for normal code, High for hard bugs or design. The levels it may pick are shaded, from Low up to the one marked most (High unless you move it, or the nearest lower level a model without High takes); click a level to move it. Its pick, and its reason, show under Details in the agent's window. Auto never picks Off. If it picks nothing, KOLONİ sends Medium (or the most, where that is lower), and the agent's window says "Thinking Medium, KOLONİ's default for Auto (the opener gave no level)".
  • One fixed level: every task gets the level you click, any level its model takes; the Orchestrator doesn't change it.

An agy model whose name ends in its level, such as gemini-3.8-flash-low, takes no other: it is sent none, and the agent's window says so. Under How hard it thinks, the role's Model card says "The model's own" and "its name sets its level: none is sent".

A role from before may still have a most next to a fixed level, or a most of Off under Auto. A line under the ladder says so ("The Orchestrator may also go up to High (set earlier)"), and Remove takes it away.

Struck levels are ones the role's model does not take, named under the ladder. A model without a level gets the nearest lower level it takes, never down to Off; one whose levels are not known gets none. Back to Auto, a most of Off, or one the model is known not to take, is taken away.

Nobody opens the Orchestrator, so it has no most: a click sets its level, and with Auto no level of its own is sent, and the chat's level, or the model's own, applies.

How much it reads (the context window) says the window found for its model, and where from. Past the % set in Settings › The app ("Summarise a long context at (%)") KOLONİ summarizes the older part, unless its CLI keeps its own session: Claude Code compacts its own; Copilot's and Codex's start anew past that % of their bound (Going on from the last turn). Where the window is unknown there is no fullness meter and nothing is summarized early - but a CLI lead that starts each turn anew, which is summarized after its turn against the catalogue's window for its model where there is one, which only a very long chat reaches (Set up a CLI). Set by hand takes a window of your own.

Who may move it: Any provider in the team guide, Only these, or No one. An agent that moves a sub-agent to another provider must say why.

Run inside the CLI: only when the agent that opens it runs in Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI run Native (experimental) - Copilot on its newer protocol (1.0.114 on), where its provider is in the team guide. Cheaper, and counts toward no turn or role limit; it is not its own agent on the canvas, stops with the agent that opened it, and is never used while you're away. Not for the Orchestrator or a team's lead. The agent's window and the canvas show it as an own sub-agent, "Checker (inside GitHub Copilot CLI)", with what it did inside it. It has its role's own tools only, each asked about as its agent's are (a card where your level says so): none of KOLONİ's tools, which are its agent's, and no sub-agent of its own. In Copilot it runs on the agent's own model; Copilot is given only these roles, none of its built-in sub-agents, and opens one only while it waits for it - one it asks to open in the background, by another name, or with a model, level or anything else of its own choosing, is refused. At Ask, a role that can change things is a card before it opens, as opening an agent is. - It may: Read and search, Write code, Run commands, Use the web, or Pick tools one by one. - This role will sums up what the role will do, as you change the form.

Press Save. A built-in role has Reset to default; your own has Delete role.

items.title: A new role
items.text:
New role (on the Teams & roles tab) opens a form. "Agents in this role are opened by the Orchestrator or a team lead." Start from:

  • Blank;
  • An expert: it reads only; an expert changes nothing;
  • A copy of another role: it gets that role's servers, skills and knowledge, but not its teams.

Press Create role. An agent can also propose a role while it works; you decide on the Create this role? card.

items.title: History
items.text: The History tab shows what the roles, teams and recipes did in the Last 30 days or Last 7 days: how many agents were opened and ended done, and the team and recipe runs. Filter by role, team or recipe, or tick Failed only. Each row shows when, the role, the chat, the model and how it ended; click the chat to open it.

items.title: Step limits
items.text: An agent works in steps. A sub-agent stops after a set number of them, so that no agent runs on without end. The Orchestrator counts no steps of its own: it stops when its work is done, when it goes round in circles, or at a limit you set. This page says where the limits are set, what happens when an agent reaches one, who may give it more, and what happens when nobody is there to ask.

items.title: What a step is
items.text:
A step is one request to the agent's model. The model answers, and may call tools: read a file, run a command, open a sub-agent. The tools run, and the next step reads what they gave back.

  • A CLI run One session per agent counts one step for each message it writes.
  • A CLI working with its own tools (Native) takes no steps KOLONİ can count: no step limit holds it. See Set up a CLI.
  • The Orchestrator's step that reads a background agent's report, or answers a word you sent now, is a step like any other: it counts to its role's limit. At that limit it waits for the agents still at work and takes no step more. Agents opened in the background are held to the chat's limits as any agent - how many at once, how many a turn opens, how deep. See Talking while agents work.
  • The Orchestrator's own tools beside its agents have limits of a turn's: ask_advisor 3 asks, note_decision 10 notes; past them a call is refused and it goes on. See What the Orchestrator has while its agents work.

When an agent has two steps left, KOLONİ tells it to start nothing new, finish what it is on, and write its report: what it did and what is left.

items.title: Where the limits are set
items.text: Where What it sets Settings › The app › Agents › More limits › Steps an agent may take The most steps one sub-agent takes on a job: its task, or one later message it works on. 25 unless you change it, a whole number from 5 to 200. It holds in every project. It does not hold the Orchestrator. The role's form (Agents page) → Safety stops for one agent → At most this many steps A limit of the role's own. Where it is lower than the app's, it holds. It counts the steps an agent of the role takes on its work in the turn, and in the earlier turns it goes on from. Empty: only the app's limit. On the Lead role it is the Orchestrator's step limit; empty, it has none. Settings › This project › Limits and money › More limits › Continue gives this many more steps How many more steps Continue gives. 25 unless you change it, 1 to 200.

items.title: More steps for coordinators
items.text: A team's coordinator needs steps to open its recipe's agents, wait, and read what comes back. It gets 4 more for each step of its recipe. Each Ask for changes that sends the recipe back gives that much again, for up to three rounds. With the app's 25, a coordinator whose recipe has six steps takes up to 49 steps. A role's own lower limit still holds over these.

items.title: The Orchestrator: no step count
items.text:
The Orchestrator runs the whole turn: it opens the teams, passes messages on and writes the answer. A fixed count of its steps ran out on honest work, after the work was already in the project, so it has none. What stops it:

  • its work is done;
  • it goes round in circles (below);
  • a limit you set: the Lead role's At most this many steps;
  • in a To-do task's turn, and in a job while you're away: nothing has moved for Settings › The app › More limits › Stuck after this many minutes with no progress (30 unless you change it) - no file of the turn changed, no agent finished its work, no failing command passed. Each of those starts the minutes again, so honest work runs as long as it needs. They do not run out while a card waits for you, a command or a model step of the turn is under way, or an agent below the Orchestrator is at work;
  • a last resort: a To-do task's turn and a job while you're away end after An unattended turn runs at most (hours) (8 unless you change it; empty: no limit), however they go. A night's stop time holds as before;
  • either way the turn fails with the reason, its work kept - never cancelled: a To-do task gets its fix round, then is stuck, and its chat's queue goes on; a night tries the job once more, then goes on;
  • money and tokens, where you set them: the project's token limit for a message, its monthly budget, a night's money;
  • Stop.

A turn you started has no clock that ends it: you are there to press Stop, and the cards below ask you.

items.title: When the Orchestrator goes round in circles
items.text:
KOLONİ watches the Orchestrator's tool calls. It stops it when:

  • the same call fails the same way 5 times, with no change of the turn and no command succeeding in between;
  • 10 calls in a row each repeat a call it had made, with the same result, since something last moved.

Something moves when a file of the turn changes, it opens an agent, or it sends a message to one it had not written to among its last three. A command that succeeds is judged by what it said, like any call. A call with other arguments, or one that gets a new result (a team's report), is new; the same call made several times in one step counts once. From the third repeat on, the Orchestrator is told what is repeating.

In a turn you started, the first time it is told, in its next step, to try a different approach or to report what it did and end. Its counts start again and it goes on; you see nothing. If it goes round in circles again, a card under the call asks you:

The Orchestrator has no step limit, and it seems to go round in circles: its last 10 calls each repeated one it had made, with the same result, with no change of this turn on record and no command of its own succeeding in between. Go on lets it carry on; Stop here ends it, with what it did so far. With no answer in 10 minutes its turn ends, its work kept.

  • Go on: it carries on, and the counts start again.
  • Stop here: the turn ends with that reason.
  • No answer in 10 minutes: the turn ends by itself. What is in the project stays, and work in agents' copies stays behind its cards, as at Stop. KOLONİ's line in the chat says how many agents it had opened, how many files it had changed in the project, and which call it repeated. A message you sent meanwhile, the chat's To-do queue or the night then goes on.

Either way the turn ends there: nothing more is waited for, and no other card comes. Where this turn's work is already in the project, it ends completed, not red, with KOLONİ's line saying why it ended; otherwise it fails with the reason.

The card waits for you at every level, Full auto too. As it goes up, KOLONİ tells you on the desktop, where you switched that on (Settings › This project › Notifications): "The Orchestrator seems stuck: it repeated list_dir with the same result…".

In a job while you're away there is no card: the Orchestrator fails with the reason on record, also where it had written something, and a night goes on with the next job. A To-do task's turn is its chat's, so the card comes there too; where the turn fails, the task gets its fix round, then is stuck with why, and the chat's queue goes on with the next task.

items.title: When the Orchestrator's model is slow to answer
items.text:
In a turn you started, when the Orchestrator's model has said nothing for 5 minutes while it was asked - no words, no call - a card under the turn asks you:

Codex · gpt-6-astra has not answered for 5 min. Keep waiting, or stop this turn and pick another model?

Time on a tool (a sub-agent, a command) or on another card that waits for you does not count.

While it waits, the card counts as waiting for you outside its chat too: on Work's Ready for you, as a mark on the chat in the Chats list, and in a note in the corner ("Orchestrator waits for you").

  • Keep waiting: the turn waits on; the next card comes only after another 5 minutes with no word.
  • Stop and pick another model: the turn ends as at Stop, what it did kept, and KOLONİ's line says to pick another model for the Orchestrator and send your message again: in the chat's model picker, or on the Agents page where the Orchestrator role has a model of its own (see A role's model).
  • No answer: it keeps waiting. The card closes by itself once the model answers.

A sub-agent has no such card (one whose provider fails is moved to the next model of its tier), and a turn nobody watches is as above.

items.title: At the limit
items.text: What happens depends on who stopped, which limit it reached, and whether it changed files.

items.title: The Orchestrator
items.text: The Orchestrator reaches a step limit only where you set one: its role's own. It gets no Continue card there. If its teams are still at work it waits for them, then the turn ends. Send a message to go on.

items.title: A sub-agent with changed files
items.text:
A sub-agent that works in its own copy and has changed something stops at once. Its work is kept on a card in the chat ("Coder did not finish its work: this is what it had changed"), and nobody waits for it. While the turn runs, that card has Continue (+25 steps), with the project's Continue amount:

  • Continue gives it that many more steps, and it goes on in its kept copy. It gets the whole amount, also when it stopped at its role's own limit.
  • The card's other buttons decide the kept work, as on any card of changes.

If it stops again with changes, its card comes back with Continue. After the turn the card has no Continue: ask the Orchestrator in a new message to go on with it.

items.title: A sub-agent with nothing kept
items.text:
A sub-agent with no changes of its own, such as a team's coordinator or a reviewer, waits at the app's limit on a card under the call that opened it:

Reviewer came to its limit of 25 steps before its work was done. Continue gives it 25 more to go on where it is; Stop here ends it, with what it did so far.

  • Continue (+25 steps): it goes on where it is, with that many more steps. If its role has fewer steps left, the card offers only those.
  • Stop here: it ends with what it did so far. Its opener is told that you chose Stop here, and does not tell it to go on.

The card comes once for a job. After Continue the agent stops at the end of the steps it was given, with no new card.

There is no card when the agent stopped at its role's own limit, when its role has no steps left, or in the cases under When there is no card.

items.title: Who answers the card
items.text:
Level Who answers Ask before changes, Auto-edit files You. The turn waits for your answer. When you're away does not answer this card. Full auto The Orchestrator, at once: Continue or Stop here, with why. You see it under Decided for you. It answers once for each agent in a turn. The next time that agent reaches its limit in the turn, it gets no card and ends.

At Full auto the card still waits for you when:

  • the project is over its monthly budget;
  • the Orchestrator's provider is over its limit;
  • the turn is over the project's token limit;
  • the Orchestrator runs on a CLI and When you're away is Everything waits for you: each answer would use a request of your plan.

items.title: Going on by message
items.text:
The Orchestrator, or a team's coordinator, may tell an agent that stopped at a step limit to go on, with a message. This works at every level, once for each agent in a turn. The agent gets a new app step limit, not the Continue amount. Its role's own limit still holds: it stops there.

It is refused when:

  • you chose Stop here on the agent's card;
  • the agent already had more steps in this turn: Continue on its Continue / Stop here card, or an earlier go on;
  • the agent has no steps left under its role's own limit. A role's limit is your safety stop: only you give more past it, at every level, Full auto and work while you're away too. Press Continue on its kept work's card, or raise the role's limit. The Orchestrator is told "Coder is at its role's limit of 12 steps; more steps are the user's to give". While you're away nothing is given, and the job's report says the part is left undone.

items.title: When there is no card
items.text:
These get no Continue / Stop here card. The agent stops, and the agent that opened it is told what is left:

  • the Orchestrator itself, at a limit you set (its loop guard asks: see above);
  • a job of work while you're away;
  • an agent answering another agent's question, or working on another agent's message, a go on included: the sender waits for its reply;
  • an agent whose work is kept on a card with Continue;
  • an agent of a team you stopped.

items.title: Afterwards
items.text:
When a sub-agent stops at a step limit, its opener is told that its part is not done. It hands what is left to another agent, tells it to go on where it may, or says in its answer what is left undone.

On the canvas the agent's box says "Stopped at its step limit". Where it had more, it says "Stopped after the {n} steps it was given": {n} is the job's whole count, so after a Continue of 25 at 25 steps it reads 50.

To give it more:

  • while the turn runs, Continue on its kept work's card;
  • after the turn, ask the Orchestrator in your next message to go on with it. That is a new turn, so the once-a-turn go on is there again for an agent that stopped at the app's limit or at the end of the steps it was given;
  • an agent that stopped at its role's own limit counts the steps it took before, in later turns too: raise the role's At most this many steps first, then ask the Orchestrator to go on. A raised limit holds from its next job;
  • for work that is always big, raise Steps an agent may take (The app › Agents › More limits): it holds every sub-agent.

items.title: One job, three ways
items.text:
A Reviewer has to read a large change. It needs about 35 steps. The app's limit is 25, Continue gives 25, and the Reviewer role has no limit of its own.

In the day, at Ask before changes. At 23 steps the Reviewer is told it has two left. At 25 it stops, and the card asks you. Continue gives it 25 more; it goes on where it is and ends at about 35. Stop here ends it with what it found so far, and the Orchestrator's answer says what was not reviewed.

In the day, at Full auto. The same card comes, and the Orchestrator answers it at once, say with Continue. Its answer and why show under Decided for you. The Reviewer ends at about 35. Had it needed more than 50, it would stop at 50 with no new card, and the Orchestrator would say what is left; more steps are then yours to give in your next message.

While you're away. In a To-do task's job no card comes: the Reviewer stops at 25, and the job's Orchestrator is told its part is not done. (In the chat you went away from, the card comes and the Orchestrator decides it at once, as at Full auto.) It may tell the Reviewer once to go on: the Reviewer gets 25 new steps and ends at about 35. Had it needed more than 50, it would stop again, and the job's report would say what is left undone. The job can still count as done when you're back: open its chat to read what was left.

items.title: Teams
items.text: A team is a named group of roles, set out in stages. A role can be in more than one team. Teams are on the Agents page, tab Teams & roles.

items.title: The ready teams
items.text:
KOLONİ comes with three teams: Web app (with the Feature recipe), Quality (Quality check) and Docs (Docs). You can change them, or make your own with New team.

Until 0.1.10 there were eleven. At the first start of 0.1.10 the other eight - Backend / API, Data, DevOps, Research, Product, Maintenance, ML and DataOps - are taken away where they are as they came. One you changed (renamed it, put a role in or took one out, changed its stages or moved a role to another stage, its coordinator, its default recipe or whether the Orchestrator may pick it) stays as your own, and so does one you use: picked for a chat in Manual, kept for a project's new chats, or named by a recipe's step. Their roles all stay: put the ones you need in a team with New team, and give it the ready recipe of your choice (Bugfix, Spec, Research, Analysis, Upkeep, Model change, Pipeline change or Infra change) as its Default recipe. A chat the Orchestrator had picked one of them for keeps its other teams; with none left, the Orchestrator picks again.

Fourteen built-in roles are in none of the three: Architect, Database engineer, Performance engineer, Data analyst, Researcher, DevOps, Dependency keeper, Hive keeper, Scout, Data scientist, ML engineer, Model evaluator, MLOps engineer and Data engineer. The Orchestrator still opens any of them when the work needs one: with No teams, and with Orchestrator decides too - the teams it picks are where it starts, not a fence (see Which roles the Orchestrator opens). In Manual it reaches one only when you name it in your message, when a recipe's step names it, or when you put it in one of the chat's teams.

To build a website, the Web app team also has a Copywriter for the site's words and an SEO specialist in Build, and an Accessibility reviewer in Check: the SEO specialist makes the site easy to find, the reviewer checks it is easy to use with a keyboard or a screen reader.

items.title: Stages
items.text:
A team starts with four stages: Plan, Build, Check and Write & keep up. Drag a role from the role list into a stage. You can rename, move or remove a stage (one must stay), and add one with + Add a stage. Each stage has an "all at once" box for roles that work at the same time.

Each team also has a Default recipe, the recipe it runs by unless a chat picks another, and The Orchestrator may pick it.

items.title: Coordinators
items.text: Each team has its own lead, shown as "Team coordinator". It "steps in only when this team works beside another team; else the Orchestrator runs it." Switched off, the Orchestrator always runs that team itself.

items.title: Teams for a chat
items.text:
On the canvas, Teams for this chat chooses how the chat uses teams:

Mode What it does Orchestrator decides "It picks the teams and a recipe for each, and says why. A small change (a few lines in one or two files) needs no team: it makes it with one agent (or itself, where the project lets it write), and KOLONİ checks it all the same." It says why in one line, and sees how many agents each recipe opens ("Feature: 3-7 agents") to weigh the cost. Manual "You pick the teams it may use; it opens only those a message needs." For each team, pick its default recipe, No recipe, or another recipe. + Add a team with a recipe adds one. No teams "As before: it calls any role itself."

Use for new chats in this project keeps the choice for the project's new chats (Settings › This project › How agents work › New chats start with shows and changes it). Plan first is the switch in the permission level's menu under the message box, not here. While a team runs, Stop stops it and Finish now ends it with what it has.

items.title: Which roles the Orchestrator opens
items.text:
• Orchestrator decides: the teams it picks are where it starts, not a fence. It opens their roles, and beside them any built-in role the work needs (an Architect, a Researcher), as the note under its picks says: "Beside its picks it calls any built-in role the work needs, though not while a recipe runs." A role of your own keeps to your teams: outside its picks it does not open. Before it picks, any role opens. Before and after, a role that is only in teams with The Orchestrator may pick it off does not.
  • Manual: only the roles of the teams you picked.
  • No teams: any role.

In every mode:

  • A role you name in your message opens, even one switched off.
  • While a team's recipe runs, only the roles of its current step open. The three ready teams each have a default recipe, so a built-in role beside them opens once the recipe has ended in the turn, or beside a team with no Default recipe.
  • With two or more teams whose coordinators are on, the Orchestrator opens only the coordinators; each coordinator then opens roles by the rules above.
  • A role the Orchestrator opens beside the chat's teams is drawn on the canvas outside their frames.

items.title: A team that was not opened
items.text: In Manual, a turn that did work may open some of the teams you gave the chat and not others. The Orchestrator is first told once to open the missing team or say why not. If it still does not, a line at the turn's end says so, just above the Orchestrator's answer: "Quality was not opened in this turn." (or "… were not opened in this turn." for several). It is not on the Teams' work is ready card. A turn that opened none of them, because the Orchestrator answered itself, gets no such line.

items.title: Waiting for another team
items.text:
An agent of one team, its coordinator for example, can wait for the work of another team of the chat that has a coordinator: a file or an endpoint it needs. Waiting spends none of its steps, and it holds no place among the agents at work: its box says it is waiting.

  • When the other team's work in this turn has ended, the waiting agent is told how it ended, its coordinator's report and the files it changed.
  • When a message reaches the waiting agent, the wait ends there: it is told a message came, reads it, and may wait again.
  • One wait lasts at most 10 minutes. After that the agent is told the other team is still at work, and may wait again, go on without it, or end with what is left undone.
  • An agent waits at most three times in a turn.
  • Two teams cannot wait for each other: the second is told to do its part first.
  • A team not opened in this turn has nothing to wait for.
  • Stop on the waiting team ends the wait, and its work.

See Step limits for what a coordinator does when its steps run out.

A team at work: its frame on the canvas fills as its recipe runs.

The Web app team at work: its frame holds the recipe's steps and the Coder, and Ready for you waits at the end.

Only recipes kept in KOLONİ are offered here, not a folder's own recipes.

See Recipes and candidates.

items.title: Which way to work
items.text: KOLONİ offers several ways to get work done, from one message to a list of jobs while you are away. Start with the smallest that fits: every extra agent is more model calls, so more tokens, money or plan use.

items.title: At a glance
items.text: You want… Use… Because… What it costs a small, clear job done just ask, in a chat the Orchestrator does small jobs itself, or opens one sub-agent the fewest calls to see the plan before anything changes Plan first each message first gets a plan to approve one planning pass more a bigger piece of work, built, reviewed and tested a team with a recipe the recipe runs the steps in order, loops back on findings, and asks you where the recipe says (Feature: the spec, and the work at the end) one agent per step, more for each loop (Feature: 3 to 7) two or more agents to build one thing at the same time sub-agents, or a recipe step All at once each works on its own part, then the work is taken in each agent's calls agents to think a question through, with nothing changed a discussion agents talk in rounds and nobody writes anything each speaker's whole work so far is sent again at each step, so tokens grow faster than the talk the best of several attempts Evolve, or another recipe with Candidates 2 to 5 agents try the same job, each is scored by your measure command, and the best goes on each candidate in each round, plus the measure runs two models' answers side by side Compare one message goes to two models, and you keep one's work two runs of the message several jobs done while you are away ☾ Away your To-do tasks run one at a time, each in its own copy, and you decide when you're back what comes in each job, within the spend limit you set, if any a list of tasks worked through in order To-do ticked tasks wait in a chat's queue and run there one by one, each story in a topic of its own each task's turn

items.title: Examples
items.text:
"Fix the failing date test." Just ask. One bug in one place is a job for the Orchestrator, or one Coder it opens. Under Orchestrator decides too, a change of a few lines in one or two files gets no team: it says why in one line, and KOLONİ's checks run at the end all the same. With Teams for this chat → No teams, it never brings in a team.

"Add a password reset page, with review and tests." A team with the Feature recipe: in Teams for this chat choose Manual, then the Web app team, whose default recipe is Feature. A Spec writer writes the spec for you to approve, a Coder builds it, then a UI designer looks at its screens; findings go back to the Coder, at most twice. Then KOLONİ runs the tests, and has a big or security-touching change looked at by its own Reviewer and Security reviewer: 3 to 7 agents as its recipe counts them, KOLONİ's own reviewers on top. You take the work in on the Teams' work is ready card. See A web app with a team.

"Fix this crash, and make sure it stays fixed." The Bugfix recipe: in Teams for this chat choose Manual, then a team - the Web app team, say - and Bugfix as its recipe. A Debugger reproduces the crash with a test that fails, a Coder fixes it, then KOLONİ runs the tests - and has a big or security-touching change reviewed; a test that still fails goes back to the Coder. Cheaper than Feature: two agents, no spec and no review of a small fix.

"The backend and frontend teams must agree the API first." Two teams. Ask the Orchestrator for both: each team's coordinator writes the contract into the shared folder (contracts/) and asks the other team for its part with request_work. To have the coordinators talk it over, ask for a discussion between them: it takes a coordinator in once it waits (its part done, or waiting for the other team). (Rooms, where 2 to 6 agents wrote in one copy at once, are gone since 0.1.10.)

"Should we keep SQLite or move to Postgres?" A discussion. Ask the Orchestrator to have the Architect and a Database engineer discuss it. Nobody changes anything; you can join in and end it. Set a token limit under Settings › This project › Limits and money › More limits › A discussion's tokens, at most. See Discussions.

"Make this function faster, and keep the fastest version." Evolve. First set a Measure command (Settings › This project › When the work is done) whose last line is a score from 0 to 100. Evolve has three Coders try the job, each their own way, and tries again while the best score is under 80, for at most four rounds. That is up to twelve Coders: the most expensive way on this page. See Picking the best of several candidates.

"While I'm away tonight: update the dependencies, tidy the docs, and add tests to the parser." Work while you're away. The Orchestrator puts each piece on To-do and offers one line under its answer, "☾ Go away now?", with Go away and Change (or press ☾ Away on the chat's status line). Tick the tasks, set a stop time or a spend limit if you want one, and go: the tasks are worked through one at a time, each in its own copy, until you are back. Leave KOLONİ running: closing it ends the jobs. See A job while you're away.

items.title: The ready recipes
items.text: KOLONİ comes with these recipes: Feature, Bugfix, Review only, Integration, Quality check, Model change, Pipeline change, Infra change, Docs, Research, Spec, Analysis, Upkeep and Evolve. The Recipe cookbook lists each one's steps and which team runs it by default.

items.title: Keeping the cost down
items.text:
• Start small. A single agent that is not enough can still hand work on; a team that was too much has already spent.
  • Review only and Research report what they found and change nothing.
  • A discussion has a budget: set it before you start.
  • Give roles a tier, so easy jobs go to a fast model. See Tiers and Agents may use and Keeping costs down.

items.title: Answering for you
items.text: When you are away, questions can wait for you, or the Orchestrator can answer the safe ones itself.

items.title: Switching it on
items.text:
Settings › This project › When you're asked › When you're away:

  • Everything waits for you;
  • The Orchestrator answers what it safely can, after a number of minutes (0 to 1440).

A new project has the second, after 5 minutes; a project from before 0.1.5 keeps what it had - turn it on here. In a chat with no folder everything waits for you. With it, once you have not answered a card for that many minutes, "the Orchestrator picks, says why, and you see it under "Decided for you"". In the chat you went away from (☾ Away) and its tasks' chats it decides at once, whatever this setting says - also the cards that waited when you pressed Go away. While you type an answer to a question, it waits (2 minutes after your last key); once you are back, a card held so waits this setting's minutes again.

"An Orchestrator on a CLI uses one request of your plan for each answer." When it answers, it also reads your preferences and this project's rules as saved on the Memory page.

items.title: What it may decide
items.text:
Only:

  • an agent's question to you;
  • a recipe's "Ask me";
  • opening a sub-agent on its role's own model, while that provider has room;
  • going on or stopping at a sub-agent's step limit, where that card comes.

items.title: What always waits for you
items.text:
Commands, file changes, the web, installing, secrets, folders, new roles or skills, deleting, Take in, Discard, Commit, a different model that may cost money, and Stop. It also does not answer when the turn is over its token limit, the project is over its monthly budget, or the provider is over its limit.

The same rule holds in To-do task chats and while you're away. Your Orchestrator's own questions to you wait for you - but in a job while you're away (☾ Away), where it decides them itself: "The user is away. Decide yourself and say what you assumed in one sentence. Only if the answer is something only the user can know (a password, an account, a personal fact), answer park." Its answer and reason are under Decided for you. What it answers park is parked for you under Waiting for you, and so is a question it could not answer (no answer it could read, a CLI past its most or with tools of its own); the job goes on. A sub-agent's question there is asked with the second sentence alone. park decides nothing by itself - an option spelled "Park" is parked, not picked. See Work while you're away.

items.title: Decided for you
items.text:
What it answered shows under Decided for you on the Ready for you page, the project's whole list: who decided, what the Orchestrator chose, and why. Press OK to keep it, or Change → to give another answer while the agent that asked still works. If the answer cannot be undone any more, the row says why. The chat says it in one line at its top, "3 things were decided for you in this project and 2 wait for you here.", with Open in Ready for you. See Decisions. A chat with no folder keeps its own Decided for you while you were away box, with the same OK and Change →.

At Full auto the Orchestrator also answers questions in a chat you watch, at once, and some of KOLONİ's own cards, such as an agent's Continue / Stop here card at its step limit; those answers are in the same list. So does a command that Check what I said first ran without a card, or did not run, on a line of yours: "Coder ran … without asking" or "KOLONİ did not run … for Coder", with that line, until you press OK. Full auto alone does not let it open a sub-agent for you; of KOLONİ's own cards only the step limit's is decided while you're away. An Orchestrator on a CLI answers at Full auto only where When you're away is set to The Orchestrator answers what it safely can.

A decision the Orchestrator took without a card - a library, an approach - it can note for you with note_decision (0.1.11): it is in the same list, "Orchestrator · Decided: …" with its reason, until your OK; Change takes your own words. See Talking while agents work.

items.title: The same question again
items.text: If the same agent asks the same question again in the turn, with the same words and choices, it gets the Orchestrator's earlier answer at once, with no new request. Its line under Decided for you says it is "its answer when this was asked before". If you changed that answer, your answer is the one given.

items.title: Work while you're away (☾ Away)
items.text:
Before you leave - for an hour, an afternoon or the night - press ☾ Away on a chat's status line, or tell the Orchestrator you are going. The chat finishes its turn, then the To-do tasks you tick are worked through, one at a time, each in its own copy of the project: your project does not change while you are gone. When you are back you decide what comes in.

Work while you're away: work that runs while nobody watches.

items.title: Going away
items.text:
☾ Away is on the line over the message box of a chat with a folder (not in a plain chat; in a chat with no turn yet it waits: "Write to the Orchestrator first: Away finishes this chat's turn"). It opens the Away panel:

  • "The Orchestrator finishes this chat, then works through To-do in order.", and the level the tasks run at: this chat's.
  • Then from To-do, in this order: the project's open tasks (proposed or to do). The tasks proposed in this chat are ticked already ("new · from this chat"); older ones are not ("on To-do since Mon"). Tick up to 10; Move up and Move down change the order, which is saved to To-do. A ticked proposed task counts as your OK.
  • Decides for you and Always waits for you: see Questions and approvals.
  • Until, spend at most and kept out: none unless you set one. If the project has a monthly budget, the work spends at most what is left of it. Name a file or folder of the project to keep out (up to 20): a pattern such as src/* or a place outside the project is refused.
  • Where the project is not on Test and review: "While you're away, Test and review is suggested: tests, and a review of big or security-touching changes." Use Test and review sets the project to it (Settings › This project › When the work is done › After a change) - while you are away, nobody but KOLONİ's checks looks at the work (What KOLONİ checked).
  • Go away, or Cancel. How it works says the rest.

The Away panel, opened from ☾ Away on the chat's status line.

Go away is refused while Stop everything holds (press Resume first), while a To-do task is at work, and from a chat with no turn.

items.title: From the chat
items.text: Tell the Orchestrator you are going away (to sleep, out, in any language) and what it should work on meanwhile. It does none of that work itself: it puts each piece on To-do and offers one line under its answer - "☾ Go away now? Add a bye line, Say hello twice · Until 08:00 · at most 2.00 USD" with Go away and Change (the panel, there). The line names, and Go away takes, only the tasks the Orchestrator itself put on To-do in that turn, each by its name: a task a sub-agent proposed (one of a CLI's own sub-agents too), or an earlier turn's, stays in the panel for you to tick. It names them only where KOLONİ tells the Orchestrator's own To-do work from that of its CLI's own sub-agents: an Orchestrator on an API model, or on Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI run Native. Any other CLI Orchestrator - Codex, agy, and Claude Code or Copilot run any way but Native - gets a line that names no task: "Tick the tasks to take in Change". The limits are only those it heard from you. Nothing starts before your Go away. Only the Orchestrator offers this, in a turn you started in a chat with a folder - not in a Plan first turn, nor while the project is away. A newer offer takes the place of one not answered yet.

items.title: While you're away
items.text: The status line says where it stands: "Away · To-do 1 of 2: Add a bye line · 3 decided for you · 1 waits", then "To-do 2 of 2 looked at". The chip becomes I'm back, and the message box says "Write to come back…". Away lasts until you are back: press I'm back, or write a message in any chat of the project. Once every task was looked at, you get one notification if you set them up.

items.title: How the jobs run
items.text:
Tasks run one at a time, in the panel's order, once the chat you went away from has finished its turn (a turn that waits for your word does not hold them back). A task added meanwhile does not join. Each starts in a new chat named after it, its first message the task and what makes it done, and works in a copy of the project of its own.

  • Level and model: the job's chat has the model and the permission level of the chat you went away from (the Away panel says which). Its other settings are the project's, as in any chat: who changes the files, opening sub-agents, and the rest. Where that chat is at Full auto and Check what I said first works in the project (Full auto's judge's box for your words), the Orchestrator may run, by your own written words, a command the night would otherwise wait for you on.
  • Team and recipe: where you picked the teams in that chat (Manual), the job's chat has them, with their recipes.
  • The copy leaves out .git/, build/, dist/ and caches, and shares node_modules/, .venv/ and venv/ with the project. A job that needs what is not in the copy changes nothing and waits for you, its report ending "Needs the project itself: …".
  • A job that fails is tried once more in its chat. Failed twice, it could not be done, and the next one goes on.
  • A job that waits for your word waits, and the next one goes on.
  • Its notebook: a job writes in its task's notebook (its story's, where the task is of one): how each turn ended, the files it changed, the Orchestrator's Task note: lines and what its agents noted for the whole turn. The next night that works the task, or your own turn in its chat, goes on from it. 📓 on the task's row in its story's panel on To-do opens it.

items.title: In a git repository: each job on its own branch
items.text:
Where the project is the top folder of a git repository, a job works on a git branch of its own, koloni/<task> (for example koloni/fix-login-3f2a; koloni/task-3f2a where the task's title holds a secret KOLONİ knows, or one's shape - a branch's name goes to origin with its push), in a worktree of your repository, and commits there as it goes. How Go away finds the project decides it, once for every job:

The project The job In the morning No git; a folder inside a repository; HEAD on no branch; no commit yet; a merge or rebase under way; a git submodule; files in Git LFS works in a copy, as above Take in; its row says "In a copy: …" and why A git repository with no remote called origin works on its branch, commits there "No remote: merge it with git, or Take in." A git repository with an origin works on its branch, commits there its push waits under Waiting for you
  • Its first message says so: the branch's name, commit as you go, do not push - KOLONİ pushes this branch when you say yes. A CLI's instructions say the same. Only the files git tracks are in the worktree; what git ignores (.env, data, build output) is read in the project.
  • Its git: git status, diff, log, add and commit on its own branch run without a card. Its own git push is refused with "KOLONİ pushes this branch when the user says yes: go on" - no card, nothing parked. What reaches the rest of your repository (switching branches, reset, stash, fetch, config) is parked for you as any card is.
  • A script's push - a test or a build step that runs git push - fails inside the job's worktree: KOLONİ starts its commands with git set to push nowhere (a fetch still works). That is a safeguard, not a wall: see Known limits.
  • Where git will not when the job starts (HEAD detached since Go away, say), it works in a copy; its Orchestrator is told why, and its row says "In a copy: …".
  • At its end KOLONİ commits what the job left on the branch ("Orchestrator: fix the login") and keeps the worktree for your Take in - the same card as a copy's, file by file. Taking all of it in, or Discard, deletes the worktree and the branch, and the row says so instead of its commits: "Its branch koloni/fix-login-3f2a was deleted: its work was taken in." Nothing of it goes into your project by itself, at Full auto too. A file that holds a secret KOLONİ knows - in its content or its name: a provider key you saved, an MCP server's variable a secret's name holds, the page's key, one of the environment's, one given on a card, or any value with a secret's shape (ghp_…, sk-…, a password in an address) and the token or password it holds alone - is left out of that commit and stays in the job's worktree only; so is a file named as a secret, whatever it holds: .env.sample, api_keys.json, token.txt, a data file in a credentials or secrets folder (which names). The job's chat and its push row say which ("· left out: conf.txt (a secret KOLONİ knows, or named as one)"), and the rest of the work goes on. A file an agent committed on the branch itself is on the branch, not left out: the chat and the row do not call it left out, and Run refuses the push ("prov.txt on the branch holds a secret KOLONİ knows - take it off the branch first") - or, for one only named as a secret, asks first ("credentials.yaml on the branch is named as a secret (its agent committed it): Run anyway pushes it"). Such a secret never deletes the job's work: only a secret given on a card during the job, which an agent committed on the branch itself, has the branch deleted, and the chat says so.
  • Its second try after a failure, and the turn that goes on after your decisions in the morning, work in the same worktree, on the same branch.
  • KOLONİ also notes your repository's branches, stash, tags and remotes as the job starts and ends: anything that changed outside the job's branch meanwhile is on its row - "Changed outside its branch: main 1a2b3c4 → 3c4d5e6", "git's config changed during the job" - for you to look at. KOLONİ does not undo it: it may be yours.

The top bar shows "☾ Away · To-do 2 of 4" with I'm back and Stop all, and "· until 07:00" after it when you set a stop time. Ready for you's report shows the jobs too: since when, what they spent against the limit, and each job as it stands, with what its agents are doing right now. A job's chat says at the top when its jobs started, with a link back to their report.

items.title: Stricter rules while you're away
items.text:
• Commands follow the job chat's level. Below Full auto, a command no rule covers is parked for you (see Questions and approvals): it does not run, and the job goes on without it. At every level these are parked too: a command that deletes, overwrites or sends something off the machine; one that hands a command to a shell or another program; and one that installs into the project's shared dependency folders.
  • Ordinary file changes in the job's copy never ask: they are kept for your Take in. Files that steer agents, secret files and places outside the project wait for you as in a watched turn, and the job with them.
  • Kept-out places: a write to one, or a command that names one, is refused, and the try is on the report.
  • No MCP server tools are used.
  • CLIs: a CLI working with its own tools that is not started in the job's copy, or not held to it (Copilot working Native, agy when it may write), cannot work on a job: "… cannot work on a job while you're away".
  • At Full auto, where Check what I said first works, a command that deletes is first checked against your own words - your preferences, the project's saved rules and your messages in the chat you went away from, never the task's words - and runs in the job's copy without a card where a line of yours names it. Only a delete in the folder, on one line: a command of more than one line or continued (a backtick or a backslash at a line's end), a line that also sends work off the machine or touches a git remote, Docker's prune or volumes, and a delete of a file that steers agents (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) keep their card - in the chat you went away from as in a task's. See Permissions.
  • At Full auto, with Full auto's judge on (the default), a command the list does not stop is first looked at by a small model, reading the chat you went away from: one it finds risky is parked for you with its sentence, "KOLONİ's judge: …", and the job goes on. (In a chat you watch it is refused unless you chose Ask me; while you're away it is always parked.)

items.title: Questions and approvals
items.text:
A card no longer stops a job while you're away. A command's card - whatever its reason: no rule covers it, it deletes or sends something off the machine, its copy asks for it, Full auto's judge finds it risky - is parked: it does not run, the agent is told "KOLONİ parked this for the user, who is away: run "…". It did not run. Do what you can without it, and say in your summary what waits.", and the job goes on. A command a CLI run Native asks for with a tool of its own is parked the same way. The job's copy is kept for the morning even where it changed nothing. When the job has done what it can, it waits - "2 parked" - and the next job starts.

While you're away the Orchestrator decides at once, in the chat you went away from and in the tasks' chats, what it may decide for you (another chat of the project keeps its own minutes): an agent's question, a recipe's "Ask me", opening a sub-agent on its role's own model, and going on or stopping at a step limit. The cards already waiting when you press Go away are decided then. In a job, its own questions go to it too: "The user is away. Decide yourself and say what you assumed in one sentence. Only if the answer is something only the user can know (a password, an account, a personal fact), answer park." Its answer is on Ready for you, in its Decided for you column. What it answers park - and a question it could not answer - is parked for you, and the job goes on. In the chat you went away from, its own questions wait for your return. It does not answer once the project is over its monthly budget or a provider is over its limit.

These still wait for you, and the job with them (the next job goes on): changes of files that steer agents or are secret, the web, secrets, folders, another model that may cost money, new roles and skills, Take in, Discard, Commit. See Answering for you.

Only a job of an Away that runs parks: after I'm back, Stop all or the Away's end, the next card of a job still at work waits for you as before. KOLONİ's own commands (its checks) are never parked. A job that waits is shown under Waits for your word, on the report and in Ready for you.

items.title: Step limits while away
items.text:
Nobody is there to answer a Continue / Stop here card in a job, so none comes (in the chat you went away from, the Orchestrator decides that card at once):

  • A sub-agent that reaches its step limit stops. The job's Orchestrator is told its part is not done, and may tell it once to go on, with a new step limit.
  • One that stopped at its role's own limit, or stops again, ends. The job's Orchestrator hands what is left to another agent, or says in its report what is left undone. The job can still count as done: read its chat.
  • The job's Orchestrator counts no steps. If it goes round in circles (the same call failing the same way 5 times, or 10 calls in a row bringing nothing new), the job fails with that reason, is tried once more in its chat, and the night goes on with the next job.

See Step limits.

items.title: What stops the jobs
items.text:
Away ends when:

  • you are back: I'm back, or a message of yours (the job at work finishes; its cards then wait for you);
  • the stop time comes, if you set one ("Stopped at 07:00, the time you set.");
  • it has spent its money - what the tasks' chats and the chat you went away from spent since Go away ("Stopped at 5.02 of 5.00 USD, the spend limit."); the chat's turn at work is stopped too;
  • the project is over its monthly budget, or the Orchestrator's provider is over its limit, when the next job is about to start;
  • you press Stop all ("Stopped by you.");
  • KOLONİ is closed ("Stopped: KOLONİ was closed while you were away.");
  • the next job cannot start.

The time and the money are checked before each model step. A clock also watches the stop time and each job's hours at most, so a long command is cut at them too. Its minutes with nothing moving do not run out while a command or a model step of it is under way, an agent below the Orchestrator is at work, or it waits for your word: those have limits of their own. When the jobs stop, the job at work stops, its work kept in its copy, and is shown as Stopped. A job that waits for your word goes on waiting - but Stop all stops it too. When KOLONİ is closed, the jobs at work and those that wait count as could not be done: answer what waits before you close KOLONİ.

Stop everything in the top bar holds the jobs instead of ending them: the job at work and a job that waits for your word are stopped, the next job waits for Resume, and the time and money you set still end them.

If you set up notifications, you get one when every task was looked at, and one when a limit or Stop all ends Away - none when you come back yourself.

items.title: When you're back
items.text: The chat you went away from has one summary: "While you were away (23:10 – 07:42): 2 of 2 To-do done · 3 decided for you · 1 waits · 0.84 USD", what was done (waiting in Ready to take in), what was decided for you, Waiting for you, what waits (with Allow and go on / Refuse), Review and take in and On the canvas. KOLONİ opened again opens on Ready for you, on the night, until you have seen it there or its report on the canvas - never over a page you opened before the night was read.

items.title: The night on Ready for you
items.text:
KOLONİ opened after the night has ended opens on Ready for you, at its first look at the night - never taking you off a page you opened before that look; once the night has been on screen (here, or its report on the canvas), KOLONİ opens as you left it. Once the night has ended, the page opens on it: "Last night, 23:10 to 07:42" ("Night of Tue 24 Nov, …" once it ended more than a day ago), a time axis, and a lane for each job. A job's bar runs from when its first turn of the night began to when its last one ended - green where it finished, hatched honey where it waits for you, a dashed edge where it was stopped or could not be done. Each decision made for you in the job's chat that night - every one, however many - is a small hexagon on its lane, at its time, in the colour of who decided: filled while it waits for your OK, an outline once you have seen it. The strip draws only what KOLONİ's records hold: a job that never started, or whose turn is still open, has no bar and is still listed; a decision made in no job's chat (the chat you went away from) is on no lane. Under the lanes: what the marks mean, Not checked and what the night spent ("Spent 1.40 USD of 5.00 USD").

  • Not checked: N things opens on the list, job by job, in the words of each job's last Checked section of the night: tests not run (a guessed command while you were away, among others), a kind's check, the Reviewer or the live or browser try not done, After a change set to Nothing - and, where its push went, that GitHub's checks on it were not waited for (KOLONİ does not wait for them yet). A job with no Checked section of the night says "not known", never "nothing".
  • The whole report opens the night's report on the canvas.
  • Copy report as Markdown copies the whole night - named by its day, its jobs, what waits for you, what was decided for you on its jobs, what was not checked and what it spent - for a pull request's description. Every job's, agent's and model's word goes in a code span, masked as the screen shows it: a parked command too, as the list shows it.

What the night parked is on the page too, first in its list and under Last night: the push first, then the commands and questions - the rows of Waiting for you, with their own words. A job that waits only for what it parked is those rows, not a row of its own as well.

items.title: Waiting for you
items.text:
One list of everything the jobs parked, task by task in the night's order, each in the order it was parked: the command whole (never cut, in a fixed font; a secret KOLONİ knows, or one known by its shape - a Bearer token, a password in an address - shows as ***, and what runs is still the line as recorded), or the question; why, in KOLONİ's words (the card's reason, the judge's sentence, the Orchestrator's reason in quotes); and a warning where it reads like orders to a model. It is in Ready for you's waiting list (first, the push first of all), on the summary and on the report.

  • Run or Reject a command; a question takes one of its options, or a line and Answer.
  • Stop this task, on the task's line: what waits of it is closed, the task is stopped, and nothing of it runs.
  • You decide only once you are back (I'm back), and only while the task's job is not at work.
