A row that cannot be decided now says why: "Needs the project itself: Take in first" (a git line, or one naming build/, dist/ or another folder a copy leaves out - a copy has no .git; in a job on its branch a git line runs in its worktree), "Its copy is gone: there is nothing to run it in" (you discarded it - Reject still works), "Where it would run is not known: Reject it, or run it yourself" (a CLI that did not say its folder), "The project runs commands elsewhere now: Reject it, or set that back" (Docker or this machine, changed since), "Its CLI's own shell would run it: Reject it, or run it yourself" (a line Claude Code, Codex or another CLI asked to run in its own shell), "A server line: run it yourself". Each row says where it would run - the job's copy, or the project itself - its card's words, and "Runs a file an agent wrote" where it does.
  • Once every row of a task is decided, KOLONİ runs what you said Run, in the order it was parked, as it was recorded - the same line, its folder, the job's kept copy (or, where you took some of that copy in before your Run, the project itself), its time limit - with no card. Just before each, it looks again: a line whose copy was taken in or discarded after your Run ("its copy was taken in after your Run - run it yourself") does not run; and if anything in the job's copy changed after a line was parked - by an agent, a command, or an earlier line of this morning - Run does not run it ("the job changed files after this was parked: run it yourself", on the list as soon as it is known; where it runs in the project after a Take in, "its work was taken in after this was parked: run it yourself"). A command that runs none of the project's code (curl, wget, a file command) is the exception. A program an agent wrote is still refused, and so is a line naming a place you kept out. A Take in or Discard under way is waited for; while the lines run, the copy can be neither taken in nor discarded. Stop in the job's chat, or Stop everything, stops a line that runs, and the task (Try again works it). A message of yours waiting behind it then goes ahead: a turn of yours in the job's chat, which marks the job done once it ends, as any turn there does.
  • Then the same Orchestrator goes on in the same chat, in one turn, on KOLONİ's message: "KOLONİ: the user decided: ran "npm test" ("…"); rejected "git push"; answered "Which database?": "Postgres". Go on with the task." - what a line printed, and your answer, in quotes; a line that timed out or was stopped says so. It is a job's turn: held to a job's hours, in the kept copy its rows were parked in
  • never a later turn's of the chat, a message of yours, say - (a fresh one where you took some of it in), its work kept for your Take in - at Full auto too - and the judge looks at its commands. It does not start where the project is over its monthly budget: the job then waits with why. A message of yours in that chat meanwhile waits behind it.
  • A job's push (a git repository with an origin): "Push koloni/fix-login-3f2a to origin (github.com/…) — one commit by KOLONİ, 5 files · checks ✓ at 3c4d5e6", and "· opens a pull request into main" where the project's How a team's finished branch reaches yours is Open a pull request (Settings). Run pushes the branch's work as ONE commit by KOLONİ onto where it left main - never the agents' own steps, never what you had not committed when it began - and opens the pull request; Reject leaves the branch as it is. It waits for the task's other rows and its going-on turn ("Waits for this task's other decisions and its going-on turn"), and is made again with the branch's new commit after that turn: a yes is never for a commit you did not see. Just before it pushes, KOLONİ looks again: a branch deleted or moved since the job ended, a secret KOLONİ knows in what would go up - a file's content or its name, one an agent committed on the branch itself ("take it off the branch first") -, a branch of that name on origin ("origin already has a branch named …"), commits of yours on main not on origin ("push main first"; KOLONİ asks origin itself, never your remote-tracking branches), origin's main ahead of what you fetched ("fetch first"), an address git's config rewrites, the project on another branch than the one the job ended on, a branch changed since you read the row - nothing goes up, the row says why and waits, to try again once that is set right. Where a push to origin goes elsewhere now than when the job began, git's config or hooks changed since then, something changed outside the branch (its branches, stash, tags, remote-tracking branches, any other ref, git's own files), it changed a place you kept out, or it began from your work not committed, the row shows that first: Run anyway pushes - on Ready for you the row's words say what they do: Push (Push and open PR where the project's way is a pull request), Not now and Push anyway. The row names the address a push went to as the job began. Take in or Discard of the job closes the row ("Its work was taken in or discarded: nothing to push"); taking all of it in deletes the branch.

Back: the summary in the chat you went away from, and the report on the canvas.

The report shows when the jobs ran, what they spent and why they ended; nothing of it is in your project before you take it in. Its sections are Done, Waits for your word, Could not be done, Stopped, Not started, Decided for you (each of them is on Ready for you too, in its Decided for you column, with OK, Change and - once the agent that asked has finished - Change and redo: see Decisions), Proposed while you were away, not started (with Add to To-do or Dismiss) and Kept out, as you asked (what tried to change those places, refused).

Each job row says what its reviews found, and warns where its copy changed a place you kept out, or a file another job changed too. A job that changed nothing is "Done, nothing changed"; one whose work you took in or discarded says which files ("taken in: hello.py", "discarded: hello.py"). For each job:

  • Allow and go on or Refuse, when it waits for a change, a web request or an agent to open. A folder or a secret is answered in its chat: Open its chat. The job then goes on in its copy. What it parked is under Waiting for you.
  • Take in brings its work into the project; Take in all takes in every done job's work. Where two jobs changed one file, the two are joined line by line where their lines do not clash. A clashing line is not taken: the card of the job's kept copy, in its chat, decides it.
  • Try again, for a job that could not be done or was stopped, once you are back. It runs in the job's chat as an ordinary turn, not in a copy: its changes go into the project as that chat's level says.
  • See the changes or Open its chat.

Ready for you's report shows the same jobs, with a row per job and what waits for you.

See A job while you're away for the steps from going away to taking the work in.

items.title: To-do
items.text:
To-do holds a project's tasks, in your order: a story holds the tasks and bugs that go on together (see Stories). Ticked tasks run in a chat you give them to, one by one; you decide when each is done (see Doing tasks in a chat).

Since 0.1.10 To-do is a tab of the Work page, beside Ready for you - what was done and what waits for your word - so the morning's report, the decisions that wait and your tasks are in one place. Open Work on the left rail and its To-do tab ("To-do · 5": the tasks not done yet); Work opens on the tab you showed last. Ctrl+K's Work › To-do, a chat's Open it in To-do, a To-do row of Decided for you and the canvas's To-do → open the To-do tab - at that task, where one is named.

Its bar has the filters All, Todo, Running and Done, + Task (to the line where a task is added) and ☾ Away. ☾ Away opens the Away panel of the chat you have open, when it is a chat of this project that has had a turn (see Work while you're away).

items.title: Adding tasks
items.text:
Type in Add a task — title, then Enter. Once there is a title you can also set its Priority (high, normal, low), a Detail, Done when (optional), its Story (none, one of the project's, or New story…, named there) and its Type (task or bug), then press Add task.

A rough note can become stories and their tasks. Under the cards, type it in Your rough note, for example "the login page is broken on mobile, and we need a password reset", and press Split into tasks: the Hive keeper - the role that keeps the To-do list - splits it. A model writes it the way that role would: tasks that go on together as a story, and each task with a title, detail, done when, priority and whether it is a task or a bug. A story may come with a few notes for its notebook. A small note stays a single story or a single task; at most 4 stories and 12 tasks in all. It is asked once, with no tools, as Or write it asks (see Recipes) - your fast models first, then the other tiers', then the Orchestrator's model in the chat you are in, then your newest chat's. One that does not answer passes it on in the same press; with none answering, the message names each one asked and why, and how to fix it. The line under the buttons says which model is asked first and whether the request costs money.

The draft appears under the box for you to change: each story's title and tasks, and the tasks that stand alone. A story's Add adds that story; ✕ drops a task; Add all adds the rest. The tasks are yours and to do, as if you had typed them. Nothing is saved until you add it. Plan it in a chat works the other way: it opens a chat in the project whose first message asks for the Hive keeper. The Hive keeper reads the project and proposes tasks, which wait for you like any agent's.

A rough note split into two stories and three tasks by Split into tasks; nothing is saved until you add it.

Agents with the To-do tools (the Hive keeper and the Scout) can propose tasks and changes. A task an agent proposes may name its story: one of the project's open stories by its title, or a new one that shows on the list once you add one of its tasks. Its card says where adding it puts it - In story “Login” (new) · bug, "(new)" where the agent's proposal opened the story. Once you add one of its tasks, the story is yours: it stays though its tasks go. A story an agent opened goes when you reject all its tasks. They wait for you under Waiting for your word, on Work's Ready for you tab, with everything else that waits:

What waits Buttons A new task an agent proposed Add to To-do / Edit / Not wanted A task an agent thinks is done ("done?") Done / Not yet A change an agent proposed Change / Reject

When several new tasks wait, Approve all adds them all. Edit opens the task's title and detail; change them, then press Add to To-do.

items.title: Follow-up tasks
items.text:
After a turn in one of the project's chats, the Scout - the role that looks for what is left after each turn - suggests what to do next. It looks at the turn's record: work left undone or for later, a TODO, a step that failed. It proposes at most three tasks, each with the words they came from ("Proposed by the Scout, from: ..."). Those words must be an agent's in that turn, or the first line of a step that failed, not your message. Backticks, * and _ are ignored, and curly quotes count as straight ones, so `CHANGELOG.md` still matches CHANGELOG.md. A suggestion without such words is dropped. So is one that looks like a task already on the list, or one you rejected before. Each one dropped is written, with why, to runtime/logs/koloni.log, and shows in the Inspector of its canvas box (below). The suggestions wait under Waiting for your word like any agent's. An added task runs once you give it to a chat (Doing tasks in a chat). A suggestion whose words look like they try to give the agent orders says so on its row.

It is one small model request, with no tools, after each turn that did something: changed a file, ran a command, handed work to a sub-agent or had a step fail. A turn that only answered asks nothing. It is made once the turn is over, so your next message does not wait for it. It goes to the first model of the fast tier, or of the tier you chose. It skips a provider that is down, at its limit, out of its plan, or whose pay-per-token use you refused in that turn. With no such model nothing is suggested. The model is sent what was said in the turn, the files it changed, the steps that failed and the open tasks' titles. The secrets KOLONİ knows, and the variables the project passes to its commands, are masked. Jobs while you're away and To-do tasks' turns get suggestions too; discussions get none. Nothing is asked while the project is over its monthly budget.

After a turn of a story - one of its tasks' turns, or yours in its topic - a suggestion goes into that story, while the story is open; after any other turn it stands alone, in no story. One that comes from the first line of a step that failed is a bug, any other a task: KOLONİ tells them apart by the words a suggestion came from, not by what the Scout says.

Each request shows on the canvas as a Scout box under the turn, on a dashed line down from the Orchestrator: the model, "2 proposed · 1 dropped" (at Full auto also "Orchestrator added 1"), its tokens ("–" where not reported), and To-do →. Click it to see why each suggestion was dropped; a double click, or To-do →, opens Work's To-do tab. A request that failed or timed out says "Sent, not heard out". A turn where it was not asked has no such box.

At Full auto, in a turn you started, you are not asked. The Orchestrator's model decides each suggestion, add or reject, with one more request, and says why in one sentence. You see its word under Decided for you on Work's Ready for you tab. OK keeps it; Change undoes it while the task is still todo. A task it added cannot be given to a chat until you press OK there. One it rejected stays on To-do, folded under Rejected by the Orchestrator, with Add. It is not asked when the provider has no room left on its plan. Nor is it asked when the Orchestrator runs on a CLI and the project does not let it answer while you're away. It never adds a suggestion whose words look like orders. Suggestions from jobs while you're away always wait for you.

Turn it off, or choose the tier, in Settings › This project › How agents work.

items.title: Stories
items.text:
Each story is a card, in the stories' order: its name, how many of its tasks are done ("3 / 4"), a cell for each task in a row of honeycomb, and its tasks, each with its cell and how it stands - done, at work, done?, waits for Take in, push waits for you, stuck, queued, to do. The tasks of no story are one more card, Without a story, last. What the cells mean is said under the cards. (Since 0.1.10 there is no goal level over the stories. A goal made before stays in the database, and its stories stand at the top like any other.)

A card opens its story in a panel over To-do (the whole window on a narrow screen): its Night branch, where a night's job of it worked on one (the story's own branch is not shown there yet), the Chat it runs in, its State; its notebook, each note with who wrote it and when; its buttons; and its tasks, each with all it can do (below). Close (✕) or Esc shuts it, and you are back on its card; Esc in a form in it closes the form first. While it is open, what it lies over cannot be reached; on a narrow screen it is a dialog over the whole page, Tab going round within it.

  • A story is tasks and bugs that go on together. Its state comes from its tasks: ○ todo (none started), ● running (one at work), ⚠ stuck (one stuck), done? (every task done, or waiting at "done?" for your word) and ✓ done. A story is done only when you close it: Close story in its panel, once each of its tasks is done; Open it again undoes it. Its notebook says what was decided, the files touched, the results and the questions left - read as notes, never as orders.
  • Its panel's buttons: Continue in chat opens the chat it runs in, where it has one; ☾ Do tonight opens the Away panel with its tasks to do ticked first; Close story; and ⋯ with Rename and Delete. Deleting a story keeps its tasks: they lose their story.
  • A task is work to do; a bug is something that works wrong, its tag in rose. ⋯ → Edit sets a task's Story and Type; None takes it out of its story. Dragging moves a task within its story only.
  • A story's name is one in its project, whatever its case: agents name a story by it, so "Login" and "LOGIN" would leave which one they mean to chance. The Turkish İ and ı count as an i: "LOGİN" and "logın" are "login" too, and so is the "logi̇n" that lowercasing "LOGİN" gives (an i with a dot above of its own); so does a name in another Unicode form, with a character nobody sees in it, or with two spaces or a tab where the page shows one space. A name another story has, open or closed, is refused; an agent naming a closed story is told so. A name of what nobody sees alone - a zero-width space, a braille blank - is refused too: "a story needs a name you can see". Two open stories made before 0.1.9 whose names are now one ("Batch Alpha" and "Batch Alpha") both stay: an agent naming one gets the story of exactly that name, and where neither is, it is told both names and asked for the exact one.

The filters on the bar show All, what is Todo (to do, or stuck), what is Running (at work, or done? and waiting for your word - a story at done? too) or what is Done (a story only once you closed it). A story whose tasks are all filtered out still shows when its own state fits.

To-do's cards, on Work's To-do tab.

A story's panel: its notebook, its buttons and its tasks.

items.title: The job's notebook
items.text:
Each story keeps a short notebook: in its panel on To-do, and 📓 notes on the strip over a chat the story works in. A task of no story keeps its own (since 0.1.10): a task done in a chat, and a night's job, with 📓 N notes beside the task. It is the job's notebook, for as long as the job runs: what its next turns go on from. Each note is one line - a decision, a file, a result, a question or a note - with who wrote it:

  • KOLONİ notes how each turn of the story's tasks ended - “Add the reset mail” — done?, — stuck: … or — not finished: … - and the files that turn changed in the project, five at most.
  • The task's Orchestrator is asked to end its answer with up to three lines Story note: <decision|file|result|question>: <one line> (Task note: … for a task of no story); KOLONİ reads them off its answer. A note is a line that starts so, at the very start of the line: before it only up to three spaces, a list's -, * or +, bold, or backticks round Story note: alone; a numbered list's item (1. Story note: …) is not one. One in a code block, a quote, a table, a heading, inline code, an HTML comment or an HTML block (<pre>, <script>… to its closing tag; <div>, <table>… to a blank line) is not, nor is a line right after a quote's with no blank line between: Markdown reads it as the quote's too.
  • The Hive keeper adds its notes as it drafts a story.
  • A note left for the whole turn on the chat's shared notebook - the Notes tab - goes in too: yours, and an agent's post_note, at most three of the agents' a turn (a team's note to its own team stays the turn's). The agent is told whether it went in.

The strip over a chat a story works in, and its notebook opened from it.

Every turn of the job is given the notebook, quoted as data, not instructions - each line saying whose it is: KOLONİ's, an agent's or yours, so an agent's note never passes for your word: each task's first message and its fix round carry it, and so do the Orchestrator's instructions in a turn of yours in the story's (or the task's) topic, as the notebook stood when that turn began. Any agent of the turn reads it with read_notes; in place of the notebook of the turn before, which a turn of a plain chat is given. Once the job is over - its task done, its story closed - a turn in its topic is a plain chat's again. What a search of earlier messages finds (Search deeper, an agent's Recall) never includes a notebook a task's message carried. A session that summarises itself keeps short notes it was given and loses details read in passing (in one measured run, 5 of 5 notes against 0 of 5 details buried in a long log): the notebook is what is not lost. Long content - a file, an output - is read again when it is needed.

What agents write there goes to models at every turn, so KOLONİ holds it to a few rules: the secrets KOLONİ knows, and the variables the project passes to its commands, are masked, and a word next to a character nobody sees - a zero-width space, a joiner, a braille blank - is hidden whole (***), so a secret split by one is not kept in parts (an emoji family, an emoji with a hidden variant mark such as ⚠️, or a Persian word joined by one shows as *** too, and so does a word another mask already cut into); a line that reads like orders is left out (in runtime/logs/koloni.log) - and so is a line with a zero-width character between two plain letters (a-z, A-Z), whole: it reads like orders hidden from the eye; each note is one line of at most 200 characters, and the newest 20 are kept. Notes kept before these rules are checked again as they are given. Masking knows a secret by its own characters: one split by a space or a line's end, or written with look-alike letters, is not found.

items.title: Your tasks
items.text:
In a story's panel, tasks are listed by priority, then in your order. Drag a task, or use ⋯ → move up / move down. The ⋯ menu also has Edit, Waits for ("it starts once these are done") and Delete.

A task's state shows as a tag, such as queued, running, "needs you", "needs you · Take in", stuck, or done.

items.title: Doing tasks in a chat
items.text:
Open a story and tick the tasks you want done - Tick its open tasks ticks them all - and the bar under them says "N selected · Do in chat ▾". Ticks stay while you open another card: tasks of two stories go to a chat together. Its menu gives them to This chat - "…" (the chat you have open, when it is a chat of this project) or to A new chat, named by the first of them. "Each story goes into its own topic; a task without a story gets a topic of its own. They wait in the chat's queue." KOLONİ checks your ticks as they stand when you press it: a task done meanwhile, one waiting in another chat's queue, a proposal, one the Orchestrator added for you that waits for your OK, a night's job or a task of another project is refused, and so is a story's task while another task of that story waits or works in another chat ("do the story there") - then nothing is queued. Over the project's monthly budget nothing is queued either.

A story given to a new chat: each task as itself, and "Done?" under it.

The chat runs them one by one. Above its message box, N wait lists the queue - the task at work "· running", each waiting one with Remove (back to To-do) - and "+ your message goes first when you send one": a message of yours goes before the next task, and goes on in the topic you were last in. A task that waits for others (⋯ → Waits for) is passed over until they are done; the next ready task goes first.

A task's turn is an ordinary turn of that chat: at the chat's level, on the chat's model (Claude Code and the other CLIs included), and what needs your word asks on its cards there. Its first message is the task - in the chat as From To-do · task 2 / 3, its title and what makes it done, the whole brief folded under. A story's tasks go on in one topic - a line Topic · Story · … · 📓 notes over it, its 📓 a button that opens the story's notebook once the notebook has a note - so the Orchestrator and a CLI that goes on in its session remember the task before; after a task that ended badly, or a day later, the story's next task starts in a new topic, told the story so far (A story's session). A task of no story has a topic of its own; given to a chat again, it starts in a new one - only a fix round, or a turn Stop everything cut, goes on in the topic it had.

"A task not finished gets one fix round; still not, it is stuck and the next goes on." Under a task's last turn the chat asks:

  • Done? - "…", with the Scout's view if a fast model wrote one: Yes, done or Not yet (back to To-do).
  • Stuck - "…", with why: Fix it (one more round in its topic), Open it in To-do, or Leave it (the card folds to one line).
  • Story done? - "…", once every task of a story is done: Close the story or Add a task (it joins the story and this chat's queue).

A task's turn works as long as it makes progress. Once nothing has moved for Settings › The app › More limits › Stuck after this many minutes with no progress (30 unless you change it) - no file of the turn changed, no agent finished its work, no failing command passed - it stops, its work kept, and counts as not finished: its fix round comes, then it is stuck and the next task goes on. The same happens, as a last resort, after An unattended turn runs at most (hours) (8 unless you change it; empty: no limit). A task's turn also waits for its checks before it ends, so a check that failed gives it its fix round.

Stop on a task's turn, a restart of KOLONİ, the project's monthly budget, a task's turn stopped by the project's token limit or its provider's limit, or archiving the chat stops the queue: the task and those waiting go back to To-do, and one line in the chat says why ("The To-do queue stopped: …"). Stop everything and ☾ Away only hold it: the stopped task goes back to the head of the queue, and Resume - or your coming back - goes on.

items.title: A story's session
items.text:
A story's tasks go on in one topic of the chat they run in: its Orchestrator sees the turns of the task before, and on Claude Code goes on in the same session. The next task starts a new topic of the story - a new session - instead where:

  • a task of it got stuck, or went back to To-do (Not yet, Stop), so its wrong guess is not carried on - that task too, given to the chat again, starts there. A turn Stop everything cut is held, not judged: at Resume it goes on in its topic;
  • a day has passed since its last turn there.

A session's size starts no new topic: Claude Code compacts its own session, and Copilot's and Codex's are bound by KOLONİ already, at 75% (by default) of their window (Going on from the last turn).

The first task in the new topic is told the story so far - KOLONİ's own record of each earlier task and how it stands, and the files their turns changed - with the notebook. This is decided as each task starts: a Not yet on a task while the next one works moves only the ones after it. Any turn's Orchestrator is told the names of the chat's other topics, with how a story's or a To-do task's stands: (done), (done?) or (stuck).

items.title: A story's branch
items.text: In a project that is a git repository, a story's tasks run on the story's own branch (koloni/<its name>-<4 characters of its id>), one after another - each turn in a worktree of it, so nothing of the story is in your project until you close it. Close the story runs KOLONİ's check on the branch - the tests its tasks wrote: it passes, the branch is merged into yours, or sent as a pull request where the project's finished work goes so (Branches); it fails, the branch waits and the story's last task is stuck with why - Fix it goes on on the branch, then close it again. It goes in by itself only at Full auto, or where its check ran and passed; below that, a branch nothing tested waits on its Merge (or pull request) card in the chat, and Discard there keeps the branch and the story open. A branch holding a secret KOLONİ knows is held too, its last task stuck with why (KOLONİ looks at the files as the branch ends; a pull request sends its whole history, so a secret committed and removed on it still goes up). Where the branch cannot be opened - your folder on no branch, or on the story's branch itself - nothing goes in and the story stays open; only a branch deleted from git counts as gone. A chat holding a story's branch is not deleted until the story is closed or deleted; a deleted story's branch stays in git, and its chat says so. A task added to a closed story opens it again. A message of your own in the story's topic works in the project, not on the story's branch. A task of no story has a small branch of its own, merged at the end of its turn as a team's branch is (at Ask before changes, on a card). A project with no git has no branch: the tasks work in the project, agents holding the files they change as in any chat. Where the chat's Orchestrator is a CLI that works with its own tools in the project, its tasks work in the project too.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
KOLONİ is one Python process that serves a React page and an HTTP API on 127.0.0.1, keeps its data in SQLite, and runs agents as asyncio tasks.

What runs where. The diagrams' sources are in docs/diagrams/, with a README on editing them.

items.title: Backend (app/)
items.text:
• main.py builds the app. At the start it applies a staged restore, backs up and migrates the database, tidies it, marks work that was cut off as interrupted, seeds the built-in roles and the first providers, and sets the page key. It serves the built page from frontend/dist on the same origin. FastAPI's own docs pages are switched off.
  • api/: the HTTP routes, all under /api.
  • agent/: the agent runner. AgentRunner runs one turn per asyncio task. It is split into mixins (spawning sub-agents, cards and approvals, memory, limits, discussions, work while you're away and more); the package docstring lists them.
  • Model clients: model_client.py (OpenAI-compatible), model_anthropic.py (the Anthropic Messages API), model_cli.py (a CLI as one step per model step), model_session.py (a CLI session whose only tools are KOLONİ's, over MCP), model_native.py (a CLI with its own tools), model_agy.py (agy). providers.py chooses which one runs a role.
  • db/ and alembic/: SQLAlchemy models and migrations. The database is backed up before a migration.
  • workspace.py: file access confined to the project folder and the folders the user opens.
  • copies.py: each sub-agent works in its own copy, outside the project; its changes come back by a three-way merge.
  • git.py: running git - a file merged line by line, your commits, and a team's branch and worktree, made from a snapshot of your folder.
  • commands.py, command_runner.py, executors/: which commands ask, and running them on this machine or in Docker. judge.py: Full auto's check of your words (Check what I said first); disposable.py: whether a delete is disposable.
  • backlog.py: To-do's tasks and a chat's queue of them (Do in chat), their fix rounds and the Scout's follow-up tasks. stories.py: stories (and the goals over them, hidden since 0.1.10), a story's topic and its notebook.
  • away.py: ☾ Away, the To-do tasks worked through while you are away.
  • cli_surface.py: the version and protocol of each CLI KOLONİ runs, and whether it was measured.
  • clock.py: the app's clock: it looks at each night while you are away, and sends the day's summary.
  • mcp_client.py: the client for the user's MCP servers. mcp_bridge.py: the small program a CLI starts as its MCP server, which relays to KOLONİ's own tools.

items.title: Frontend (frontend/)
items.text: React, Vite, React Flow (the canvas) and Zustand (the store, src/state/store.ts). src/api/generated.ts holds the API's types, generated from the backend's schema by scripts/export_openapi.py; after changing an API shape, run npm run generate:api in frontend/.

items.title: How the page talks to the API
items.text:
Every /api request carries the page key in the X-KOLONI-Key header (or ?key= for event streams and downloads). The page takes the key from the link KOLONİ prints, or swaps a one-time code for it, and keeps it in the browser's local storage. A few doors need no key: the health check, Claude Code's status line, and the one-time code exchange.

Events reach the page over server-sent events, per conversation.

items.title: How a turn flows
items.text:
1. The page posts a message to the conversation.
  2. The server records it and starts a run as an asyncio task.
  3. The Orchestrator (the Lead role) works with its tools and may open sub-agents, each in a working copy.
  4. Anything that needs the user becomes a card; the run waits for the answer.
  5. A finished sub-agent's changes are taken into the project, or put before the user on a card first.
  6. Every step is recorded, and the canvas draws the turn from that record.

The same turn, step by step: where it waits for you, and how the page hears of each step.

A message's journey, from Send to the chat and the canvas. (full size)

items.title: The data model
items.text:
The database is SQLite, its tables in app/db/models.py. A project has chats; a chat has turns (runs); a turn has agents, and an agent has messages, tool calls, file changes, commands and take-ins (merges). Memory, knowledge and to-do tasks belong to a project; providers, roles, teams and recipes are the same for every project. Working copies are folders, not rows.

The main tables, their keys and how they link. (full size)

items.title: Inside the agent runner
items.text:
app/agent/ holds AgentRunner, built from mixins, one per part. A turn picks its model by tier, then loops: in step mode KOLONİ builds the history (compacting it when it is too long), asks the model, and runs each tool call it asks for. A CLI in session or native mode keeps the loop itself. Limits, slots, observing, recording and the rest work around every step.

The agent runner's parts and how a step flows through them. (full size)

items.title: Contributing (DCO)
items.text:
• Sign off every commit (Developer Certificate of Origin): git commit -s.
  • CLA: a pull request agrees to the short-form CLA.md in the repository, which lets the project relicense the contribution. KOLONİ is AGPL-3.0-or-later.
  • Keep a change small and focused, and deliver a behaviour end to end: backend and page together.
  • scripts/verify.ps1 must pass. See Tests and verify.
  • Review the staged diff before you commit. Never add secrets, caches or runtime/ output.
  • Check the licence of any source code or asset before you take it.
  • No fake agents, progress or usage: a value KOLONİ does not know stays unknown.

items.title: The changelog
items.text:
CHANGELOG.md is in English and every release looks the same:

  • One heading per version: ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD. Unreleased work goes under ## [Unreleased]. Versions follow Semantic Versioning.
  • Inside a version, only these sections, in this order, and only those with entries: Added, Changed, Fixed, Security, Removed, Deprecated.
  • One line per entry: - **Area**: what the user can now do or will notice, in plain words. The area is a page or part the user knows (Canvas, Chat, Ready, To-do, Agents, Models, Tools, Memory, Knowledge, Usage, Settings, CLIs, Install, Docs).
  • Say what changed for the user, not how it was built. No commit hashes or internal names. A breaking change starts with Breaking:.
  • A migration that changes saved data says so.
  • Link to the docs where a feature is explained.

items.title: Run from source
items.text: KOLONİ always runs from its source folder; Install covers that.

items.title: Live reload for the page (Windows)
items.text:
./scripts/dev.ps1

It starts the backend with KOLONI_DEV=1 and KOLONI_OPEN_BROWSER=0, and Vite's dev server on port 5173. Open the link the backend prints, with the port changed to 5173. KOLONI_DEV=1 lets the backend accept the page from port 5173. Stopping the script stops the backend too.

Vite sends /api to 127.0.0.1:8790, so run the dev backend on the default port.

items.title: After changing an API shape
items.text:
cd frontend
npm run generate:api

This writes frontend/src/api/generated.ts from the backend's schema. The full check fails while the committed file is stale.

items.title: Build this guide
items.text:
uv pip install -e ".[docs]"
zensical build      # the site in runtime/site
zensical serve      # or watch it at http://127.0.0.1:8000

.github/workflows/docs.yml builds the guide, checks it, and pushes it to the gh-pages branch under manual/, beside the site's root files in pages/, when started by hand, and on each push to main that changes the guide once the repository variable PAGES_ENABLED is true. Pages must be switched on once in the repository's Settings → Pages: Deploy from a branch, gh-pages, / (root) (.github/CI.md has the custom domain and DNS steps).

items.title: Licenses
items.text: KOLONİ, the whole project (backend and frontend), is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later (AGPL-3.0-or-later): see LICENSE and NOTICE in the repository. COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md says what the AGPL asks and how to ask for a commercial license, and contributions come under the short CLA.md.

items.title: What KOLONİ includes
items.text:
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md lists every third-party package KOLONİ ships, with its licence text: the page's bundled packages, its fonts (IBM Plex, under the SIL Open Font License), the Python packages, and other assets. It is generated by scripts/notices.py from pyproject.toml, frontend/package-lock.json and the installed packages; run it again after npm ci. Its last section lists the packages whose licences need a closer look.

Other included works:

  • The model catalogue (app/models_dev.json), trimmed from models.dev, under the MIT licence (app/models_dev.LICENSE).
  • The draw.io viewer (frontend/public/drawio/), unchanged, under the Apache License 2.0. KOLONİ's own script beside it keeps the viewer from loading anything from outside.

items.title: The full check
items.text:
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium   # once
cd ..
./scripts/verify.ps1

verify.ps1 stops at the first step that fails. In order:

  1. pytest -q -n auto (in parallel);
  2. ruff check app tests scripts alembic;
  3. scripts/check_file_size.py (below);
  4. ty check app;
  5. vulture: code nothing calls, in app/ and scripts/ (below);
  6. pyrefly check: a second type checker beside ty (below);
  7. in frontend/: the generated-API-types check, oxlint, the type check, the complexity check, Vitest, the build, the guide's checks (below; skipped when Zensical is not installed), and the Playwright end-to-end tests.

-BackendOnly runs only the first six. On Linux and macOS, run the script with pwsh; on Linux, install Playwright's browser with --with-deps.

The parallel test run can load a machine heavily. PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS sets how many processes -n auto starts.

items.title: Complexity
items.text:
No function may be more complex than 12 (McCabe: 1 plus each branch, loop, case, catch, ?:, &&, || and ??). Python's gate is ruff's C901 in the ruff step: a failure names the function and its value (is too complex (14 > 12)). The frontend's is npm run check:complexity (frontend/scripts/complexity.mjs), which fails when a function not in frontend/complexity-baseline.json is over 12, or a baselined one went up; each line gives the file, line, key (file::Outer>name) and value. Split the function; don't raise the limit.

Functions that were already over 12 when the gates came in are debt: a # noqa: C901 on the def line in Python, an entry in the baseline in the frontend. Both lists only shrink. When a function drops under 12, delete its noqa; the frontend check says you can lower or remove N baseline entries, and npm run check:complexity -- --update rewrites the baseline, lowering or dropping entries, never adding one. Renaming a baselined function makes it look new: rename its key in the baseline by hand.

items.title: File size
items.text:
No source file may be longer than 1,500 lines. scripts/check_file_size.py reads the .py, .ts and .tsx files under app/, frontend/src/, scripts/ and tests/ that git tracks or would track (gitignored files and the generated frontend/src/api/generated.ts are skipped) and fails on a file over the limit. Split it; don't raise the limit.

The files that were already over it when the check came in are listed in scripts/file_size_allow.txt, each with its line count then (10612 app/agent/__init__.py). The list only shrinks: a listed file fails when it grows past its count, and when it drops to 1,500 lines or under or is gone - take its line off. A listed file that shrank is a note with its new count. scripts/check_file_size.py --update lowers each count to its file's own and takes off the files at the limit or under, or gone, then checks; it never raises a count nor adds a file. Moving or renaming a listed file makes it look new: change its path in the list by hand.

items.title: Dead code and a second type checker
items.text:
These two are the maintainers' and CI's only: they are in neither requirements-dev.lock nor an install or update of KOLONİ. Install them into your .venv once (the lint extra, locked against the dev lock):

uv pip install -r requirements-lint.lock

Without them, verify.ps1 stops at its vulture step with that line.

vulture fails on code nothing calls in app/ and scripts/, where it is 80% sure or more ([tool.vulture] in pyproject.toml; under 80 it is mostly FastAPI routes and pydantic fields it cannot see used). Delete what it finds; a name it takes for dead wrongly goes in ignore_names there, with why.

pyrefly check --min-severity warn is a second type checker beside ty, on app/ (pyrefly.toml): its default checks but invalid-annotation, which the runner's mixins (self: "AgentRunner") trip, and its warnings fail it too. Fix what it finds. Where it is wrong, put # pyrefly: ignore[<kind>] # (why) on the line as its first comment - ruff then leaves the line's length alone; where ruff format would split the line for the comment, a # fmt: skip on the statement keeps it. pyrefly-baseline.json holds, for now, findings in files that other open branches change.

items.title: End-to-end tests
items.text:
The Playwright tests start their own KOLONİ and a scripted model server, never a real one. They run with one worker.

  • KOLONI_E2E_PORT sets the test KOLONİ's port (9480 by default).
  • FAKE_MODEL_PORT sets the scripted model server's port (8081 by default); a stand-in llama server uses the next port. Two runs at once need model ports at least 2 apart.

items.title: The guide's checks
items.text:
uv pip install -e ".[docs]"                       # Zensical, once
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/check_docs.py    # --no-build: check runtime/site as it is

It builds the guide, then fails on a link to a missing page or #anchor, a link in README.md, SECURITY.md or CHANGELOG.md to a missing file, a file a diagram's "From:" line names that is gone, or a setting the guide's Settings and Every setting pages name that the app's Settings page does not show (exact text, ignoring case). CI runs it on each push, and the Pages workflow before it publishes the guide.

items.title: Refreshing the guide's pictures
items.text:
The guide's screenshots in docs/images/ and its short videos in docs/videos/ are taken from the real app by frontend/e2e/guide-shots.spec.ts, with the scripted model, in the light theme: pictures at 1280×800 (the Away panel's at 1280×900, so it shows whole), videos at 1280×720. A video is Playwright's own WebM recording, with a JPEG poster beside it; a page shows it with a <video> tag. The spec is skipped in an ordinary run. To take them again, build first, then from frontend/:

npm run build
$env:KOLONI_SHOTS = '1'; $env:KOLONI_E2E_PORT = '9500'; $env:FAKE_MODEL_PORT = '9510'
npx playwright test e2e/guide-shots.spec.ts --workers=1

A picture or video whose text names a folder of your home fails its test, so neither shows your own paths. Look at each one before you commit it.

In a page, a video's src is written from the page's own file (../videos/team.webm in docs/agents/teams.md) and its poster from the built page, one folder deeper (../../videos/team.jpg): Zensical rewrites the first and not the second.

items.title: Tests against real things
items.text:
Tests marked live are left out of verify:

.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_live.py -m live
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_docker_executor.py -m live

The first needs a model server on port 8080 and, for its CLI tests, signed-in claude and codex. The second needs a Docker daemon and the alpine image.

items.title: CI
items.text:
Each push and pull request to main runs the same checks once, on Ubuntu with Python 3.12 (.github/workflows/pr-check.yml): pytest, ruff, the file size check, ty, vulture and Pyrefly, the API types, the frontend's lint, typecheck, complexity, unit tests and build, and the guide's checks. A change to the guide or the plans alone runs only the guide's checks, or nothing.

End-to-end tests and the backend on Windows and on Python 3.13 and 3.14 run in heavy.yml, on each pull request to main beside PR Check, by hand from the Actions tab, or weekly once the repository variable HEAVY_WEEKLY is true; the Docker image only by hand. full.yml runs both on a branch with no pull request (gh workflow run full.yml --ref <branch>). The repository is public, so GitHub's standard runners cost nothing; .github/CI.md has the table and the reasons.

items.title: The guide's diagrams
items.text:
Each picture in the guide is a draw.io file here, name.drawio, with the SVG the pages show beside it, name.svg. The .drawio is the source: change it, then draw the SVG again. Each diagram's footer names the code it was drawn from and the day it was checked against it.

File Shown in system-map.drawio Architecture concept-map.drawio Home, KOLONİ in 5 minutes turn.drawio Chat and canvas permissions.drawio Permission levels memory.drawio Memory topics.drawio Memory › Topics models.drawio Providers teams.drawio Recipes and candidates night.drawio Work while you're away security.drawio Security model message-flow.drawio Architecture data-model.drawio Architecture runner.drawio Architecture cli-modes.drawio Set up a CLI working-copy.drawio Working copies and Take in recipe-engine.drawio Recipes and candidates install-update.drawio Backup and update proven-finish.drawio What KOLONİ checked

items.title: Opening and editing
items.text:
• In KOLONİ: open this folder as a project and click a .drawio file in the Workspace. KOLONİ's own draw.io viewer draws it; it shows the diagram, it does not edit it.
  • To edit: draw.io desktop, or app.diagrams.net (File → Open from → Device).

Keep the files easy to diff and the SVGs plain:

  • Save uncompressed (draw.io: File → Properties, untick Compressed). The files are plain XML, one shape per line.
  • Keep labels plain text: no Formatted Text (html=1) and no word wrap (whiteSpace=wrap); break lines yourself. Plain labels become plain SVG text, which every viewer shows the same way.
  • Give every shape a place. A shape without one is placed by KOLONİ's viewer, not where you meant.
  • When the code a diagram rests on changes, change the diagram and its footer's date.

items.title: Drawing the SVG again
items.text:
Draw the SVG with KOLONİ's own viewer, so every picture is drawn the same way:

  • In the Workspace, open the diagram and press Save as SVG. The picture is written beside it, over the old one: docs/diagrams/memory.drawio gives docs/diagrams/memory.svg.
  • Or ask an agent with the Diagram pictures tool for it ("draw docs/diagrams/memory.drawio as an SVG").

Both run the vendored viewer (frontend/public/drawio/) in a browser that loads nothing from the network. draw.io's own File → Export as → SVG also works, but its SVG differs from KOLONİ's; don't mix the two.

items.title: Picking the best of several candidates
items.text:
Give one job to several agents, score each result, and keep the best. The ready recipe Evolve does this with three Coders.

  1. Set a measure command. Settings › This project › When the work is done › Measure command: a command whose last line of output is a number from 0 to 100, for example python measure.py. Higher is better.
  2. Make the recipe. Agents → Recipes: pick Evolve and press Copy it, or draw your own step whose Who is Candidates (the best one goes on). Choose how many (2 to 5), their models (Auto, the Orchestrator picks, Same model or I pick each), and a Target score if you want one. With a loop, the step is tried again while the best score is below the target - with no measure command, one round only: there is no score to compare.
  3. Use it. On the canvas, Teams for this chat → Manual, pick a team and this recipe. Then write your message.
  4. Pick the winner. Each candidate works in its own copy and is scored. A card lists the scores and asks which candidate's work goes on. At Full auto the best score goes on by itself.
  5. Take it in on the Teams' work is ready card.

A new round's result replaces the kept one only if it scores higher.

See Recipes and candidates.
path: Picking the best of several candidates

items.title: Adding an MCP server safely
items.text:
An MCP server runs with your rights on this machine. These steps add one while keeping its tools behind your cards.

  1. Add it. Tools → Add → A server, ready-made (or from its page, pasting its setup text). Check the command and its arguments. Put any token in a variable, not in the arguments: "Other programs on this machine can see the arguments of the command".
  2. Look inside first. For an npx or uvx server, open its row and use What does it do?. It reads the package without running it and lists what it may reach: files, programs, the network. "This is where to look, not a verdict."
  3. Read its tools. Press Read its tools. Keep First look for it in osv.dev's known-malware records ticked.
  4. Leave it watching for a while. Until you trust it, every call of its tools asks you on a card, at every level, and the card shows the tool's own description. Use it in a chat and read what it asks.
  5. Trust it with Trust this server once you are content. If the page warns that it updates itself, pin a version in its command; otherwise your trust covers future versions too.
  6. Choose per tool. Under When an agent calls it, keep Ask for anything that changes things, choose Runs without asking only for tools that just read, and Off for what you do not need. (Ask asks at every level, Full auto too.)
  7. Give it only to the roles that need it, under Roles that may use it. Every tool's description is sent at every model step.

KOLONİ takes trust back by itself when the command or its variables change, or a new reading finds new or changed tools.

See MCP servers and trust.

items.title: A job while you're away
items.text: To-do tasks that run while you are away, for an hour or the night, each in its own copy of the project, so nothing changes until you take it in.

items.title: Before you go
items.text:
1. In a chat with a folder, tell the Orchestrator you are going away and what to work on meanwhile. It puts each piece on your To-do list and offers one line under its answer: "☾ Go away now?". The tasks run on this chat's model, at its permission level (the Away panel says which): below Full auto, a command no rule covers is parked for you - it does not run, and the task goes on without it.
  2. Press Change on that line - or ☾ Away on the chat's status line - to see the Away panel: the tasks from this chat are ticked; tick others from To-do too, and put them in order with Move up / Move down. Set when to stop (Until a time, or spend at most an amount) and what is kept out (files or folders no task may change). With neither limit set, the tasks run until they are done: there is no default spend limit, only your monthly budget if you set one.
  3. Press Go away. The chat finishes its turn, then the tasks start one at a time. The status line says which, and how many cards were decided for you.

The Orchestrator decides for you, at once, what it may: an agent's question - in a task, its own too -, a recipe's "Ask me", opening a sub-agent on its role's own model. What only you can know, and every command's card, is parked for the morning; the task goes on. A change of a file that steers agents, the web, a secret or a folder waits for you. Leave KOLONİ running: closing it ends Away.

items.title: When you're back
items.text:
1. Press I'm back, or write in the chat. The chat shows one summary: "While you were away (23:10 – 07:42): 2 of 2 To-do done · 3 decided for you · 1 waits".
  2. Under Waiting for you, Run or Reject each parked command and answer each parked question; once a task's are all given, what you said Run runs in its copy and its Orchestrator goes on in its chat. Stop this task closes the rest.
  3. For a task that waits for a change, a web request or an agent to open, press Allow and go on or Refuse. For a folder or a secret, Open its chat and answer there.
  4. Review and take in opens Ready for you; On the canvas opens the report. Look at each task's changes (See the changes), then Take in the ones you want, or Take in all.
  5. Try again runs a task that could not be done, or was stopped, again as an ordinary turn.
  6. Proposed while you were away, not started lists tasks the agents thought of; Add to To-do keeps them.

See Work while you're away.

items.title: Teaching an expert
items.text:
An expert is a role that knows one topic from its sources, advises and reads only.

  1. Make the expert. Agents → New role → An expert. Fill in Knows with the topic, and its sources, one a line: a docs site's address, files or a folder in the project. Press Create expert. The role is named "topic expert".
  2. Let it learn. On the Memory page's sources part, the topic's card shows what learning may cost beside Learn. Set At most this much a learning (USD) and Learn with (the model that writes the guide) if you want, then press Learn. KOLONİ reads the pages and a model writes a short guide.
  3. Check what it learned. Open the card: Guide shows the guide, Pages what was read and skipped, and Not known yet what it could not answer. Press Try it and ask what an agent would.
  4. Give it more if needed: add sources on its Settings tab and press Learn more. Learning again reads only what changed.
  5. Use it. The Orchestrator opens the expert when a job needs the topic. Other roles can use the same knowledge too: on a role's Knowledge tab, switch it on as Map.

When the guide has no answer, an expert with Agents may search the web when it has no answer may search; below Full auto that asks you first. What it finds can be added to the guide on a card.

See Knowledge and experts.

items.title: A web app with a team
items.text:
A small web app, built by the ready Web app team, from the first message to Take in.

  1. Open a folder for the app (the folder button → Open a folder…). An empty folder is fine.
  2. Pick the team. On the canvas, Teams for this chat → Manual, then the Web app team with its default recipe. Or leave Orchestrator decides and let it pick.
  3. Choose a level. Keep Ask before changes the first time. The team works in a working copy, so your folder does not change until you take the work in.
  4. Write the message, for example: "A one-page to-do list app in plain HTML and JavaScript, with a test." With Plan first on, you approve a plan first.
  5. Watch the canvas. It draws the team as a frame with its steps and agents, their tools, commands and files. Answer the cards as they come; Work on the rail counts what waits.
  6. Preview it. An agent can start a dev server and show the page; running servers are listed under Previews in the Workspace.
  7. Take it in. When the recipe ends, the Teams' work is ready card asks: Take in, Fix the findings (if reviewers left findings), or Ask for changes with what to change.
  8. Undo if needed. Undo these changes takes a turn's changes back, and names what it cannot take back.

See Teams and Ready and approval cards.
path: A web app with a team

items.title: KOLONİ in 5 minutes
items.text:
KOLONİ's words, each in two or three sentences, with a link to the page that goes deeper. The map shows how they hang together.

KOLONİ's words and how they hang together.

items.title: Where you work
items.text: Project A folder of yours that agents work in. Each project has its own settings, memory, knowledge and   To-do list. To only talk, with no files and no commands, choose No folder · a plain chat.   See Quick start. Chat One conversation with the Orchestrator, in a project. Each chat has its own permission level, and   other folders can join it, read only or read & write. While agents work, Send now puts a new   message into the turn at work, and After this turn keeps it in a queue for a turn of its own. See   Chat and canvas and Talking while agents work. Turn Everything that happens for one message, and for those you send into it with Send now: the   Orchestrator's answer, the agents it opened, their tools, commands and changes. The canvas draws one   turn at a time, from what really happened.   See Chat and canvas.

items.title: Who does the work
items.text: The Orchestrator The agent you talk to in a chat. It plans, asks and checks, and hands changes to files to   sub-agents, unless you let it change files itself (Settings › This project › How agents work › Who   changes the files). Behind the scenes its role is named Lead. See Roles. Sub-agent An agent that the Orchestrator, or another agent, opens for one part of the work. It changes files   in its own working copy, not in your folder. Opening one can ask you first (Settings › This project ›   When you're asked › Opening a sub-agent). See Permission levels. Role What an agent is for: a description, instructions, the tools it may use and, if you like, its own   model. KOLONİ comes with roles such as Coder, Reviewer, Tester, Planner and the Hive keeper (it keeps the   To-do list), and you can   add your own on the Agents page. See Roles. Tier How strong you say a model is: fast, balanced or strongest, set for each model on the   Models page. A role or a job can ask for a tier instead of one model; a model with no tier is only   ever picked by name. See Tiers and Agents may use.

items.title: Working together
items.text: Team A named group of roles, set out in stages: Plan, Build, Check, and Write & keep up. KOLONİ comes with three teams: Web app, Quality and Docs. Teams for this chat on the canvas decides whether the Orchestrator picks teams, you pick them, or no teams are used. See Teams. Recipe The drawn steps of a piece of work: who does each step, what runs at once, where it loops back and how it ends. A team runs by a recipe, such as Feature, Bugfix or Evolve. See Recipes and candidates and the Recipe cookbook. Discussion Several agents talking one question through in rounds, while nobody changes anything. An agent with the discuss tool starts it (the Orchestrator has it); you can join in or end it. See Discussions.

items.title: Your say
items.text: Working copy and Take in A sub-agent changes files in a copy of your project (outside your folder, or in its .koloni/copies/ where it has no git), so your folder does not change until you say so. Its work comes back on a card: Take in or Discard. A team's recipe keeps its work in one copy until you press Take in. See Working copies and Take in. Ready for you (cards) A card is a box that waits for your answer, such as "Run this command?" or a file change. Everything that waits is listed in the Ready for you panel (the pill in the top bar) and on the Work page's Ready for you tab. The card where a recipe's work ends is Teams' work is ready, with Take in, Fix the findings and Ask for changes. See Ready and approval cards. Permission levels What agents may do without asking: Ask before changes, Auto-edit files or Full auto. Each chat has its own. Harmful commands, secret files and files that steer agents ask at every level, with a few exceptions for CLIs run with their own tools (Known limits). See Permission levels.

items.title: What it remembers
items.text: Memory What a project remembers between chats: your preferences, the project's rules, facts you approved,   and notes agents wrote while they worked. Your preferences and rules reach every agent; a fact reaches   an agent whose task names its subject; notes are found only when an agent looks. See   Memory. Knowledge What agents can look things up in: a docs site, files, a repository or a topic, read once and turned   into a short guide. A role uses a knowledge only if you give it to the role. Memory is what the project   learned; knowledge is reading you hand to agents - both on the Memory page, its two parts, and one   tool, Recall, looks in both. See Sources to look things up in.

items.title: Work that starts by itself
items.text: To-do A project's tasks, in your order, on the Work page's To-do tab, beside Ready for you: a story holds tasks   and bugs. Tick tasks and   give them to a chat (Do in chat): they wait in its queue and run there one by one, each story in a   topic of its own, with a short notebook. Agents can propose tasks, and you decide when a task is done.   See To-do. ☾ Away Press ☾ Away on a chat's status line: your To-do tasks are worked through, each in its own copy of   the project, until you are back. See Work while you're away.

items.title: Next
items.text:
• Which way to work: a single agent, a team, a discussion?
  • Glossary: every word KOLONİ uses on screen.

items.title: Install
items.text: KOLONİ runs from its source folder. You install a few tools once, then build and start it.

items.title: What you need
items.text:
• Python 3.12, 3.13 or 3.14, and uv, which installs KOLONİ's Python packages.
  • Node.js 24, to build the page.
  • Git on your PATH. KOLONİ uses it to merge an agent's changes with yours and to commit when you ask.
  • At least one model, any of:
    • a model server that speaks the OpenAI API and supports tool calls, for example llama.cpp's llama-server started with --jinja, or a hosted API. Other OpenAI-compatible servers (Ollama, …) should work but are not tested;
    • an Anthropic API key;
    • a CLI installed and signed in in your own terminal. KOLONİ never signs in for you.
CLI Command Sign in Claude Code claude claude auth login Codex codex codex login GitHub Copilot CLI copilot gh auth login, or a GitHub token, or a model server of your own agy (experimental) agy agy's own sign-in

Using a CLI through KOLONİ counts against your plan with that vendor.

  • Docker is optional: to run agents' commands in a container, or to run KOLONİ itself in one.

items.title: How well each system is tested
items.text: System State Windows Used and tested every day, with the real CLIs. Linux The automatic tests run on every change. A clean install and daily use are less tested. Desktop notifications come through notify-send on a desktop (none on a server or over SSH); not yet tried on a real Linux desktop. macOS Not tested yet. Docker The image has been built and started; it is the newest and least tested way to run KOLONİ.

items.title: Install and start
items.text:
Get KOLONİ's source folder, open a terminal in it, and run:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
uv venv .venv --python 3.12
uv pip install --python .venv/Scripts/python.exe -r requirements-dev.lock
uv pip install --python .venv/Scripts/python.exe --no-deps -e .
npm --prefix frontend ci
npm --prefix frontend run build
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m app.main

uv venv .venv --python 3.12
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements-dev.lock
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps -e .
npm --prefix frontend ci
npm --prefix frontend run build
.venv/bin/python -m app.main

The window prints one line:

KOLONİ is open at http://127.0.0.1:8790/#key=…

Started from a terminal, KOLONİ also opens the page in your browser. Set KOLONI_OPEN_BROWSER=0 to stop that.

The part after #key= is the page key. Every request from the page must carry it, so a program on your machine (such as a command an agent runs) cannot approve its own cards or change your settings. Each start makes a new key. An old tab or bookmark shows "Open KOLONİ from the link in its window"; paste the new link there.

Stop KOLONİ with Ctrl+C in its window: it closes at once, the page open or not (a connection that does not end is given up to five seconds). A model server you started from the Models page and the agents' browsers stop with it - on Windows, Linux and macOS.

If you skip the build step, KOLONİ serves only its API and there is no page to open.

items.title: This guide inside KOLONİ
items.text:
KOLONİ serves this guide at http://127.0.0.1:8790/guide/, and the Learn more → links in its hints open it there. It works offline and matches the version you run. Build it once with the optional Zensical package:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
uv pip install --python .venv/Scripts/python.exe -r pyproject.toml --extra docs
.venv/Scripts/zensical build

uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r pyproject.toml --extra docs
.venv/bin/zensical build

Without it KOLONİ runs as usual, and /guide/ says how to build the guide. Once Zensical is installed, the update scripts rebuild the guide on each update.

items.title: Where your data goes
items.text: Your data goes in runtime/ inside the KOLONİ folder: the database, working copies, backups and logs. To keep it elsewhere, set KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT before you start. API keys are stored in plain text in that database, so keep the folder private.

items.title: Another port
items.text:
KOLONİ uses port 8790. To use another one, for example to run a second KOLONİ next to the first:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
$env:KOLONI_PORT = 8800; .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m app.main

KOLONI_PORT=8800 .venv/bin/python -m app.main

Give each KOLONİ its own KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT too: two of them must not share a database.

items.title: Update
items.text:
Stop KOLONİ first (Ctrl+C in its window). Then, in its folder:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
./scripts/update.ps1

./scripts/update.sh

The script refuses while you have uncommitted changes in KOLONİ's files, or while something answers on KOLONİ's port (KOLONI_PORT, 8790). Otherwise it backs up the database, pulls the new version, updates the packages and rebuilds the page, and this guide where Zensical is installed. It stops at the first step that fails. Start KOLONİ again; the database is upgraded as it starts. -DryRun (Windows) or --dry-run (macOS and Linux) prints the steps without running them.

items.title: Docker
items.text:
The image holds the page, the API and the database in one container. It is for API keys and model servers: no CLI is in it. (This is not the project setting that runs agents' commands in Docker.)

docker build -t koloni .
docker run -it --name koloni -p 127.0.0.1:8790:8790 \
  -v koloni-data:/data \
  -v "$HOME/code/my-app:/projects/my-app" \
  koloni
  • Keep 127.0.0.1: in -p. Without it, the page is open to your network.
  • The link with the page key is printed at the start; docker logs koloni shows it again.
  • Your data is in the koloni-data volume: the database, working copies and logs, with keys in plain text.
  • Your projects are the folders you mount under /projects. Open one with the folder button. The container runs as user koloni (uid 1000); on Linux, files it writes in a mounted folder belong to uid 1000.
  • A model server on your machine: add -e KOLONI_MODEL_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8080/v1. On Linux, also add --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway, and start the model server on the docker0 address (for example --host 172.17.0.1), never on 0.0.0.0.
  • Another port: use the same number on both sides and in KOLONI_PORT, for example -e KOLONI_PORT=8800 -p 127.0.0.1:8800:8800.
  • To update: git pull, build the image again, remove the old container (docker rm -f koloni), and start a new one with the same koloni-data volume. The database is backed up and upgraded as KOLONİ starts.
  • Do not mount Docker's socket into the container: whoever has the socket has full control of your machine.

The image has no Node.js, npx or uv, so MCP servers started with npx or uvx do not run in it.

items.title: Settings from the environment
items.text:
KOLONİ does not read a .env file. Set these in the shell before you start it.

Variable Default Meaning KOLONI_PORT 8790 The port on 127.0.0.1. KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT runtime/ Where the database and working files live. KOLONI_OPEN_BROWSER 1 0 does not open the browser at the start. KOLONI_PAGE_KEY a new one each start A fixed page key. KOLONI_MODEL_BASE_URL http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 First start only: the address of the "Local" provider. KOLONI_MODEL_ID the first model the server lists First start only: Local's default model. KOLONI_MODEL_API_KEY none First start only: Local's key. KOLONI_DETECT_CLI 1 First start only: add Claude Code and Codex if they are installed. 0 skips this.

After the first start, change providers on the Models page; the first-start variables no longer change them. The full list is in Environment variables.

items.title: Quick start
items.text: From install to your first approved change, in five steps.

items.title: 1. Install and start
items.text:
Follow Install for your system. When KOLONİ starts, its window prints one line:

KOLONİ is open at http://127.0.0.1:8790/#key=…

Started from a terminal, KOLONİ also opens this page in your browser. If it does not, open the link from the window. Keep the window open while you use KOLONİ; Ctrl+C in it stops KOLONİ.

On first open, the canvas shows First steps: a provider, a folder, and your first message. The step you are on has a button that takes you where you do it.

items.title: 2. Add a model
items.text:
Press Add a provider (in First steps, or on the Models page). Fill in:

  • Name: any name you like.
  • Kind: OpenAI-compatible server, Anthropic API, or a CLI: Claude Code (CLI), Codex (CLI) or GitHub Copilot CLI (agy (CLI) under Experimental, once you show it).
  • For a server: its Address (a llama.cpp server is usually http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1) and an API key if it needs one.
  • For the Anthropic API: your API key and a Default model.
  • For a CLI: nothing more, as long as the CLI is installed and you signed in to it in your own terminal. KOLONİ never signs in for you. If the CLI is missing or not signed in, its card shows the command to install it or sign in.

Press Save, then Test to check that it answers.

The first provider on the Models page is the default: new chats run on it. KOLONİ makes one called "Local" at the first start, for a model server on this machine. If you do not run one, First steps says that Local isn't answering. If the Models page holds another provider that is switched on, First steps offers Use … for new chats with its name: press it to make that provider the default. Or open the provider on the Models page and press Make default. KOLONİ never changes the default by itself, and the step is done once the default answers.

If a CLI was installed when KOLONİ first started, you may find it on the Models page already.

items.title: 3. Choose a folder
items.text: Press the folder button at the top left and choose Open a folder…. Pick the project your agents should work in. To only talk, without files or commands, choose No folder · a plain chat.

items.title: 4. Write your first message
items.text:
Next to the message box, check the permission level. Keep Ask before changes for now: commands that do more than read wait for you, and no change reaches your folder before you say so. See Permission levels.

Write what you want done, for example "Add a README that explains how to run this project", and send it.

The chat shows the Orchestrator's answer and a row for each agent it opened. The canvas draws the turn: each agent as a box with its tools, commands and files.

items.title: 5. Answer the cards
items.text:
In a new project the Orchestrator plans, asks and checks, and hands every change to files to a sub-agent (for code, a Coder). The sub-agent usually works in its own copy of the project, not in your folder. So the first turn asks you on cards in the chat:

Open this sub-agent? shows the role, the model it runs on, its task and its tools. Press Open agent to let it start, or Reject.

Run this command? comes when an agent wants to run a command:

  • Run once runs it this time.
  • Always run … runs it, and keeps a rule so the same kind of command runs without a card in this chat.
  • Reject turns it down.

Take in …'s work? (with the sub-agent's name) comes when the sub-agent has finished. It lists the files it changed; click a file to see its diff. Nothing is in your folder yet. Press Take in to bring the changes into your project, or Discard to throw the copy away. See Working copies and Take in.

If you let the Orchestrator change the files itself (Settings › This project › How agents work › Who changes the files), or no copy can be made (a very large project), each change comes on a card with its diff and Approve or Reject instead, and after it is written you can still Revert it.

While something waits for you, the project's tab above the canvas turns orange, and Work on the rail counts it, so you can do something else meanwhile.

items.title: Next
items.text:
• Permission levels: what asks and what runs at each level.
  • Memory: what KOLONİ remembers between chats.
  • Settings: the app's and the project's settings.

items.title: Why KOLONİ
items.text: An agent CLI on its own works in one terminal, one session at a time. KOLONİ puts the agents you already use, and the models you choose, in one place on your own machine, and shows you what they really did.

items.title: What it adds
items.text:
• Many agents, one chat. The Orchestrator hands parts of a job to other roles (Coder, Reviewer, Tester and more), each in its own working copy, so your folder changes only when you take the work in.
  • Any model you have. Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI and agy on your own plans, an API key, or a model server on your own machine, side by side. Each agent shows the provider and model it really ran on.
  • Evidence, not a story. The canvas draws every turn from the record: the agents, their tools, commands and the files they changed, with real diffs. A value KOLONİ does not know is shown as unknown.
  • You decide. Before anything risky, an agent asks you on a card. The permission level sets how much runs without asking.
  • Memory with sources. Facts rest on lines of files and are checked again each time; a fact whose source changed is not used until you look.
  • Work that goes on. Teams follow recipes, and with ☾ Away your To-do tasks are worked through in copies while you are away.
  • Local. KOLONİ listens on 127.0.0.1 only, keeps its data in a folder on your machine, and sends no telemetry.

items.title: What it is not
items.text:
• Not finished: KOLONİ is an alpha, so expect rough edges. See Known limits.
  • Not a sandbox by itself. Below Full auto your cards are the wall; for more, run commands in Docker. See Security model.

items.title: Copilot on your GitHub account
items.text: GitHub Copilot CLI on your GitHub account runs only what your Copilot plan offers, and what it offers changes with the plan. On 24 Nov 2026 an account whose premium requests were used up listed no model by name, only auto at Standard and Fast. The day before, the same account listed about 14 models. So KOLONİ asks Copilot itself what your account offers, and offers only that. (Set up the provider first: Set up a CLI.)

items.title: What KOLONİ asks, and when
items.text:
KOLONİ asks Copilot two things in one start, with no model turn: which models and Auto tiers your account offers (models.list), and what is left of your plan (account.getQuota). It starts Copilot the way the plan meter does, in an empty home of KOLONİ's own, signed in with your gh login or the provider's token.

It asks:

  • as the provider is added (the top bar reads it within seconds),
  • by the top bar's plan meter, at most once in 10 minutes, and on Read now on its card in Models,
  • when you fill its tiers (Fill from the catalogue, Fill tiers),
  • at once after Copilot refuses a model or a routing.

Opening the Models page or the chat's model panel asks nothing: they show what your account offered when it was last asked.

A Copilot on a model server of your own is never asked: its models are the server's.

items.title: Models
items.text:
What your account says What KOLONİ does It lists the model The model stays on. It does not list the model KOLONİ switches the model off on the provider's list and says why: "not on your Copilot plan now". It has no premium requests left The models it no longer lists go off with "your Copilot plan has no premium requests now". One of its Auto tiers is on auto stays on. No Fusion tier is on fusion goes off, in Copilot's own words: "This tier is not available for the user's Copilot plan." It lists a model it did not list before KOLONİ switches the model back on.

A model you switched off yourself stays off: KOLONİ switches back on only what it switched off. So does a model Copilot refused while your account listed it, whatever the list says later; its row says so. Switch it on yourself once you think it works.

  • Fill from the catalogue proposes only what your account offers. When it lists no model by name, the fill says so. A Copilot not added yet is not filled: add it first, and KOLONİ then asks your account. Fill tiers asks it too; a Copilot whose account does not answer is left as it is.
  • The model names the chat's model panel offers are your account's too.
  • An agent picked by tier never gets a model that is switched off. A model Copilot refuses at its first turn is switched off the same way, and your account is asked again at once.

items.title: Routing
items.text:
auto and fusion take a routing, on the model's row of the Models tab and in the chat's model panel.

  • Once your account was asked, auto offers only its Auto tiers, by Copilot's own names. On 24 Nov 2026 those were Standard (Copilot's balance) and Fast. Fast is on in the account, though Copilot's own picker does not show it. KOLONİ offers it and sends it as you chose it.
  • A tier your account has off is dimmed, "not on your plan", with Copilot's own words in its tooltip. A routing a row already had that the account no longer lists stays on the row, dimmed, until you pick another.
  • fusion offers its Fusion tiers the same way: on 24 Nov 2026 High and Max, both off. Where no Fusion tier is on, fusion itself is switched off.
  • Before your account was asked (a new provider, or Copilot not answering), the routing offers every tier Copilot's package knows: Efficiency, Balance, Intelligence and Fast; Standard, High and Max.

items.title: Plan limits
items.text:
The provider's card, the top bar and Plan limits on the Usage page show Copilot's chat requests and premium requests apart, for example "0% of chat requests used (200 of 200 left) · premium requests: none on your plan". A plan with no premium requests says "none", never "100% used".

Before a turn, KOLONİ checks whether the account has room:

  • A named model is held back when either counter is used up.
  • auto runs while chat requests are left, even with premium requests used up: on 24 Nov 2026 auto ran with premium at 0 and chat requests left. It is held back when every counter is used up, and on a plan with unlimited chat requests (no chat counter) once premium requests are used up - which counter auto spends there is not measured.
