  • A plan with no premium requests at all (0 of 0) holds nothing back by itself: the models your account no longer lists are switched off instead (above).

items.title: Not measured yet
items.text:
• Whether Copilot takes fast from KOLONİ as Fast, not as its own default. A run with it went well, but the tier it ran at was not read back.
  • Which of the two counters auto spends.
  • What a listed model carries: KOLONİ reads only its name.

items.title: Limits
items.text: Each provider's window has a Limits tab. What it offers depends on how the provider is paid.

items.title: A CLI on a subscription
items.text: Step down a tier at [ ] % of the plan: once this much of the plan is used, agents picked by tier move one tier down. A whole number from 50 to 100, or empty for never. "A role that always runs on one tier, or on one model, is never stepped down: your own rule wins." On the Usage page, Plan limits marks that share with a line on the plan's bar; past it the bar turns orange.

items.title: An API key
items.text:
• This key is a plan: count no money: its runs show no cost on Usage and count nothing in a project's budget.
  • Otherwise, At most $ … a day and At most $ … a month, spent at your prices, in every project. Empty means no limit. Past the limit, a new message whose Orchestrator runs on this provider asks you first, a model picked by tier moves to the next one of its tier, and no sub-agent is opened here.

Press Save limits to keep them.

items.title: A model server on this machine
items.text: "A model server on this machine spends no money and has no plan: there is nothing to limit."

items.title: When a message would go over a limit
items.text: When a provider's limit or the project's monthly budget is reached, a new message asks first. It says which limit and how much was spent, then "Send it anyway?". Press Go on anyway to send it, or Cancel.

items.title: When an agent would move to a paid provider
items.text:
If KOLONİ would open a sub-agent on a provider that is paid per token, while the chat runs on one that is not, it asks on the Open this sub-agent? card. The card's reason says that the new provider is paid per token and the other is not. Press Open agent or Reject. Your answer counts for that provider for the rest of the turn.

See also Usage and budgets.

items.title: Providers
items.text:
A provider is where your agents' models run. Open Models on the left rail to see them. Each provider is a card that shows how it is paid for (subscription for a CLI, this machine for a server on your own computer, API key otherwise) and what it has left. A click on a card opens its window.

The Models page with one provider, a model server on this machine.

items.title: Kinds of provider
items.text: Kind What it is OpenAI-compatible server A server that speaks the OpenAI API and supports tool calls, such as llama.cpp's llama-server or a hosted API. Other OpenAI-compatible servers (Ollama, …) should work but are not tested. Anthropic API Anthropic's API, with your key. Claude Code (CLI), Codex (CLI), GitHub Copilot CLI, agy (CLI) (experimental) A CLI on this machine that you are signed in to. It runs on your plan with that vendor.

items.title: Adding a provider
items.text:
Press Add a provider ("A CLI with your subscription, an API key, or a server of your own"). Give it a Name and a Kind, then:

  • For a server: its Address and, if it needs one, an API key. "Keys are kept in plain text in KOLONİ's local database on this machine."
  • For the Anthropic API: an API key and a Default model.
  • For a CLI: Path to the command, if it is not found by its name. KOLONİ never signs in for you. If the CLI is missing or not signed in, the window shows the command to install it or to sign in, with links to the vendor's docs.

Press Add provider to save it.

items.title: The provider window
items.text:
The window has the tabs Models, Connection and Limits. A server on this machine also has Server.

Connection holds what you filled in when you added it, and:

  • Default model: the model used when nothing else names one.
  • At most this many agents at once: how many agents may run on this provider at the same time.
  • How it runs (CLIs only):
Option What it means One session per agent, with KOLONİ's tools (recommended) One CLI session per agent, using KOLONİ's tools and cards. One run per model step, with KOLONİ's tools Claude Code only: the CLI runs once per model step, slower, and the answer arrives all at once. Native: its own tools, in the project The CLI uses its own tools in your folder, and asks KOLONİ before each one. Under Experimental: offered with Show experimental features on (Experimental CLIs). Reads with its own tools; started without leave to write or run agy only: it reads, and cannot change anything.
  • Sign-in (Claude Code and Codex): My own uses the sign-in in your home folder; Its own for KOLONİ keeps a separate one, and the window shows the command to log in to it. "KOLONİ never sees the token."

The buttons at the bottom:

  • Save saves the changes.
  • Test checks the provider. For a CLI it only says whether the command was found: "It was not run, so sign-in is not checked." For the Anthropic API it asks for the model's details, which spends nothing. For an OpenAI-compatible server it sends one small request ("Call the ping tool.") to see whether the model can use tools; on a paid service that costs a few tokens. It then says "Reachable" and the model.
  • Try a real run (CLIs): runs the CLI once on a one-word question. This counts against your plan.
  • Make default: makes this provider the default, the first one in the list.
  • Remove key: shown when a key is saved.
  • Delete provider: deletes it at once, without asking. The last provider cannot be deleted ("At least one provider is needed"). Chats and roles that used it go back to having no choice.

items.title: Switching a provider off
items.text: Each provider has an on / off switch, on its card and at the top of its window. "Off: nothing new starts on it - no chat, no agent, no learning; its key and settings stay. A turn already running goes on until it ends; Stop ends it now." Its card then says "switched off".

items.title: The models of a provider
items.text:
The Models tab lists the models that agents and you can pick, at most 30. Each row has:

Column What it does Tier How strong the model is: fast, balanced or strongest. See Tiers. Context, Max output, Thinking What the model can take in, write out, and its thinking levels. On GitHub Copilot CLI on your GitHub account, Context sets its context tier, and on auto and fusion their Routing (GitHub Copilot CLI). Price in / out (1M) The price per million tokens; "plan" for a CLI. Agents may use On: agents may pick this model by themselves. Off: only you pick it. On Off: the model is not used.

Open a row for more, such as Its note for agents (what the model is for, up to 120 characters) and Used in 30 days. Each change saves at once.

Add a model adds one by name. Fill from the catalogue proposes a list: your rows first, then what the provider lists with your key, then the bundled models.dev catalogue's models, with their details; nothing changes until you press Save these models. At the top of the page, Update catalogue downloads a newer catalogue, and Keep the catalogue fresh lets KOLONİ do that by itself.

items.title: Which model a chat uses
items.text:
The model button under the message box opens Model for this conversation: a Provider (the first option is the default) and a Model name. Use this model applies it from the next turn. "A role with its own model keeps it."

An agent's model is chosen in this order:

  1. the models the role lists under Try first, in your order, unless the agent that opens it gave the job a tier;
  2. the role's own model (One model);
  3. the first model of the role's tier, or of the tier the opener gave the job;
  4. the chat's model;
  5. the default provider, the first one in the list.

A model past its limit, down, switched off or not one agents may use is passed over, and the next is tried. Roles and their models are set on the Agents page.

Where an agent runs: the full order, tiers, limits and moves. See also Tiers and Limits.

items.title: Plan meters
items.text: For Claude Code, Codex, agy and Copilot, the top bar shows how much of the plan is used, from what each CLI last reported. Click a meter to open Usage. On a provider's card, Read now reads the plan again; for Claude Code that is one short request.

items.title: A model server on this machine: the Server tab
items.text: For an OpenAI-compatible server on this machine, the Server tab starts and stops your llama.cpp llama-server. Set Program to the full path of llama-server in your llama.cpp build (the one on PATH is filled in when there is one), choose the Model from the models folder next to it, set the context, GPU layers and the other values, then press Start. Server output shows what the server prints. "It starts only when you press Start, and stops when KOLONİ closes. No agent can start it; Start runs exactly what is shown here."

items.title: Set up an API provider
items.text: An API provider is a service you pay per token, with a key: the Anthropic API, or any service that speaks the OpenAI API.

items.title: Anthropic API
items.text:
1. Models → Add a provider. Kind: Anthropic API.
  2. API key: your Anthropic key. "Keys are kept in plain text in KOLONİ's local database on this machine." Once saved, the key "is never shown again".
  3. Address: leave it empty for https://api.anthropic.com.
  4. Default model: needed, for example claude-sonnet-5-5.
  5. Workspace ID: "Only needed for a key that is not scoped to a workspace. Copy it from the Anthropic console."
  6. Press Add provider, then Test. For the Anthropic API, Test reads the model's details and spends nothing.

items.title: A service that speaks the OpenAI API
items.text:
1. Models → Add a provider. Kind: OpenAI-compatible server.
  2. Address: the service's API address, starting with http:// or https://. The field suggests the services KOLONİ knows from its model catalogue; an address that only names a known service is completed to its full API address.
  3. API key: the service's key. The field says what the service calls its key.
  4. Default model: if you leave it empty, KOLONİ uses the first model the server lists.
  5. Press Add provider, then Test. Test sends one small request to see whether the model can use tools, which costs a few tokens on a paid service. It then says "Reachable" and the model, and adds "this model does not take tools" if it cannot use them.

A model that does not take tools can chat, but agents cannot use KOLONİ's tools with it.

items.title: After adding
items.text:
• At most this many agents at once: 8 by default for a service.
  • On the Models tab, give the models a Tier, and set Agents may use. See Tiers and Agents may use.
  • On the Limits tab, set dollars a day or a month, or mark the key as a plan. See Limits.
  • Prices come from the catalogue unless you set your own. See Usage and budgets.

items.title: Set up a CLI
items.text: A CLI provider runs an agent CLI that you installed and signed in to yourself: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI or agy. It runs on your plan with that vendor. KOLONİ never installs a CLI and never signs in for you. Read Subscription rules first.

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Install the CLI in your own terminal. If it is missing, the provider's window shows the install command for your system, with a link to the vendor's install docs.
  2. Sign in in your own terminal (see the table). If it is not signed in, the window shows the sign-in command.
  3. Models → Add a provider, and pick its Kind. Set Path to the command only if KOLONİ does not find it by its name.
  4. Choose How it runs (see below), and press Add provider.
  5. Test only checks that the command is found; it does not run it. Try a real run runs it once on a one-word question, on your plan.

At the first start, KOLONİ adds Claude Code and Codex by itself if they are installed. It never adds Copilot or agy by itself (agy is experimental, and Google's terms forbid using Antigravity through another app: see Subscription rules). An agy card on the Models page, switched on or off, says "Google's terms forbid using Antigravity through another app; your Google account may be suspended." KOLONİ adds providers only at the first start, so an agy already on the Models page is left as it is.

items.title: The CLIs
items.text: Kind Command Sign in Claude Code (CLI) claude claude auth login Codex (CLI) codex codex login GitHub Copilot CLI copilot gh auth login, or a GitHub token agy (CLI) agy agy's own sign-in

items.title: How it runs
items.text:
CLI Choices (the first is the default) Claude Code One session per agent · One run per model step · Native (experimental) Codex One session per agent · Native (experimental). As a session its own patch tool cannot be switched off: KOLONİ refuses every patch it asks to make, and it writes with KOLONİ's write_file and edit_file instead. Unlike Native, it runs wherever the other sessions run: While you're away, recipe steps and comparisons. On a model server of your own its session is not yet measured. Codex's One run per model step was cut in 0.1.10: a Codex provider saved so runs as One session per agent. Copilot One session per agent · Native (experimental) agy (experimental) Reads with its own tools · Native
  • One session per agent and One run per model step use KOLONİ's tools and cards, with the CLI's own tools off.
  • Native uses the CLI's own tools in your folder; it is experimental since 0.1.10. Claude Code and agy ask KOLONİ before every tool they use; Codex before each command and patch, but not those its own allow rules cover, which it runs without asking; Copilot before every tool it uses (on its newer protocol, 1.0.114 on, through KOLONİ's own hook; on the older one, before each command, write and read). KOLONİ's own team tools reach a Native CLI over its tool bridge: opening sub-agents, asking you, the To-do list, notes and memory, and Notify you (only where the project has its desktop notifications on; at most 6 a minute for one chat, as for any agent).
  • Reads with its own tools (agy): it reads, and is started without leave to write or run.

items.title: Experimental CLIs
items.text:
agy is experimental since 0.1.8, and a CLI run Native since 0.1.10: less measured and tested than the rest, so they are not offered unless you ask for them. Turn on Show experimental features in Settings › The app › Agents (it is kept as you change it). Then Add a provider's Kind lists agy (CLI), and Claude Code's, Codex's and Copilot's How it runs list Native, each under Experimental; and This project › Memory and web offers Let agy search too. (Codex and Copilot, with Native not offered, have one way left: How it runs is not shown.)

Nothing that already uses them is hidden or stopped: an agy provider, or a CLI run Native, keeps working with the switch off, its card tagged Experimental, and its window still shows the way it runs; while you edit it, Native stays offered. A project that already lets agy search keeps its box.

The modes, KOLONİ's tool bridge, and how each CLI asks. (full size)

items.title: Going on from the last turn
items.text:
Claude Code and Codex, run Native with Sign-in: Its own for KOLONİ, and GitHub Copilot CLI, run Native, go on in their own session from one turn to the next: each is sent only what is new, and compacts that session itself (Codex's: see Codex). They go on only from the same topic's previous turn, run with the same model, folder, permission level and setup: New topic starts a new session (Topics). Copilot's session is kept in a folder of its own under KOLONİ's runtime (Data and privacy); where Copilot cannot go on in it (the session is gone, or Copilot is older than 1.0.114's protocol), it starts a new one sent the whole chat, and the agent's record says so once. When Copilot compacts its session, its record says so too, with the size before and after: from then on what it knows of the earlier turns is its own summary, so a brief should say again what matters. Its tokens and AI credits are counted per turn, not as the session's growing total. A Copilot session costs more past its models' price step (100,000 tokens of prompt; one 553,000-token message cost 34.6 AI credits in a measurement), so KOLONİ does not let one grow that far: once it holds Summarise a long context at (%) of 100,000 tokens - or of the window set on its role, or with none set there of Copilot's own window, where that is smaller: a larger window on the role does not lift the bound - or did not say its size, the next turn starts a new session sent the chat as KOLONİ keeps it, which KOLONİ summarises - and the agent's record says so. While it works, the agent's details show how full Copilot says its session is; once a Native CLI's turn is over no fill is shown, since its tokens in are its turn's model calls added up. Every other CLI lead starts each turn anew and is sent the whole chat. KOLONİ compacts that, as it does for an API model, past Summarise a long context at (%) of the window set on its role, or with none set there, of the window the catalogue has for its model (Claude Code's, Codex's and Copilot's models; none for agy's, where only Compact now compacts it). Against a catalogued window this is seldom reached: what is measured is the chat KOLONİ sends, with its older tool outputs already left out past about 240,000 characters, so only a chat whose own words are very long gets there; what the CLI reads by itself during a turn is not counted. To have it summarised sooner, set a smaller window on its role. A CLI run One run per model step is never compacted: each step is sent a trimmed history.

When the context of a lead on a CLI fills during a turn in a chat you are in and it was working alone, KOLONİ summarises its earlier work and starts the turn again from the summary by itself, once, with a line in the chat saying so; Stop stops that too, and what the summary costs counts in the turn (the CLI's refused start reports no tokens). If its context fills again, the turn fails and says so: use Compact now or set a smaller context window on the role. Where nothing of its earlier work is left to summarise - a single message larger than its model takes, say - nothing is started again, and the failure says that after the CLI's own line: send a shorter message, or use a model with a larger context window. Where the lead had opened sub-agents or a team's recipe, the turn is not started again: KOLONİ summarises its earlier work after it and the failure says so - send your message again and it goes on from the summary. A plan, a To-do task's turn and a night's job are neither started again nor summarised this way. (A lead on an API model is summarised and asked once more inside its step, as before.)

KOLONİ knows such a refusal only by the CLI's own error, never by words its model may have written. GitHub Copilot CLI's wordings are known: one seen in a live refusal ("Request exceeds the model's prompt budget …", CLI 1.0.107), the others taken from its package and not yet seen live. That refusal gave Copilot's own limit for gpt-6-luna on the default context tier as 272,000 tokens of prompt; KOLONİ's catalogue has a larger window for that model (1,050,000). Run Native, Copilot says its session's own window as it works (272,000 for gpt-6-luna, 872,000 for claude-haiku-5.5, measured): the agent keeps that one, at most 100,000 (its price step), from its first turn, where its role sets none, and it is what the agent's context is measured against; a kept session is held to 100,000 whatever the role's window. Run as a session, set the role's window to what your tier takes. Claude Code reports a failed turn in a text that can be its model's words, so its is not recognised yet, and the other CLIs' own wordings are not known. Where the failure says nothing of a summary, use Compact now and send the message again.

Compact now is in the top bar's context button (see Chat and canvas).

items.title: Qoder is no longer supported
items.text: Since 0.1.8 KOLONİ does not run Qoder, and Add a provider no longer offers it. A Qoder provider you added before stays on the Models page, switched off, with its settings: its card says "no longer supported", its switch cannot turn it on, and its window says why and has Delete provider. A chat or a role that still names it fails as on any provider switched off, with the reason, until you pick another model; once it is deleted, they run on your default provider. Move what used it, then delete it. If Qoder was your default provider (the first on the Models page), make another one the default first, since a new chat runs on the default; and if it is your only provider, add another: the last one cannot be deleted.

items.title: Sign-in for Claude Code and Codex
items.text:
Sign-in offers My own (the sign-in in your home folder) or Its own for KOLONİ: a sign-in folder for this provider alone, so that several accounts can run side by side. For its own, save the provider, then the window gives the command to log in to it in your own terminal. "KOLONİ never sees the token." Run Native, a provider on its own sign-in goes on in its session (Claude Code's) or thread (Codex's) from a topic's previous turn; on yours, the default, each turn starts anew and is sent the whole chat.

Claude Code and Codex can also Use a model server of your own instead (optional): a Model server address on this machine or your network.

items.title: Codex
items.text:
Going on in its thread (only with Sign-in: Its own for KOLONİ). Sign-in: My own stays the default and needs no sign-in of KOLONİ's: Codex runs Native as before, each turn a new thread that is not written to disk and is sent the whole chat. A Codex provider set to Its own for KOLONİ and run Native goes on in its own thread from the topic's previous turn, as Claude Code does: each turn starts a new codex app-server that resumes the thread with this turn's folder, permission level and sandbox given again, and is sent only what came since its last answer. The thread is kept by Codex itself in the provider's sign-in folder, runtime/cli-homes/<provider id>/sessions/…/rollout-…-<thread>.jsonl - never in your own ~/.codex (Data and privacy). Choosing it means a login of its own: on the Models page set the provider's Sign-in to Its own for KOLONİ, save, press Log in to Codex for this provider and run the command it gives in your own terminal (it sets CODEX_HOME to that folder and runs codex login), finish the login in your browser, then press Check again: the provider shows "signed in" once Codex's own codex login status says so. KOLONİ never sees the token. Until it is logged in, that provider does not run.

Not yet tried with a real Codex. Going on in a thread is built on measurements of Codex 0.164 (a thread resumed in a new app-server remembers) and tested with a stand-in only. On Codex 0.164 a new, empty KOLONİ folder also answered read-only when asked for its workspace-write sandbox (a turn is then refused before Codex acts), so a role that writes or runs commands might not run on such a provider until this is measured on a newer Codex.

  • A new topic, another model, folder, permission level or what the role may do (its sandbox's mode with it) starts a new thread. Where Codex cannot go on in the kept one (it is gone, or Codex refuses), it starts a new thread sent the whole chat, and the agent's record says so once.
  • Its tokens are counted per turn: Codex reports its thread's running total, and a turn counts the difference.
  • KOLONİ does not let a thread grow until Codex compacts it by itself, since Codex's summary is not readable: once it holds Summarise a long context at (%) of 166,000 tokens (about 124,500 by default), or of the window set on its role where that is smaller, the next turn starts a new thread sent the chat as KOLONİ keeps it, which KOLONİ summarises - and the agent's record says so. 166,000 is the largest size a Codex thread was measured to reach without compacting itself (on a 258,400-token window); where Codex compacts by itself is not measured yet. When Codex does compact its thread, the agent's record says so, and the next turn starts a new thread the same way.
  • The thread of another topic is removed when a turn of yours starts in another topic, with its chat or project, and at KOLONİ's start for one no agent goes on in; so is one whose turn failed or was stopped, and one that is not gone on in.

A call still running when Codex answers. Codex has been seen to give its final answer, and end its turn, while one of KOLONİ's tools it called was still at work (a 120-second command, "It is still running"). The turn then waits for that call to end by its own limit - a command's time limit, a sub-agent's run - and Codex's answer ends with a line saying so: what the call comes to is on its record, not in the answer. Stop ends the wait, and the call with it, at once. A question to you that is still open (ask_user, a folder or a secret asked for) is not waited for: nobody would read its card once the turn is over, so it closes with the turn, as before. Why Codex answered early is not known yet.

items.title: GitHub Copilot CLI
items.text:
• API key: leave it empty to use your own GitHub sign-in (gh), or give a fine-grained GitHub token with the Copilot Requests permission. A token has not been tried on a real account yet.
  • Thinking: KOLONİ sends Copilot's levels Off to Max (Off as none), whether it runs as a session or Native; the Models page shows "Off–Max". A level the model does not take gives no error.
  • Model auto: Copilot picks the model for each request. It is in Copilot's model list (tier fast) and takes no thinking level, so KOLONİ sends none. Pick a model for Copilot, auto or another: with no model and Medium thinking, Copilot's default spent 7.12 AI credits for the same short answer that auto answered for 0.18 (measured once, 7 Nov 2026, Copilot CLI 1.0.105). The agent's node and window, and in the chat the Orchestrator's turn head and the model button, show the model auto picked (auto → gpt-6-luna); Copilot's reason is on a quiet line under the turn head, in the button's tooltip and in the agent's Details. An agent that goes on from it asks for auto again. fusion (Copilot Fusion, only on plans that have it) runs each turn on several models and keeps one; its pick shows the same way (fusion → gpt-6-luna) and an agent goes on with fusion. It takes no thinking level either, and has no tier, so agents never pick it by themselves.
  • Routing (auto and fusion on your GitHub account): on the model's row of the Models tab, beside its Context, and in the chat's model panel under Thinking. Auto: Efficiency, Balance, Intelligence or Fast; Fusion: Standard (as Auto Balance), High or Max - High and Max cost more than auto. Once your account was asked, only the tiers it offers can be chosen, by Copilot's own names (Copilot on your GitHub account). Default sends none: Copilot's own. It is saved on the model's row, so every chat and agent on that provider and model uses it; for two chats to differ, add a second Copilot provider. Run live on 1.0.114: Copilot keeps the tier and says the model it picked and why. On a plan without a tier Copilot refuses the turn, and KOLONİ says to pick another routing.
  • Your account's models: KOLONİ asks Copilot which models your account offers, and switches off the ones it does not list - see Copilot on your GitHub account.
  • Versions: KOLONİ asks Copilot its version and protocol as it starts it, the way a run starts it. Copilot updates itself when you run it yourself, and KOLONİ then runs that version too. On the newer protocol (1.0.114 on) it runs Native through KOLONİ's hook, and each PowerShell command starts in the project folder. On the older protocol only a version measured with KOLONİ (1.0.91, 1.0.103, 1.0.105) runs Native - its run asks again, in case Copilot changed since; any other version, a Copilot that does not say its version, or a protocol KOLONİ does not know runs as One session per agent, and the provider's card on the Models page says why.
  • Changes on models other than Claude: Copilot gives such models (gpt-6-luna, mai-code-2-flash) its apply_patch tool instead of create and edit. Run Native, each file of a patch is asked about on its own card, as a write is; refusing one refuses the whole patch.
  • Usage: Copilot's tokens and AI credits (or premium requests) are counted from its usage checkpoint, run as a session as in Native. As a session that was measured with copilot -p (CLI 1.0.103), not yet seen in a live session. See Usage and budgets.
  • Copilot can also use a model server of your own, with Server type, Most prompt tokens and Most output tokens. Never connect to GitHub then means no sign-in, telemetry or update check, and web tools are off.

items.title: Plan meters
items.text:
For Claude Code, Codex, agy and Copilot, the provider's card shows what is left of the plan, and Read now reads it again (for Claude Code, one short request). For Claude Code, the Limits tab also offers Keep it fresh from your Claude Code sessions: a status line you add to your own Claude Code settings, so that your sessions report what is left of your plan.

See CLIs for what has been measured.

items.title: Set up a local model
items.text: A model on your own machine spends no money and sends nothing out. KOLONİ talks to it through the OpenAI API, so the model server must support tool calls.

items.title: llama.cpp
items.text:
KOLONİ is built and tested with llama.cpp's llama-server. Start it with --jinja, so that tool calls work. Its usual address is http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1.

At the first start, KOLONİ makes a provider called "Local" at that address (or at KOLONI_MODEL_BASE_URL). It counts as set up only while its server answers.

items.title: Starting the server from KOLONİ
items.text:
For an OpenAI-compatible provider whose address is on this machine, the provider's window has a Server tab:

  • Program: your llama-server program.
  • Model: a model file, or none.
  • Context (-c), GPU layers (-ngl), Default thinking, Temperature, Top-p, Top-k, Min-p.
  • Advanced: every other argument, as given.

The tab's first values are only a starting point: the llama-server on your PATH (if there is none, set Program to its full path), --port 8080 --jinja, and no model. For your own build, set Program to the full path of llama-server in its bin folder. Model lists the .gguf files in the models folder next to that program. KOLONİ keeps the tab's values when you press Start or Restart, in local-server.json under runtime/; until then, KOLONI_LOCAL_SERVER can name the program (see Environment variables).

Check the values for your machine, then press Start. The tab shows whether it runs, the GPU's memory and load (from nvidia-smi), and Server output. "It starts only when you press Start, and stops when KOLONİ closes. No agent can start it; Start runs exactly what is shown here."

At most this many agents at once: for a server on this machine, KOLONİ reads the server's slots when its first agent starts.

items.title: Other model servers
items.text: Any server that speaks the OpenAI API and supports tool calls can be added the same way: Models → Add a provider → OpenAI-compatible server, with its address. Such servers (Ollama, …) should work but are not tested: the local server KOLONİ is measured with is llama.cpp's llama-server. KOLONİ has no settings of its own for those servers, and the Server tab starts only llama-server. Press Test to see whether the model can use tools.

items.title: After adding
items.text:
• Give the models a Tier and set Agents may use on the Models tab. See Tiers and Agents may use.
  • "A model server on this machine spends no money and has no plan: there is nothing to limit."
  • If the model takes long to load, raise KOLONI_MODEL_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS. See Environment variables.

items.title: Subscription rules
items.text: When you use a CLI through KOLONİ, you use your own subscription with that vendor. Each vendor has its own terms for that. This page says what each vendor's official page says, as read on 5 November 2026. It is not legal advice: read the terms yourself, and decide.

items.title: What KOLONİ does
items.text: KOLONİ starts the CLI that you installed and signed in to yourself, unchanged, and sends it prompts. It does not read the CLI's sign-in token, and it does not talk to the vendor's service for the CLI. For Claude Code, you can have KOLONİ keep a separate sign-in folder; you still sign in through Anthropic's own sign-in.

items.title: What each vendor's page says
items.text: Vendor Its page What it says Anthropic (Claude Code) Legal and compliance Third-party developers may not offer a Claude.ai sign-in in their own apps, or collect, store or route users' credentials or session tokens. The exception is an end user signing in to the unchanged Claude Code program with their own subscription. The page does not speak of another app starting the CLI. OpenAI (Codex) Authentication The page could not be read in full. For apps, the official way is "Sign in with ChatGPT" (preview). No text was found that allows or forbids another program using Codex's own ChatGPT sign-in. GitHub (Copilot CLI) Use Copilot CLI It documents running the CLI from scripts and with -p. It says nothing against another tool running it. Requests count as premium requests (Copilot requests). Copilot's own terms were not read. Google (Antigravity, agy) Terms, section 6 "Using third party software, tools, or services to access the Service (e.g. using OpenClaw with Antigravity OAuth) is a breach of this Agreement." It warns that Antigravity and Gemini CLI accounts can be suspended.

items.title: Open questions
items.text:
agy: switched off

Whether KOLONİ starting agy counts as "third party software … to access the Service" is not settled, but it is close to the example Google gives. So KOLONİ never adds agy by itself, offers it only under Experimental, and an agy card on the Models page says why. Switching it on is your choice, and your risk with your Google account.

  • Codex: no rule either way was found.

What a CLI's use costs you is set by your plan; see Usage and budgets.

items.title: Tiers
items.text:
A tier is how strong you say a model is: fast, balanced or strongest. You set it in the Tier column of a provider's Models tab. Fill tiers fills them from the catalogue.

Tiers let KOLONİ pick a model for a job instead of one fixed name:

  • a role can ask for a tier instead of one model;
  • an agent can call a job easy or hard, to go one tier down or up;
  • a chat's Orchestrator can follow how hard your message is.

A model with no tier is only ever picked by name.

items.title: The tier lists
items.text:
Below the provider cards, the Models page shows three lists: Strongest, Balanced and Fast. Each lists its models, numbered in the order they are tried. Drag a model, or use its move up and move down buttons, to change the order; each move saves at once. A model that agents may not use is marked "off for agents". With no tiers at all, the page says "No model has a tier yet".

A model greyed with its provider's state ("not answering") shows how that provider looked when the page read it. A provider that is not installed, not signed in or without a key is passed over until KOLONİ sees it again: the page reads it, or you press its Check. A model server is passed over after not answering for two minutes. Where every model of a tier looks so, the first is still tried.

items.title: Agents may use
items.text:
Each model has an Agents may use switch. On, agents may pick the model by themselves, for example by its tier. Off, only you pick it: in a chat's model picker, or as a role's own model.

A provider with no list of models has one switch for the whole provider: Agents may use this provider. Never run a model that is not on this list keeps agents to the listed models.

What it is good for (for a provider) and Its note for agents (for a model) are short notes that agents read when they choose.

items.title: A role's model
items.text: On the Agents page each role chooses who picks its model: Orchestrator, As the chat, One tier (Fast, Balanced or Strongest) or One model. See Roles.

items.title: Orchestrator model: automatic
items.text: In the chat's model picker, Orchestrator model: automatic sends each message to a fast model, which judges it easy, normal or hard. The Orchestrator then runs on a fast, balanced or strongest model. That is one more request for each message you send. It overrides the Orchestrator role's own model and tier.

items.title: What spends extra requests
items.text:
Some settings make one more model request each time. Each says so where you switch it on.

What When it spends Note what the work found, by itself (Settings › This project › Memory and web) One request after every message. Orchestrator model: automatic (the chat's model picker) One request for each message you send. The Orchestrator answers what it safely can (Settings › This project › When you're asked › When you're away), on a CLI One request of your plan for each answer. Full auto's judge (Settings › This project › When you're asked; on by default) One request of your Judge model (Settings › The app › Agents; the Fast tier's first unless you choose one - on a CLI, of your plan) for each command at Full auto the list does not stop that is not a read or ordinary work. Check what I said first (Settings › This project › When you're asked, under Full auto's judge: It also lets a delete or a push run when a line you saved names it) One request of your Judge model (on a CLI, of your plan) for each harmful-looking command at Full auto. Try a real run (Models page, a CLI) One short run, on your plan. Read now for Claude Code (a provider's card) One short request. Learning a knowledge topic (Memory › Sources to look things up in) Model requests, up to the limit you set. Candidates in a recipe Each candidate is its own agent. Agents on a CLI working at the same time They spend your subscription at the same time.

items.title: Ways to keep a job cheap
items.text:
• Give models tiers, and let roles ask for a tier, so easy jobs go to a fast model. See Tiers.
  • Turn off Agents may use for an expensive model you want to pick only by hand.
  • Set a Monthly budget and a job's budget, Stop the work on a message over this many tokens (Settings › This project › Limits and money), and dollar limits on API keys (a provider's Limits tab).
  • Keep Agents at the same time and Sub-agents per request low (Settings › This project › Limits and money › More limits).
  • Give an MCP server only to the roles that need it, and switch off tools you do not use: every tool's description is sent at every model step.
  • Use a model server on your own machine for work that does not need a large model: it spends no money.
  • On GitHub Copilot CLI, give the provider a model. Copilot's auto picks one for each request; with no model and Medium thinking, Copilot's default spent 7.12 AI credits for the same short answer that auto answered for 0.18 (measured once, 7 Nov 2026, Copilot CLI 1.0.105). Copilot Fusion (fusion, and its High and Max routing) runs each turn on several models: it costs more than auto. See GitHub Copilot CLI.

See Usage and budgets.

items.title: The Usage page
items.text:
Open Usage on the left rail. Choose a period - Today, 7 days, This month, 30 days or All - and This project or All projects. This month is the calendar month, as the budget counts it.

The Usage page, counted from the record: no model is asked.

The page reads from the top:

  • A sentence on the period, such as "This month about 23.40 USD was spent. This month's budget is 46% used. Claude Code has used 62% of the week." The budget's part shows with This project where the project has a monthly budget; the plan's part is the plan window used most, as the CLIs last said it. With nothing priced it says "no money was counted". Under it: Messages, Tokens sent, Tokens written and Cost, with set prices. Messages says how many agents worked in them and, apart, KOLONİ's own requests outside a message: "12 agents", "1 request by KOLONİ itself". The Orchestrator's ask_advisor is such a request of KOLONİ's in its turn: under the advisor's model, and in the turn's spend that the line over the chat says.
  • This month's budget as ten cells, each a tenth of the budget: honey as it fills, a red-orange rim on what is left from 80%, all red-orange once it is over, with the amount, the share used and the days left in words beside them. Once all are full, new work waits for your word (see A project's monthly budget).
  • Plan limits beside it: a bar for each window of a plan, with Check now (see Plan meters).
  • With This project and Today, the day's own numbers: Failed and Files changed, and Say it in words.
  • Day by day: the last 30 days in one strip, whatever the period, a bar a day. It is money where any of it is priced, else the tokens the models reported. A day that ran with nothing known has a dashed stub, never a zero. Under it: the first day, the day that spent most, and today.
  • By provider and model: messages, agents, tokens and cost for each model. A CLI on a subscription, or an API key marked as a plan, says plan instead of a cost; Copilot's AI credits stand beside it, such as "plan · 41 AI credits". A model's Agents count KOLONİ's own requests to it outside a message too, and the line under the table says how many there were: 12 agents and 1 request are 13 there.
  • Chats that spent most: the top three, each opening its chat. All N chats, in numbers unfolds the full table, which every column sorts.
  • Who started it: a bar each for You, KOLONİ itself (requests KOLONİ makes outside a message, such as a real run of a CLI from the Models page) and A trigger, with nobody watching (a turn before 0.1.10, when triggers were removed). In numbers unfolds its table. A night's work while you are ☾ Away counts as yours.
  • With This project, one line on the period's decisions: "12 decisions were made for you this month, 2 of them you haven't seen.", with Open in Ready for you, where Decided for you lists each. See Decisions.

A chat's or a day's cost is its models' costs added up, as the budget adds them. Where none of them has a price, or the costs are in more than one currency, the chats, the starters and the strip are compared by their tokens instead, and a sum of only part of them says "≥".

"Nothing is estimated": tokens are only what the models reported, and what was not reported shows as "–".

GitHub Copilot CLI reports what it spent in its usage checkpoint: its tokens, and its own unit, AI credits (or premium requests, its older unit). They show on the agent's context line, under Details in its window, such as "1,200 in / 300 out · 0.42 AI credits", and added up by model on the Usage page, beside its cost. Run as a session, they are counted from that checkpoint as in Native: measured with copilot -p (CLI 1.0.103), not yet seen in a live session.

items.title: Cards
items.text: Usage's Cards section, which counted the command cards asked by why and suggested a delete rule, was taken out in 0.1.10. What was decided for you, and why, is on Ready for you under Decided for you (Decisions).

items.title: Where the money comes from
items.text:
KOLONİ shows money only from prices:

  1. your own price for a model, if you set one;
  2. otherwise the price in the bundled models.dev catalogue, in USD.

A CLI on a plan has no price for a token, so it never has a cost here. Neither does an API key marked This key is a plan: count no money. A cost shown with "≥" means part of it has no price. Amounts in different currencies are never added together.

items.title: Prices
items.text: The Prices fold lists the models and their prices per million tokens sent and written, and optionally for cache reads and writes. Type a price and a currency, then Save price. "A price belongs to the model's name, whichever provider runs it." Use models.dev's goes back to the catalogue's price.

items.title: A project's monthly budget
items.text:
Set it under Settings › This project › Limits and money › Monthly budget, in the currency of your prices (else USD). It covers this calendar month, by this machine's clock.

  • At 80%, KOLONİ tells you once, and the top bar shows it.
  • At 100%, a new message asks first: "Over this month's budget. Send it anyway?" Press Go on anyway or Cancel. Learn on a knowledge asks the same way.
  • Work on a model with no price is not counted.
  • If your prices are in more than one currency, the budget is not enforced, and the page says so.
  • A plain chat (no folder) belongs to no budget.

The Usage page shows This month's budget as ten cells, how much is used, the days left in the month, and Change in Settings →.

items.title: A job's budget
items.text:
Settings › This project › Limits and money › Stop the work on a message over this many tokens, in sight next to the monthly budget. A job is the work on one message: yours, a To-do task's, or a job's while you're away. KOLONİ checks it before each model step (and as a CLI session's messages arrive) and stops the job once all its agents together have gone over it: "this turn used N tokens, over the project's limit of M". It counts tokens, not money, so it holds a CLI on a plan too, where the CLI reports them. A job tried again, or a message that goes on with it, starts from zero.

The limits few change - how many agents work at once, Continue's steps, a discussion's tokens - are under More limits in the same section.

items.title: Providers' own limits
items.text: Each provider can have a limit in dollars a day or a month, or step down a tier when a plan runs low: its Limits tab on the Models page. See Limits.

items.title: A night's limits
items.text: On the Go away card: Until a time, and spend at most an amount. A night with a monthly budget is held to what the month has left too. See Work while you're away.

items.title: Plan meters
items.text: For Claude Code, Codex, agy and Copilot, the top bar shows how much of the plan is used, from what each CLI last reported. Copilot's chat requests and premium requests show apart (Copilot on your GitHub account). Near the limit (90%), KOLONİ tells you. On the Usage page, Plan limits shows the same with Check now: "These are the limits of the account the CLI on this machine is signed in to." Where a subscription steps down a tier (its Limits on the Models page), a line on its bar marks that share; past it the bar turns orange and its row says so: "Past 80%: a model picked by tier on it is one tier lower".

items.text: Where each setting is. Follow the links for what each does.

items.text: Teams and Folders (each set in its own panel), Page scripts, and, in a chat with no folder, Runs without asking. The same rows are in the sheet Chat settings opens, under the message box. See Settings.

Under the message: Attach, the permission level (its menu holds Full auto's judge, Plan first and Test and review changes), Auto-read, Dictate and Send. Under the box: Workspace, New topic, Chat settings (this chat's sheet) and More (Compare…). See Chat and canvas.

items.title: Models page
items.text:
• Each provider: on / off; tabs Models (each model's Tier, Agents may use, On, note; on GitHub Copilot CLI also Context, and Routing on auto and fusion), Connection, Limits, and Server for a model server on this machine. See Providers.
  • The page: Update catalogue, Keep the catalogue fresh, Fill tiers, the tier lists.

Tools KOLONİ's own tools on / off; each MCP server's trust, tools and roles; each skill's roles and scripts. See KOLONİ's tools. Memory Your preferences · This project's rules. See Memory. items.title: Before the start
items.text: Environment variables: see Environment variables.

items.title: CLIs
items.text:
What KOLONİ supports for each CLI. How to set one up is in Set up a CLI.

CLI Command How it runs (default first) Native asks KOLONİ before Plan read Versions measured with KOLONİ Claude Code claude session, step, native every tool it uses yes (one short request) 2.1.310, 2.1.311, 2.1.312 Codex codex session, native each command and patch, but not those its own allow rules cover yes 0.163.0, 0.164.0 GitHub Copilot CLI copilot session, native every tool it uses, through KOLONİ's own hook (1.0.114 on); on the older protocol, each command, write and read yes 1.0.91, 1.0.103, 1.0.105, 1.0.114 agy (experimental) agy reads, native every tool it uses yes 1.3.3, 1.4.7, 1.4.8

Qoder is no longer run since 0.1.8: see Qoder is no longer supported.

items.title: A version that was not measured
items.text:
KOLONİ records the versions of each CLI that its use of the CLI's protocol was measured with: the last column of the table. A newer version is never refused. KOLONİ tries it once; if it answers as expected it runs, with a note that this version was not measured with KOLONİ. If not, it runs the old way: with KOLONİ's tools, and the CLI's own tools off.

Single behaviours were measured on newer versions too, which does not make them measured versions: Codex 0.172.0 (what it asks KOLONİ before, its own sub-agents switched off, Send now), Claude Code 2.1.332 (Send now) and agy 1.5.18 (a word sent waits for its turn's end). Each is told in Known limits, under Secrets and CLIs.

GitHub Copilot CLI is asked its version and protocol as KOLONİ starts it: on the newer protocol (1.0.114 on) any version runs Native, with that note when it was not measured; on the older one only a measured version does. A Copilot that does not say its version, or speaks a protocol KOLONİ does not know, runs the old way, and the provider's card on the Models page says why. See Set up a CLI.

items.title: What every CLI has in common
items.text:
• You install it and sign in yourself, in your own terminal.
  • Its use counts against your plan with that vendor; KOLONİ shows no money for it.
  • When a CLI runs Native, its model reads its commands' raw output; KOLONİ masks keys only in what it records and shows.

See Subscription rules and Known limits.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
KOLONİ reads these when it starts. It does not read a .env file: set them in the shell before you start it.

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
$env:KOLONI_PORT = 8800; .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m app.main

KOLONI_PORT=8800 .venv/bin/python -m app.main

items.title: Where and how KOLONİ runs
items.text: Variable Default What it does KOLONI_PORT 8790 The port KOLONİ listens on. KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT runtime/ in KOLONİ's folder Where the database, working copies, backups and logs are kept. Two KOLONİs must not share one. KOLONI_HOST 127.0.0.1 The address KOLONİ listens on. Anything other than 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost is refused at the start, except inside the Docker image. KOLONI_PAGE_KEY a new one each start A fixed page key. KOLONİ takes it out of its own environment once read, so its commands and agents do not get it. KOLONI_OPEN_BROWSER 1 0: do not open the page in the browser at the start. KOLONI_DEV not set 1: also accept the live-reload page on port 5173 (for development).

items.title: The first start only
items.text:
These make the first providers. After the first start, change providers on the Models page; changing these does nothing to providers that already exist.

Variable Default What it does KOLONI_MODEL_BASE_URL http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 The address of the "Local" provider. KOLONI_MODEL_ID the first model the server lists Local's default model. KOLONI_MODEL_API_KEY none Local's key. KOLONI_DETECT_CLI 1 First start only: add Claude Code and Codex as providers if they are installed. 0 skips this.

items.title: Models and agents
items.text: Variable Default What it does KOLONI_MODEL_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS 900 How long a model may take to start answering before the run fails. KOLONI_MODEL_STALL_SECONDS 120 How long an answer may pause before the run fails. KOLONI_CONTEXT_CHARS 240000 How much history, in characters, an agent keeps when its model's context window is not known. KOLONI_SEARCH_SECONDS 20 How long a search through the project's files may take before it is given up. A value that is not a positive number is ignored.

items.title: Background work
items.text: Variable Default What it does KOLONI_CLOCK 1 0: the app's clock does not run: a night while you're away does not go on by itself, and the day's summary is not sent. Its old name, KOLONI_TRIGGER_CLOCK, is still read for one release. KOLONI_CATALOGUE_REFRESH 1 0: never download the model catalogue at the start. Otherwise it is downloaded again once it is a week old, unless Keep the catalogue fresh is off on the Models page.

items.title: The local model server and MCP servers
items.text: Variable Default What it does KOLONI_LOCAL_SERVER llama-server on PATH The program the Models page's Server tab starts, until you choose another there: the full path of llama-server in a llama.cpp build's bin folder. KOLONI_NVIDIA_SMI nvidia-smi The program the Server tab asks for GPU memory and load. KOLONI_MCP_HOME KOLONI/mcp/ in your cache folder (%LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows), one folder per runtime Where the MCP servers KOLONİ starts keep their files.

items.title: Variables KOLONİ gives to commands
items.text: Agents' commands get this machine's environment, except variables with secret names (such as GITHUB_TOKEN or OPENAI_API_KEY) and the ways into a program you are signed in to (GIT_ASKPASS, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, VSCODE_*, CLAUDE_CODE_* and the like), unless you name them under Settings › This project › When you're asked › Secret variables commands may see. A project whose tests use git over ssh needs SSH_AUTH_SOCK named there. KOLONİ's own git, which pushes for you, keeps all of them. With Planted test key (canary) on, they also get a made-up KOLONI_CANARY_KEY. In Docker, commands get none of this machine's environment.

items.title: KOLONİ's own data: runtime/
items.text:
In KOLONİ's folder, or wherever KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT says.

Path What it holds data/koloni.db The database. API keys are in it, in plain text. data/backups/ Copies of the database made before upgrades and by the update script (the last five), and at the first start of a day (daily-…, the last three). logs/koloni.log The log; it rotates at 10 MB and keeps five old files. attachments/ Files attached to messages, per chat. skills/ KOLONİ's copies of skills. copies/ Sub-agents' working copies (see below). cli-homes/ Claude Code's and Codex's sign-in folders, one per provider, when you chose Its own for KOLONİ. Kept across restarts. And copilot-sessions/, one home per GitHub Copilot session run Native, kept while its topic goes on. server-homes/ Empty settings folders for Claude Code and Codex when they run on a model server of your own, with none of your sign-in. agy-home/ A new folder for each agy run, cleared when KOLONİ starts. models_dev.json The model catalogue, once updated. local-server.json The Server tab's settings. before-restore/ Your data as it was before a restore. Never removed by KOLONİ.

runtime/ is in .gitignore.

items.title: Outside runtime/
items.text:
• Working copies of a project in git: if runtime/copies would be inside a git repository (as it is in KOLONİ's own folder), copies go to %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOLONI\copies on Windows, or ~/.local/share/KOLONI/copies elsewhere. A project with no git has its copies in its own .koloni/copies/, and a branch's worktree is in the project's .koloni/worktrees/ (where).
  • GitHub Copilot CLI run as a session gets an empty settings folder inside each run's temporary folder, removed when the run ends; run Native, its session's home is under runtime/cli-homes/copilot-sessions/. It never uses your own ~/.copilot. It signs in with the provider's token, or else with your own gh login.
  • Claude Code and Codex with My own sign-in use yours (~/.claude, ~/.codex).
  • MCP servers start in %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOLONI\mcp on Windows, ~/Library/Caches/KOLONI/mcp on macOS, or ~/.cache/KOLONI/mcp on Linux.

items.title: In your project
items.text: KOLONİ's own files are under .koloni/; see Recipe, role and skill formats. KOLONİ never changes your project's own .gitignore. Files you save from a message go to docs/attachments/.

items.title: What an export holds
items.text: Export everything holds the database, skills/, attachments/, models_dev.json and local-server.json. It does not hold your projects, their .koloni/, working copies, logs, CLI sign-ins or the database backups. See Backup and update.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
A recipe kept in a folder is a JSON file in .koloni/recipes/, named from the recipe in lowercase ASCII with hyphens. KOLONİ writes it when you save from the Recipes tab; you can also read or change it by hand. A file KOLONİ cannot read is listed with the reason.

{
  "name": "Fix and test",
  "graph": {
    "version": 1,
    "steps": [
      { "id": "fix", "name": "Fix it", "who": { "role": "Coder" } },
      { "id": "test", "name": "Test it", "who": { "role": "Tester" }, "done_when": "no_findings" }
    ],
    "groups": [],
    "ends": [{ "id": "end", "then": "in" }],
    "arrows": [
      { "from": "start", "to": "fix" },
      { "from": "fix", "to": "test" },
      { "from": "test", "to": "end" }
    ],
    "loops": [{ "from": "test", "to": "fix", "rounds": 2 }]
  }
}
  • name: 1 to 60 characters.
  • Ids: letters, digits, _ and -, at most 40. start is the user's message.
  • steps (at most 60): id, name, who, and optionally done_when (done or no_findings), if_fails (ask or stop), ask_me (true or false), group (a group's id), when ("problem": only if the step before found a problem), pos ({"x", "y"} in the recipe editor).
  • who is one of:
    • {"role": "Coder", "most": 2}: a role, with at most 1 to 5 agents;
    • {"team": "Web app"}: a team's stages;
    • {"lead": true}: the Orchestrator picks;
    • {"room": ["Coder", "Reviewer"]} (before 0.1.10): read as an "all at once" group in its place, a step of each role;
    • {"experts": "all"} (or "stale", "learned"): the team's experts;
    • {"candidates": "Coder", "most": 3, "target": 80, "models": "auto"}: 2 to 5 candidates; models is "auto", "same", or a list of {"provider_id", "model_id"}.
  • groups (at most 20): id, name, pos, wait (all or first). Steps join a group by its id.
  • ends (at most 10): id, then (in: take the work in; report: say what was found).
  • arrows (at most 200): {"from", "to"}.
  • loops (at most 20): {"from", "to", "rounds"}, going back, 1 to 5 rounds.

A recipe must start from start, reach an end on every path, and loop only backwards with a round limit. Only recipes kept in KOLONİ can be a team's default or picked for a chat.

items.title: Roles
items.text: Roles have no file format. You make and change them on the Agents page.

items.title: Skills
items.text:
A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md, in Claude Code's form:

---
name: my-skill
description: What it is for, in a sentence or two.
license: MIT
allowed-tools: Bash, Read
---

Instructions for the agent.
  • name (required): letters, digits, ., _ and -, starting with a letter or digit, at most 64.
  • description: at most 1024 characters are kept.
  • license: used if the folder has no LICENSE or COPYING file.
  • allowed-tools: KOLONİ maps these to its groups of tools. A role that lacks them is shown, with a way to give them.
  • At most 200 files and 5 MiB in all; SKILL.md at most 256 KiB; a .zip at most 25 MiB. Secret files are not copied.

items.title: The folder's .koloni/
items.text:
Path What it is rules.md The project's rules (Memory page, at most 1500 characters). Every agent is told them. settings.json Where commands run and the web search order (see below). recipes/ Recipes kept in this folder. knowledge/ Knowledge topics: each one's guide; the pages read are kept out of git. shared/ Files teams share while they work; kept out of git. tmp/ The agents' scratch space; kept out of git. The copies of images an agent looked at (tmp/images/) and the browser's screenshots go after a week, as new ones come. worktrees/ KOLONİ's git worktrees for a branch's agents (a ☾ Away job, a team on a branch), each KOLONİ's in a folder of its own; kept out of git by the repository's .git/info/exclude and by .koloni/.gitignore (where). copies/ Sub-agents' working copies, in a project with no git only; likewise.

settings.json holds only these keys:

{
  "exec_location": "docker",
  "docker_image": "python:3.12",
  "docker_network": false,
  "search_order": "builtin"
}

exec_location is host or docker; search_order is builtin or cli. Other keys are ignored. Settings that came from another machine are shown to you before they are used (Use them / Not now).

items.title: Glossary
items.text:
KOLONİ's own words, as they appear on screen.

Advisor model A model the Orchestrator may ask for advice on a hard choice (ask_advisor, at most 3 times a turn). You choose it in Settings › The app › Agents. See Talking while agents work. After this turn A button of the message box while a turn runs: your message waits in the queue and starts a turn of its own. See Send now. Agent One worker in a turn: a role running on a model. The canvas draws each agent as a small box: its name and model, its state, and what it did. Its tools, commands and files are in the Inspector. Agents may use A switch for each model on the Models page. When it is on, agents may pick that model by themselves, not only you. Away (☾) On a chat's status line: that chat finishes its turn, then the To-do tasks you tick are worked through, each in its own copy, until you press I'm back or write again. The Orchestrator decides for you what it safely can meanwhile. See Work while you're away. Always run A button on a command's card. It keeps a rule for that chat, so the same kind of command runs without a card next time. See Permission levels. Background agent An agent the Orchestrator of an API model opened in the background: the Orchestrator goes on at once and reads the agent's report when it comes. See Agents in the background. Branch (a team's) A git branch koloni/<name> that the Orchestrator can give a team's work. It starts from your folder as it is, your uncommitted files too, and its card carries the agent's work alone. Stopped, the agent's work stays committed there; told to go on, it goes on on the same branch. The card offers Merge or Open pull request. See Branches. Candidates A recipe step given to several agents at once, each in its own working copy. Each one's work is scored from 0 to 100 by the project's Measure command, and the best one is kept. Card A box in the chat that waits for your answer, for example "Run this command?" with Run once, Always run … and Reject. There are cards for file changes, commands, web searches, secret files, opening a sub-agent, plans and more. Check what I said first Full auto's judge's question of your words (its box in Settings › This project › When you're asked, since 0.1.9): at Full auto, before a delete, a push or a send waits for you on a card - or a delete in the project, or a plain push of your feature branch, goes to Full auto's judge -, a fast model reads your own words, and the command runs without a card only where a line of yours names it - never a force push. A line of your preferences can only stop a command, and of your messages only this turn's run a push, a pull request or a merge. Until a model has passed its measurement, a push, a pull request or a merge you asked for gets a card that quotes you instead, one click. See Permission levels. Compare Compare… under More next to the message box. One message goes to two models side by side, each in its own working copy. Nothing reaches your project until you keep one. Coordinator A team's own lead, shown as "Team coordinator". It runs its team's stages and reports to the Orchestrator. Core The facts in a project's memory: what you approved or wrote yourself. See Memory. Decided for you Where you see the cards the Orchestrator decided for you: while you were away (☾ Away), or once a card waited the project's minutes (Settings › This project › When you're asked › When you're away); the decisions the Orchestrator took without asking and noted, "Decided: …" (their Change takes your own words); the commands KOLONİ's judge refused; and the commands Check what I said first ran, or did not run, on a line of yours. The project's whole list is on Work's Ready for you tab, with OK and Change; a chat says it in one line: Decisions. Discussion Several agents talking one question through in rounds, with nobody changing anything meanwhile. An agent starts one; it has a token budget. Fact A short piece of memory that you approved or wrote, usually pointing to lines of a file. It is given to an agent whose task names its subject. Hive keeper The built-in role that keeps the To-do list: it turns a goal into stories and tasks, each with what makes it done, and puts them in order. The rough note's Split into tasks on To-do asks the Hive keeper for its way of writing a note as stories and their tasks. See To-do. Journal The notes in a project's memory: what agents wrote while they worked. Agents find notes only when they look. Knowledge The Memory page's second part, Sources to look things up in: expert topics, each read once from web pages or project files into pages and a guide. Roles that know a topic use it while they work, and an agent's Recall looks in its role's. See Sources. MCP server A program on your machine that gives agents more tools. You add it on the Tools page, under Servers. Each tool asks before it runs unless you say otherwise. Measure command A command, set under Settings › This project › When the work is done, whose last line of output is a score from 0 to 100. It scores candidates. Memory What a project remembers between chats: your preferences, the project's rules and Project notes, facts and notes. See Memory. Note A piece of memory an agent wrote with its Remember tool. See Memory. Notebook A job's short notebook - a To-do story's, or a task's of no story (a task's chat, a night's job) - given to each of its turns as data, for as long as the job runs. KOLONİ, the Orchestrator, the agents' notes for the whole turn and yours go in. See The job's notebook. Orchestrator The agent you talk to in a chat. It plans, asks and checks, and hands changes to files to sub-agents, unless you let it change files itself (Settings › This project › How agents work › Who changes the files). (Behind the scenes its role is named Lead.) Outside content Text that comes from outside your messages: web pages and searches, MCP tools' results, Knowledge pages and GitHub issues. KOLONİ frames it as data, not instructions, for the agents. See Outside content. Page key A secret that the KOLONİ page sends with every request, so that a program on your machine cannot approve cards or change settings in your place. It changes each time KOLONİ starts. Open KOLONİ from the link in its window. Part In the project map, a folder with its own project file (such as pyproject.toml or package.json), with its language and test command. In a recipe drawing, a step or a group of steps. Permission level What agents may do without asking: Ask before changes, Auto-edit files or Full auto. See Permission levels. Plain chat A chat with no folder ("No folder · a plain chat"). It is only talk: no files and no commands. Plan first A switch in the permission level's menu under the message box. Each new message first gets a plan to approve before anything changes. Project A folder your agents work in. Each project has its own settings, memory and To-do list. Project notes The lines you keep from the Add to Project notes? card at the end of a turn: part of Memory, under the project's rules, given to the Orchestrator every turn as notes. Provider Where a model runs: an OpenAI-compatible server, the Anthropic API, or a CLI you are signed in to (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, agy). You add providers on the Models page. Ready for you The panel and page that list everything waiting for your word. The panel lists the open chat's in two parts, Needs your answer and Ready to take in, then what waits elsewhere. The page holds the last ☾ Away's report, Waiting for your word in one list and Decided for you - what was decided for you in the project (Decisions) - with To-do beside them (Ready and approval cards). Recipe The drawn steps of a piece of work: who does each step, what runs at once, where it loops back and how it ends. Recipes are on the Agents page. Role What an agent is for: a description, instructions, the tools it may use and, if you like, its own model. KOLONİ comes with built-in roles such as Planner, Coder, Tester, Reviewer, Researcher, Debugger, Architect and Docs writer. You can add your own. Room Until 0.1.10, two to six agents working on one goal at the same time, in one working copy. Rooms are gone: a discussion lets agents talk a question through, and sub-agents (or a recipe's All at once step) work at the same time, each on its own part. An old chat's room is one line where it was; what was said in it is kept in KOLONİ's record. Scout The built-in role that keeps watch on the To-do list: it splits vague tasks, asks what is missing, flags duplicates, stale and blocked tasks, and checks finished tasks against what makes them done. After a turn that did something, KOLONİ also makes one small model request with no tools in its name, which suggests at most three follow-up tasks, each with the words it came from; on the canvas that is a small box under the turn. See Follow-up tasks. Send now The message box's first button (Enter) while a turn runs: your message goes into the turn at work, and the Orchestrator reads it in this turn. See Send now and After this turn. Skill A folder with a SKILL.md and its files, in the form Claude Code reads. You add skills on the Tools page and give them to roles. Stop everything The button in the top bar that stops every turn in every chat and holds the To-do tasks waiting in a chat's queue, and work while you're away. While it holds, it reads Held · Resume. See Chat and canvas. Story On To-do (a tab of Work), tasks and bugs that go on together. Its state comes from its tasks; it is done only when you close it. It has a short notebook, given to each of its turns as data, and its tasks go on in one topic of a chat. A bug is a task about something that works wrong. See Stories and The job's notebook. Sub-agent An agent that the Orchestrator (or another agent) opens for a part of the work. It works in its own working copy. Take in Bringing finished work from a working copy into your project. Every card that does this says Take in. Team A named group of roles with stages: Plan, Build, Check, and Write & keep up. A chat can work with teams, picked under Teams for this chat: Orchestrator decides, Manual or No teams. Teams' work is ready The card where a recipe's work ends. It asks whether to take the work into the project, with Take in, Fix the findings and Ask for changes. Thinking How hard a role's model thinks, set on its Model card: Auto (the agent that opens it picks a level for each task, up to a most) or One fixed level, on a ladder from Off to Max. See Roles. Tier How strong you say a model is: fast, balanced or strongest. You set it for each model on the Models page. A model with no tier is never picked by itself. To-do A project's tasks, in your order, on the Work page's To-do tab: stories hold tasks and bugs. Ticked tasks run in a chat you give them to (Do in chat), one by one, at that chat's level and on its model. Agents, and the Scout after a turn, propose tasks; you decide. See To-do. Topic The turns of a chat that go on with one piece of work. The Orchestrator is sent its own topic's turns, and the chat's other topics by name only; an agent of an earlier turn is gone on with only inside its topic. New topic, under the message box, starts one with your next message. A To-do story given to a chat goes on in a topic of its own, its tasks one after another. See Topics and Doing tasks in a chat. Turn Everything that happens for one message, and for those you send into it with Send now: the Orchestrator's answer, the agents it opened, their tools, commands and changes. The canvas draws one turn at a time. Where the work is The panel the git button in the top bar opens ("⑂ main · 4 changed"): your branch, the agents' copies in this chat, and other branches, each saying how the work stands. See Branches. Work A page on the rail (0.1.10; once Ready), with the count of what waits for your word: two tabs, Ready for you and To-do. It opens on the tab shown last. See Ready and approval cards. Workspace The side window with the project's files, what agents changed, wrote or showed, and what waits for you. Working copy A copy of your project, outside your folder (in its .koloni/copies/ where it has no git), where a sub-agent makes its changes. Its work comes back to you on a card to take in or discard.

items.title: How a CLI runs
items.text:
A CLI provider has a setting How it runs:

On screen What it means One session per agent, with KOLONİ's tools (recommended) One CLI session per agent, using KOLONİ's tools. One run per model step, with KOLONİ's tools Claude Code only: the CLI runs once for each model step, slower, and the answer arrives all at once. Native: its own tools, in the project The CLI uses its own tools in your folder and asks KOLONİ before each one. Experimental: offered with Show experimental features on. Reads with its own tools; started without leave to write or run agy only: it reads with its own tools and cannot change anything.

items.title: Known limits
items.text: What KOLONİ does not do yet, or does only in part.

items.title: An alpha
items.text: KOLONİ is an alpha (0.1.x): expect rough edges. Several paths were built against stand-ins only, including the Server tab for llama.cpp, Copilot with a GitHub token, and some limit and credit messages.

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
• A command that names a secret file, or searches the whole folder when the folder holds one (grep -r, rg, gci | gc), is asked about at every level, Full auto too. A script that opens a secret file without naming it (it builds the name, say) is not caught. Only Docker and Copilot's sandbox hide secret files from commands; KOLONİ's own commands on this machine, Claude Code, Codex and agy do not.
  • When it runs Native, Codex asks KOLONİ before its commands - a read of .env too (measured on 27 Nov 2026 with Codex 0.172.0: it asked before both Get-Content readme.txt and Get-Content .env; this guide said it ran its own safe commands unasked, and older versions were not measured again). A command an allow rule of Codex's own covers still runs without asking; KOLONİ records it after it ran, so no card stands in its way. agy reading with its own tools has no hook: its reads, of a secret file too, are not asked about at any level.
  • A command you approve can still print, encode or send a secret it was given.
  • An agent's request for a key on a hidden card is not available to CLIs working with their own tools.
  • A branch deleted because it held a secret you gave still has its commits in git's reflog until git prunes them.

items.title: Outside content
items.text:
• Text from the web, MCP tools, Knowledge and GitHub issues is framed as data, but the frame only tells the model; a model can still follow what it says.
  • Only KOLONİ's own tools frame what they bring in. A CLI's own web fetch, MCP servers or file reads are not framed.
  • A forged end of the frame is not caught when it is written with look-alike letters from other scripts, with full-width or mathematical letters, with words joined by marks (end-of-the, end_of_the), or with markdown or HTML inside it. See Security model.

items.title: CLIs
items.text:
• When a CLI runs Native, it runs its commands itself, so its model reads their raw output; KOLONİ masks keys only in what it records and shows. Measured once on Copilot (Native) with a made-up GitHub token (ghp_…) in a command's output: it was *** in the model's answer and absent from Copilot's raw stream, so Copilot hid that kind of key itself; other kinds of key were not tried. Claude Code, Codex and agy run Native were not measured. With KOLONİ's tools (as a session, or one run per step), the keys KOLONİ knows and values shaped or named like keys are masked before the model reads the output.
  • Copilot does not report which paths its PowerShell commands touch, so at Full auto a command that writes a protected file without naming it (a script, a path it builds) runs without a card. The same goes for KOLONİ's own commands at Full auto: one that names the file (echo … > .claude/settings.json) is asked about, but a script that writes ~/.claude/settings.json is not. Such a file in the project is put back, and you are asked whether to keep it; one outside the project is not.
  • Claude Code and agy run Native (and Copilot where it cannot sandbox its commands) have no sandbox of KOLONİ's: it can stop what they do only at their hook. A write with their own file tools outside the project and the folders it also works in (or that you allowed) is asked about on a card at every level, Full auto too (in a working copy, refused: it may write only in the copy); one into a CLI's own folder (.claude, .gemini, .codex or .copilot in your home folder) or another place KOLONİ never opens (.ssh, browser profiles) is refused. Their commands are judged by what they name: a command that writes outside the project, for example to the Startup folder or a PowerShell profile, runs without a card at Full auto, and at any level where an allow rule covers it, unless it names a CLI's settings folder such as .claude or .gemini, or a secret file, or it deletes or sends data off the machine.
  • Claude Code run Native does not say where its commands run, so KOLONİ judges each one as run in the project folder. If the CLI keeps a cd from an earlier command, later relative paths are judged at the wrong place: after you approve cd .., reading a file there by its name is taken for a read in the project and is not asked about below Full auto. Claude Code's Bash tool was measured not to keep one (2.1.325, Windows, run without its screen and as KOLONİ runs it: each Bash command starts in the project folder again, and KOLONİ starts it with the setting that asks for that); its PowerShell tool is said by the CLI to keep its folder, and other versions, Linux and macOS are not measured - so a cd into .koloni/tmp/ by Claude Code's PowerShell tool is still asked. A command of its that itself names a folder to run in is asked at every level: KOLONİ cannot check it.
  • GitHub Copilot CLI run Native does not say where its commands run either. On its newer protocol (Copilot 1.0.114 on) KOLONİ puts each PowerShell command in the project folder itself (a Set-Location into it before each, through its hook: where it cannot go there, the command does not run) and judges it there, so a cd into .koloni/tmp/ runs without a card at Full auto; a delete inside .koloni/tmp/ is still a card. Bash (Linux, macOS) gets no such prefix: there the cd is asked as before. On the older protocol, a Copilot version measured with KOLONİ - 1.0.105 so far, by the version Copilot itself reports - starts a command that names no shell of its own in a new shell in the project folder, with the same result; once a command has named a shell, the cd is asked as before.
