  1. Model providers: your messages and the agents' work go to the providers you add. CLIs talk to their own vendors. The Orchestrator's ask_advisor sends its summary, its question and its turn's last steps, masked, to the Advisor model - by default a provider other than the Orchestrator's.
  2. Web searches: to your own SearXNG if you set one, then DuckDuckGo and a CLI's search, in the order you set, and last the Anthropic API with a provider's key. Below Full auto a search asks first, unless you allowed searching in that chat.
  3. Web requests agents make, to public addresses, after a card or a rule.
  4. The agents' browser: previews on this machine, and sites you allowed.
  5. Voice: Gemini's voices send the text they read to Google, only with your key. Speech recognition is your browser's: in Chrome and Edge what you say is sent to Google's or Microsoft's service. A system voice marked online sends what it reads to its maker. KOLONİ keeps no sound and sends none.
  6. The model catalogue (models.dev): when you press Update catalogue, and at a start once your copy is a week old, unless Keep the catalogue fresh is off or KOLONI_CATALOGUE_REFRESH=0.
  7. Skills from GitHub, when you read or add one.
  8. Checking an MCP package: its name to npm or PyPI, and to osv.dev for known malware, when you ask.
  9. Knowledge: the pages a topic learns from, its research searches, and a repository cloned from GitHub when you press Learn.
  10. Pull requests: pushing a branch and opening a pull request, when you choose that; and reading one's reviews and checks with your own gh when the Orchestrator calls read_pr_feedback.
  11. Plan and balance checks: when you press Check now or Read now.
  12. What agents' commands and MCP servers reach. MCP servers run with your own rights, outside KOLONİ's cards.

items.title: Deleting
items.text:
• Chats: archive them first, then delete them from the archive. "This cannot be undone in KOLONİ." Their messages, their agents' work and their usage go too, and the Claude Code sessions their agents kept under cli-homes/ (each one's transcript and file history; anything else Claude Code keeps of a session stays), their Codex threads' records there, and their Copilot sessions' homes under cli-homes/copilot-sessions/, whole.
  • Providers, roles, skills, MCP servers, teams, recipes, knowledge and To-do tasks can each be deleted on their page. A provider's sign-in folder under cli-homes/ goes with it, its login and kept sessions with it.
  • Memory is never deleted from the page: removing a fact hides it from agents and keeps it in History.
  • A project is deleted in Settings › This project › This folder, once you type its name: its chats, memory, knowledge, To-do tasks and usage go, with the files KOLONİ kept of its chats under runtime/ (attachments, CLI sessions), as a chat's delete takes them. Its folder, its git and its .koloni/ stay.
  • Old live updates go by themselves: at each start, KOLONİ deletes the events older than 30 days that it sent to the page, each tool call with its arguments and result among them. Chats, messages and the agents' work are kept apart and stay. Text tried to give orders warnings are kept.

To remove everything, stop KOLONİ and delete its runtime/ folder, and KOLONİ's folders named above (KOLONI under %LOCALAPPDATA% or your cache), if they were used.

items.title: A security problem
items.text:
Do not open a public issue: until it is fixed, anyone could use it. Report it privately on GitHub:

  1. Open the repository's Security tab.
  2. Choose Report a vulnerability.
  3. Say what you found, how to reproduce it, and what an attacker could do with it.

Only the maintainers see it. The fix is prepared there in private; once a release carries it, the advisory is published and you are credited unless you ask not to be.

What to report: an agent writing, running or reaching the network where your permission level says it must ask; another site driving KOLONİ; KOLONİ's own data, keys or CLI sign-ins reachable from a project; a provider key shown in the page, a log or an export. The limits the Security model names are known; a way around a check it says holds is a vulnerability.

items.title: A bug
items.text: Open an issue on the repository. Say what you did, what you expected, and what happened instead. Say which release or commit you run (git log -1 in KOLONİ's folder); the backend's log is runtime/logs/koloni.log. Look through a log before you attach it: it can hold file paths and parts of your chats.

items.title: KOLONİ's tools
items.text: Tools are what agents can do: read files, run commands, search the web and more. Open Tools on the left rail: "What agents can do. Which role has which is on that role's Tools tab; here, the tool itself." The page has three tabs: KOLONİ's tools, Servers and Skills. The Add button next to the heading adds a server or a skill.

items.title: The cells
items.text:
Each tool and each server has a honeycomb cell that says how it is let run. Its key is under the heading, once for the three tabs:

Cell Meaning Green, filled runs without asking Honey rim, lightly filled asks you first - on a card: most as the permission level says; a server's tool, a new skill and a folder outside the project at every level Empty off: given to no agent Red-orange, filled changed: trust taken back - a server whose new reading found new or changed tools (Trust)

The colour is never all there is: a cell's meaning is its name for a screen reader and its tooltip, and the words beside it say it too. The Servers tab says how many servers are watched ("2 watching"), and Skills how many skills agents proposed.

items.title: The KOLONİ's tools tab
items.text:
"KOLONİ's own tools, grouped as a role's Tools tab has them: one "by role" is given there; one with a switch, switched off here, is given to no agent." Each tool has its cell: green where it runs without asking, a honey rim where it waits for your yes on a card ("asks you first, on a card"; the groups below mark those "asks"), empty where it is switched off here. Five of them can be switched off for every agent at once:

Tool What it does Search the web "Looks things up on the web: a few results with their addresses" Web requests "Calls an address on the internet and reads its answer" Read attached files "Reads the text of files you attach to a message: code, PDF, Word" Read earlier output again "Reads the whole output of an earlier command or tool in this chat that was cut short" Diagram pictures "Draws a draw.io diagram of the project as a PNG or SVG picture beside it"

A tool switched off here is given to no agent, whatever its role says. Claude Code's and Codex's own web tools switch off with Search the web and Web requests. While either is off, a command that reaches the internet (curl, git clone, an https address, bash's /dev/tcp/) asks you on a card at every level, Full auto too.

items.title: Every tool, by group
items.text:
Which tools an agent has is set per role, on the role's Tools tab on the Agents page. There they are grouped like this, and so they are on the KOLONİ's tools tab, marked "by role". Read attached files (with Files) and Read earlier output again (with Commands) have no role tile: only their switch here. "Asks" means it waits for your card, as the chat's permission level says (see Permission levels).

Group Tools Files List folders · Read files · Search · Look at images · Write files (asks) · Edit files (asks) · Show you a file · Diagram pictures · Ask for a folder (asks) Commands Run commands (asks) Web Search the web (asks) · Web requests (asks) Browser Open a page (asks) · Screenshots · Click · Type · Press keys · Scroll · Read the page · Console Team Notify you · Open sub-agents · New roles (asks) · New skills (asks) · Ask you · Message agents · Discussions · Leave notes · Read notes To-do Read the To-do list · Add tasks (asks) · Change tasks (asks) Memory Remember · Recall

New skills and Ask for a folder always go to a card. Open a page asks for a site off the browser's list below Full auto, and for a site marked Ask first at every level.

Recall is an agent's one tool to look things up: the project's memory and earlier messages, and, for a role that uses knowledge, that knowledge's pages too (How agents look things up).

A role with Run commands also gets two tools for a command that keeps running in the chat (a dev server), in a turn you watch: one reads what it printed since, the other stops it - only one the agent started itself. See Preview. Reading, it can first wait for a piece of text to be printed - "listening on", "passed" - up to 2 minutes (30 seconds unless it says), instead of spending a step on each look: it is told the line it was seen in, or that it was not seen in that time, or that the command ended first. It is a piece of text as printed, not a pattern, and it is looked for only in what the agent may read: a secret, hidden in the output, is never found.

The Orchestrator, at its own work in a project, also has run_checks: KOLONİ's checks of its work now - the tests, the type and style checks, the Reviewer and the live try, as the turn's end runs them -, waited for. Its answer starts with CHECKS: green, CHECKS: red or CHECKS: not complete. Say "if the tests pass, commit it" and the Orchestrator commits only on green. A red answer is no fix round, and the turn's end still runs its own checks. See Checks on asking.

It also has read_status, which only reads: KOLONİ's records of this project, now - what waits for you (cards, what a night parked, the morning's push, To-do proposals, tasks at "done?"), work kept and not taken in, the koloni/ branches on record with their commits where KOLONİ counted them, this month's spend against the budget - turns with no price said apart, never a made-up zero - (and a night's against its money limit while you're away), and the newest 10 decisions taken for you. It never reads another project's, nor git or the network. Every command, path, question, title and reason in it is an agent's or your words: masked, cut and quoted as data, with KOLONİ's note where it reads like orders. Its answer is at most 3 KB; past that, whole lines are left out and a last line says how many. A sub-agent is not given it, nor a side of a comparison, nor an Orchestrator whose role has no To-do tools.

While its agents work (0.1.11), the Orchestrator also has stop_agent: it stops one agent it opened in this turn with Open sub-agents, alone - its work so far kept for your Take in, nothing of it in the project; any other is refused ("… is not one you opened in this turn", "… has finished"). The Orchestrator of an API model may open an agent in the background (Open sub-agents with background) and run a command in the background (Run commands with background, where it has the two tools for a command that keeps running): it goes on at once and is told when each ends. Beside them it has agents_at_work (who of the turn is at work, since when, what each waits for and last said), update_plan (its plan shown to you, an API model's), ask_advisor (a second model's advice, three times a turn: your Advisor model, else another provider's), note_decision (a decision it took for you, a row of Decided for you), suggest_preference (your own sentence of the turn for Your preferences, added with Undo, or on a card you Add - as you set it) and, where gh is installed and the origin is on GitHub, read_pr_feedback (one pull request's reviews, comments and failing checks, read only). None is a sub-agent's. See Talking while agents work.

A role needs at least one tool. Tools from MCP servers and skills are given to roles on the Tools page; see MCP servers and Skills.

items.title: Big files
items.text:
• Write files and Edit files leave a file larger than 1 MiB alone, and do not make one larger than that. To replace such a file, the agent is told to run a command, which Revert cannot take back, or to write the new content to another file.
  • Search does not read files over 256 KB. Its answer names them, up to five and then how many more, so the agent can read them in parts or search them with a command. Big binary files are left out without a word.

items.title: MCP servers and trust
items.text:
An MCP server is a program on this machine that gives agents more tools. "A server runs with your rights on this machine": it can read and write files anywhere you can, and reach the network. KOLONİ's cards do not stand between a server and your machine; they stand between an agent and the server's tools.

Servers are on the Tools page, tab Servers: "Programs that give agents more tools. A new one asks before every call until you trust it." The tab says how many servers are watched ("2 watching").

Each server is a card. Its head has its on / off switch, its cell - how far its tools may go without you -, its name and state (trusted, watching, trust taken back or could not be read), its command, how many tools it has and when they were read, and the roles that may use it. Click its name to open it under its head; one is open at a time.

Cell The server Green Trusted, and at least one of its tools runs without asking - or, its tools not shown after a failed reading, may. Honey rim Watched: every call asks. Or trusted, with every tool on Ask. Empty Off, not read yet, or none of its tools on. Red-orange A reading on this page took its trust back.

items.title: Adding a server
items.text:
Press Add and choose:

  • A server, ready-made (from KOLONİ's list): Filesystem, GitHub, Browser (Playwright), Fetch, REA, Context7, Chrome DevTools and Git. A card only fills in the form for you.
  • A server, from its page: paste the setup text from the server's page. KOLONİ reads an mcpServers block, a single server, VS Code's servers, or a claude mcp add line, and shows what it read. Tokens are kept secret. Press Add for the servers, or Edit before adding. Servers reached by a web address are not accepted.
  • A server, by hand: a Name (it cannot be changed later; agents see its tools as name__tool), the Command with one argument a line, and any variables (Add a variable). Press Add server.

Variable values are kept in plain text in KOLONİ's local database and never shown again. "Other programs on this machine can see the arguments of the command: put a secret in a variable."

A server gets its own variables and, of this machine's environment, only what programs need to run (PATH, the home and temp folders, APPDATA and the like): none of KOLONİ's or a CLI's sign-in variables. What it needs beyond that goes in its own variables: npm_config_* or UV_* (a private registry or index), NODE_OPTIONS, HTTPS_PROXY or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (a proxy, its own certificates), on Linux DISPLAY, WAYLAND_DISPLAY and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (a browser with a window), DOCKER_HOST or DOCKER_CONTEXT, and SSH_AUTH_SOCK.

A project's own .mcp.json is not read.

items.title: Reading its tools
items.text:
A new server offers no tools until it is read. Open its card and press Read its tools.

If the command may download a package first (npx, uvx and the like), a card says so before it starts. First look for it in osv.dev's known-malware records is on by default: a package osv.dev lists as malware is not started. If osv.dev cannot be reached, the server starts anyway.

What does it do? looks inside an npx or uvx package before you run it: it downloads the package, checks it, and reads it as text without running it. It lists what the package may reach (files, programs, the network, a port, the system), the addresses and variables it names, and what runs when it is installed. Its dependencies are not read. "This is where to look, not a verdict."

items.title: Trust
items.text:
A server you have not trusted is watching: its cell is a honey rim and its card says "every call asks until you trust it". Every call of its tools asks you on a card, at every level, Full auto too. The card shows the server's own description of the tool.

After its tools are read, Trust this server on its card's head trusts it - the card can be closed. What is trusted is the tools you read: before the first reading, or after another command or other variables until its tools are read again, there is nothing to trust - KOLONİ refuses it ("read its tools first, then trust it"). The button also waits while its tools are being read or a change of it is saved. If the package has no fixed version, the page warns that it updates itself and that trust covers future versions.

Trust is taken back by itself when the command or its variables change, or when a new reading finds new or changed tools. When a reading you start on the page takes a trusted server's trust back, its cell turns red-orange and its state says trust taken back: See the difference lists what the reading found new, changed or gone - by name: a tool's words before are not kept - and Trust it again trusts it as it is now. A later reading adds what it finds to the difference. It is shown only until you leave the page: opened anew, such a server shows as watching. Another command or other variables saved since make it watched for themselves, not for that reading.

items.title: When a tool runs
items.text:
Each tool has three buttons side by side under When an agent calls it; the one it has is pressed, with a ✓. A choice changes only when you press another: arrow keys move nowhere.

Choice What it does Runs without asking For a trusted server, it runs at every level, where its tools are offered at all (below). A watched server's still asks, and is not green. Ask A card asks you first, at every level, Full auto too. Off No agent is given it.

A choice is saved as it is made. New tools come in as Ask. A tool whose description or inputs change goes back from Runs without asking to Ask. Set all to Ask and Set all to Off change every tool of the server at once.

items.title: Giving a server to roles
items.text:
Under Roles that may use it, tick the roles whose agents get its tools. Every tool's description is sent to the model at every step, so a server with many tools makes each step bigger: the page says by about how much.

No server's tool - one that runs without asking neither - is offered to CLIs that work with their own tools, in projects whose commands run in Docker, in a ☾ Away job, in a side of a comparison, or in a turn taken only to answer another agent.

items.title: Switching off and deleting
items.text:
Each server has an on / off switch ("off: given to no agent"). Delete server removes it, and takes it from every role.

See Adding an MCP server safely.

items.title: Skills
items.text:
A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md, in the form Claude Code reads: a name and a description at the top, instructions below, and files beside it. A role that has a skill is told its instructions and can use its files.

Skills are on the Tools page, tab Skills: "KOLONİ's own store: a copy no agent writes."

Each skill is a card: its on / off switch, its name, where it came from ("from …") and how many files it has, its line, the roles it is given to (✗ before one that cannot run it there) and the last 30 days (see How a skill did). Click its name to unfold it across the page; skills that agents proposed are above the cards (When an agent proposes a skill).

items.title: Adding a skill
items.text:
Press Add → A skill · from a folder or GitHub. Then:

  • Skill folder: type the folder's full path and press Read the folder. Or Choose folder… (at most 5 MiB) or Upload .zip… (at most 25 MiB) from your browser.
  • From GitHub: a public repository, or a folder in it, such as https://github.com/owner/repository/tree/main/folder. Press Read from GitHub. First only the list of files, the SKILL.md, the licence and the scripts are read; the rest is downloaded when you add it.

KOLONİ keeps its own copy. Secrets and links in the folder are not copied.

Before you add it, a card shows what the skill holds: its licence (or that it is unknown), its files, which files run as programs, what was not copied, and a look at its scripts. Show SKILL.md shows its text. Press Add skill, or Replace skill if a skill of that name is kept already.

items.title: Example: skills from superpowers
items.text:
superpowers is a public set of skills under the MIT licence; each is a folder under skills/. To add its test-driven-development skill for the Coder:

  1. Press Add → A skill · from a folder or GitHub.
  2. In From GitHub, type https://github.com/obra/superpowers/tree/main/skills/test-driven-development and press Read from GitHub.
  3. Read its SKILL.md on the card (Show SKILL.md), then press Add skill.
  4. Open the skill's card and tick the Coder under Roles that may use it.

Some of them may fit these built-in roles:

Skill May fit test-driven-development Coder systematic-debugging Debugger verification-before-completion Coder, Tester receiving-code-review Coder requesting-code-review Coder; the Reviewer may use its template

Don't give them to the Orchestrator: its own way of working is KOLONİ's, and a workflow skill there (brainstorming, writing-plans, using-superpowers) makes it plan and decide in your place.

Several are written for Claude Code's own way of working: they name its tools, worktrees, sub-agents and a browser companion. These fit KOLONİ's roles poorly: brainstorming, subagent-driven-development, using-git-worktrees, executing-plans, dispatching-parallel-agents and using-superpowers. A skill's card says when a role lacks a tool its allowed-tools line lists; tools named only in its text are not checked. brainstorming and systematic-debugging hold scripts: on the card, before Add skill, untick Run the scripts of … without asking unless you have read them.

A skill steers every agent that has it, so give each one only to the roles that need it.

items.title: Scripts
items.text:
Files ending in .py, .js, .mjs, .cjs, .sh or .ps1 count as scripts. Run the scripts of … without asking is on by default. "Saying yes to this is agreeing to run them. Any other command is asked about as before, and once a file of the skill has changed since it was added its scripts are asked about too."

A skill's scripts need the role to be able to run commands, and they do not run in projects whose commands run in Docker.

items.title: Giving a skill to roles
items.text:
Open the skill's card and tick Roles that may use it. If a role lacks a group of tools the skill needs, the card says so and offers to give it.

A skill's text is what the agents that have it are told, so a skill from elsewhere can steer them. Read it before you give it to a role.

items.title: When an agent proposes a skill
items.text:
An agent can propose a skill. The Add this skill? card shows the same things as above, and which roles it would be given to. Press Add skill or Reject.

While it waits, the Skills tab lists it too, under Proposed by agents, with a honey cell ("waits for your word"), its line and its roles; the tab says how many ("1 proposed"). Its yes is not given there: Open on Ready for you goes to its card, which shows its text and its scripts first.

items.title: How a skill did
items.text:
A skill's card shows the last 30 days at a glance: each model and role it was given with, and how many of their agents read it ("read in 4 of 6"), with a bar once there are 5 jobs or more. Up to three rows; the rest are under it, unfolded. With no agent given it: "No agent had it in the last 30 days". While the record cannot be read, the card says nothing of it.

Open a skill's card: Did lately shows the last 30 days, one row per provider, model and role that had the skill. Its bars show Taken in, Cost or Steps, once there are 5 jobs or more. Each row says how many of those agents read the skill whole ("read in 2 of 6"), or "given, not read", in grey: then its numbers say little of the skill. An agent that cannot read a skill itself (it has no use_skill) is given its skills in full in its brief instead. The row counts those too, as "given in full in its brief in 3 of 6", not as "given, not read".

items.title: Switching off and deleting
items.text: Each skill has an on / off switch. Delete skill removes it: "Every role that has it loses it, and KOLONİ's copy of it is removed."

items.title: Attachments
items.text: Attach files to a message with the attach button: Files from this computer…, A screenshot from the clipboard (Ctrl+V), or A file of the project…. You can also drop files on the message box.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
• At most 10 files per message, 25 MB each.
  • A video is sent as at most 8 frames.

items.title: What the agents get
items.text:
KOLONİ looks at each file's content, not only its name:

Kind What is sent Text and code The text. PDF Its text ("N pages, text taken out"), up to 500 pages. A locked PDF gives no text. Word Its text. Image The picture, to providers that take images: OpenAI-compatible servers, the Anthropic API, Claude Code and Codex. Others say it is not shown. Program or script Only its name and size. A secret file (keys, passwords) Nothing of what it holds.

Links in a message are never fetched by KOLONİ.

Save these to the project too saves the attachments into the project's docs/attachments/, without asking; undo takes them back.

Agents read attachments with the Read attached files tool, which can be switched off on the Tools page.

items.title: Chat and canvas
items.text:
The chat is where you talk to the Orchestrator. The canvas behind it draws each turn from what was recorded: the agents, their tools, commands and the files they changed. Nothing on it is simulated.

A turn on the canvas, with the chat beside it.

A turn's life, from your message (and its plan, with Plan first) to the work in your folder, and the Scout after it.

items.title: The chat
items.text:
Open, the chat is a column at the left of the canvas, as tall as it. Drag its right edge to make it wider or narrower (or focus the edge and use the arrow keys); the width is kept.

The chat panel has three tabs:

  • Chat: "Your conversation with the Orchestrator".
  • Talk: "What the agents say to each other, to hand work on or ask one another".
  • Notes: "A shared notebook: you and the agents leave notes here, kept from message to message and given to new agents". In a To-do story's or task's turn, and a night's job's, a note for the whole turn also goes into that job's notebook.

Hide chat (or Esc) folds it to one line at the canvas's bottom left that says how many messages are unread and how many things wait for you.

items.title: Writing a message
items.text:
• While agents work, Send becomes Send now (Enter): your message goes into the turn at work and the Orchestrator answers it in that turn. After this turn, beside it, queues it as before: it waits and runs after the current work. A queued message can be removed. See Talking while agents work. Stop, on the line over the message, stops the work. If KOLONİ restarts before a queued message runs, it stays in the chat as "Not sent: KOLONİ restarted", with Send to send it now.
  • Stop everything, in the top bar on every page, stops every turn in every chat and holds what starts by itself: the To-do tasks waiting in a chat's queue, and work while you're away. It asks first, saying what runs and what will be held. Then the button reads Held · Resume; its panel lists the chats it stopped and what is held, with Resume. Your own messages still run while it holds.
  • On Stop or Stop everything, an agent on a branch of its own keeps its work committed there, and a team's recipe keeps its copy for Take in, and so does a job while you're away (see Work while you're away). A sub-agent's plain working copy with changes is kept on a card for Take in or Discard. See Working copies and Take in.
  • Pasted code becomes a code block by itself, with Paste as plain text to undo that.
  • New topic starts a new topic with the next message: the Orchestrator is then sent that topic's turns only, and the earlier ones by name. See Topics.
  • The message box is one box. Its top line says what the chat does now: "Orchestrator is ready" with the model (choose the model there; on GitHub Copilot's auto or fusion it names the model Copilot picked last, "fusion → gpt-6-luna", with Copilot's reason in its tooltip); while a turn runs, what it does now, for how long, the tokens written and the tier or model, with Stop and how many messages are queued; "waits for your answer" while it asks. In a chat with a folder the line also has ☾ Away, before the model, which opens the Away panel (Work while you're away); while you are away it reads I'm back. What is not known is left out: a CLI that does not tell its tokens shows none. Where the line is narrow, the tier goes first, then the tokens, then the time, then the model's name (down to its icon); what it does is cut last.
  • Under the message, one row: Attach, the permission level as three comb cells and its name (a click lists the levels, each with a line on what it does, and the Plan first switch - see Permission levels and Plan first; while Plan first is on, the level reads, say, "Auto-edit · plan"), Auto-read, Dictate and Send.
  • Under the box, quiet words: Workspace with its number, New topic, Chat settings, More (Compare) and, at the right, how many things wait elsewhere ("2 more wait elsewhere"), which opens Ready for you.
  • Chat settings opens this chat's own settings: its teams and folders (each opens its own panel), its page scripts, what runs without asking in it, and, read only, what it takes from its project. Its All settings opens Settings at This chat.
  • In a narrow chat the model shows as its arrow alone (its tooltip and its window say the whole name); while the row under the box has no room for all its words, Chat settings reads Settings and what waits reads "2 wait"; at the narrowest New topic and More keep only their icon, Settings its word. The level always shows its name ("Ask", "Auto-edit", "Full auto").
  • Type / for slash commands: /new, /stop, /model, /mode, /plan, /compare, a role's name to hand it a task, and your own commands (Settings › This project › How agents work › More).

items.title: What the chat shows
items.text:
• The chat reads at VS Code's sizes: answers and your messages at 13 px, headings at 16, 14 and 13 px, code at 11.5 px. Each turn of the Orchestrator's has no card around it: a small head (who answered, with which model, when), its steps, its answer. Where GitHub Copilot's auto or fusion picked the model, the head says so ("fusion → gpt-6-luna"), and a quiet line under it gives Copilot's own reason (two lines at most, the whole of it in its tooltip). The Orchestrator's name in the head opens its window.
  • A step is a quiet row with an icon for its kind (a book reads, a pencil edits, a terminal runs), its file as a small pill. Two or more tool calls in a row by the same agent are one line, such as "Read 4 files, listed 4 folders"; the newest is open while it runs and closes once words come after it. A command opens by itself while its output comes or when it failed, its output 6 lines tall, then scrolling.
  • Once the turn is over, everything before its answer folds into one line, "Completed 5 steps in 32s", which counts what failed or was rejected ("1 failed"); a click opens it. With a step that failed, the first one's reason is a line under it ("↳ …"), so why something did not happen is in sight. Sub-agents, discussions, a server that still runs and every card that waits for you stay outside it, in sight.
  • The Orchestrator's question waits just above the message box: numbered options, your own answer and Submit; keys 1-9 pick an option and Enter sends it; "‹ 1/2 ›" when it asks two. In its turn one line says it asks (a click goes to the card) and, once answered, "Question: … / Answered: …" opens to its options with the one given ticked. KOLONİ's own cards and sub-agents' questions stay in the turn.
  • A To-do task given to the chat (Do in chat, To-do) shows as the task: From To-do · task 2 / 3 (of its story; task or bug for one of no story), its title and "Done when: …", its whole brief under The whole brief. A story's topic has the line Topic · Story · … · 📓 notes; once the story's notebook has a note, its 📓 is a button that opens it. Under a task's last turn the chat asks Done? - "…" (Yes, done / Not yet) or, stuck, Stuck - "…" with why (Fix it / Open it in To-do / Leave it); once every task of a story is done, Story done? - "…" (Close the story / Add a task). Above the message box, N wait lists the chat's queue - the task at work, those waiting with Remove - and "+ your message goes first when you send one".
  • While a turn runs with agents at work, a plan of the Orchestrator's or something that waits for you, one line over the chat says so: "3 agents at work · step 3 of 6 · 1 waits for you · ≈ 0.40 USD". A click opens At work in this turn, each agent with Stop and Message. See Talking while agents work.
  • At the foot of a turn that did something, once it is over, one line sums it up at the right, such as "2 agents · 3 files changed", with what is left open. details ▸ shows the files, sub-agents, tokens and known cost.
  • Copy (the answer as written) and Read aloud stand at the foot's left: always under the latest answer, under older ones when you point at them or tab into them.
  • A message's ⋯ menu has Copy, Restore to before this message and Show its work on the canvas. The ↺ button on a message whose work changed files is Undo these changes.
  • While a story of To-do works in the chat, one line over the messages says so: Story · Login · 2 / 3 · next: Add a test · 📓 notes - the story, the place of its task at work among its tasks, and its next task while one waits in the chat's queue. 📓 notes, there once the notebook has a note, opens the story's notebook. In a narrow chat only the story and its place stay.
  • A long chat opens on its newest 40 turns, and on every older one that still waits for you (a card to take in, a question, a decision to OK). Over them, Show 40 earlier turns reads the 40 before, as often as you press it; "560 older turns are not shown" says how many are left. The canvas's turns, the Workspace's Changes and Undo reach the turns read so far; search, the decision log and the night's report read the whole chat.

items.title: Undo and restore
items.text: Undo these changes reverts a turn's file changes. Restore to before this message goes back to before a message. Both show first what will be reverted and what will be skipped. "The chat stays as it is: no message is deleted." What commands did, and notes put in memory, are not taken back.

items.title: The context button
items.text: The top bar has a context button for the turn, such as "context 62%". It opens what each agent of the turn holds, of its model's window, with Compact now for a lead that KOLONİ compacts: its older part is summarised now, as it would be once past Summarise a long context at (%) in Settings. The button is there for every turn, as "context –" where nothing was measured. Which CLIs KOLONİ compacts is in Set up a CLI.

items.title: Tabs above the canvas
items.text: Each open folder (project) is a tab; a chat with no folder is under No folder. A tab's dot turns orange while a chat in that folder waits for you. + goes to another folder; closing a tab closes no chat.

items.title: The folder button
items.text:
At the top left. Its panel, This chat's folders, shows the main folder ("agents work here, commands run here") with Change, and offers Open a folder… and No folder · a plain chat. A chat that has messages keeps its folder; picking another opens a new chat there.

Also in this chat lists other folders the chat's agents may use, each read or read & write (click to switch). + Add a folder adds one, read only at first. Keep for this project and Save as this folder's default keep the list.

items.title: The canvas
items.text:
Every agent is a small box of at most three lines: its name and model, its state, and what it did, counted. The window icon at the right of its name opens its window. An agent at work that an agent opened has Stop (it alone stops, its work kept for Take in) and Message (its window, at its Tell box) beside it (Talking while agents work). An agent at work says on its state's line what it does now, how long it has worked, the tokens it wrote (where its CLI tells them) and its tier or model: "pytest -q · 12s · ↓ 1.2k tokens · Fast". Where the box is narrow, the tier goes first, then the tokens, then the time; what it does is cut last. Its tools, commands and files are in the Inspector and its window (below). Lines show work handed to a sub-agent, agents that talked, findings handed on, and an agent waiting for a file another holds. Canvas legend explains every line and sign.

Click an agent that talked and What X said and was told opens on the right, under the Teams button: its messages and findings as a short conversation. Click a line between two agents and the same box shows what they said to each other, titled "A ↔ B". Drag it by its title, or move it with the arrow keys on its grip. This browser keeps one place for it, the same in every chat. A double click on its title, or Enter on its grip, puts it back.

A plan turn (see Plan first) shows a small Plan node under your message, on a short dashed line down from it. In the work turn of an approved plan, the plan stands over the Orchestrator, on a dashed line down to it.

In a turn with no team, a discussion stands in the column after the agent that opened it, above its members; several stand in the order they began. The dotted line of each member under it, in a colour of its own, goes round the right side of that column and comes into the discussion from the right, with an arrow; an opener that takes part comes in at its left, from the column before. An agent waiting for a file another agent in its column holds is joined to it the same way. Click a discussion to light the agents in it.

In a turn with teams, each team has a frame. Discussions between teams stand in a lane of their own, outside every frame. A member's dotted line runs from its team's frame to the lane; the legend calls it "A member's line to its discussion: with no team, from the members under it round the right of their column and in at its side, with an arrow; between teams, from its frame to the lane".

Where the Scout - the role that looks for what is left after each turn - was asked, a small Scout box stands under the turn, on a dashed line down from the Orchestrator. It shows the model asked, how many tasks it proposed and dropped ("2 proposed · 1 dropped"), at Full auto how many the Orchestrator added ("Orchestrator added 1"), its tokens ("–" where not reported) and To-do →. Click it for why each one was dropped; a double click, or To-do →, opens Work's To-do tab. A turn where it was not asked has no such box. The legend has a row for its dashed line. See Follow-up tasks.

A step that runs in rounds, such as a review loop or Evolve's tries, folds each earlier round into one line, such as "Round 2 · 4 reviewed · 2 blocking" or "Round 1 · Coder, Coder 2 · ✓ 2". Click it to open that round's agents in place.

The controls: Collapse all / Expand all, Follow running, and the Recent button, which lists the last five turns (and older ones that wait for you) to pick which turn is drawn.

Click an agent to open the Inspector, a short report card. From the top:

  • if it failed, why, in red, with the one thing to do about it;
  • a tag where its CLI works its own way: "reads only" (started without leave to write or run) or "works with its own tools";
  • anything it waits for you on (a command to run, its changes, a question). It is the same card as in the chat, and answering in one place answers it everywhere;
  • who asked it what, on one line;
  • its Report, or while it works "No report yet" and what it is on now. A long report is cut at six lines, with Show all. A sub-agent whose role writes (a Coder, a Debugger) that finished with no file changed on KOLONİ's record has No file changed over its report, and on its row in the chat; the Orchestrator gets the same fact, "KOLONİ: this agent changed no file", before the report's own words, so a report that claims a change it never made is not passed on to you. A role that only reads (a Reviewer, a Tester) is never marked so;
  • Changes: the files it changed, each with View diff, which opens the file in the Workspace;
  • what it did, counted, and its tokens. A number its provider did not report is "–".

Its model, how full its context is, and Compact now are in its window's Details.

Open window opens the agent's whole story; so do the window icon on its box, a double click on its box and, in the chat, the Orchestrator's name over its turn. No agent's window opens by itself. Read from the top:

  • its report;
  • What it did, told in a few plain steps. Reads in a row are one step ("Looked around — read 6 files, searched 1 time"), and so are edits ("Changed a.py +17 −1") and commands ("Ran the tests — passed"). Each step shows what the agent said before it. Unfold a step to see its files or its commands, with Stop on one that runs. While something waits for you, it is the last step, with its card;
  • its Changes, Earlier work and Sub-agents;
  • Details, folded: its model and who chose it, its times, how full its context is, Compact now and its working state, its tools, Copy raw, and Every step as recorded (the raw list of every call).

While the agent works, its window's head has Stop and Message (for an agent the Orchestrator or one of its agents opened), and a Tell box at its foot sends your word into its work. An agy agent's box says it can't hear messages while it works, and sends your word to the Orchestrator. An Orchestrator that shows its plan has it under Plan (its own words). See Talking while agents work.

An agent's window, opened from the Inspector with Open window.

items.title: Preview
items.text:
An agent can start a dev server that keeps running, on this machine only, and show its page. At most three run in a chat. They are listed under Previews in the Workspace; a preview has Reload, Open in browser and Stop.

While one runs, an agent that may run commands can read what it printed since ("the server gives a 500: read its log"), in a later turn of the same topic too, and the last output of one that has ended. It can stop only a server it started itself, and waits until it has ended (to start it again, say); one another agent or an earlier turn started is yours to stop here. Neither works in a job while you're away, nor for a CLI run Native, which runs its commands with its own tools. What it reads is hidden as any command's output is (secrets), and text in it that tries to give orders shows the Text tried to give orders card: a server's log holds what any request to it carried. What a server whose line names a secret file prints (node --env-file=.env server.js, asked about on its card at every level) is not read again later, as with any output read on your word for that once.

See Working copies and Take in.

items.title: Chats
items.text: Chats on the left rail opens the list of your chats: on top Now, what is at work and what waits for your word in every folder, and under it each chat with how it stands.

items.title: The list
items.text:
Chats are grouped by folder, the open chat's folder first; chats with no folder are under No folder. Each folder says how many chats it holds; click its name to fold it. Inside a folder, chats sit under Today, Last 7 days and Older, or are listed by name. A chat that waits for your word comes first in its group. Archived chats are listed last, under Archived.

  • Search by name finds chats by their title.
  • Show keeps All states, Failed or stopped, or Done.
  • Sort by: Last activity or Name.
  • A chat that came from the To-do list has a mark, and its task's state beside it when the chat's own line does not say it already; one with kept work says "changes kept".

Refresh conversations (the round arrow beside the heading) reads the list again. The list also refreshes by itself when you come back to the page or the window, and every 30 seconds while the page is in view.

items.title: How each chat stands
items.text:
Each row starts with a cell - the same hexagon as on Ready for you, with the same meanings - and has one line under the chat's name:

Cell The line says Honey rim, lightly filled Waits for your word, and what: a command, a question, a file change, a plan… Honey, full who is at work and how ("Orchestrator working, Coder waiting for a file"), and the branch they work on Red-orange, full Stuck: its last turn failed or was interrupted, or its To-do task is blocked Green, full Done, and what its last turn ran with: its agents, model and tokens Empty Stopped, or No turn yet

A chat whose last turn ended - done, stuck or stopped - while you were not looking at it says so after how it ended: "Done · not seen", "Stuck: its last turn failed · not seen", "Stopped · not seen". It is seen once you open it, or once a turn of it ends while it is on screen in front of you (herdr's "done, not seen"); a desktop notice about it does not count as seeing it. Every chat there was when you upgraded to 0.1.11 counts as seen.

What waits for your word in a chat is what Ready for you lists for it, and Show goes by the same. A chat Ready for you has not read yet - or could not read - says what KOLONİ's list of the project's chats says, Waits for your word with nothing after it, until it is read or that chat's state changes. A chat whose state is not read at all has no cell and no line: the page says nothing it does not know.

items.title: Now
items.text:
Now is the strip across the top of the page, over every folder, and it stays in sight while you scroll the list:

  • a cell for each thing that waits for your word, each chat whose last turn ended where you have not looked since ("done · not seen", whatever the day), each chat at work (one that waits for your word too, while another of its agents works), and each chat whose last turn ended today stuck or done - in that order, what needs you most first (herdr's order); hover a cell, or let a screen reader say it, for its chat and its state;
  • one sentence that counts them - "2 chats at work; 2 things wait for your word. Today 1 stuck. 1 chat ended where you have not looked since." The number that waits is the top bar's pill's;
  • Go to Ready for you, Work's tab where what waits is answered;
  • what the cells mean.

On a narrow window (980 px or less) Now wraps onto a few lines; it is still on top of the list but scrolls away with it, so the list keeps the screen.

items.title: Starting a chat
items.text:
• New chat starts a chat in the open chat's folder.
  • From a GitHub issue… starts a chat from an issue, with the issue attached. See Starting from a GitHub issue.

items.title: Archiving and deleting
items.text: Archive puts a chat away; Unarchive brings it back. Tick chats, or Select all, then Archive selected. Only archived chats can be deleted: Delete selected asks first, and "This cannot be undone in KOLONİ."

items.title: Checked
items.text:
A turn that changed code does not end on the model's word. Before the Orchestrator's answer ends the turn, KOLONİ runs the project's tests once on the work as it now stands. Under the answer a Checked section says what ran, how it went, and what was not checked. KOLONİ writes it from its own records, not from the model's words, and no model is asked for it.

It works the same for every model and CLI.

What KOLONİ checks at a turn's end, and where you set each part. (full size)

In order, the first check that sends work back ends the pass, and the Orchestrator's next answer is checked again:

  1. The tests - the ones related to the change first, the whole suite after the answer (Which tests, Asking, How long it waits). What is not this turn's - a flaky test, one failing before - is told apart (Not this turn's).
  2. What it wrote besides code - documents, diagrams, data, slides, config files and scripts, and the changed code by the project's own ruff, eslint, tsc and mypy (Documents, diagrams, data and slides), and, where you ticked Pages, a changed page opened in KOLONİ's own browser at a phone's, a tablet's and a desktop's width - its console, its width and its accessibility (Pages).
  3. A Reviewer's look at a big or security-touching change (The review); long documents are read once against your request (Documents read against your request).
  4. The live try, once a turn: a changed command-line tool is asked for its --help, and a big change of screens is tried by a Tester on the chat's preview (The live try).
  5. A test for the change, where you ticked it: asked once where code changed and no test did (A test for the change).

A failure goes back to the Orchestrator until it passes - while each round makes progress - or as many times as Fix rounds says (When the tests fail); then a stronger model tries, and failing work is never taken in (A stronger model). Checked under the answer says it all, line by line (What each line means), and the canvas's Checks node shows it (On the canvas). A recipe's turn follows the recipe's own Checks step (The Checks step).

items.title: When it runs
items.text:
• After a turn in a project folder that changed a file. A turn that changed nothing, a plain chat, a plan, and a side of a comparison get no Checked section - except a turn that changed nothing right after one whose checks still failed: it says "Still failing as last checked - this turn changed nothing" with those failing lines, and Fix it stays under the newest turn (not once the turn they came from is undone - also after turns that said them again, and no Fix it is offered for it then -, nor once this chat's checks are off; the canvas draws no Checks node for it, as no check ran). A change made only by a command (python -c "open(…).write(…)", sed -i, a heredoc to a file, a redirection into one
  • cat a > b, git show HEAD:f > f, not 2>&1 or > /dev/null -, a formatter, black . && pytest -q, a test run that writes - jest -u, pytest --snapshot-update, --junitxml=a.py, a coverage report that is a file, --cov-report=html -, a line handed to a shell that does) is on no record, so KOLONİ runs the tests all the same and says "A command of this turn may have changed files KOLONİ did not record: …", with "No review: changes made by a command are not recorded". In a git project such commands count only where git lists a file written since the first of them began, or one committed during the turn, and the line names them ("… did not record: gen.py - python gen_it.py"): a python main.py that only answered changes nothing. A tracked test file such a command deleted is said "Test removed", as one deleted on record is. A turn whose commands only read or ran tests is still a turn that changed nothing.
  • Where the work now is: in the project, or in the Orchestrator's own working copy (a team's branch, or a job while you're away). Work that waits in Ready for you is not part of it.
  • Once, after the turn's work is in: the agents run only the tests near their change while they work, and KOLONİ runs the whole test command at the end, like a pull request's CI - in a turn you watch, the tests related to the change first and the whole suite after, in the background (see How long it waits).
  • KOLONİ runs one such test run at a time across the app, unless Settings say more (see How many run at once). A second turn that ends meanwhile waits for the first. A run whose card waits for your yes holds up no other: it takes its turn once you answer.

Settings › This project › When the work is done › After a change turns it on or off for the project:

  • Test and review (the default) runs the tests, and has a big or security-touching change looked over by a read-only Reviewer (see The review).
  • Tests only runs the tests and nothing more.
  • Nothing runs nothing and sends nothing back. The Checked section still says that nothing was checked, and names the last test run an agent made in the turn.

The line under the choice says what it does in this project now, from its real state - for example "Runs python -m pytest -q in ./ (found by KOLONİ), related tests first, the whole suite in the background; a change over 80 lines or 3 files, or one touching sign-in, secrets or commands, is read by a Reviewer (one more model request). Failing work goes back until it passes, while each round makes progress." It names each test command you set for a part on the project map ("npm test in web/"), then what KOLONİ saved for any other folder - and changes as you save one there. Before a test command is known it says KOLONİ finds one and asks you once. Its ⓘ leads here.

items.title: For one chat
items.text:
Test and review changes, in the permission level's menu beside Plan first, turns it on or off for this chat only. Its line says what this chat's changes get: "As the project: runs python -m pytest -q after each change, then a Reviewer reads big or security changes. Failing work goes back to be fixed, up to 2 times.", "Off for this chat: nothing is tested or reviewed; each answer says “Not checked”.", or "On for this chat · the project's is Nothing: runs …" (on in a project at Nothing is Test and review for this chat). Its ⓘ leads here. Off, the level's button says "· no checks", no Checks node is drawn for its turns, the Checked section says "Not checked: off for this chat" and the Orchestrator's box "not checked · off for this chat". Other chats go on with the project's setting.

It is free at every level. At Full auto with it off, the menu says so under it: "Full auto with no checks: nothing checks this chat's changes". A turn that runs a team's recipe follows the recipe's Checks step, not this switch: the project's setting, unless the recipe sets its own - a recipe you picked may check less, one the Orchestrator picked only adds checks (The Checks step).

A project that had turned off the old Finish only when the tests pass switch is on Nothing, and Settings says so under the setting.

items.title: Which tests
items.text:
1. Each part's test command from the project map (yours, or the map's guess), run in that part's folder - the whole project's too, set on the map's first row (the whole project) where no project file makes the root a part. It runs beside the other parts' commands, not instead of them: where it runs every test, a Python part's tests run twice - in its own command and in the whole project's. A part you set to no test is never guessed - the whole project set to no test stops the guess (3-5) too. (0.1.7: Test before adding is gone, and the command you had in it was not kept: write it here.)
  2. Otherwise the test command KOLONİ saved before (below).
  3. Otherwise a command KOLONİ guesses from each part's files, in any language: python -m pytest -q (a pyproject.toml, pytest.ini or tests/), npm test (a test script in package.json), go test ./... (go.mod), cargo test (Cargo.toml), mvn test (pom.xml), ./gradlew test or gradle test (build.gradle), dotnet test (a .sln or .csproj), bundle exec rspec (a Gemfile and spec/), composer test or vendor/bin/phpunit (composer.json), mix test (mix.exs), swift test (Package.swift), ctest --test-dir build (CMakeLists.txt), make test (a test: target in the Makefile).
  4. Otherwise a test command an agent ran in this turn that really ran tests, in a turn you are there for (not while you're away).
  5. Otherwise KOLONİ asks the project's Fast tier's model once, in a turn you are there for, where its tests are. KOLONİ shows it the project's parts and languages, its test files and the start of its README, CONTRIBUTING and Makefile (never a secret file, nor one reached through a link), with no tool. It answers with command lines, which are read as data. The request shows in Usage. It is asked again only when the project's parts change; until then the commands it named are tried again. With no Fast-tier model the section says so.

A line an agent ran (4) or the model named (5) is tried only if it is one of the commands in 3, or pytest, npx vitest run, npx jest, yarn test, pnpm test, bun test, tox, nox or ctest - with at most -q or -v after it, in a folder of the project. Any other line (more options, a wrapper, a chain) is never run: the look's row says how many it named that were not tried.

A guessed command is tagged guessed. If nothing can be found, the section says "No test command: nothing was run"; after the look found no tests at all, "No tests in this project".

items.title: From your CI
items.text:
Where the project has GitHub Actions workflows (.github/workflows/*.yml), KOLONİ reads their lint, typecheck and test lines - ruff, eslint, mypy, ty check, tsc, pytest, vitest and the like, each in its step's working-directory (or the job's or workflow's defaults.run). Each line must be one plain command of at most 500 characters: a line that chains, pipes, redirects or substitutes (pytest; curl …, npm test && …, cd web && npm test, pytest $(…)) is not taken. It never takes an e2e step, nor a step with a ${{ … }} expression, a secret or an install in it, one whose shell: is another language, or one whose folder is outside the project. The workflow files are read with limits - at most 50 files, 256 KB each and 1 MB in all, no links, no YAML aliases; a file past them is not read. What was left out is said beside the lines it offers or runs ("e2e not run: …", "CI step Tests: not run: not a plain command", "CI file not read: …"); where no line is taken, nothing of the CI is said.

It asks once a project: the section lists them - "CI commands found: ruff check app, python -m pytest -q - not run until you approve them once (Run these)" - and Run these approves exactly the lines that row shows.

If the workflow files changed since, or another turn offered other lines, nothing is approved and they are offered again after the next change. From the next change on they are the turn's test run, one line each, said "(from CI)". Until you approve them they are not run - at Full auto and while you're away too. A change to a workflow file asks again; a workflow changed in the turn itself is not used ("CI commands not used: a workflow changed in this turn"). Each still goes through KOLONİ's reading of commands: a harmful one is asked as your level says. An approved line runs as your own command does: make test, npm test or tox run the project's own Makefile, package scripts or tox file, whatever they hold.

A line is offered only in a form that checks. One that changes files (ruff check --fix, ruff format, eslint --fix, tsc --build, a test run's -u or --junitxml=…), downloads or installs (npx, uv run --with, mypy --install-types), sends (--pastebin), does not end by itself (ruff server, --watch), runs code of its own beside the tool (pylint --init-hook, pytest -p x, go test -exec) or runs a file in place of the tool by its name (./pytest, lint.cmd, python -m lint) is not, and its step says why: "CI step Fix: not run: it changes files".

A file git tracks that changed while one of KOLONİ's own runs went on is said: "Changed while KOLONİ's run of ruff check . went on: calc.py". The end check's runs - the related tests, then the whole suite, in the turn or gone on after the answer - are looked at against one look taken before the first of them, on one row. It may be a run's doing (a check that formats, a test that rewrites a data file) - or yours, saved in your editor meanwhile, or another chat's: KOLONİ never puts it back by itself. Put back on that row does, for each file still as the run left it: as it was when the run started. One changed before the run comes back byte for byte; one that was as committed comes back from its commit through git's own filters, so its line ends are git's (CRLF where core.autocrlf is on) - git diff shows nothing, though the bytes may differ from before the run. One changed again since is not put back, and says so. Each turn's Put back is for its own run - its tip says "as they were before this turn's run" -, so an older turn's puts back only what is still as its run left it. While a test run of the turn still goes on, Put back waits ("put back once it ends"). A file the run made that git does not track (a report, a cache), and one an agent wrote on record meanwhile, are not listed; nor is a secret file (.env, a key) - KOLONİ keeps no copy of one, so putting it back is yours. What Put back keeps goes once nothing of the run waits, and after three days.

items.title: Saved by KOLONİ
items.text:
The first time a guessed command really runs tests (its runner counted some that passed or failed), KOLONİ saves it as this project's test command for that folder, with no question. The section says "Saved as this project's test command - change it in Settings". A guess that ran no test, or no test tool, is never saved, and a command of yours is never replaced.

Settings › This project › When the work is done shows each saved command under Found by KOLONİ as soon as it is saved, where it came from and when. Forget it clears them; they are found again at the next change. A saved command runs as the project's for this check only, and below Full auto on a card until you say Always on it (see Asking). Agents do not get to run it unasked. To make it yours, set it as a part's test command on the project map.

Where KOLONİ reads a count from the runner's summary (pytest, jest, vitest, go, cargo, dotnet, Maven, Gradle, RSpec, PHPUnit), the line gives it. Any other runner is judged by its exit code alone, and the line says so: "Tests passed (by exit code, no count)". Coloured output - --color=yes in the project's pytest settings, or FORCE_COLOR where KOLONİ was started - is read as plain: its counts still show, a run that only skipped tests is no pass, a failure it prints is one even where its exit is hidden, and a guessed command whose coloured run really ran tests is saved like any other.

A turn whose changes are all documents, slides, diagrams or data runs no tests and says so. A change to a configuration file (requirements.txt, package.json, a CI workflow, a Makefile) counts as code: the tests run.

items.title: Asking
items.text:
KOLONİ's test run is asked about as the Orchestrator's own command would be:

  • Your own command (a part's test command you set on the project map) runs without a card.
  • A guessed command at Ask before changes or Auto-edit files waits on one command card. Your yes holds for the rest of the turn, for that command in that folder only: the same command in another part of the project is asked again. At Full auto, or under an Always run rule, it runs by itself.
  • A command KOLONİ saved (see Saved by KOLONİ) is not a leave of yours: at Ask before changes and Auto-edit files it waits on a card like a guess. Always on that card (or on the guess's card before it was saved) keeps it as yours for that very line in this project: from then on it runs without a card, in every chat, and while you're away. An Always run rule you gave another command's card (python -m pytest) lets it run without a card in that chat only. Forget it forgets that too. At Full auto it runs by itself.
  • While you're away (a job of Away) a guessed command is not run: the section says "Tests not run: a guessed command, you were away", and the job finishes. Nor is a saved command you have not said Always to: "Tests not run: a saved command no Always rule covers, you were away". Your own command still runs. A To-do task's turn in a chat asks as any turn of that chat does (a chat's To-do queue waits while you're away).

The run shows in the turn like any command, as KOLONİ's own. The Orchestrator does not see it in its history: it is told the result when the tests fail.

items.title: When the tests fail
items.text:
The Orchestrator is told that the tests failed, with the end of their output, and goes on to fix what fails, by itself or with an agent that writes code. It is told never to delete or skip a test to make it pass. Then KOLONİ runs the tests again.

How often is Settings › This project › When the work is done › Fix rounds - one count with the Reviewer's findings and the other checks:

  • Until it passes (the default): it goes back while each round makes progress. It stops - and says why - where a round changed nothing (the same tests failing, or the same blocking findings by who found them and the file each names, two rounds in a row), at the turn's token limit or the project's monthly budget, or after 20 rounds at most: "Sent back to fix: round 3 (until it passes, 3 failing → 1)", "Stopped after round 4: no progress in two rounds - you decide (Fix it)". An answer to a round that changes nothing is no progress either.
  • 1 to 10: at most that many rounds; after them the turn ends, and the section says "Still failing after 2 fix rounds: you decide (Fix it)".

A project still on the old default, 2, moved to Until it passes with 0.1.6; a number you had chosen is kept. Fix it, on the newest turn, sends a new message that asks for the fix. Nothing starts until you click it.

Rounds never stack: where a recipe of the turn has already run its own test-and-fix rounds to the end (a recipe's Test it back to Fix it), KOLONİ does not send the Orchestrator round again on top of them. A recipe's review loop that ran out leaves KOLONİ's own rounds. The section says "Still failing after the recipe's fix rounds: you decide (Fix it)".

The check before a sub-agent's work is taken in is a separate check with its own two rounds: the tests that sub-agent wrote or changed, only those (test_x.py, x.test.ts, x_test.go, FooTest.java, FooTests.cs, Rust's tests/*.rs, x_spec.rb …) - each part's test command narrowed to them (python -m pytest -q tests/test_new.py), in its working copy. Those tests are the sub-agent's own code, so they run by themselves only at Full auto, or where every part's command is yours (yours on the map, or a saved one an Always rule covers). Otherwise - KOLONİ's guess at Ask before changes or Auto-edit files - the card shows the command, "not run", and waits for your Run the test; nothing is taken before. While you are away a guess never runs them (the work is taken as without a test, said "not run"); your own command runs there. A sub-agent that wrote no test is added with no test before (its card says "No tests of its own to run before it is added"). A part whose test command cannot run just those files is not run, and the card and Checked say which and why ("web/: its test command (npm test) cannot run just these files (its test script is not vitest or jest alone) - not run") - beside a pass of the other parts, never hidden in it. Tests that ran none (pytest's "no tests collected", vitest's "No test files found") are a note, not a pass. Where the sub-agent changed its part's package.json test scripts or .npmrc, they are not run (they would run instead of yours). The check at the turn's end runs every test. A turn can have both.

items.title: Not this turn's: flaky tests and failures from before
items.text:
Before a failure goes back, KOLONİ tells what is not this turn's:

  • Flaky. The failing tests run once more, alone. One that passes then failed in the full run and passed alone: "Flaky: test failed in the full run and passed alone (noted in this project's memory)". It is not sent back. The project's memory gets a note on it, "Failed in a full run and passed alone (date); seen 2 times", counting each time. A run alone that ran no test (it only collected them, say) tells nothing: no test is called flaky by it.
  • Failing before. What still fails runs on the code as it was before the turn: a throwaway copy of the work with each file the turn changed written back byte for byte as it was. Tests that fail there too were failing before: "1 were failing before this turn, 1 new". Only the new ones go back, and the Orchestrator is told the others are not its to fix. The copy is deleted after, its linked folders (.venv, node_modules) let go of first, never emptied.
  • A lint, format or type check failing before. A line such as ruff format --check ., ruff check ., eslint ., mypy app or tsc --noEmit - from your CI or your own - that fails only on files the turn did not change (by the file each finding names: old.py:1:3, "Would reformat: old.py") runs once on the old code too. Where each finding - every line that reads like a problem, an error or a code such as TS5023, as many times - is there as well: "Were failing before this turn: old.py (from CI: ruff format --check .)" - not sent back, and no stronger model is called for it. A file the turn changed named anywhere in the output, a finding the old code does not have (a type error the turn caused in a file it did not touch, a config option it broke), output that names no file, or a name that is no file of the project: the turn's, as before.
  • Where a command of the turn may have changed the project (one that is not a test run and not a mere read), what it changed is not on record: "Not checked against the old code: a command changed the project this turn …", and every failure counts as new.
  • A run that would ask its card again is not run again: "… not re-run alone or on the old code: it would ask again".
  • A test's name comes from what the run printed, and KOLONİ runs these lines without asking - so only a plain name goes on one: letters, digits, _ - . / \ : and [ ], inside the folder (no leading -, / or drive, no ..). Any other is not run again, and it counts as new: "Not re-run alone or on the old code: an unusual test name (…)". The same holds for a bug fix's new test file.
  • A command whose last run by KOLONİ, in an earlier turn, failed and passes now: "1 were failing at the last run (date), 0 now".

items.title: The last green state
items.text:
When a whole suite passes, KOLONİ keeps what it counted - the tests that ran and the skipped ones - as the project's last green state. A later pass with fewer tests, or more skipped ones, is a failure unless the Orchestrator's answer says why - in one sentence that says it removed, deleted, dropped or skipped them and names the tests (test, tests, skip, xfail; for more skipped ones, skip or xfail): "Tests went from 214 to 210 (4 removed)", "Skipped rose from 3 to 9" - sent back like a failing test. Said why, it is still shown, as a note quoting that sentence - "Tests went from 4 to 3 (1 removed) - the answer says why: “I removed the obsolete test of the old parser”" - and the new counts are the green state from then on. Fewer tests are put down to something outside the turn only where KOLONİ can show it, test by test: the green run listed each of its passes by name and this run does too (pytest with -v; jest and vitest list files, not tests, so theirs never add up), and every test missing now lives in a file the turn did not touch in any way - nor did any of these happen:

  • a command of the turn that may write files ran, in the project or in a recipe's copy (a script, sed -i, git rm … && git commit, git mv - a test run alone writes nothing);
  • it changed what decides which tests run (a conftest.py, pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, tox.ini, package.json, a Makefile, a Vitest, Jest or Cypress config or setup, a Python file in a tests folder not named as a test, the script the test command runs);
  • it touched a test file at all - changed, made, deleted or renamed one, or anything in a tests folder (a new spec's .only switches the others off, wherever they are; a test added to a file is the turn's too, with tests deleted by hand elsewhere);
  • a change on KOLONİ's record since that green run took lines out of a test file.

Then it is said and not sent back, "Tests went from 48 to 45 (3 removed) - not this turn's change", and the new counts are the green state: tests deleted by hand, a pull, another branch checked out. Anything less sure is the turn's, as a turn's own removal always is: a test file it touched in any way, a runner that lists no names, names that do not add up to the drop; more skipped tests are the turn's too (no runner here lists what it skipped by name). Not seen: a test generated from data the turn changed elsewhere - a parametrize list built from the app's data, a flag a skipif reads - lives in a file it did not touch, and its drop reads as outside. A whole suite that goes on after the answer is held to the green run too: a drop of the turn's is said on its Checked as failed, and the green state stays where it was. Where the rounds end with no test failing but fewer run, or more skipped, the line says so: "Still fewer tests, or more skipped, after 2 fix rounds: you decide (Fix it)"; work in a copy is then not taken in, "Not taken in: fewer of its tests run, or more are skipped, after its fix rounds". Where the green run listed its passes, KOLONİ keeps those names (at most 5 000): a test that passed then and fails now is named, "Regression: test passed at the last green run and fails now" - never one added since. Where it listed none, the counts are kept and a failing test in a file the turn did not add is named "… (by file)".

items.title: A bug fix
items.text:
In a turn that fixes a bug (the request says fix, bug, broken, crash, error, hata, düzelt …) and adds a test beside a change of the code, the new test runs alone on the old code (a throwaway copy that keeps the new test). It must fail there: "The new test fails on the old code ✓"; one that passes there too is said - "The new test passes on the old code too: it may not catch the bug".

In a recipe, the Reproduce it step must leave a test run of its own that failed - of a test file it wrote, where it wrote one: a test of that file named failing (by its file, or, where the runner names none - jest, go - by its name in that file). A run that failed because the file did not even load (a syntax error, collecting) shows no bug. One that did not is held, and the recipe stops at Ready for you: "Reproduce did not show a failing test: none of the tests it wrote failed (…)", or "… no test run of its own on record failed".

items.title: A stronger model
items.text:
When the Fix rounds are spent and a test still fails - until it passes: where a round made no progress, or after 20 -, KOLONİ hands the fix to the next stronger tier on the Models page (fast, then balanced, then strongest), the same role on that tier's model, for the same number of rounds (until it passes: while each of its rounds makes progress - "big-model's rounds stopped: no progress in two rounds" - and within the turn's 20 rounds in all, the first model's counted). Rounds stopped by the turn's token limit or the budget are not handed on, and a stronger model's stopped so tries no tier more. Each tier tries at most once a turn, and its model's use is always said: "Handed to model (Strongest) after 2 rounds by model". A tier whose provider is over its limit is skipped ("Strongest skipped: over its limit"), and none is tried where the project's month budget or the turn's token limit is spent. Switch it off in Settings › This project › When the work is done › Then a stronger model; then the work waits after the first model's rounds.

Before the stronger model's rounds, KOLONİ looks at what is not this turn's: a flaky test and one that was failing before the turn are said, not handed on (see Not this turn's above). Then the stronger model first says what is wrong, in one line of its own, before it changes anything:

  • fix-incomplete - the fix is not finished: it goes on from the work as it is.
  • test-wrong - the test asks for something the request does not: it may change the test, only with its reason in the request's words - never deleting or loosening one silently. The section says "Test changed: why", and the Reviewer reads that change too.
  • approach-wrong - the way the work went cannot pass: where the work is in its own working copy, what it changed there is dropped and the work starts again from the start state in a fresh copy, the stronger model told only what was tried and why it failed - "Started over in a fresh copy: why". Work already in the project (which KOLONİ never reverts), or on a branch of its own, goes on from the work as it is, and the section says so.

A line that only looks like a verdict - in the work itself, in a quote or a code block of its answer - is not one; with none, or two different ones, it goes on as fix-incomplete. A test-wrong without the request's own words in quotation marks goes on as fix-incomplete too.

Each of its rounds is judged on the whole test run's own verdict, run to its end there and then - never one that goes on after the answer. A new test it adds is fine; a test it changed or deleted, or a file that steers the tests (a conftest.py that leaves one out), without a test-wrong is no pass: "Not a pass: model changed a test without leave (file)", and that test is not listed as one of the turn's new tests. A round whose work fails the project's own check before Take in stays in its copy: "Not taken in: model's round - the project's check failed on it before Take in". Work its rounds make pass gets the look the failing tests held back, once, by the same rule (a big or security-touching change): its Review line takes the place of "No review: the tests still fail"; a hold that stands keeps work in a copy out, as below.

Failing work is never taken in, at any level - Full auto and while you're away too. Where nothing passes after the strongest tier (or none is set, or the switch is off), the work stays in its copy and the section says "Not taken in: 2 tests still fail after rounds by A and B", with what the stronger model found as one question to you, and two buttons on that line: Take in anyway and Fix it: your answer to the question starts a turn that goes on in the kept work's copy - what was done there holds - and it goes into the project at that turn's end when its tests pass. Once the kept work is taken in, Take in anyway goes, the line says "Taken in anyway." and Fix it asks for the fix as for work in the project; discarded, or gone on in a Fix it turn, both buttons go (after a reload as well). Taken in, discarded or gone on in a Fix it turn, the turn's line of where its work is ("Not in the project yet: …") is written anew. An Away job ends there, and its report lists it. Work that is already in the project (no copy) gets the stronger model's rounds, then the failing line: "Still failing after rounds by A and B". A recipe whose own check ran nothing still waits on its Ready for you card, as before - never taken in unasked. A Reviewer's hold at the end of the Fix rounds is not handed to a stronger model yet: the user decides (Fix it). Work in a copy - a recipe's, before Ready for you - that a look still holds is not taken in by itself either, at any level: no Ready for you card, not even at Auto-edit, and not at Full auto; the section says "Not taken in: on hold - a look's findings still stand after its fix rounds", with Take in anyway and Fix it. So is work in a copy whose check by kind of work (a page, a document, a config file, a script) still fails after its fix rounds: "Not taken in: KOLONİ's checks of what it wrote still fail after its fix rounds". A later pass of the same turn never lets that one go - it may not check the kind again (not judged, not run, out of time): Take in anyway or Fix it. Work held for its tests goes to Ready for you where the Orchestrator changes it in the same turn and KOLONİ's next pass runs every test command to a pass (one not run, timed out or still running keeps it out). Work stopped at the turn's token limit or the month's budget with tests failing stays out too.
