Fix it goes on in the kept work's copy, and that turn's end check covers the whole kept work as Take in would bring it - the held change and the fix, by the same rule (a big or security-touching change gets the look), never the fix alone: a MERGE takes it in (Full auto) or asks on its card, a hold keeps it held again. That turn keeps the held turn's checks - never fewer than the tests and the review, whatever this chat's switch or the project's After a change say since; its old code, for "were failing before", is the project's, so the held work's own failure is never excused. The Reviewer sees the kept work as Take in shows it: what Take in leaves out is not in it, and a secret file, one holding a secret you gave on a card, or one that is not text is named, never shown. Take in anyway is your word: the work goes in as it is, with no look first.

The order is always the same: KOLONİ's checks first, on the work where it is (a recipe's copy), then Ready for you. Its card, or Full auto's own Take in, comes only after the Checked section - never for work the checks left failing. A fix round there sends the recipe back to work, as a wordless Ask for changes would: its own roles fix it in its copy, and its end checks it again. Unlike your Ask for changes, it gives the recipe's loops no rounds again: a review whose loop ran out runs once more, and what it finds then is left for you: the card names it and offers Fix the findings.

items.title: Documents, diagrams, data and slides
items.text:
Under Test and review, a turn that wrote documents, diagrams, data, slides, config files or shell scripts gets KOLONİ's checks of them, with no model and nothing installed: each file its own line under the answer. Which kind a file is, its ending says. They come after the tests and before the review. A turn that wrote only documents, slides, diagrams or data runs no tests ("No tests: only documents, slides, diagrams or data changed") and gets these checks; a config file or a script counts as code, and the tests run. Changed code also goes to the project's own ruff, eslint, tsc and mypy, where it has them (Code style and types, below). Under Tests only, Nothing, or where checks are off for the chat, they do not run.

Kind Checked Said, not failed Code style and types (.py, .js, .ts, .tsx, .vue …) a problem the project's own ruff, eslint, tsc or mypy finds on a line the turn added or changed, in a file it changed ("app/x.py:12: ruff F401 - os imported but unused") - a file it cannot parse too ("ruff invalid-syntax - …") the problems on lines the turn did not change, counted; eslint's and tsc's warnings on its lines, counted; a tool set up but not installed here; one the project's own check ran this turn (its CI lines, its test command - the tool as a command's program there, never pip install ruff or pytest -k mypy); a tsconfig that names no files - itself or by what it extends (a solution's references) - or that extends a file outside the project, not there or more than 8 deep: tsc is not run on it; a file too large to compare in time ("not judged"); the tool's settings the turn changed ("ruff's settings changed this turn (pyproject.toml)"); a run that found none of the turn's files to check (ruff's "No Python files found", eslint's ignored file) - never "no problems" Documents (.md, .docx, .txt, .rst) a relative link or image that leads to no file (a site's page name, guide for guide.md, counts as found; a link in code does not count); a Word file that does not open an anchor not found, a heading that skips a level, two top headings, a link out of the project, the sections you listed in your message (- results, 1. costs) that no heading names, "Spelling: not checked" Diagrams (.drawio, .svg, .mmd, .puml) a draw.io file (a compressed page too) or an SVG that does not parse; an edge that points at nothing; PlantUML without @startuml … @enduml (or @startmindmap … @endmindmap and the like) labelled shapes on one box, shapes not connected where the page has edges, a Mermaid type KOLONİ does not know, "drawn: not checked" for Mermaid Data (.csv, .tsv, .ipynb) rows with another number of fields than the header; a notebook that does not parse, or a cell that ends in an error cells not run 1, 2, 3 … in order; "not re-run: KOLONİ does not run notebooks"; Parquet and Excel are not read Scripts (.sh, .bash, .ps1, .psm1) a script that does not parse, with its shell's first complaint and line ("build.sh:4: does not parse - syntax error near unexpected token fi'") - read bybash -n` or PowerShell's own parser, never run no bash or no PowerShell here; a secret file, one over 1 MB, more than 20 a turn: not read Slides (.pptx) a file that does not open; a slide with no text and no picture the slides and how many have notes; "overflow and contrast: not checked"; .odp and .key are not read Config (.json, .yaml, .yml, .toml) a file that does not parse, with its parser's first complaint and line ("package.json:3: does not parse - Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes") - NaN or Infinity in a .json too, which npm's reader and JSON.parse break on; a package.json that is no object, or whose name, version or a script is no string; a pyproject.toml whose [project] has no name or whose [tool.…] is no table; a GitHub workflow (.github/workflows/*.yml) with no on: or no jobs, or a job with neither runs-on nor uses, or with no list of steps; a Compose file (compose.yaml, docker-compose*.yml) whose services is no mapping a secret file (.env.json, secrets.yaml) is never read, nor one whose name often holds a secret (credentials.json, token.json, kubeconfig…, client_secret….json); a file nested over 100 deep (a TOML key of over 100 dotted parts too), a YAML or TOML file over 256 KB, YAML past 1 MB in all in a turn, or YAML with aliases is not read; a YAML tag KOLONİ does not know (!!python/name:, !reset) is read as the value under it; JSON with comments and trailing commas passes where its tool reads them (tsconfig.json, .vscode/*.json; a comment after the last comma too), never a package.json; a key twice in a .json passes (JavaScript reads the last); a value a YAML tag cannot read (!!int "x") is not checked, and never said back

Code style and types runs the project's own tools - only where the project sets one up and has it installed here, never a download: ruff ([tool.ruff], ruff.toml; the project's .venv, else one on PATH) and mypy ([tool.mypy], mypy.ini; the .venv's) on the changed .py files, eslint (its config and node_modules/.bin/eslint) on the changed scripts, and tsc (tsconfig.json and node_modules/.bin/tsc) on its project - eslint and tsc from the nearest folder up from a file that has them. Running one runs the project's code (an eslint.config.js is JavaScript), so it goes as the project's test command goes: at Full auto it runs; at Ask and Auto-edit it waits on a card - your yes covers that very line in that folder for the rest of the turn, and Always keeps that line (the program and its options, never the bare program: a line that adds another config, a plugin, parser or formatter, a plugin folder, --fix, a report or trace elsewhere, or tells tsc to build or write (--incremental, --noEmit false, -b) asks again); while you are away it is not run and its line says "needs your leave once". A program an agent wrote - this turn, or an earlier turn in an install folder (node_modules, .venv, site-packages), in the project or in a working copy, taken in or not, while the file still holds what it wrote - in any case of its name, or through a link, is never run and offers no card, nor one whose real place is outside the project, nor eslint or tsc where the turn wrote in a node_modules above the folder they run in (Node loads their packages from there too), nor a tool where the turn wrote a node.cmd or python.exe (a name a tool's shim runs bare) in the folder it runs in. A file's lines are compared with what it was before the turn only where a tool says a problem in it, within the 2 minutes: one too large to compare in that time is said "not judged", never passed. It waits for KOLONİ's test-run slot (Settings › The app), so a type check never runs beside the whole test suite. tsc is told to write nothing outside the project (KOLONİ's own line, --noEmit --incremental false --composite false --generateTrace null: its command line wins over its tsconfig and what that extends) and mypy to keep its cache in the folder (.mypy_cache). In a recipe's copy it runs there - without the copy's own code first on its Python path, so a module an agent wrote there (mypy/) is never imported in place of the tool's own - and what it writes (a cache, a report) is put back - never taken in. At most 50 files a run, 2 minutes for them all, its wait for the slot too. Where the project sets none of them up, nothing at all is said of it.

A deck, Word file or other file a command made (a script that writes a .pptx) is checked too, when the turn has a change on record. A checked problem goes back to the Orchestrator as a fix round, with the lines that failed (at most 20 named): one count with failing tests and the Reviewer's findings (Fix rounds), "(1 problem in what it wrote)" beside the round. Where the rounds are spent with it still there - or the Orchestrator answered one without changing anything - the section ends as for failing tests, "Still failing after 1 fix rounds: you decide (Fix it)", and work in a copy is not taken in (see A stronger model). A problem the file had before the turn is said, not sent back: the turn did not make it. A file KOLONİ cannot read (over 8 MB - or over 8 MB once its zip members or draw.io pages are inflated, all together, whatever size the file says they are; a deck of over 1,000 slides - outside the project, an XML file that declares a DTD or entities in any encoding, a CSV field over the reader's limit) is said as not checked; one file gives at most 12 lines. Each kind can be switched off in Settings › This project › When the work is done › Check by kind of work; then its line says "Not checked: slides switched off for this project". Where the turn ended before the check, or changed such a file after it, the section says so instead of an old result. On the canvas, the Checks node shows each kind as one line: "documents · 2 ✓ · 1 ✗".

A script is code too: the turn's tests run and the review reads it as before - Scripts only adds whether it parses. KOLONİ reads it as its shell would and runs nothing of it: a .sh or .bash file with bash -n (on Windows Git's bash, never WSL's), a .ps1 or .psm1 file with PowerShell's own parser - the script's text given on its input, never in a command line, the shell started with none of your variables in an empty folder of its own, 10 s (bash) or 20 s (PowerShell) at most, then stopped with all it started; its folder is removed after it. bash reads with extglob on. A .sh whose first line names another shell or language (#!/bin/zsh, #!/usr/bin/env fish, python3) is not bash's to read: "not checked: its first line says it is a zsh script" - one with no such line, or sh, bash or dash, is. What bash only warns of (a here-document ended by the file's end) is said as a note, never as a failure; where bash also fails, its error is said. A using assembly, using module or #requires statement that names modules or assemblies is left out before PowerShell reads it, so nothing is looked up or loaded; a script that would still make its parser look one up - a using it cannot take out (a comment between its words, a line continued with a backtick, any using but using namespace, an English "using" in a comment or a string too), an Import-DscResource - is not read: "not checked: it may load a module or an assembly (it names using or Import-DscResource)". KOLONİ looks at the whole text for these, none of it taken for a comment or a string first: only PowerShell's own parser knows where those end, and it is the very reader that would look the module up. A type of a module left out is said, not failed. With Windows PowerShell 5.1 alone (no PowerShell 7 here), a Configuration or PowerShell 7's own syntax (??, &&) is "not checked: it needs PowerShell 7". A .sh with Windows line endings (CR LF) is read as Git's bash reads it, and said: bash on Linux will not run it as it is. Where this machine has no bash or no PowerShell, its scripts are said as not checked.

items.title: Pages
items.text:
Off unless you tick Pages in Settings › This project › When the work is done › Check by kind of work (since 0.1.10; a project where you had ticked it keeps it). Unticked, a turn that wrote a page says "Not checked: pages switched off for this project". Ticked, a changed web page (.html) is opened in KOLONİ's own headless Chrome or Edge - the browser the agents' browser tools use, on this machine, never out on the internet - at 375, 768 and 1280 px (a phone, a tablet, a desktop). Console errors and a page wider than the screen (it scrolls sideways) are failed, and go back as a fix round with the first error: "index.html: 2 console errors at 375, 768, 1280 px - error: x is not defined", "index.html: wider than the screen at 375 px". Where it passes: "index.html: no console errors at 375, 768, 1280 px". KOLONİ's browser never goes out: a load from outside this machine (a CDN's script, a web font) is no error of the page's, and the page is said to be checked without it; where such a script is missing, the page's own errors are a note, not sent back (they may come of it). The favicon.ico a browser asks every site for is not counted either. A missing file of the project's own is an error. A changed component or style (.tsx, .jsx, .vue, .svelte, .css, .scss) is looked at on the chat's preview, where one runs that serves the work (started from the Preview, or by an agent, where the work is); with none: "Pages not checked: no preview running". At most three pages a turn, two minutes in all. With no Chrome or Edge here: "Pages not checked: no Chrome or Edge here". Each page's screenshots, one a width, are kept for you in the project's .koloni/tmp/checked/<turn>/ - never shown to a model; what reaches the Orchestrator of a page is only these lines, as data. Pages is switched off with the other kinds.

At each width the page is also read for accessibility - by KOLONİ, in the page, with no model and nothing installed - half a second after it loaded, and again 0.3 s later (some 0.8 s a width). Each rule is judged by how many it finds in each read. Found in both, the fewer fail as below, named as the second read names them, however the rest of the page moves (a count going up, a clock, an image's address that rotates, controls that swap places); what one read finds more of - an image with no alt drawn as its data comes - and a rule found in one read only - a name put a moment late - are not judged, said by the rule: "accessibility not judged at 375 px for what changed after it loaded - images without alt text". Neither is sent back for what the page had not drawn yet nor passed for what it drew late. The notes (contrast and what it could not judge) are the second read's; a second read cut at its 3 seconds leaves the width to the first. A change after the second read is not seen. What the read finds:

  • an image with no text for it: "index.html: 2 images without alt text at 375, 768, 1280 px - logo.png, hero.jpg". alt="" marks a picture as decoration, and one hidden from screen readers (aria-hidden, role="presentation") is not counted. An image of the page's own bytes (a data: address) is named by its id, class or place: "an inline image (#hero)", "an inline image (image 3)";
  • a button, link or field with no name - no words of its own, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, label (its words, or the alt of an image in it), placeholder, a button's value or an image's alt in it, and else the words of the CSS ::before or ::after of it or of what is shown in it (content: 'Menu'; one with display: none, or an icon font's glyph, is no name): "1 buttons, links or fields with no name at 375, 768, 1280 px - input[type=email]#email". A control one can tab to counts whatever its size - an empty <a href> is a tab stop with no name; any other (tabindex="-1", inside inert) only where it is drawn more than 1 px each way, as an image and a text are. A hidden or disabled one never counts;
  • a page hidden whole from screen readers (aria-hidden on html or body), and a control one can tab to inside aria-hidden (a button, a link, a field, tabindex 0 or more, not disabled, not inside inert): "2 controls one can tab to inside aria-hidden at 375, 768, 1280 px - button, a[href=/x]".

These are failed and go back as a fix round, the page's words in them as data; the "no console errors" line stays with them.

Contrast is a warning: said with its ratio, never sent back - a colour is the page's design, and a reading of it is not sure enough to send work back for. Text below the contrast WCAG 2 asks - 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text (24 px, or 18.66 px bold) - its colour over the backgrounds under it, up to the first opaque one (the page's white where there is none), any CSS colour: "3 texts below the contrast they need at 375 px - “Muted words” 2.84:1 (needs 4.5:1)". Each colour, background, size and weight is named once, the lowest first. Its colour is -webkit-text-fill-color where that is set. Read with the light colour scheme (prefers-color-scheme: light, set before the page first loads), whatever this machine's is. What the read cannot judge is said, not sent back, never guessed:

  • text with something drawn under it - an image, a gradient, gradient text (its fill see-through), or a picture or a layer of another element over its words, drawn inside the background found under it, or anywhere where none is (a positioned overlay, a hero image under a dark layer, a fixed backdrop): "contrast not checked … on 2 texts with something drawn under them". A fixed header or bottom bar counts only where it is at the page's top; a backdrop that is hidden (visibility: hidden, opacity: 0), as a closed modal's is, not at all;
  • a page whose colour scheme is dark only (color-scheme: dark): "contrast not checked … the page's colour scheme is dark only" - its canvas is dark, not the white the rule reads under it;
  • frames and shadow roots: counted, not read ("accessibility not read inside 1 frames or shadow roots"); a closed shadow root is not seen at all;
  • a page whose script took its body or its root away: "accessibility not read … the page has no body" ("… no root"). One that moved its content out of the body is read all the same: the read starts at the page's root;
  • a page's first 2,000 elements are read (an inline <svg> counts as one, not its shapes), none nested over 1,000 deep, for 3 seconds at most a width, and a text's words are compared with the 200 drawn elements over its box at most; past that: "accessibility checked only in part", with which limit it met ("only its first 2000 elements are read", "nested over 1000 deep", "a text has more than 200 drawn elements over it" …). A read cut at its 3 seconds is not read again: that width stands on its first read.

A page nested deeper still (some 1,600 elements, measured on Windows) crashes the browser's tab as it is drawn, before any read: "index.html: not checked: the page crashed the browser's tab", said at once, and the turn's next page is read in a new browser.

The read goes through the browser's own getters, so a field named after one of the page's properties (<input name="parentElement">) cannot steer it. Hidden and disabled elements are left out. A text's opacity (its own or a parent's), its shadow, an outline drawn by a parent's ::before or ::after, and a field's typed value are not looked at.

items.title: A test for the change
items.text:
Off unless you tick A test for the change in Settings › This project › When the work is done › Check by kind of work (since 0.1.10). Unticked, a turn that changed code and no test says "Not checked: a test for the change switched off for this project". Ticked, it is asked under Test and review and Tests only alike. A turn that changed source code (a script of a language: .py, .ts, .go, ...) and no test is asked, once, for a test: "Not the end yet: a.py changed and no test did." The Orchestrator has one written - by an agent that writes code, or itself; for a bug fix, first a test that fails without the fix - and KOLONİ runs the tests again on it. Where no test fits (documents, settings, a one-off script), it says so in one line instead, and that line is quoted under the answer. The ask comes last, after the tests, the review and the live try, spends no fix round, and is made under Test and review and Tests only, never under Nothing or where checks are off for the chat. A turn of a recipe whose steps wrote a test (Bugfix's Reproduce it) is not asked. It works the same while you're away and at Full auto: the Orchestrator writes the test or gives its reason.

A test is known by its name or folder: test_a.py, a_test.go, a.test.ts, a.spec.js, a file under tests/ or __tests__/. A test file the turn deleted is said under the answer as "Test removed", failed, and under Test and review the Reviewer looks at it whatever the change's size: one removed to make the tests pass is a blocking finding.

While they work, agents that write and run code are told to run only the tests near their change; KOLONİ runs the project's whole test command once, at the end. The Orchestrator is told so too.

items.title: Coverage
items.text:
Where the project already measures coverage, KOLONİ says what share of the turn's changed lines the tests ran: "Coverage: 72% of the changed lines are run by tests (pytest-cov)". It installs nothing; it uses what the project has:

  • pytest-cov, named in pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or a requirements*.txt, for a pytest run;
  • Vitest's coverage (@vitest/coverage-v8 or @vitest/coverage-istanbul in package.json) for a vitest run, or an npm test, pnpm test or yarn test whose script runs vitest;
  • c8, in package.json and in the project's own node_modules/.bin, run as npx --no c8 … around a node test run, which never downloads it.

A part with a test command of its own (see Which tests) is measured from its own folder.

Only the whole suite is measured, never the related tests run first, whether it ends before the answer or goes on after it (then the line comes when it ends). KOLONİ adds only report flags, and the report is written under the project's scratch folder (.koloni/tmp/), read there (up to 20 MB) and deleted. The run keeps its own command everywhere: its line under the answer, its leave on your card (an approved command is approved with the flags too) and whether an earlier run of it still stands. Where the flags fail (the runner does not know them, a coverage threshold of the project's fails once coverage is on, or the run did not go for another reason than your no or your Stop), KOLONİ runs it again without them and says "Coverage: not measured (the flags failed)". Then it does not try them on that command again - "not measured (the flags failed before …)" - until the folder's coverage settings change (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, .coveragerc, package.json, the Vitest config, ...) or KOLONİ starts again. A run that stood from earlier is not measured again; where it was KOLONİ's own measured run on the same work, its share is said again.

Lines a test could run but none did go to the Reviewer, as data: "New lines no test runs: a.py 3, 12-14". A turn with no Reviewer just shows the share.

items.title: The review
items.text:
Under Test and review, once the tests pass, a change of more than 80 lines or 3 files of code, config or screens - or one that touches security - is looked over by the Reviewer, an agent KOLONİ opens itself. A security touch is a path with a word like auth, login, session, token, secret, password, permission, crypto, cookie or cors as a whole word of a name in it (auth.py, oauth2/, tokens.ts - not author.py or tokenizer.py), a .env, .pem or .key file, a Dockerfile or a CI workflow, or an added line that runs a command (subprocess, shell=True, os.system, child_process), runs or loads code (eval(, exec(, pickle.load, yaml.load(), reaches the network (fetch(, requests., httpx., socket.), puts HTML in a page (dangerouslySetInnerHTML, .innerHTML =), or loosens a check or a file's rights (verify=False, chmod, setuid). Then the Security reviewer looks too, told to try to refute that the change is safe. Both may look at once. The whole change is read for these, also what does not fit in the diff the Reviewer is shown.

  • They read: the user's request, the turn's change as a diff (cut at 12 000 characters, the files left out named; a secret file is named, never shown), KOLONİ's own test lines, and any file of the project they open - where the work is: in a recipe's turn, the recipe's copy, as KOLONİ's own tests there; what their commands write there (a report, a cache, a file a test rewrites) is put back, never taken in - so is what KOLONİ's own test runs write there, one run at a time in a copy. What an agent's own command writes there (a Coder's test run) is that agent's work, and goes in with it. They get read tools only and no MCP server, whatever their role is given: they change nothing. They may run two kinds of command, never asked about: one that only reads (git diff, cat a.py, ls src), and the project's approved test command exactly as it is set, in its folder - a part's test command you set on the map, a saved one an Always rule covers, or a CI line you approved with Run these. Any other (rm, pip install, the test command with an option added) is refused, and they are told which test commands they may run; no card is ever opened for a Reviewer's command. One whose model is a CLI that works with tools of its own is not opened ("Review not run: …"), as KOLONİ could not hold it to reading.
  • For a change a user sees (a screen's file, a command's option) in a project with docs/, a README or a CHANGELOG, they also check the docs: "Docs not updated for: …" is a suggestion, blocking only where the project's own rules say docs must change with it.
  • Each ends with MERGE (it may stand) or HOLD (it must change first) and its findings, each blocking or a suggestion. Blocking findings go back to the Orchestrator as a fix round, as failing tests do; KOLONİ runs the tests again, and the Reviewer looks again at the new change - until MERGE with the tests passing, or the Fix rounds are spent. Then the section lists the findings and says "Still on hold after 2 fix rounds: you decide (Fix it)"; Fix it sends a new message asking for them to be fixed, and the Orchestrator is handed the findings as data, never as your words. The findings are the rows of all its Findings sections - a ## Findings heading (or "## Findings (2)", "## Review findings") or a "Findings:" line, each to the next heading of its level or above (a ### Blocking or ### Suggestions under ## Findings is part of it; after a "Findings:" line, any heading ends it). A line that starts with # and no space, or an indented # comment, is no heading. A fenced code block in it is not read, and the section goes on after it - a code span at a line's start is no fence; a label line in it (Checked: ran pytest) ends nothing. A "Findings:" line that sums up - "Findings: 1 blocking" above the rows, "Findings: see above, nothing blocking." closing the report - takes no row away; "Findings: none" says it found nothing where no section has a row. A section quoted from an earlier look (indented four spaces, or after >) opens none: alone it is not read, and inside a section of this look's it ends nothing - its rows are read with the rest. Rows nested under a section of its own are read; the instruction's own row echoed back (<what> | kind: <kind>) is not.
  • Each look is an agent's work on its model: on the canvas, in its window and in Usage. In the chat its step reads "KOLONİ's look: Reviewer", not as one of the Orchestrator's. KOLONİ's looks
  • a review, a look again, the live try's Tester, a stronger model's diagnosis and fix - use none of the turn's sub-agents per turn: their bound is the Fix rounds, and the Orchestrator's own sub-agents are counted without them.
  • Where a look again cannot be had (it failed, it was refused, the turn's token limit), the hold stands and says why: "Still on hold: Security reviewer could not look again (…) - you decide (Fix it)".
  • In a chat with teams the look is KOLONİ's, not a team's: no team's lead or door holds it, and it gets no team's tools (their shared folder, a request for another team's work).
  • The Orchestrator may answer the findings without changing anything: the turn ends there, and the section says "Still on hold after round 1: not settled by the last look - you decide (Fix it)" ("nothing changed" where KOLONİ checked again and found no change).
  • A HOLD is a hold: one that marks no finding blocking, or writes its findings as prose, goes back with its own words as the finding. The verdict is a line of its own (not one quoted, in a code block - `` or ~~~ - or indented as code):Verdict: MERGE,Final verdict: HOLD,1. Verdict: HOLD, a## Verdictheading orVerdict:` with the word on the next line. Its first verdict word decides: HOLD, REQUEST CHANGES, REJECT and BLOCK hold, unless a "not" or "no" stands just before it ("MERGE - no reason to hold this back", "I'd not block: MERGE" merge); a MERGE negated or said not to be ("do not MERGE", "MERGE is not possible yet", "MERGE? No - HOLD", "not ready to merge", "MERGE is unsafe", "MERGE - blocked", "MERGE (blocked)") holds, and so does a MERGE on a condition ("MERGE once the SQL injection is fixed", "MERGE only after the fix"); NEEDS CHANGES and FAIL hold, APPROVE and LGTM merge. A negation reaches no further than a comma, a full stop or a dash: "No. HOLD until the test is fixed" holds. A "Previous verdict" line is not this look's. Any HOLD wins; a report with no verdict is "Review gave no verdict: not counted".
  • Stop this check ends a look that runs now too: "Review stopped by you - not checked".
  • No look: a small change, Tests only, tests that still fail (they are fixed first - not those that were failing before this turn: said, not sent back, they hold no look back), a turn over its token limit, or a recipe whose own Review step looked already - rounds never stack. A recipe without a Review step gets this review at its end.

items.title: Documents read against your request
items.text: A turn that wrote more than 80 lines of documents (.md, .rst, .txt, .docx...) and no code that is looked over has them read once by the Reviewer, against what you asked for: what your request asks for that they leave out or contradict - and, where it asks for sources, whether they are there. Its line is "Documents read: Reviewer (…) - MERGE, no findings" or "- HOLD, …"; a blocking finding goes back as a fix round, as a review's does. It is read once a turn: after that round, the turn's end says "Still on hold after round 1: not settled by the last look - you decide (Fix it)" where the hold stood. Where code is looked over too, the Reviewer's brief takes the documents in: one look a turn in all.

items.title: The live try
items.text:
Under Test and review, once a turn, after the tests and the review, KOLONİ tries the change as a user would:

  • A command-line tool the turn changed - a script in bin/, a bin of package.json, a console script of pyproject.toml - is asked for its --help, and nothing more: KOLONİ never runs it plainly, as a deploy or a sync script would do its work. Only a script that answers --help by itself is asked: a Python script that imports argparse, click, typer, docopt, fire or optparse; a Node script that requires or imports commander, yargs, meow or cac; a shell script with its own case for --help (-h|--help), "--help") - read outside its comments. Another is "Not tried: … it does not answer --help". Its line is KOLONİ's own command, asked about as an agent's would be (a card below Full auto where one is asked). "Tried python 'bin/tool.py' --help: exit 0, 12 lines" passes; a --help that fails (or runs on past 30 s) goes back as a fix round. A file name or a module that is not plain (letters, digits, _ . / -, no part starting with -, no ..) is never put on a line: "Not tried: … an unusual name". A console script whose module does not run itself (if __name__ == "__main__") is said as not tried.
  • A big change of screens (more than 80 lines or 3 files of .tsx, .jsx, .vue, .svelte, .html, .css...) is tried by the Tester, an agent KOLONİ opens itself as it opens the Reviewer: it opens the chat's preview in KOLONİ's own browser, goes through what your request changed - clicks, types, reads, takes screenshots - reads the console, and ends with MERGE or HOLD and its findings: "Tried: Tester (…) on http://127.0.0.1:5173/ - HOLD, 2 findings, 1 blocking". A blocking finding goes back as a fix round; the try is not made again that turn. The Tester gets what the Reviewer gets - its role's read tools, and commands that only read or are the project's approved test command exactly, never a card - and its browser tools; it writes nothing, and opens the preview it tries alone (that address, nothing else of this machine, no file - nor do its pages load from elsewhere); its screenshots are shown to its model only where that model takes images (else it is told so, and reads the page's text). Its spawn opens no card at any level.
  • With no preview running, KOLONİ starts the project's dev server itself - npm run dev (else npm start) of the nearest package.json above the changed screens - on a free port (PORT, for a server that reads it; no browser window of its own), as one of KOLONİ's own runs (Settings › The app: with them all busy, "Not tried: KOLONİ's own runs fill the machine"), and stops it after the try. Starting it is asked below Full auto, as any server is. A preview runs in the project itself only: where the work waits in a working copy, "Not tried: the work waits in a working copy…".
  • Not tried, and said: while the turn's tests still fail (not those failing before it), in a turn nobody watches (Away), or where the Tester's role has no browser tools. A To-do task's turn is tried as the chat's other turns are.

On the canvas the Tester is drawn in the Checks box (On the canvas); KOLONİ's own runs of the try (the --help, the dev server) are not counted as test runs there.

items.title: Checks on asking
items.text:
The Orchestrator can ask for these checks in the middle of its turn, with its run_checks tool, and wait for them. You use it in words: tie a step to a condition - "if the tests pass, commit it", "testler geçerse commit et", "if no problems are found, commit the branch". The Orchestrator is told to call run_checks first and take that step only when the answer is green; otherwise it fixes the work or tells you. It never assumes the condition holds.

  • What runs: the same pass as at the turn's end - the tests, the type and style checks, the Reviewer's look and the live try -, on the work as it is then. The ask for a test comes at the end only.
  • The end runs its own checks too: asking is an extra pass, never the end's. Whatever an answer said, the turn's end runs its own checks - a test run KOLONİ made after the last change may stand for it, as at any end (Which tests); after a command that may have written, such as a commit, they run again. What it found on asking stands for that answer only: the end looks again for itself (a Reviewer's MERGE, the reviewers taken, the live try made on asking are not the end's). Asking costs one more pass - its test runs and, where the change is big, one more Reviewer. A call stopped half way counts toward the most below.
  • The answer's first line is KOLONİ's own: CHECKS: green, CHECKS: red or CHECKS: not complete, whatever the tests printed. The Checked lines and where the work stands in git ("At commit 3c4d5e6 on main; not committed: a.py.") follow fenced, as data - a test's summary or a file's name says what it likes, each on one line of its own. A red answer adds what KOLONİ would send back at the end, the failing output marked as data.
  • Green is strict: a test command of yours, or one KOLONİ saved, passed - never a guess -; no line failed, even one failing before this turn; none was not run or still running; the Reviewer does not hold; no test was deleted or loosened. Anything else that is not red is not complete: only documents changed, no test command, a guessed command while you're away, a check that broke. A turn that changed nothing - or whose checks are off - gets "KOLONİ found nothing of this turn to check" and no test runs.
  • No fix round: a red answer is the tool's answer, not a round of Fix rounds - the turn's end checks again and sends the work back as ever.
  • How long: each test command to its own limit - not the 2 minutes a turn you watch waits at its end, and no whole suite goes on after the answer.
  • How often: each call runs a pass, at most Fix rounds + 1 times a turn - 3 at 2 rounds; under Until it passes (the default) its ceiling of 20 rounds + 1, so 21. Asked again after that, it runs nothing and answers CHECKS: not complete, saying "KOLONİ ran its checks 3 times this turn, the most it runs on asking" - the turn's end checks the work.
  • One at a time: a second call while one runs is refused, and so is one while Ready for you's own checks or its card are open; Ready for you does not start in the middle of one.
  • Who has it: the Orchestrator at its own work in a project - an API model's, and a CLI's working with its own tools, over KOLONİ's bridge, as its other KOLONİ tools. Not a sub-agent, a plan, a side of a comparison, an answer to a message, nor a chat with no folder.

At Full auto a commit in the project runs without a card; a push still asks as the level says (Permission levels). In the Checks box's panel such a pass is "Round 1 · asked by the Orchestrator" (On the canvas). Looking at your folder for it, KOLONİ runs no program your repository's settings name (a filter of .gitattributes).

items.title: How long it waits
items.text:
A long test suite does not hold up the answer. In a turn you watch, whose work is in the project itself, the end works like a pull request's CI:

  1. Related tests first. KOLONİ runs only the tests related to the files the turn changed, and the answer waits for those. A failure goes back to the Orchestrator as above. They are read from the test command itself, where its runner can name them:

    Runner Related tests pytest the changed test files, and the test files named for a changed module (test_greet.py or greet_test.py for greet.py) vitest vitest related --run with the changed files jest --findRelatedTests with the changed files go go test of the changed packages, where the command is go test ./... cargo cargo test -p each changed crate of a workspace dotnet dotnet test of the one test project of the change

    The runner must be the command's first word or follow its launcher (python -m, uv run, npx, ...): tox -e pytest or make pytest gets no related step. Where none can be named (another runner, a change to a configuration file or to conftest.py, a command that names its own tests), there is no related step. A guessed command, or a saved one you have not said Always to, that would need its card has no related step either: one card per command.

    A test file named on the command line would get past what you left out of your tests, so where you left tests out there is no related step, only the whole suite: for pytest, an --ignore, --ignore-glob or --deselect (in the command or in addopts), a norecursedirs, or a conftest.py with collect_ignore or pytest_ignore_collect, and a command that picks or overrides pytest's config (-c, --config-file, -o, --rootdir, -p) or a PYTEST_ADDOPTS in the environment; for jest, a testPathIgnorePatterns. Test files under pytest's default norecursedirs (build, dist, venv, node_modules, a dot folder) are never named. pytest's testpaths are kept: only test files under them are named. vitest's related keeps the config's exclude itself. An npm test with a pretest script gets no vitest related step (it would skip the pretest).

  2. Then the whole suite. After related tests it goes on in the background at once. Without them the answer waits up to 1 minute for it: one that ends by then is said, and a failure goes back as above. One that runs on goes on after the answer. The section says "Full tests running: command (2:14)", and the line over the message box says "Full tests running… (2:14)". When it ends, its line is written again with the result. A failure then offers Fix it: nothing starts by itself.

    If the related tests fail on the last round, the whole suite is not run: "Full tests not run: the related tests fail".

The whole suite's own limit is the project's Longest command, 10 minutes unless you raise it (up to 60, in Settings › This project › When you're asked). Past it the section says "Tests timed out after 10 min" (or the minutes you set).

Stop this check, under a suite running after the answer, stops it: what finished stays, and the line says "Full tests stopped by you at 1:02 - not checked" (counted from when it started), or "before they started" if it was still waiting for the machine. It works at every permission level. The canvas's Checks node has it too, in its ⋯ menu, also while the answer waits for the related tests (see On the canvas). Stopped while the answer still waits for them, the line says "Tests not run: you stopped the check".

  • A newer turn that changes the same project and runs the same suite stops one still running in the background, as a new push stops a pull request's old CI run: "Tests not finished: the project changed, and a newer run took their place". A result that comes after the project changed beneath it adds "- the project changed while they ran", and a pass then is not shown as passed: a change on record (written, taken in or undone) or a command of any turn that may have changed files.
  • What the suite writes of the files that steer later work (.vscode/, .claude/, an instruction file, .koloni/) is taken back when it ends, as for any command; after its turn, with no card. What another turn wrote there meanwhile stays. Where its card asks you ("KOLONİ's test run wrote AGENTS.md without naming it — taken back. Keep it?"), the section says "Full tests waiting for your answer on a file the tests wrote: command" until you answer, with no clock.
  • Stop everything and putting the chat away stop it too. If KOLONİ closes while it runs, the next start says "Tests not finished: KOLONİ restarted".
  • A job while you're away and a To-do task's turn have nobody waiting for the answer, and their fix rounds need the result: they wait for the whole suite, up to the project's Longest command (10 minutes unless you raise it), with no related step.
  • A turn whose work is in its own working copy (a team's branch) cannot leave its tests running after it: the copy is taken in or set aside when the turn ends. There KOLONİ waits at most 2 minutes for the tests, all of the turn's test commands together and another turn's run before them. A longer run is stopped, and the section says "Tests not waited for: still running at 2:00"; one that never got to start says "Tests not run" and why. Until the run takes less than that again (for example, when an agent's run of the same command does), later such turns say "Tests not run" and why, instead of waiting again.
  • Stop during the turn ends the turn as Stopped. The section says "Tests not finished: stopped".

items.title: How many run at once
items.text: KOLONİ's own test runs queue: Settings › The app › More limits › KOLONİ's test runs at once (1 unless you change it, up to 4) go at the same time, and the rest wait. A whole suite waiting its turn says "Full tests waiting for another test run to end". Test processes per run (2 unless you change it, up to 16) is given to each of KOLONİ's runs where its runner reads it: pytest-xdist's -n auto. The agents' own commands are not limited by either.

items.title: On the canvas
items.text:
A checked turn has a Checks node. While KOLONİ's test run works, it shows the tool and how long it has run; once the turn is over, each line of the Checked section, with the runner's counts ("pytest · 214 ✓ · 2 ✗"), the related step's ("related tests · 12 passed"), and a whole suite running after the answer with its clock from its own start ("full tests · 2:14 …"), or "full tests · waiting for another test run to end", then its result or "full tests · stopped by you at 1:02 - not checked", and the coverage line where it was measured. It stands under the Orchestrator - or, where the Orchestrator opened agents of its own, under them, in their column.

The agents KOLONİ's checks opened - the Reviewer and the Security reviewer, a look again, the live try's Tester, a stronger model's diagnosis and fixer - are drawn in it, not as agents of the Orchestrator's, each role once as a card of its own: then it is the Checks · KOLONİ box, right of the Orchestrator's work with an arrow from it, its title on its frame's top edge, the test runs short at its foot ("✓ related 19 · ✓ pytest 36"). Where KOLONİ sent the work back, the box is a loop, dashed as a recipe's "back, at most N rounds": the agents the Orchestrator opened to fix what was sent back are in it too ("Coder · fix"), the looks in a column ⇄ the fixes; each role is its latest agent, the earlier ones shadows behind it with a count (×3). Its title says the rounds - "⟲ 3 looks · 2 fix rounds · on hold", "✓ checked" -, or at work "● round 2 · looking…" ("· waits for you" where one of them asks you something: the card says it too); its foot a dot a round (red: it went back or held, green: passed, amber: at work, grey: it only asked for a test - no fix round). One look and nothing sent back is a plain box: no count, no shadows, no loop. Who is in it, and each round, is what KOLONİ wrote down as its checks went - each pass's tests, its looks and their verdicts, why it went back, and the agents its send-back had the Orchestrator open -, never guessed from the order agents were opened in: an agent of a discussion, or one written for KOLONİ's ask for a test (which is no fix round), stays the Orchestrator's; what a fixer opened under it is in the box with it; a stronger model's diagnosis is a card of its own kind, not a look. That record comes with the Checked section at the turn's end: while the turn works, the box holds the agents KOLONİ's own checks opened, and the Orchestrator's fixers join it then. A turn checked by an older version has its plain box of lines. The box's title and each card are buttons: Enter or Space opens its panel, or that agent's window.

Click the box for its panel on the right - the canvas stays as it is, the box's frame amber: Tests, the Checked section's test runs; then Round 1, 2, …: who looked (its name opens its window), what each said ("MERGE", "HOLD · 3 blocking", "HOLD · 1 blocking - its report said MERGE"), the first blocking finding, and "→ fixed by Coder 4 · 3 files" - or, where the Orchestrator fixed it itself, what sent it back; under the last round why it was the last ("Still on hold after 2 fix rounds: you decide (Fix it)", "Stopped after round 3: no progress"). Fix it is the one under the answer (on the chat's latest turn), and Open the Checked section - once it is written - brings that section into view in the chat, the focus on it.

The Orchestrator's own box gets one line: "● checking…" while a run goes on, "✓ checked · 1 round", "✓ checked · related only" (the whole suite stopped or not run), "✗ still failing", "✗ on hold" (the tests passed, a Reviewer or the Tester holds) or "not checked". In a recipe's turn the box is the frame's last part - inside it, right of the recipe's steps; the Orchestrator's line reaches the frame at its door only. The frame keeps the recipe's own steps and its own loop (a Tester's findings back to the Coder, a grey dashed line - KOLONİ's loop is red); KOLONİ's looks and the Coders of its send-back rounds are in the box ("Coder · fix ×2"). Where KOLONİ sent the work back for the tests alone, nothing looking, the loop's left end is the tests - "48 → 45 (3 removed)" ⇄ Coder · fix -, and "⟲ 2 fix rounds · not taken in" where the work stayed in its copy for it. With nothing opened the box is plain and says "end of the recipe". A turn KOLONİ did not check has no Checks box: off for this chat, the Orchestrator's box says "not checked · off for this chat"; off in the recipe's Checks step, "not checked · off in the recipe’s Checks step"; in a project whose After a change is Nothing, it says nothing of it - the Checked section does.

Its ⋯ menu has Stop this check while one of its runs goes on - the same as under the answer, at every permission level: what ran stays, the rest says "not checked" -, Off for this chat (the level menu's Test and review changes, for the chat open now) and Open its log, the Orchestrator's window, whose record holds the runs.

items.title: What each line means
items.text: Line Means ✓ Tests passed: command - summary The command ended with exit code 0 and its output counted no failure. ✓ Tests passed (by exit code, no count): command Exit code 0 from a runner whose output KOLONİ reads no count from (an npm test that prints none). ✓ Tests passed: command - run by who after the last change The Orchestrator ran the same command after the turn's last change, or a recipe's Tester did on the work that was then taken in, it passed, and no command that may change files (a formatter, a generator) ran after it. KOLONİ did not run it again. – Tests gave no verdict: command masks its exit The test line hides its exit code (piped into tail, or followed by ; true) and its output counts no failure. This is not a pass. ✗ Tests failed: command - summary Any other exit code, or an exit code of 0 with a failure counted in its output. – Tests ran none: command collected no test The runner found no test: pytest's or unittest's exit code 5, "Ran 0 tests", jest's "No tests found", vitest's "No test files found". This is not a pass. – Tests skipped only: command - summary Every test it found was skipped. This is not a pass. – Tests could not start: why The program was not found, the command could not start, or KOLONİ's check itself broke. Nothing is sent back. – Tests not run: why It was declined on its card, the web is off and it reaches the internet, you stopped it while the answer waited for it, or the turn ended first. – Tests timed out / not waited for It did not end in time. This is neither a pass nor a failure. ✓ Related tests passed: command files - summary The tests related to the changed files passed. The whole suite runs after them. … Full tests running: command (2:14) The whole suite goes on after the answer. Its line is written again when it ends. … Full tests waiting for another test run to end: command It waits its turn: see How many run at once. – Full tests not run: the related tests fail The related tests still failed on the last round. – Full tests stopped by you at m:ss - not checked You stopped it. Nothing it had run is counted. – Tests not finished: why Stopped, a newer run took its place, or KOLONİ restarted while it ran. – … - the project changed while they ran The project changed under the run. Its result stands for no state of the work, and a pass is not shown as passed. – Tests not run on the last change: why A file changed after the last run, and the turn ended before KOLONİ could run the tests again. The lines above it are of the earlier run. Kept work Fix it went on in, taken in at the turn's end, is no change after the run. – Still failing as last checked - this turn changed nothing The turn changed no file, right after a turn whose checks still failed: the failing lines below are that turn's, said again, and Fix it is offered under them. – No test command There was nothing to run; the line says where to set one: the project map's whole project's row or a part's (Settings › This project › This folder). – Were failing before this turn: files (from CI: command) A lint, format or type check failed only on files the turn did not change, and each of its findings is there on the old code too. Not sent back. – Sent back to fix: round 3 (until it passes, 3 failing → 1) Until it passes: the rounds sent back, and how many failed at the first and fail now. ✗ Stopped after round 4: why - you decide (Fix it) Until it passes, the rounds stopped short of a pass: no progress in two rounds, at most 20 rounds, the turn's token limit or the project's monthly budget. ("Still on hold after round 4: …" where a review's hold stood.) – model's rounds stopped: no progress in two rounds Until it passes, a stronger model's round left the same tests failing. – Sent back to fix: 1 of 2 rounds How many times the Orchestrator was sent back this turn, of the project's Fix rounds; "(tests fail; 1 blocking finding)" after it where a review sent one back. ✗ Still failing after 1 fix rounds: you decide (Fix it) The Fix rounds were spent with a test still failing, or a problem KOLONİ's check by kind of work found (a page, a document, a config file …) - or the Orchestrator answered a round without changing anything, which ends its turn there. For a kind's problem, Fix it asks for it to be fixed, and the Orchestrator of that turn is told the problems as data. ✗ Still fewer tests, or more skipped, after 1 fix rounds: you decide (Fix it) As above, where no test fails but fewer ran, or more were skipped, than at the last green run. – Tests went from 48 to 45 (3 removed) - not this turn's change Fewer tests, or more skipped, than at the last green run, where nothing of the turn's could take them away (deleted by hand, a pull, a branch): said, the new counts the green state. ✓ Review: Reviewer (provider · model) - MERGE, no findings The Reviewer looked over the whole change and let it stand ("after 1 round" where it held it first). ✗ Review: Reviewer (provider · model) - HOLD, 2 findings, 1 blocking It held the change; each finding follows as "Blocking: …" or "Suggestion: …". ✗ Review: Security reviewer (provider · model) - 1 blocking finding, though its verdict said MERGE A blocking finding holds the change, whatever its verdict word says. – Review: … in the part it saw (3000 of 15000 characters; not shown: …) The diff was cut: what it said is of that part only, never a pass. – Review gave no findings section: not counted Its report had no findings section: nothing was sent back. – Review gave no verdict: not counted (role, provider · model) Its report had no verdict line KOLONİ could read: nothing was sent back. ✓ Documents read: Reviewer (provider · model) - MERGE, no findings · ✗ … - HOLD, 1 finding, 1 blocking The turn's long documents, read once against your request; a blocking finding goes back as a fix round. – No review: changes made by a command are not recorded The turn's only change was a command's: there is no diff for a Reviewer to read. – Changed while KOLONİ's run of command went on: files A file git tracks changed while one of KOLONİ's own runs went on - by the run, or by you meanwhile. Put back (your click) restores each still as the run left it. – A command of this turn may have changed files KOLONİ did not record: files - command A command (a sed -i, a formatter, a script) wrote files no record holds; in a git project the files git lists are named. The tests ran on them. – Review not run: why It could not look: it failed, it was refused, or the turn's token limit was reached. – No review: a small change (12 lines, 1 files) Not big, and no security touch. – No review: After a change is Tests only / the tests still fail / the recipe's own Review step looked it over Why no Reviewer looked. ✗ Still on hold after 2 fix rounds: you decide (Fix it) The Fix rounds were spent with blocking findings left. ✗ Still on hold: role could not look again (why) - you decide (Fix it) A look after a fix round could not be had: the hold stands. ✓ file: 3 links, all found · file: 120 rows × 4 columns · file: 12 slides, 3 with notes A document, diagram, data file or deck KOLONİ checked and found right. ✗ file: link to target not found · edge id points at nothing · rows 3, 7 have 2 fields, not 4 · slide 2 is empty A problem in what the turn wrote: sent back as a fix round while Fix rounds are left. – file: … - so before this turn A problem the file already had - the same complaint on a line of the same text, where a line added above moved it: said, not sent back. The same complaint on a line the turn wrote is the turn's. – Not checked: kind switched off for this project Its kind is off in Check by kind of work. ✓ page: no console errors at 375, 768, 1280 px A page the turn changed, opened in KOLONİ's own browser at each width. ✗ page: 2 console errors at 375 px - first · page: wider than the screen at 375 px A page that logs errors, or scrolls sideways: sent back as a fix round. ✗ page: 2 images without alt text · 1 buttons, links or fields with no name … The page is hard to use with a screen reader: sent back as a fix round. – page: 3 texts below the contrast they need at 375 px - “Muted words” 2.84:1 (needs 4.5:1) A warning: hard to read, said with its ratio - never sent back. ✗ page: the whole page is hidden from screen readers (aria-hidden) · 2 controls one can tab to inside aria-hidden … A screen reader is told nothing of the page, or a control one tabs to is not there for it: sent back as a fix round. – page: contrast not checked … on texts with something drawn under them · … the page's colour scheme is dark only · accessibility not read inside N frames or shadow roots · accessibility checked only in part · accessibility not read (… the page has no body · … no root) · accessibility not judged at 375 px for what changed after it loaded - images without alt text What the accessibility read could not judge: said, not sent back. – page: not checked: the page crashed the browser's tab The browser could not draw the page (one nested some 1,600 deep crashes Chrome's tab, measured on Windows): said at once; the turn's next page is read in a new browser. – Pages not checked: no preview running · no Chrome or Edge here A component changed and no preview serves the work; or no browser to look with. ✓ Tried python 'bin/tool.py' --help: exit 0, 12 lines A command-line tool the turn changed answered its --help. ✗ Tried line: exit 2 · Tried line: it did not end in 30 s Its --help failed or ran on: sent back as a fix round. ✓ Tried: Tester (provider · model) on address - MERGE, no findings · ✗ … - HOLD, 2 findings, 1 blocking The Tester went through the change on the chat's preview; a blocking finding goes back as a fix round. – Not tried: why No live try: the tests still fail, nobody watches the turn, the tool does not answer --help or has an unusual name, no preview can run, the work waits in a working copy, KOLONİ's own runs fill the machine, or the Tester has no browser tools. – Try gave no verdict: not counted (Tester, provider · model) The Tester's report had no verdict line: nothing was sent back. – Not checked: kinds - the turn ended before KOLONİ's check / Not checked on the last change: kinds The turn ended before these checks, or changed such a file after them. – Coverage: 72% of the changed lines are run by tests (tool) Of the turn's changed lines a test could run, the share the whole suite ran, by the project's own coverage tool. – Coverage: not measured (why) The flags failed (the run went again without them; not tried again till the coverage settings change), or no report was written or it could not be read. – New tests: files The test files the turn added or changed. – No new test: the Orchestrator said “line” It was asked for a test and gave this reason instead (its first line). ✗ Test removed: path The turn deleted a test file that was there before it. – Not in this run: name's work waits in Ready for you That work was not tested. It is still in its working copy. – Not checked: After a change is set to Nothing The project's setting. – Not checked: off for this chat This chat's Test and review changes is off. – Handed to model (Strongest) after 2 rounds by model The Fix rounds were spent with a test still failing: the next stronger tier tries. Its model's use counts. – model says fix-incomplete: why The stronger model's diagnosis, before it changed anything (fix-incomplete, test-wrong, approach-wrong). – Test changed: why The stronger model changed a test, with its reason in the request's words. The Reviewer reads it, whatever the change's size. ✗ Not a pass: model changed a test without leave (files) Its diagnosis was not test-wrong, yet it changed or deleted a test - or what says which tests run: a conftest.py, pytest.ini, tox.ini, setup.cfg, pyproject.toml, package.json, a Vitest, Vite, Jest, Karma, Mocha or Playwright config: the tests passing then is no pass, and the work stays as failing. Fix it asks for the fix, saying why in KOLONİ's own words (never the file names or output a model chose). pytest.toml and .pytest.ini count, and a Vitest workspace. ✗ Not a pass: the Reviewer held model's test change Its test-wrong change did not get the Reviewer's MERGE: the work stays as failing. ✗ Not a pass: the Reviewer did not read model's test change (why) Its test-wrong change needs a fresh MERGE from the Reviewer; the Reviewer could not look, gave no verdict, or the turn's token limit was reached: the work stays as failing. – Started over in a fresh copy: why The stronger model said approach-wrong: the copy's changes were dropped and the work began again from the start state. – Strongest skipped: over its limit That tier's provider is past its limit of spend: it is not handed the fix. ✗ Not taken in: 2 tests still fail after rounds by A and B The work stays in its copy, with the stronger model's question: Take in anyway or Fix it with your answer. ✗ Not taken in: on hold - a look's findings still stand after its fix rounds Work in a copy (a recipe's) that the Reviewer or Security reviewer still holds stays there, at every level: Take in anyway or Fix it with your answer. ✗ Not taken in: KOLONİ's checks of what it wrote still fail after its fix rounds Work in a copy (a recipe's, an Away job's, a branch turn's) whose page, document, config file or script still fails its check by kind of work stays there, at every level: Take in anyway or Fix it with your answer. Taken in anyway. You took the held work in as it was: said under the lines, not as a line of its own. Fix it now asks for the fix as for work in the project, where a line still fails; a turn that changes nothing after it says the work still fails. ✗ Still failing after rounds by A and B: you decide (Fix it) The work is in the project already; the stronger models' rounds did not make it pass. – Not checked: this recipe's Checks step checks nothing The recipe's Checks step is set for the recipe with every check off. – Tests not checked: off in this recipe's Checks step · No review: off in this recipe's Checks step · Not checked: kind off in this recipe's Checks step The recipe's Checks step leaves that check off. ✗ Checked only: this recipe's Checks step sends nothing back to fix - you decide (Fix it) The recipe's Fix rounds are 0: the tests failed and nothing went back. – CI commands found: lines - not run until you approve them once (Run these) The project's CI lint, typecheck and test lines, offered. Run these approves exactly these. – CI step name: not run: why / e2e not run: name / CI file not read: file - why What of the CI is left out beside the lines it offers or runs: an e2e step, a line not plain, an install, a secret, another shell, a folder outside, a file past the limits. – CI commands not used: a workflow changed in this turn A workflow file changed in the turn: its lines wait for the next one.

items.title: Command palette (Ctrl+K)
items.text:
Press Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) anywhere to open Go to: "A page, a conversation, a role, a model…". Type to filter, use the arrow keys to move, Enter to go, Esc to close.

It finds:

  • Pages: Canvas, Chats, Work › Ready for you and Work › To-do (Work on that tab; "ready" finds the first), Agents, Models, Tools, Memory, Knowledge, Usage, Settings.
  • Conversations, by title.
  • Roles and Models.
  • Tool servers.
  • Settings: each section of the project's settings, while a chat with a folder is open.
  • Help: Show the first steps.
  • Search in messages: searches the project's memory and earlier messages for what you typed (see Memory).

items.title: Compare
items.text:
Compare… under More (or /compare): "Send a message to two models side by side, and keep the work of one".

  1. Write the Message. The first model is the chat's own; choose the Second model's provider and its Model name.
  2. Press Compare. Each model does the work itself, in its own copy of the project, one after the other.
  3. Each side shows its time, tokens and cost, and View diff shows what it changed.
  4. Use name's work brings that side's changes into the project; the other side's are thrown away. Or Discard both: nothing reaches the project.

After you pick, Undo these changes takes the chosen work back.

items.title: Decisions
items.text:
Some things are decided for you while you are away, or at Full auto: the Orchestrator answers a question or opens a sub-agent, KOLONİ's judge refuses a risky command, and Check what I said first runs a command on a line of yours. Decided for you on the Ready for you page shows them in one list for the project: who decided what, and why - and what you can still do about each.

KOLONİ builds the list from its own records, at the moment you open it. No model is asked, and no agent can change a row or take one out; the Orchestrator's note_decision only adds one of its own. The list stays in KOLONİ: nothing is written into your project.

items.title: Where you see them
items.text:
• Ready for you, a tab of the Work page: the night's report, what waits for your word and, under it, Decided for you - To-do is its other tab. The night's report says how many were decided for you that night and how many you have not seen; See them brings them here, at Not seen. The page's first line counts both: "4 things wait for your word. 5 decisions were made for you since you left." The second part shows only when the project had a ☾ Away and the number is known.
  • In the chat, one line at the top, where something was decided for you in it - while you were away, or in a turn you watched: "3 things were decided for you in this project and 2 wait for you here." Open in Ready for you opens the page with Decided for you in view, at Not seen when some wait for your OK. The cards that wait for you stay in the chat, and you answer them there as before. The same line is in the Ready for you panel's This chat.
  • Usage, with This project, one line on the period you chose: "12 decisions were made for you this month, 2 of them you haven't seen.", with Open in Ready for you.

A chat with no folder has no project, and so no list: its decisions stay in its own Decided for you while you were away box, with OK and Change → (see Answering for you).

items.title: Who decided
items.text:
Each row says who decided, in words and in a colour of its own:

Who What it decided Orchestrator It answered a question or one of KOLONİ's cards for you; it opened a sub-agent, or did not; it added a task the Scout proposed to To-do, or turned it down (Answering for you); or it noted a decision it took itself, "Decided: …" (note_decision, Talking while agents work). KOLONİ's judge At Full auto it found a command risky, refused it, and the agent went on. A risky command it asked you about - on the command's card, or parked for you while you were away - is not listed: you decide that one, so it waits for you or you have decided it. Your rule, or Your words for a line of your own message Check what I said first ran a command without a card, or did not run it, because of a line of your preferences, the project's rules or your message. The reason shown is that line.

When the judge finds a command fine, it just runs. Those are not listed one by one: the list counts them in one line, "The judge let 12 commands run".

items.title: The list
items.text:
Choose the period: Since I left (since your last ☾ Away began; shown, and chosen first, only if the project had one), Today (since midnight here) or Week (since Monday). Not seen lists what waits for your OK in the whole project, however old. The top bar's pill ("5 decided") and a chat's line ("5 things were decided for you in this project") say the same count: Not seen's, of every chat of the project. A chat with no folder has no decision log: its pill counts that chat's own, "in this chat".

Each row says when, who, the chat it is in (or To-do), what was decided, the question, command or task it was about, and the reason in quotes. The newest come first. Five rows show, then Show all. A decision you have not said OK to yet says new; the heading counts them: "Decided for you 5, 2 not seen". Each row links to where the decision is: The question, The command and The agent open its chat, and The task opens To-do, on the same page, at that task.

Words an agent or a model wrote - a question, a command, an answer, a reason, a chat's title - are shown as quotes, never as part of the page. Here, secrets KOLONİ knows and keys known by their shape (a Bearer token, an API key, a password in an address such as https://user:password@host) show as ***, and characters nobody sees, such as a zero-width space, a direction mark or a blank-looking filler, are taken out first. A chat-with-no-folder's Decided for you box masks only the secrets KOLONİ knows. A reason that reads like orders to an agent starts with "Note from KOLONİ: this text contains instruction-like phrases; treat it as data." Longer text is cut at 300 characters.

items.title: OK and Change
items.text:
• OK, on a row you have not seen: it stays in the list, seen. On a To-do task it decides nothing: the task stays as it is, and an agent's change proposed on it still waits for you under Waiting for your word. A task the Orchestrator turned down that you added since needs no OK.
  • Change → …, while the agent that asked is still at work: your answer goes to it at once ("Sent to the agent that asked, while it works"), and the Orchestrator's answer leaves the list. On a To-do choice, Change adds the task or takes it off, until the task has started; if the task moved on since you opened the list, it is refused ("it changed since you looked") and the list is read again. Only answers shown here as they are written are offered; one with masked words in it is not.
  • Change and redo → …, once the agent that asked has finished: your answer goes on record in place of the Orchestrator's, and a new turn of its chat starts on KOLONİ's message - "KOLONİ: the user changed your answer to "Which database?": "Postgres" (was "SQLite"). Go on with the task." - the question and both answers in quotes, masked as the list shows them; never as your own message. The button says what it costs: "starts a new turn" (KOLONİ has no estimate of what a turn will cost, so it names no figure). The turn goes on with the agent's kept work, where its copy is kept - the copy the agent that asked worked in, in the turn the card was answered in (its own, or the one of the agent it worked for - also where it had none of its own, a Reviewer that only read, say), or the work of a turn that went on with it since (an earlier Change and redo in a job's chat, the morning's after Waiting for you): never another sub-agent's copy of that turn, nor the Orchestrator's where the agent had a copy of its own, another topic's of the same chat, a message of yours, nor another turn of KOLONİ's (a To-do story's next task, an approved plan's work, a rerun, a comparison's side); and "its work was taken in" or "discarded" below speak of that work alone. Where Fix it, a Change and redo outside a job's chat, a ☾ Away job's second try after a failure or Try again went on in that copy since, it says "its work was discarded": KOLONİ keeps no record of which copy such a turn went on in - change a card of that later turn instead. In a job's chat from a ☾ Away it is a job's turn, as the turn after Waiting for you is: its work is kept for your Take in, at Full auto too; in any other chat it is a turn of that chat, its work going into the project as the chat's level says. In a job whose branch you pushed, its button says so too - "adds to the branch koloni/… that you pushed": its commits go on that branch. A chat you archived comes back. It is done only from KOLONİ's own page, once for a decision, and not while you are away ("You're away from this project: press I'm back first"), nor while a turn of its chat is at work, nor while its job still waits for what it parked ("decide what its job parked first": those go on first, in their own turn), nor over the month's budget. It does not move the night's end: its turn is after the night, not of it.
  • Change, on a decision the Orchestrator noted itself: a box for what you decide instead, in your own words, and Send. While the turn it was noted in is at work, your words go into it as your own message, as Send now does - "I change your decision …: use Postgres", with KOLONİ's id of the decision, never the Orchestrator's words in a message of yours. Once that turn is over, a turn of KOLONİ's in its chat tells the Orchestrator: "KOLONİ: the user changed your decision "Use SQLite" (decision …): "use Postgres". …" - waiting behind a turn at work. Only from KOLONİ's own page, not while you are away, nor over the month's budget. The row is seen once you change it.
  • Where nothing can be changed, the row says why: "can't be undone: it ran", "its work was taken in", "its work was discarded", "its work waits for your Take in in its chat", "the next step ran".

items.title: Copy as Markdown
items.text: Copy as Markdown copies the period's whole list as plain Markdown, for example into a pull request's description. It is masked as the screen is. An agent's or a model's words go in code spans, so a pasted link, image, heading or @mention in them stays plain text.

items.title: What is not in it
items.text: A decision leaves the list when its record changes: if you changed the Orchestrator's answer - with Change or Change and redo -, the answer is yours; a task you turned down - one it added, with Change, or one it turned down, with Reject on To-do - is gone from To-do. The list is read again when something changes it, and when you come back to the window. Your own answers on cards are not decisions made for you, and are not listed. The list holds the newest 500 decisions of the period; with more, it says "Showing the newest 500".

items.title: Permission levels
items.text:
The permission level decides what agents may do without asking you first. It stands in the message box's row as three comb cells and its name (Ask one cell, Auto-edit two, Full auto three): a click lists the levels, each with a line on what it does - Ask before changes: "Each file change and command waits for your card"; Auto-edit files: "Writes files at once (revertible); commands still ask"; Full auto: "Changes and commands run; only harmful or risky actions ask" - Plan first, and in a project's chat Test and review changes (what KOLONİ checks after a change, on or off for this chat; off, the level says "· no checks"). Each chat has its own level.

Level In short Ask before changes Each file change and each command waits for your card. Auto-edit files File changes are written at once and can be reverted. Commands still ask. Full auto Changes and commands run without asking. Only harmful or risky actions still ask.

items.title: What asks at each level
items.text:
"Card" means the agent stops and waits until you answer on a card in the chat. "Runs" means it goes ahead without asking.

The levels at a glance; the table below has every case.

Action Ask before changes Auto-edit files Full auto Reading, listing or searching files in the project Runs Runs Runs Changing a file Card Runs Runs A command that only reads, such as cat, ls or git status (every path it names - an option's value (--file=x, -Path:'x') and a name written in quoted pieces (.e'nv') too - followed through links and junctions, inside the project and no secret file - else it is any other command) Runs Runs Runs Any other command Card, unless a rule covers it Card, unless a rule covers it Runs, unless Full auto's judge finds it risky A command that keeps running, such as a dev server Card, every time Card, every time Runs A command that deletes or empties files in the project, or throws away git work, written as a plain line (rm -rf src, Remove-Item, git reset --hard, git clean -fd, git checkout -- ., git stash drop, git branch -D) Card Card Runs, unless Full auto's judge finds it risky - a card with the judge off or no judge model to answer (which) A command that sends data off the machine (git push, scp, a curl that posts data, …) Card Card Card, unless Check what I said first finds a line of yours that names it; a plain push of your feature branch goes to Full auto's judge A plain push of the branch you have checked out to its own origin (git push, git push -u origin feature/x) - never main, master or origin's default branch Card Card Runs, unless Full auto's judge finds it risky - then its card, never a refusal; a card too with the judge off, no judge model to answer, or anything it does not know as plain A delete out of the project or of all of it (rm -rf ../x, rm -rf ., find . -delete, git clean -fdx), one not written as a plain line (bash -c "rm -rf build", … \| xargs rm, rm -rf .gi\t), a worktree removed, git's recovery pruned (git gc --prune=now, git reflog expire), a Docker delete, or a git remote's branches overwritten or deleted (git push --force, git push origin :x) Card Card Card A delete KOLONİ checks is disposable - a build folder git ignores, a clean worktree of yours, a merged branch - where you allowed such deletes Card Runs Runs A command handed to a shell (cmd /c, powershell -c, sh -c) Card, every time Card, every time Runs, unless Full auto's judge finds it risky;
