With no night, or one you have seen that ended more than a day ago, this is one line: "Nothing new since you last looked" - with The whole report of that night, where there is one. Where the record says why the night ended (its money limit, its time, Stop all), the report says it too. KOLONİ opened after a night opens on this tab, until the night has been on screen - not where you opened another page before it was read. (While Work shows its To-do tab, the night is not on screen.)
  • Waiting for your word: everything that waits, oldest first - what the night parked for you first -, in one list. Each row starts with its cell and says what it is - Push, Parked command, Question, Command, Proposed task, Done?, Memory proposal, Ready to take in and so on - and whose: a chat's row names its agent, "Coder asks" for its own question or request, "for Coder" on KOLONİ's own card about it, such as its step limit or its work waiting for Take in. Each says how long it has waited, and has Open chat to go to its chat. The buttons over the list show one kind at a time: All, Chats, To-do, Memory, Last night and Other folders. When new To-do tasks are proposed, Approve all approves them one by one.
  • Decided for you: the project's decisions, with OK and Change - see Decisions.

The To-do tab is To-do: each story a card, a story opened in a panel over the cards, and the rough note the Hive keeper splits into tasks.

items.title: The cells
items.text:
A small hexagon - a cell of the hive - says how a thing stands, the same way in the report, in Waiting for your word, on To-do and on Chats. Its colour never says it alone: a word stands beside it, and the cell's own name (its tooltip, and what a screen reader says) is its state.

Cell Means Green, full done Honey, full at work Honey rim, lightly filled waits for your word Red-orange, full stuck: it could not be done, or is blocked Empty queued, not started, or stopped A thin rim proposed

To-do lists them under its cards.

What waits:

  • Chat cards from every chat, including chats in other folders.
  • To-do decisions: a new task (Add to To-do / Edit / Not wanted), a "done?" (Done / Not yet), or a change (Change / Reject). New tasks include the Scout's suggestions after a turn. At Full auto, a task the Orchestrator added for you is under Decided for you (OK / Change → Reject): it does not start until you press OK.
  • Memory proposals (Approve, Approve as edited, Reject) and suggested preferences (Add / Reject). See Memory.
  • Last night: what the night's jobs parked for you, and the jobs that wait. A job's push comes first: Push - Push and open PR where the project's way is a pull request - or Not now; where KOLONİ notes something first, its notes and Push anyway. Then each command it parked, Run or Reject, and each question, its answer - the rows of Waiting for you, decided only once you are back and the job is not at work; a row that cannot be decided now says why. A job that waits for something else is answered in its chat (Open its chat to answer).

A Project notes offer or the Orchestrator's Go away line waits only in its own chat unless that chat has something else waiting.

items.title: The "Teams' work is ready" card
items.text:
When a team's recipe has finished, its work waits in a working copy. The Teams' work is ready card asks once whether to take it into the project. In the chat it is one line, such as "Teams' work is ready · Web app 3 files". It can also say that a team failed or stopped.

Button What it does Take in Brings the work into your project. Fix the findings Takes the work in, then has a Coder fix what the reviewers found. Shown only when findings were left and the team has a Coder. Ask for changes Opens "What to change (optional)…". The work goes back to its loop, with your words added to the next agent's task.

The card does not ask:

  • at Full auto, when nothing failed or went unchecked: the work is taken in by itself;
  • when the work changed nothing;
  • at any level - Auto-edit and Ask too - when KOLONİ's checks left it failing or a Reviewer still holds it after the fix rounds: the work stays in its copy, and the turn's Checked section says "Not taken in" with Take in anyway (no look first) and Fix it (its turn checks and looks at the whole kept work again) (docs).

On the canvas the same card is a box titled Ready for you. Open the list → opens the panel.

items.title: The kinds of card
items.text:
Card Buttons When Run this command? Run once, Always run …, Reject Before an agent's command runs. A file change (the file's name and lines changed) View diff, Approve, Reject; after: Revert An agent wants to write a file. Search the web? Search once, Always allow searching in this conversation, Reject Before a web search. Make this request? Send once, Always allow GET to …, Reject Before a web request. Open this site? This time, Allow this site, Reject An agent's browser would open a site. Send this form?, Click this?, Type into this field?, Type into a password field? Yes, this once, Reject A form, sign-in or payment step in an agent's browser. Asked every time. Read outside the project? (or Change …, Run a command outside the project?) Allow once, Allow reading this folder, Allow changes in this folder, Reject A path outside the project. Read a secret file? (or Read this computer's settings?) Allow once, Reject Reading a .env file, a key or a similar file, or a CLI's own settings folder. Add a folder to this chat? Add to this chat, This time, Reject An agent asks for another folder. Give a secret to its commands? a hidden field, Give, Reject An agent asks for a key by name. The value goes only into the environment of that turn's commands; the model, the chat and the record never get it. See Security model. Open this sub-agent? Open agent, Reject Before a sub-agent starts, when your settings ask. Also when KOLONİ would move an agent to a provider that is paid per token. Create this role? Create role, Reject An agent proposes a new role. Add this skill? Add skill, Reject An agent proposes a skill. Approve this plan? Approve, Edit, Reject With Plan first on. See Plan first. Take in …'s work? Take in (or Merge, Open pull request), Discard A sub-agent's work waits in its working copy. An agent's question itself, saying who asks (Orchestrator asks, Coder asks), or a title of KOLONİ's own such as Allow this? or Go on with the recipe? (KOLONİ asks), with its words whole under it its own options, or Or answer in your own words… An agent, or KOLONİ, asks you a question. KOLONİ's Deny is shown as Reject. A question KOLONİ did not put to you (your message was waiting, or it offered Take in) is a row in the chat, "Wanted to ask: … · not asked"; open it for why. Add to Project notes? ticks, Add, Not now After a turn found things worth noting. It never holds the turn. Suggested by the Orchestrator ("Add this to your preferences: "…"?") Add, Not now The Orchestrator suggests a line for your preferences from your own words, where it does not add it at once (how). It never holds the turn. ☾ Go away now? Go away, Change The Orchestrator put work on To-do and offers to go away; nothing starts before Go away. Decided for you (on Work's Ready for you tab; a chat with no folder: Decided for you while you were away) OK, or Change → another answer - Change and redo → once the agent that asked has finished The Orchestrator answered for you (see Answering for you) or noted a decision it took itself, "Decided: …" (its Change takes your own words), KOLONİ's judge refused a command, or Check what I said first ran a command without a card, or did not run it, on a line of yours (OK). See Decisions. Go on past its step limit? Continue (+N steps), Stop here An agent came to its step limit before its work was done. See Step limits. "Model has not answered for 5 min. Keep waiting, or stop this turn and pick another model?" Keep waiting, Stop and pick another model The Orchestrator's model said nothing for 5 minutes in a turn you started. See Step limits.

See Permission levels for when each card is asked.

items.title: Cards that only tell
items.text:
These have a grey edge. Nothing waits on them.

Card Buttons When Text tried to give orders False alarm Text from outside (a web page, an MCP tool's result, a file, another agent's message) looks like it tries to give the agent orders. It names the rule that matched, never the text. The agent was already told to take it as data; nothing was held back. False alarm is counted for that rule. See Outside content. Not all of …'s work reached the project none Some of an agent's changes did not come in. Each file says why.

items.title: When a turn ends, stops, or KOLONİ restarts
items.text:
• When a turn ends or you stop it, its open questions are cancelled, and commands, changes and web requests you did not decide are rejected. A recipe's working copy is kept, and waits under Ready to take in. An agent on a branch keeps its work committed there. See When an agent stops.
  • Under the Orchestrator's last answer of a turn that changed files, KOLONİ says where the work is, from its own records rather than the model's words: "In the project: server.py (+1 −1).", "Not in the project yet: server.py waits in Ready for you - Take in to apply it.", or "Nothing reached the project." The line is written when the turn ends: a copy you take in later does not change it.
  • When KOLONİ starts again, work that was open is marked interrupted. Nothing is ever run again by itself: a message that was still queued says "Not sent: KOLONİ restarted", and runs only when you press its Send.
  • A question that ended without an answer shows in the chat as "not answered".

items.title: Talking while agents work
items.text:
A turn stays open while the Orchestrator's agents work, and you can talk to the Orchestrator in it: ask how things stand, add a wish, have it open, message or stop an agent - without waiting for the turn to end.

A word sent now answered in the same turn, while the Coder works: the line over the chat, opened.

items.title: Send now and After this turn
items.text:
While a turn runs, the message box has two ways to send:

  • Send now (Enter): the Orchestrator reads it in this turn. Your message goes into the turn at work. If the Orchestrator is waiting for its agents, it wakes and answers you; if it is in the middle of a step, it reads your message at its next step. The turn does not end before it has read it.
  • After this turn: it waits in the queue and starts its own turn, as a message did before.

The box says what it does: "Write to the Orchestrator - it reads it in this turn…". With no turn at work there is only Send.

Some turns take no message while they run. Then Send now puts your message in the queue and the box says why under it - Queued: and one of:

Why When the turn was ending the Orchestrator had given its last answer this turn takes no message now (a plan turn) the turn writes a plan (Plan first) this turn takes no message now (a comparison) the turn is one side of a comparison this turn takes no message now (a To-do task's turn) the turn works on a To-do task this turn takes no message now (a job while you were away) a ☾ Away job's turn this turn takes no message now (not one you started) the turn was not started from your own page it is for another topic you wrote into another topic, or started a new one

A message is in exactly one place: in the turn at work, or in a turn of its own. If the turn ends before the Orchestrator read it - you pressed Stop, or the turn failed - your message goes on in a turn of its own, queued, so it is never lost. One already written into a CLI Orchestrator's turn is not sent again: what came of it is said instead (below).

When it answers your message, the Orchestrator changes nothing itself: its steps until that answer are refused Write files, Edit files, Diagram pictures, Run commands, a skill's script, Web requests and any MCP server's tool. It hands new work to an agent (opens one, messages one, stops one) or says it in its answer; it may still read, look things up, Remember and propose To-do tasks, which wait for your OK as ever. A CLI Orchestrator's own tools are only told so. Its own work goes on as before once it has answered. While it answers it waits for no place among the agents at work: its agents keep theirs, and it answers you at once (Settings › This project › Limits and money › More limits).

Only you can send now: the message must come from KOLONİ's own page. What you write is your own word, as any message of yours is - Full auto's judge reads it as yours.

items.title: With a CLI as the Orchestrator
items.text:
CLI Send now Claude Code, Codex, Copilot run Native goes into its turn at once (measured 27 Nov 2026: Claude Code 2.1.332, Codex 0.172, Copilot 1.0.114) agy, and any CLI run One session per agent read when its current run ends, in one more run of the same turn

A word to the Orchestrator about an agy agent (its window's box) wakes the Orchestrator as your own word does, while it waits for its agents.

items.title: What came of a word sent into a CLI's turn
items.text:
A word written into a CLI's running turn - Send now to a CLI Orchestrator, an agent's Tell box, or another agent's message to it - comes to one of three ends, by what the CLI itself shows:

End What the CLI shows What you see taken Claude Code echoes it before its turn's result; Codex answers with its turn; Copilot names it as taken into its work before it goes idle nothing more: it reads it in that turn not sent its turn was over (Codex: "no active turn to steer"), or it could not be written Send now: the Orchestrator reads it at its next step, or in one more run of the turn; Tell: the box says the turn is ending - try again once it has finished. Where Codex's no came only after 5 seconds, Tell's word waits for the agent's next step and a line in the chat says so: Coder's turn was over before your word reached it: "use blue" - it is handed to Coder at its next step, if it takes one; say it once more if it still matters unknown it was written, but by the end of its turn the CLI showed no sign it took it - or the CLI said no in a way not measured a line in the chat: Lead may not have read your word before its turn ended: "use blue" - it is not sent again; say it once more if it still matters

A word of Send now, Tell or an agent's message that is unknown is never sent again: the CLI may have read it. A Claude Code that echoes your word only after its result takes one more turn on it; KOLONİ reads that turn to its end in the same run, and your word is still said unknown - it was not taken in the turn it was sent into. The agent's own record says the same: Lead may not have read this before its turn ended; it is not sent again. A Change of a decision or of an answer is different: it stands whatever came of it, and the agent is given it again from its next step or run on - as is KOLONİ's own word to an Orchestrator that changed files with a command.

An agent that messages a CLI agent at work is told what came of it the same way - in the message's answer where it is known at once (Codex), else by KOLONİ once it is: Coder took your message ("use blue") into its turn: it is read in its turn (from its next step on - it takes no step of its own for it); your message ("use blue") did not reach Coder's turn: it is handed to Coder at its next step, if it takes one or Coder's turn ended before it showed it took your message ("use blue"): it may not have read it; it is not sent again (a note, read at once).

items.title: Agents in the background
items.text:
The Orchestrator of an API model can open an agent in the background: it starts it and goes on at once - talks to you, opens others, messages or stops it. When the agent ends, its report comes to the Orchestrator as a note and it takes one step to read it. Until then it says the agent is still at work, never what it found. A CLI's Orchestrator always went on like this; it reads its agents' reports once all of them are back.

Background agents are held to the chat's limits as any agent: how many work at once, how many a turn opens, how deep (Step limits). Their cards come to you as usual, and Full auto's judge looks at their commands as at any. Each wake is a step of the Orchestrator's, counted to its role's limit. Stop on the turn stops them all.

The Orchestrator can also run a command in the background (run_command with background): it goes on, reads the command's output with command_output, stops it with stop_command, and is told when it ends. At most as many run at once as the chat lets agents work at once. The turn's end stops them.

items.title: Messages between agents: reply, leave, now
items.text:
The Orchestrator of an API model also says how a message to one of its agents (message_agent) goes - only to an agent it could message anyway:

How The agent is not at work The agent is at work reply (as ever) it takes a turn on it while the Orchestrator waits for its reply it is handed it at its next step - or, a Claude Code, Codex or Copilot agent, in its running turn leave it takes it up now, in a turn of its own; the Orchestrator goes on, and the reply comes to it as a note, as a background agent's report does it is handed it at its next step; where its work ends before that, it takes it up in a turn of its own, and its reply comes the same way now as leave into its running work: a CLI's running turn - with what came of it, as below - else at its next step, as leave

A turn an agent takes on a message left waits for its other turns and for a place, as any agent's turn; a turn in which it only answers another agent's question is not handed it - its own work is. A message left counts twice toward the turn's messages between agents (its note and the turn it may start) from the moment it is left, so it is refused where there is room for one only. However it ends, the Orchestrator is told: the agent read it (from its next step on, without a step of its own for it), its reply, or why it was not taken up - the agent was stopped, or can no longer be messaged, or the turn ended first, or it was stopped as it took it up (then it may have read it); it is not sent again. Every other agent, and a CLI Orchestrator, sends a message as a reply, as does a message to an agent of an earlier turn: one that asks otherwise is told so.

items.title: Stop and Message on one agent
items.text:
An agent at work that the Orchestrator (or one of its agents) opened has Stop and Message on its node on the canvas and in its window's head:

  • Stop stops that agent alone. The chat says "You stopped Coder. Its work so far is kept for your Take in; nothing of it is in the project." The Orchestrator is told, as KOLONİ's word, not to open it again unless you ask; the rest of the turn goes on. The Orchestrator has its own stop_agent for one it opened.
  • Message opens the agent's window at its Tell box.

KOLONİ's own checks (Stop this check) and the agents of a team's recipe (the team's Stop) are stopped their own way, so they have no Stop of their own here.

An agy agent cannot hear messages while it works: its box says so - "Coder can't hear messages while it works (agy). Tell the Orchestrator instead - it can stop it and start it again." - and sends your words to the Orchestrator. A Claude Code, Codex or Copilot agent hears them in its running turn.

items.title: When an agent ends and nobody is looking
items.text:
When a background agent ends while nobody looks at its chat, KOLONİ shows a desktop notice - "Reviewer finished: 2 findings", "Coder stopped", "Tester failed" - where the project has Show a desktop notification on (Settings › This project › Notifications). The notice holds only the agent's name and how it ended, never its words. A card or a question that starts to wait for you gets a notice too ("Coder asks you a question", "3 cards wait for you") - also only while nobody looks at its chat.

"Nobody looks" is herdr's rule: no page of KOLONİ's has the chat on screen with its tab seen and its window in front. A tab you hid, another window you went to, or another page of KOLONİ's open over the chat (Chats, Settings) is nobody looking - the notice comes; the chat on screen in front of you is somebody - it does not.

items.title: The line over the chat
items.text:
While a turn runs with agents at work below the Orchestrator, a plan of the Orchestrator's, or something that waits for you, one line sits over the chat, under its tabs:

3 agents at work · step 3 of 6 · 1 waits for you · ≈ 0.40 USD

  • agents at work: those working, waiting for their own agents, for a place or for a file. One that waits for your yes to start is a card, counted with what waits for you.
  • step 3 of 6: the step of the Orchestrator's plan after those done (see update_plan below), there only while it shows one.
  • waits for you: the cards of this chat that wait for your word, as the canvas counts them.
  • what the turn cost so far at your prices - its agents and KOLONİ's own requests for it, the advisor's too. "≥" where a part of it has no price; left out where nothing of it is priced (a CLI on a plan, a model with no price), never a made-up zero. It is read again at most every 5 seconds as the agents report their tokens.

Click the line for At work in this turn: each agent, "Coder · working · since 14:02", with its Stop and Message; the Orchestrator's plan, a step a line; and Open Ready for you.

items.title: What the Orchestrator has while its agents work
items.text:
The Orchestrator at its own work - not a sub-agent, an answer or a discussion, nor a plan turn or a side of a comparison - also has these, besides stop_agent; anywhere else they are refused, also when named. Each answer of theirs is data for it: what agents, models and other people wrote stays in quotes, with secrets masked.

  • agents_at_work - who of this turn is at work now: "2 at work in this turn:", then a line each, "- Coder (Coder role): running since 14:02 (3 min), in the background; waits for: its command "pytest -q", running since 14:03; last said: "Reading the tests…"". An agent's last words are cut at 300 characters and marked where they read like orders; one that waits for your yes "waits for the user's yes", one that waits for a place "waits for a place". A CLI Orchestrator has it too. What it waits for comes from KOLONİ's records alone, never guessed: a card for you (its command or its change, named), an answer to its question or on one of KOLONİ's cards, its command running and since when, another agent (the one that holds a file it wants, or its own agents at work), a place (at its provider, "1 of 1 at work there", or among the turn's agents), your yes to open it - or "unknown" where the records say nothing. At work in this turn, over the chat, says it too: "Coder · working · since 14:02 · waits for its command "pytest -q", running since 14:03" (nothing where the records say nothing).
  • update_plan - the Orchestrator of an API model shows you its plan: its steps, each pending, in progress or done, at most 30 of 200 characters. It is its own words, and says so: its window shows it under Plan (its own words) (a Codex Orchestrator's own plan shows there too), and the line over the chat says its step. The plan goes with the turn. A CLI's own plan is its own, so a CLI is not given it.
  • ask_advisor - a second model's advice on a hard choice, at most 3 times a turn. The advisor is your Advisor model (Settings › The app › Agents: "A model the Orchestrator may ask for advice. It sees the Orchestrator's summary and the turn's recent steps, masked."); with none chosen, a model on another provider than the Orchestrator's, the strongest first. Only models that can answer with every tool off are offered, as for the Judge model. It is sent the Orchestrator's question (1,000 characters) and summary (4,000), its last 12 steps of the turn and who is at work - every secret KOLONİ knows, and keys known by their shape, masked - and no tools. Its answer (2,000 characters) is data. Where no advisor can be asked - none to ask, no room on its provider, the turn past its token limit, no answer within a minute (two for a CLI) - the Orchestrator is told why and goes on. Its request counts in the turn's spend and on Usage under its model.
  • note_decision - a decision the Orchestrator took for you without asking (a library, an approach) goes under Decided for you on Ready for you: "Orchestrator · Decided: "Use SQLite for the cart"" with its reason, marked new until your OK. At most 10 a turn, each one line of 200 characters. It changes nothing by itself. Change takes your own words: while that turn is still at work they go into it as your message ("I change your decision …: …"), else a turn of KOLONİ's in that chat tells the Orchestrator. See Decisions.
  • read_pr_feedback - one pull request of the project's GitHub repository, by its number or address: the review decision, the checks that failed or have not ended, each review and comment with who wrote it, and the comments on lines. It is read with your own gh - offered where gh is installed and the project's origin is on github.com; not logged in, it says so - and it only reads: there is no way to reply with it. What reviewers and checks say is theirs, never yours: framed as data, masked, cut at 20,000 characters. Where it reads like orders to an agent, the chat warns you, as it does for a web page or an MCP tool.
  • suggest_preference - when you say how you want work done from now on, your own sentence for Your preferences, quoted from your prose of the turn: added at once with Undo in the chat, or - with New preferences from your words at Ask me first - on a card with Add and Not now. See Memory.

items.title: Reading answers aloud
items.text:
• Read aloud, under a turn's answer in the chat, reads the turn's answer; Stop reading stops.
  • Auto-read is the 🔈 beside 🎙 (Dictate) in the message box's row; lit while it is on.
  • Auto-read reads each answer when the work ends: the Whole answer, or a Short summary ("A sentence or two the Orchestrator adds to be said").
  • How the Orchestrator speaks (up to 300 characters) is sent with your message when Auto-read reads a short summary.

Answers are read with this computer's voices, or with Gemini's:

  • Gemini: add a Gemini API key and Save key. The key stays in KOLONİ; the page never sees it again. "When off, this computer's voices read."

items.title: Dictating
items.text: Dictate: "what you say is written into the box, and nothing is sent". Dictation language sets the language you speak; it also sets the language answers are read in.

items.title: Privacy
items.text:
• "Speech recognition is your browser's: in Chrome and Edge what you say is sent to Google's or Microsoft's service to be written down."
  • A computer voice marked online sends what it reads to its maker.
  • "Text read with Gemini is sent to Google. On the free tier Google may use it to improve its products; on a paid key it does not."
  • "KOLONİ keeps no sound and sends none anywhere."

Voice settings are kept in this browser: Settings › The app › Voice.

items.title: The Workspace
items.text:
The Workspace button, the first under the message box, opens "the project's files, what agents changed, wrote or showed, and what waits for you". Its number is what waits for you in this chat, a copy kept for Take in too (in Changes that copy is under Kept).

  • Files: the project's files. Open files show as tabs.
  • Changes: what changed, sorted by what you have to do: Waits for you, At work, Kept, In the project, Not by an agent, Needs a look, and Closed (shut at first). Inside a group, each change sits under its agent and your message. Each file says in words what happened ("changed", "new", "deleted", "you said no"). With git, the tab shows this chat's work and what git sees changed since the last commit. Without git (or when git does not answer in time), it shows this chat's record and says so. The tab's count is git's (as in the top bar), or without git what is not closed. Show folders as a tree puts the files in their folders. When changes wait for you, it says how many and offers Next waiting ▸. A file that waits opens on its diff with Approve and Reject; one in the project offers Revert. An agent's copy opens on what it holds, with Take in… (or Look) to its card.
  • Previews: dev servers agents started.
  • Working copies: each sub-agent's copy ("name's copy").

items.title: Working copies
items.text:
Each sub-agent changes files in its own copy of the project (where it is, below). Your folder does not change until its work is taken in.

  • .git and caches are not copied. node_modules, .venv and venv are linked, not copied.
  • A project over 20,000 files or 500 MB gets no copy: the agent works in the project itself.
  • When you and an agent changed the same file, KOLONİ merges line by line (for files up to 1 MiB).
  • On Linux and macOS a copy keeps whether each file is runnable, so a script such as ./gradlew still runs, and Take in carries that back to your project. A new file written with Write files gets your usual mode (0644 with the common umask).
  • Work goes into your folder one way at a time: a Take in waits while a branch is merged, and the other way round. What went in reaches the other agents' copies where they did not change those files, and a copy made at that moment gets all of it.

Agents at work beside each other are told that each works in a copy of its own: change only what their task needs, write nothing outside their copy, stop no program by its name, start a server on a free port, and install nothing into the linked node_modules, .venv or venv. A command an agent runs in its copy is asked at every level, Full auto too, when it:

  • names another agent's copy, a worktree of your project, or a place above its copy (../..) - also past a cd KOLONİ cannot follow, where any .. counts;
  • writes in the linked node_modules, .venv or venv, which are your project's own, or installs into them (in a turn you watch);
  • stops programs by their name (taskkill /IM, pkill, killall, Stop-Process -Name), or looks a process up and stops it (lsof -ti:8000 | xargs kill, fuser -k). By its id (taskkill /PID, kill 1234, Stop-Process -Id 1234), or one the line itself started (kill $!), is fine. In your project, at Full auto, Check what I said first may let a stop by name run on a line of yours, but never one that may stop KOLONİ itself or another agent's CLI (python, node, uvicorn, claude, codex, copilot, qodercli, agy, a filter, a wildcard, kill -1 or kill 0, or a process looked up).

KOLONİ reads the command as written: a path built in a script is not seen.

items.title: Where copies and worktrees are
items.text:
Your project A sub-agent's copy A branch's worktree (a ☾ Away job's, a team's on a branch) In git Outside it: runtime/copies/, or your data folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\KOLONI\copies\ on Windows, ~/.local/share/KOLONI/copies/ elsewhere) where the runtime folder sits in a repository or beside an AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md In the project: .koloni/worktrees/<id>/<agent>/tree Not in git In the project: .koloni/copies/<id>/<agent>/tree - (no git, no branch)
  • <id> is this KOLONİ's own folder there: two KOLONİs on one project (yours and a test copy) never clear away each other's.
  • A copy inside a project in git would have no .git of its own, so git in it would answer with your repository: that is why such copies stay outside. A worktree has its own .git, so git in it answers with its branch. Whether your project is in git is looked at each time a copy is made: once you git init, the next copy is made outside.
  • The first time a worktree is made, KOLONİ adds /.koloni/worktrees/ and /.koloni/copies/ to your repository's own .git/info/exclude (in a linked worktree of yours, the main repository's), so git status stays clean. Your .gitignore is not touched. In a project with no git, .koloni/copies/ holds a .gitignore of its own that ignores all of it, so the copies stay out of the git it gets later; KOLONİ's .koloni/.gitignore lists worktrees/ and copies/ too once it writes one for its scratch (a line it lacks is added after yours).
  • Each is one agent's work: that agent works in it as its own folder; any other agent, or a command at the project's root, may look in but not write, delete or run anything there (permissions).
  • Neither is copied into another copy, shown in the Files window, searched by an agent's search, nor listed as a change of your project. When you delete the project from KOLONİ, they go with it (your branches stay). A worktree whose records your git clean -fdx removed is left as it is, with its uncommitted work, for you to delete.
  • A CLI started in a copy or worktree in .koloni/ reads your project's AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md from the folders above it, and the copy's own as well: the same words, read twice.
  • Copies and worktrees made before 0.1.10 stay where they were made, and are found and decided there.

A working copy's life, from the copy to your project; the "On a branch" lane is Branches below. (full size)

items.title: Taking work in
items.text:
When a sub-agent finishes, its changes come back on a card: Take in …'s work?, with Take in and Discard. At Auto-edit files and Full auto they come in without a card when the agent finished, nothing clashes and the tests it wrote passed. See Permission levels.

  • Changed on both sides: files you and the agent both changed. "Nothing is chosen for you"; pick a side for each, or press Let an agent resolve the conflicts.
  • Run the test runs, on the copy, the tests the agent wrote or changed - only those, each part's test command from the project map narrowed to them. They are its own code: KOLONİ's guess runs them by itself only at Full auto, so at Auto-edit the card waits for this click. One that wrote no test has none to run: "No tests of its own to run before it is added - KOLONİ's check at the turn's end runs every test." See Checked.
  • Part of it taken: a card can take some of its files and keep the rest - a file that changed since you looked is shown again, not taken, and the API's Take in may name the files it takes (files). Those taken say they are in the project; the rest wait on the same card for Take in or Discard, the agent's copy kept for them. Discard then throws away only the rest: what was taken stays, and the card says its work was taken in. The commit offered once the card closes - where Save each sub-agent's work as a git commit is on, as after any Take in - holds only the agent's change in each file taken, whichever step took it - even across a restart of KOLONİ. A branch's work goes in whole: naming some of its files is refused, also on the card of a branch copy kept after KOLONİ stopped.

A team's recipe keeps its work in one copy until you press Take in on the Teams' work is ready card. See Ready and approval cards.

Take in: the team's work comes into the project only now.

A team's work waits under Ready to take in until you press Take in.

items.title: Branches
items.text:
The Orchestrator can give a team's work a git branch of its own. Then the card offers Merge or Open pull request, as you chose under Settings › This project › When the work is done › How a team's finished branch reaches yours. Until you choose, the first finished branch on a GitHub project asks. A pull request lets KOLONİ push the branch; it never merges one. Keep this branch after merging keeps the branch.

Opening a pull request needs gh (GitHub's CLI) installed and signed in (gh auth login), and the project's origin must be the GitHub repository gh sees. Until then the card says why it cannot open one. A branch that holds commits of yours that origin does not have - your branch or another merged into it, fast-forwarded to, rebased onto or cherry-picked - is not pushed until you push them, also after you amended, rebased or dropped them; the card names them. What counts as the agent's own is what its branch's history says was committed on it. A commit not on origin that this history does not show and no branch of yours holds - an agent's cherry-pick of yours (a new commit), or the agent's own once that history is gone (git reflog expire, or git's cleanup of an old branch) - is not pushed either: the card says KOLONİ cannot attribute it, rather than calling it yours. Nor is a file that holds exactly what a commit of yours not pushed yet put there (an agent's squash, pick or amend of it, or a copy of a stashed file, of a commit on a detached HEAD - in this folder or in another worktree of yours -, or of a file you had not committed when the branch began). What is on GitHub is what origin itself says its branches hold, asked right before the push - never your remote-tracking branches (origin/*), which anything in your repository may write: a commit only such a ref says is pushed is yours, and a stale one (a branch deleted on GitHub, a teammate's push you have not fetched) changes nothing. Where GitHub's branch the pull request goes into has commits you have not fetched, it asks you to fetch first; where git's config rewrites the address the push goes to (an insteadOf or pushInsteadOf rule matching it), nothing is pushed. And while you have any commit or stash not on GitHub - on a branch, in a stash, on a detached HEAD, in any worktree of yours - or the branch began from your uncommitted work, a pull request waits for your click at every level, Full auto too: the card says why ("you have 2 commits not on GitHub yet", "you have a stash not on GitHub yet"; "not on origin" where the push goes to a folder or another host), so you can check its files are the agent's work. KOLONİ never pushes onto a branch of the same name origin has already, a fast-forward too: "origin already has a branch named …: nothing was pushed". Nor does a secret KOLONİ knows - a provider key you saved, an MCP server's variable a secret's name holds, the page's key, one given on a card, one of the environment's or a value the project passes to its commands, or the token or password such a value holds alone (a DATABASE_URL's password in a settings.py) - go up or into your branch, in a file or in its name: KOLONİ's own commit leaves such a file out and its card says so, and a branch an agent committed one on itself is neither merged nor pushed ("take it off the branch first"). The rest of the work goes on; an ordinary value (production, a path) stops nothing. A file named as a secret (.env.local, token.json, a data file in a secrets folder - which names) goes up with a pull request only on your click, at Full auto too: its card says "token.json: named as a secret - it goes to GitHub only on your click". A task's name goes up as the commit's subject and the pull request's title mentioning nobody and closing no issue, a token by its shape (ghp_…, a password in an address) masked: a zero-width joiner follows each @ and comes before the number a closing keyword names (Fixes #12, Fixes GH-9, an issue's link), and no control character is kept; the pull request's body puts what an agent wrote - the task, the files' names, the check, its notes - in code. Where git checks your files out with CRLF (core.autocrlf=true, Windows' default) and they are LF, a file whose line ends alone differ is no change of yours, and Take in keeps your file's own line ends. Where a commit of yours not pushed is in another worktree, the card names that worktree's folder; if you deleted that folder by hand, git still keeps the worktree and its commit, and git worktree prune lets git drop it. A worktree of yours where you look at the agent's branch (git worktree add --detach <folder> koloni/…) does not make its commits yours, nor does a worktree of another KOLONİ on its own koloni/… branch - but a commit you made there before it went onto such a branch, or one a branch, tag or other remote of yours holds too, stays yours; a worktree of yours whose branch you deleted still holds your commits.

The Inspector and Where the work is label such an agent "works on branch koloni/name" (an agent in a plain copy: "works in its own copy").

The branch starts from your folder as it is, not only from your last commit: your edits, staged files and new files that git does not ignore are in the agent's worktree. KOLONİ makes that one commit ("KOLONİ: your folder as koloni/name began") from an index of its own, so your files, your index, your branch and HEAD are not touched; it is the branch's first commit and shows in git log koloni/*name*. Left out, whether you staged them or not: what git ignores (.env, build output), files named as secrets (.env.local, .env.sample, a key file, credentials.json, token.json, a data file in a credentials or secrets folder - which names), node_modules, .venv and venv (linked in instead), a git repository inside your folder, KOLONİ's own .koloni folder, and every link or junction with what it leads to. Code named like a secret (credentials.py, .env.example) is taken as any file. The card says in one line which of your files were left out as a secret or a link: "Not in its branch: 2 of your files (.env, token.json) - a secret by its name, or through a link".

The card, the merge and a pull request carry the agent's work alone, measured from that commit - never your uncommitted files. A merge waits for your commit:

  • If the agent changed a file you have uncommitted changes in, the card lists it under what is in the way; commit yours, then Merge.
  • If it changed the very lines you had not committed when it began (or a new file of yours), the card says so - nothing is merged or sent as a pull request over them, and no agent puts them together. Commit yours, then Merge.
  • If what is in the way is another agent's work you took in and did not commit yet, the card names that agent's Take in: commit it (on its card, where a commit is offered), then Merge.

Where the agent's work changes a file you had not committed when it began, the card says so and waits for your Merge, at Full auto too.

If your folder had more new or changed files than a copy takes, your git is older than 2.40, or git could not take your folder as it is (a file another program holds open, a path too long for git, a folder it may not read, or longer than three minutes), the branch starts from your last commit as before, and its card says so in one line under its heading: your uncommitted changes were not in it.

Its worktree, in your project's .koloni/worktrees/ (where), is locked while the agent works (git worktree list -v says "KOLONİ: an agent works here; KOLONİ removes it"), so your own git worktree prune, remove or move leaves it alone. KOLONİ unlocks it before it removes it. When KOLONİ starts, it removes git's records of its own worktrees whose folder is gone (after a crash, say), and nothing else: never your worktrees, never a branch. The Orchestrator is told that koloni/… branches and these worktrees are not its to delete, rename or switch to.

In its copy, git works for the agent on its own branch, and it is told so: status, diff, history and its commits there, with a few plain options, run as its other commands do. Any other option, and git that reaches your own repository - switching branches, stashing, reset, merge, push, config - is asked at every level, Full auto too. In a project that runs in Docker the agent is told that git does not work in its copy: the worktree points to a folder on this machine, not in the container.

Your repository's git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, also those of a core.hooksPath such as husky's) do not run for an agent's own git commands in its copy - a commit on its branch included - nor for an MCP server's it starts there; nor does your core.fsmonitor, and its commits are not signed. On a branch, a command that clears or sets git's own environment (unset GIT_…, env -i, $env:GIT_… =) would bring them back: it is asked at every level, Full auto too.

Those settings reach whatever the agent runs in its copy, your project's tests too: a test that needs your git hooks or signed commits does not get them there.

A secret you gave in this turn (see Security model) never leaves on a branch:

  • If a file on a finished branch holds it, the card does not merge it or open a pull request, at any level, even on your click. Take the secret off the branch, or press Discard, which deletes the branch.
  • If the agent stopped first, or nobody watched the turn, a branch that holds it is deleted whole and the Orchestrator is told (on a Stop, the chat says so too). For a branch opened again from an earlier turn, the work of those turns goes with it.
  • Keep this branch after merging is refused when any of its commits holds it.

items.title: When an agent stops
items.text:
An agent on a branch that stops before it finishes leaves its work committed on the branch. That holds also when you press Stop or Stop everything while it works; the chat says so. A Stop while KOLONİ merges a finished branch by itself (at Full auto) waits for git to finish: the merge is on its card, and the branch's worktree goes.

Told to go on (by the Orchestrator, in this turn or a later one you watch), it goes on on the same branch: its earlier commits are there, and new work goes on top. Its merge is still held to where the branch was first made from: if the project is on another branch now, or that commit is gone from it, the merge waits for you, at Full auto too. Its work is still measured from your folder as the branch began.

A branch copy kept over a restart comes back as a kept card, like a plain copy's: a file you changed too is merged line by line, from what the branch was made of. Discard deletes its branch and git's record of its worktree; so does a Take in that took all of it, unless the agent may still go on on that branch.

Sometimes it cannot go on on its branch. Then it works in a fresh copy of the project instead:

  • The branch was merged or sent as a pull request already: it and the Orchestrator are told why.
  • Git refuses the branch (it was deleted, another branch has its name now, or it is checked out somewhere else): they are told why too.
  • You pressed Discard, which deleted the branch: no message.
  • The branch was made by an older KOLONİ that did not record where it started: no message.

An agent in a plain working copy that stops unfinished keeps what it changed: by itself (it failed, or hit its step limit), and on Stop or Stop everything too, also when its Take in card was already waiting for you. A card under Ready to take in offers Take in or Discard; nothing of it reaches your folder before that, at Full auto too. An agent told to go on gets that copy back. A copy with no changes is removed. A team's recipe and a job while you're away keep their copy on a Stop as well. Every copy kept for your word, in any chat, is listed in Settings › The app › Your data, with what it takes and Discard; KOLONİ deletes none unasked.

The git button in the top bar ("⑂ main · 4 changed") opens Where the work is. It reads git and changes nothing but the branch you switch to. It has three parts, each saying in words how a piece of work stands:

  • Your branch: what is not saved in git yet (See changes), the last commit, and + New branch. While a turn works or files are not committed, it says why you can't switch.
  • Agents' copies · this chat: "working" (See changes), "finished, waits for you" (Take in…), or "kept" (Look).
  • Other branches: "not joined" or "joined ✓", how many commits ahead and behind, with Look and Switch to. What an agent said it made, but git does not show, is listed last.

While a branch is open in the Workspace (Look), it shows read only, against your branch, with Back to the project.

items.title: Starting from a GitHub issue
items.text:
On the Chats page, From a GitHub issue… (beside New chat) starts a chat in the open chat's folder from an issue. Paste the issue's address, or its #number in the project's repository, or pick one of the repository's open issues from the list. KOLONİ opens a new chat, attaches the issue's title, text and comments as a file (github-issue-12.md), and writes a short first message. Nothing runs until you press Send. Long issues are cut at about 20,000 characters.

Anyone can write an issue, so KOLONİ marks its text as data for the agents, never as your instructions. See Outside content for what that does and does not stop.

KOLONİ reads GitHub with your own gh (GitHub's CLI) and never stores or sees a token. Install gh from https://cli.github.com and sign in once with gh auth login. Until you do, the dialog says why no issues are listed. The project folder must be a git repository. Listing issues, or picking one by #number, also needs its git remote to be on GitHub; an issue's address works without that.

items.title: Committing
items.text: With Save each sub-agent's work as a git commit on (Settings › This project › When the work is done), the card offers a commit once the changes are in: one commit per piece of work, only where the folder is the top of a git repository. It is always your click, and nothing is pushed.
